findings.title: PTC1 carries the whole input current and its post-reflow resistance is up to 160 mOhm; the same-family 0805L150SLYR is a drop-in at 15-65 mOhm
findings.current_part: PTC1 = Littelfuse 0805L075SLYR, LoRho 0805L SL series PPTC. Verified from the Littelfuse LoRho datasheet table: Ihold 0.75 A, Itrip 1.50 A, Vmax 6 V, Imax 50 A, Pd 0.6 W, R_min 0.040 Ohm, R_1max 0.160 Ohm (R_1max is defined as the maximum resistance at 20 C measured one hour after tripping OR after 260 C reflow, i.e. it is the relevant bound for a soldered board). Package A = 2.00-2.20 mm, B = 1.20-1.50 mm, C = 0.40-0.75 mm; solder pad layout F/G/H = 1.00/1.20/1.50 mm. Digi-Key's page for the same part independently lists 40 mOhm initial / 160 mOhm post-trip. Board netlist confirms PTC1 pad1 = VBATT, pad2 = VCC, and VCC feeds C37, L1, L2 and U5 VIN/VIN1/VIN2 — i.e. 100% of converter input current passes through it.
findings.proposal: Littelfuse 0805L150SLYR, same LoRho 0805L SL series, same datasheet, same 0805 body (A 2.00-2.20, B 1.20-1.50, C 0.40-0.75 mm) and the SAME recommended solder pad layout (F/G/H = 1.00/1.20/1.50 mm), so it drops onto the existing Fuse_0805_2012Metric land with no PCB change. Specs: Ihold 1.50 A, Itrip 3.00 A, Vmax 6 V, Imax 50 A, Pd 0.6 W, R_min 0.015 Ohm, R_1max 0.065 Ohm. Conservative middle option if you want to keep the trip point lower: 0805L110SLYR, Ihold 1.10 A, R_min 0.030 / R_1max 0.130 Ohm.
findings.benefit: Only the resistance bounds are published, so I give the range and a central value. Series resistance drops from 0.040-0.160 Ohm to 0.015-0.065 Ohm; central estimate 0.080 -> 0.030 Ohm (2x R_min, which is where reflowed parts typically land). At the max in-use input current of 480 mA (1175 mW / 2.45 V): loss now = 0.480^2 x 0.080 = 18.4 mW, after = 0.480^2 x 0.030 = 6.9 mW, SAVING 11.5 mW. Bounds: best case 0.480^2 x (0.040-0.015) = 5.8 mW, worst case 0.480^2 x (0.160-0.065) = 21.9 mW. With the ClockxControl at 1.75x the extra 62 mA on VOUT3 = 207 mW of rail power = ~232 mW at VCC at 89% = +97 mA of input current, so 577 mA: saving = 0.577^2 x 0.050 = 16.6 mW (range 8.3-31.6 mW). At idle (68 mA) the saving is 0.068^2 x 0.050 = 0.23 mW — nil. This is an in-use-only lever, but at 12-17 mW out of a 1175 mW budget it is ~1.4% of total system power and it is a two-cent part change.
findings.risk: Raises the trip point from 1.50 A to 3.00 A, so PTC1 no longer catches faults between 1.5 and 3.0 A. What it still protects: a hard short on the VCC node. That is fine because (a) F1 upstream is a 2 A Accu-Guard whose 5-second fusing current is 4.00 A, still above the new PTC trip point, and (b) the LTC3527 cannot itself draw more than its two switch limits (800 mA + 400 mA peak inductor current, folded back to 500/350 mA when VOUT < 1 V), so the converter can never present a 1.5-3.0 A load. The 0805L150SLYR is 0.15 mm taller at worst (C max 0.75 vs 0.75 — identical per the LoRho table), so no height risk. If you want to keep more fault sensitivity, take 0805L110SLYR instead and accept ~7 mW instead of ~12 mW.
findings.verify_reason:
I fetched the Littelfuse LoRho datasheet myself (RS Components mirror, Littelfuse rev 08/06/19 — the Mouser 2011 link the finding cites is now JS-blocked). CONFIRMED: 0805L150SL = Ihold 1.50 A, Itrip 3.00 A, Vmax 6 V, Imax 50 A, Pd 0.6 W, R_min 0.015 Ohm, R_1max 0.065 Ohm — exact. Drop-in CONFIRMED: 0805L075SL and 0805L150SL share identical rows in the Dimensions table (A 2.00-2.20, B 1.20-1.50, C 0.40-0.75, D 0.20-0.55, E 0.05-0.45 mm) AND the identical solder pad layout F/G/H = 1.00/1.20/1.50 mm, so it lands on the existing Bucketmouse:Fuse_0805_2012Metric with no PCB change. Part exists and is stocked (Digi-Key 3593808/3429597, LCSC C207025, Farnell 2752735). Netlist premise CONFIRMED by my own dump: F1 pad2 = VBATT; VBATT fans out to PTC1 pad1, SW1 pad1 (CSS-1310B slide switch — logic only, net 'SW', NOT in the current path), D2 and R9; PTC1 pad2 = VCC, and VCC has exactly 8 pads: C37, L1, L2, TP32, U5 VIN/VIN1/VIN2. So 100% of converter input current does pass through PTC1. Foldback claim CONFIRMED verbatim from the LTC3527 datasheet p.13: 'the peak switch current limit is reduced to 500mA (typical) for converter 1 and 350mA (typical) for converter 2 when VOUT is less than 1V'. F1's 4.00 A 5-second fusing current CONFIRMED from the Accu-Guard II table.

CORRECTIONS. (1) 0805L075SL R_1max is 0.150 Ohm in the datasheet, not 0.160 (Digi-Key's page does say 160 mOhm — the two sources disagree; cite both, do not state 0.160 as the datasheet value). (2) The 0805L110SLYR fallback is mis-specified: the datasheet gives Itrip 1.80 A (not 3.00) and R_min 0.030 / R_1max 0.120 Ohm (not 0.130). (3) 'central estimate 2x R_min, which is where reflowed parts typically land' is an unverified rule of thumb — nothing in the datasheet supports it. The defensible statement is the bound, not a central value. (4) Worst-case saving recomputed with the datasheet's 0.150: 0.480^2 x (0.150-0.065) = 19.6 mW, not 21.9 mW.

ARITHMETIC REDONE. 1175 mW / 2.45 V = 479.6 mA (the wiki actually measures at 2.4 V, giving 489.6 mA — either way ~480-490 mA). Best case 0.480^2 x (0.040-0.015) = 5.8 mW; central 0.2304 x 0.050 = 11.5 mW; worst 0.2304 x 0.085 = 19.6 mW. Overclocked: my own recomputation of the input current (see clockxcontrol-converter-tax) gives 580 mA, not 577 — 0.580^2 x 0.050 = 16.8 mW. At idle (68-70 mA) it is 0.24 mW, correctly called nil. All plausible inside the 1175 mW envelope (1.0-1.7% of it). Minor cosmetic: the risk field's sentence 'is 0.15 mm taller at worst (C max 0.75 vs 0.75 — identical)' is self-contradictory; the parts are dimensionally identical, so there is no height risk. Direction, drop-in status and order of magnitude all survive; the quoted spec values do not.

findings.title: PTC1's hold current at 60 C (0.47 A) is BELOW the measured peak in-use input current (0.48 A), and the ClockxControl pushes the draw to ~0.58 A
findings.current_part: PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR. Littelfuse LoRho datasheet temperature rerating table for 0805L075SLYR, hold current in A: -40 C 1.24, -20 C 1.07, 0 C 0.94, 20 C 0.75, 40 C 0.62, 60 C 0.47, 70 C 0.37, 85 C 0.23. Trip current 1.50 A at 20 C, maximum time-to-trip 8.00 s at 0.20 A above... (datasheet column: 8.00 s at the stated test current).
findings.proposal: Littelfuse 0805L150SLYR (drop-in, see finding ptc1-lorho-1a5-swap). Its rerating table: 20 C 1.50 A, 40 C 1.25 A, 60 C 0.93 A, 70 C 0.74 A, 85 C 0.50 A. Note that 0805L110SLYR is NOT a clean fix on this axis: its 85 C hold current is 0.21 A, actually worse than the 075SL's 0.23 A, per the same table.
findings.benefit: This is a reliability fix, not an efficiency one, so benefit_mw = 0. The arithmetic: MouseBiteLabs' own maximum measured in-use draw is 1175 mW; at a 2.45 V eneloop pack that is 480 mA, all of it through PTC1. The 0805L075SLYR holds 0.62 A at 40 C and 0.47 A at 60 C. A GBA shell with a Hispeedido IPS backlight at max brightness will sit well above 25 C internally, so the operating margin is between 1.29x (40 C) and 0.98x (60 C) — i.e. at 60 C the part is already at or past its hold current before any modification. Add the ClockxControl: +62 mA on VOUT3 = 207 mW of rail power = ~232 mW at VCC at 89% converter efficiency = +97 mA of input current, giving 577 mA. Margin then falls to 1.07x at 40 C and 0.81x at 60 C — i.e. guaranteed to be in the trip region at 60 C. A tripped PPTC latches (it stays hot and high-resistance until power is removed), so the failure mode is the console dying mid-game and not restarting until the batteries are pulled. With 0805L150SLYR the margin at 577 mA becomes 2.6x at 20 C, 2.17x at 40 C and 1.61x at 60 C.
findings.risk: Same as the efficiency finding: higher trip threshold. I have NOT measured the actual internal temperature at PTC1 — the 40 C and 60 C rows are the honest bracket, and if the real internal temperature is only 30 C the current part is marginal rather than failing. Also note the 480 mA figure assumes a 2.45 V pack; with a nearly flat pack at 2.0 V the same 1175 mW would be 588 mA, making the margin worse still.
findings.verify_reason:
The CONCLUSION is right and in fact understated, but EVERY rerating number quoted is wrong — the engineer read the 0603 rows of the Temperature Rerating table instead of the 0805 rows.

What the Littelfuse LoRho datasheet (rev 08/06/19) actually says, Hold Current (A) at -40/-20/0/20/40/60/70/85 C:
  0805L075SL: 1.15 / 1.00 / 0.85 / 0.75 / 0.55 / 0.40 / 0.30 / 0.20
  0805L110SL: 1.70 / 1.50 / 1.30 / 1.10 / 0.85 / 0.60 / 0.50 / 0.30
  0805L150SL: 2.25 / 2.00 / 1.75 / 1.50 / 1.15 / 0.85 / 0.65 / 0.45
The finding's '0805L075SLYR' row (1.24/1.07/0.94/0.75/0.62/0.47/0.37/0.23) is the 0603L075SL row (1.23/1.08/0.94/0.75/0.61/0.45/0.36/0.23). Its '0805L150SLYR' row (1.50/1.25/0.93/0.74/0.50) is the 0603L150SL row (1.50/1.25/0.95/0.80/0.50). Diagnostic of a row-read error, not a revision difference.

REFUTED outright: 'the 0805L110SLYR is NOT a clean fix on this axis: its 85 C hold current is 0.21 A, actually worse than the 075SL's 0.23 A'. The datasheet says 0805L110SL is 0.30 A at 85 C against the 0805L075SL's 0.20 A — it is 50% BETTER, not worse. 0.21 A is the 1206L110SL figure and 0.23 A is the 0603L075SL figure.

MARGINS REDONE at the correct 0805 numbers, 480 mA in-use: 40 C 0.55/0.48 = 1.15x (finding said 1.29x); 60 C 0.40/0.48 = 0.83x (finding said 0.98x) — the stock part is already ~17% below its rerated hold current at 60 C, worse than claimed. At my recomputed overclocked 580 mA: 20 C 1.30x, 40 C 0.95x, 60 C 0.69x. With 0805L150SL at 580 mA: 20 C 2.59x, 40 C 1.98x (not 2.17x), 60 C 1.47x (not 1.61x). With 0805L110SL: 1.90x / 1.47x / 1.03x — a genuinely usable middle option, contrary to the finding.

ONE OVERSTATEMENT: 'guaranteed to be in the trip region at 60 C' is too strong. Ihold is defined as the maximum current the device will pass WITHOUT tripping; Itrip (1.50 A at 20 C) is the minimum current at which it WILL trip. Rerating Itrip by the same 0.40/0.75 factor puts it near 0.80 A at 60 C, so 0.58 A sits in the indeterminate band between rerated Ihold and rerated Itrip — 'may trip, eventually' rather than 'guaranteed'. Also worth stating: 480 mA is the absolute worst case (max brightness + Everdrive + max volume + speaker); the low end of the in-use envelope, 568 mW, is only 232 mA, where there is no issue at any temperature. And the 60 C internal temperature at PTC1 (located at 31.9, -27.6, the battery end, away from the screen) is unmeasured — the finding admits this. Reliability finding, benefit 0 mW, correct.

findings.title: The LTC3527 makes one Burst Mode decision for both channels, so the ~0.7 mA 5 V rail is forced into 1.2 MHz PWM — this is the single largest identified piece of the 29 mW AGBM-01/02 gap
findings.current_part: U5 = LTC3527, MODE pin (3) tied to GND per the board netlist, so automatic Burst Mode is selected. Datasheet, Burst Mode Operation section, verbatim: "To realize the efficiency benefits of Burst Mode operation, both VOUT1 and VOUT2 must be under a light load current condition, if they are both enabled." and "Once the LTC3527/LTC3527-1 have left Burst Mode operation and returned to normal operation, they will remain there until both output loads are reduced below the burst threshold current." Burst Mode Threshold Current vs VIN for VOUT1 = VOUT2 = 3.3 V (Fig. G14, 2.2 MHz) reads ~16 mA (converter 1) / ~18 mA (converter 2) leave-burst at VIN 2.4 V; at the board's 1.2 MHz the per-cycle energy is ~1.8x higher so the threshold scales up to roughly 30 mA — the datasheet publishes no 1.2 MHz threshold curve, so that is my extrapolation.
findings.proposal: No drop-in fix exists inside the LTC3527 — the shared-burst behaviour is architectural. It is fixed only by the AGBM-02 transplant (finding agbm02-converter-transplant), where each TPS63802 makes its own PFM decision. Partial mitigation: see l2-3u3-raise-burst-threshold.
findings.benefit: Quantified off the datasheet's own curves. VOUT5 idle load ~0.7 mA -> P_out = 5.014 V x 0.7 mA = 3.5 mW. From Fig. G07 (VOUT1 = 5 V, 1.2 MHz), the VIN = 2.4 V BURST curve at 0.7 mA reads ~84%, the VIN = 2.4 V FIXED curve at 0.7 mA reads ~33%. Burst: 3.5/0.84 = 4.2 mW in, 0.7 mW loss. Fixed: 3.5/0.33 = 10.6 mW in, 7.1 mW loss. Delta = 6.4 mW, i.e. 22% of the whole 29 mW AGBM-01/AGBM-02 idle gap, spent switching a 4.7 uH inductor at 1.2 MHz to deliver 3.5 mW. Accounting for the rest of the 29 mW: ch2 conduction loss at the 37 mA idle point is I_rms^2 x (0.5734 + 0.120) = 0.0604^2 x 0.6934 = 2.5 mW versus ~0.2 mW for a TPS63802 with 18-43 mOhm switches and a 22 mOhm inductor, so ~2.3 mW; the LTC3527's active quiescent current is 500 uA typ / 900 uA max measured into VOUT (5.014 V) = 2.5 mW at the output = ~2.8 mW reflected to the input versus 2 x 11 uA x 2.5 V = 0.055 mW for two TPS63802s, so ~2.7 mW (partly already inside the efficiency curves, so do not simply add it). Identified total ~9-11 mW of 29 mW; the residual ~18 mW is 1.2 MHz gate-drive, switching and ferrite core loss in two 3x3x1.5 mm drums versus 2 MHz PFM with 0.47 uH metal-composite parts, which is not separable from published data. CRITICAL for this fork: the ClockxControl's own 12 mA lands on VDD3, which is fed from VOUT3, so idle VOUT3 goes 37 -> 49 mA. That takes the 3.3 V channel unambiguously above the leave-burst threshold at ALL times, permanently locking the 5 V channel into fixed-frequency operation. ECO-6 therefore costs ~6 mW of converter loss on top of the 40 mW its 12 mA actually consumes.
findings.risk: No change proposed, so no risk. The 84%/33% efficiency reads are eyeballed off a log-x graph and are good to maybe +/-4 points; that puts the 6.4 mW figure in a 5-8 mW band. My 0.7 mA VOUT5 idle load is an estimate from R25 = 3.3 k and the green LED — if it is really 2 mA the delta grows to ~7.6 mW, if it is 0.2 mA it shrinks to ~2 mW.
findings.verify_reason:
The architectural claim is CONFIRMED. I pulled the LTC3527 datasheet text myself: 'To realize the efficiency benefits of Burst Mode operation, both VOUT1 and VOUT2 must be under a light load current condition, if they are both enabled' and 'Once the LTC3527/LTC3527-1 have left Burst Mode operation and returned to normal operation, they will remain there until both output loads are reduced below the burst threshold current' — verbatim, exactly as quoted. My own pinout dump confirms MODE (pin 3) = GND and FSEL (pin 10) = GND, and the EC table confirms FSEL = 0 V selects 1.2 MHz (0.9/1.2/1.5 MHz). The datasheet also confirms the device 'powers itself from the higher VOUT' once it exceeds VIN by 0.24 V, so charging the 500 uA active Iq to 5.014 V is correct. Figure identification is correct: page 4 lays out G01-G08 in the order the titles appear, so G05 = VOUT2 = 3.3 V at 1.2 MHz and G07 = VOUT1 = 5 V at 1.2 MHz. G13/G14/G15 are indeed labelled '2.2MHz OPERATION' on the plots, so the finding is right that no 1.2 MHz threshold curve is published.

FOUR CORRECTIONS, all reducing the number. (1) I re-read G07 by pixel analysis rather than by eye (600 dpi render, axis gridlines located at 100/90/.../20% and the 0.01/0.1/1/10/100/1000 decades). At 0.7 mA the lowest BURST trace (2.4 V) reads 82.5%, not 84%, and the lowest FIXED trace (2.4 V) reads 37%, not 33%. (2) The VOUT5 idle load is not 0.7 mA. I dumped the net: VOUT5 has 13 pads, and the dominant DC load is R25 3.3k -> DL1 (150060VS75000 green LED) -> /D1A -> Q9B drain, i.e. the power LED, which alone draws (5.014 - ~2.1)/3300 = 0.88 mA whenever the console is on; add R65/R66 100k, R21+R22 (2.14 uA) and the U11/U14 quiescent currents and the rail sits at roughly 1.0-1.1 mA, not 0.7. (3) Gross delta redone at 1.0 mA and the corrected curve reads: P_out 5.01 mW; burst loss 5.01/0.85 - 5.01 = 0.88 mW; fixed loss 5.01/0.43 - 5.01 = 6.6 mW; gross delta 5.8 mW. At the finding's own 0.7 mA with my curve reads it is 5.2 mW, not 6.4 mW. (4) The important one: the G07 FIXED curve was measured with only converter 1 loaded, so it carries the ENTIRE 500 uA device active quiescent current (500 uA x 5.014 V = 2.5 mW). On this board converter 2 is in PWM regardless, so that 2.5 mW is already being spent — it is not a marginal cost of converter 1 leaving burst. The marginal penalty is therefore roughly (6.6 - 2.5) - 0.88 = 3.2 mW, not 6.4 mW. The finding half-sees this ('partly already inside the efficiency curves, so do not simply add it') but then still books the full curve delta.

So: gross 5-6 mW, marginal ~3 mW, out of a 29 mW gap. Still a real effect and still probably the largest single identified item, but roughly half the claimed size. The ~30 mA extrapolated 1.2 MHz burst threshold remains unsupported by any published data — the finding says so, which is honest, but everything downstream of it (including l2-3u3-raise-burst-threshold) inherits that uncertainty. One further datasheet fact the finding missed that reinforces its own case: 'Burst Mode operation is inhibited during start-up and soft-start and until both VOUT1 and VOUT2 are at least 0.24V greater than VIN' — with a fresh alkaline pack at 3.2 V, VOUT3 (3.336 V) clears VIN by only 0.136 V, so the part cannot enter burst at all. Benefit 0 mW is correct (no change proposed).

findings.title: The heavy 3.3 V rail is on the LTC3527's WEAK channel 2 (0.50/0.60 Ohm, 400 mA) and the near-idle 5 V rail is on the strong channel 1 (0.30/0.40 Ohm, 800 mA) — swapping them is free in BOM terms
findings.current_part: Board netlist (pinout.py U5): pin 5 VOUT1 -> VOUT5, pin 6 SW1 -> L1; pin 8 VOUT2 -> VOUT3, pin 7 SW2 -> L2. LTC3527 datasheet Electrical Characteristics: NMOS on-resistance SW1 0.30 Ohm, SW2 0.50 Ohm; PMOS on-resistance SW1 0.40 Ohm, SW2 0.60 Ohm; NMOS current limit SW1 800 mA (min), SW2 400 mA (min). Maximum Output Current vs VIN for Converter 2 (Fig. G11) at VOUT = 3.3 V reads ~200 mA at VIN 1.8 V, ~280 mA at VIN 2.4 V, peaking ~390 mA near VIN 3.0 V. Converter 1 (Fig. G10) at VOUT = 3.3 V reads roughly double throughout.
findings.proposal: Re-map the two channels at U5: VOUT3 to VOUT1/SW1 (with L1 and C42), VOUT5 to VOUT2/SW2 (with L2 and C21), and move FB1/FB2, SHDN1/SHDN2 and PGOOD1/PGOOD2 with them so the existing sequencing is preserved (today: /EN -> SHDN2 starts the 3.3 V channel, PGOOD2 -> /PG_3V3 enables the LDOs, /PG_2V5 -> SHDN1 starts the 5 V channel, PGOOD1 -> /~RESET). No component values change; R21/R22 stay with the 5 V rail and R23/R55 with the 3.3 V rail, and C40/C41 follow their dividers. Zero BOM cost, zero extra parts.
findings.benefit: Using the CCM model in measured_anchors. At the typical in-use point (VOUT3 = 150 mA, VIN 2.45 V): I_L,avg = 0.150/0.7344 = 0.2042 A, I_rms^2 = 0.2042^2 + 0.1154^2/12 = 0.042823 A^2. On channel 2 the total series R is 0.5734 + 0.120 = 0.6934 Ohm -> 29.7 mW. On channel 1 it is 0.3734 + 0.120 = 0.4934 Ohm -> 21.1 mW. Saving 8.6 mW. With the ClockxControl at 1.75x (VOUT3 = 212 mA): I_L,avg = 0.2887 A, I_rms^2 = 0.084434 -> 58.6 mW on ch2 vs 41.7 mW on ch1, saving 16.9 mW. Penalty on the 5 V rail, which moves to channel 2: at max brightness (88 mA, D = 1 - 2.45/5.014 = 0.5114, dI = 0.2221 A, I_rms^2 = 0.036548) the loss goes 0.036548 x 0.4689 = 17.1 mW to 0.036548 x 0.6689 = 24.4 mW, i.e. +7.3 mW; at min brightness (10 mA) the 5 V channel is in DCM and the penalty is under ~1 mW. NET: 8.6 - (1 to 7) = 2-8 mW without the overclock, 16.9 - (1 to 7) = 10-16 mW with it. I quote the mid of the overclocked band. Second, larger benefit: it moves the heavy rail off the 400 mA current limit — see finding converter2-current-limit-vs-overclock.
findings.risk: Needs a schematic edit plus a PCB revision: L1/L2 stay on the same land patterns but SW1/SW2, VOUT1/VOUT2, FB1/FB2, SHDN1/SHDN2 and PGOOD1/PGOOD2 all re-route around a QFN-16 whose pads are 0.3048 x 0.8128 mm on a 0.5 mm pitch in a very congested area. The 5 V channel on converter 2 must still deliver ~88 mA: Fig. G11 shows converter 2 at VOUT = 5 V reaching roughly 130 mA at VIN 2.4 V and ~90 mA at VIN 1.8 V, so at end-of-discharge with a max-brightness screen the 5 V rail would be at its ceiling. If your screen kit draws more than ~90 mA on VSHA this swap trades one ceiling for another — verify your screen's 5 V current before committing. Efficiency numbers are conduction-only (they exclude switching and core loss, which are essentially unchanged by the swap), so they are a lower bound on the benefit but also do not capture any second-order penalty.
findings.verify_reason:
Every stated spec CONFIRMED verbatim from the LTC3527 EC table: NMOS Rds SW1 0.30 Ohm / SW2 0.50 Ohm, PMOS SW1 0.40 Ohm / SW2 0.60 Ohm, NMOS current limit SW1 800 mA min / SW2 400 mA min. Netlist CONFIRMED by my own pinout dump: pin 5 VOUT1 -> VOUT5, pin 6 SW1 -> L1; pin 8 VOUT2 -> VOUT3, pin 7 SW2 -> L2. The heavy rail is indeed on the weak channel.

I REDID THE ARITHMETIC LINE BY LINE and it is correct to the last digit. D = 1 - 2.45/3.336 = 0.2656. R_eff(ch2) = 0.2656 x 0.50 + 0.7344 x 0.60 = 0.57344; R_eff(ch1) = 0.2656 x 0.30 + 0.7344 x 0.40 = 0.37344. At 150 mA: I_L,avg 0.2042 A, dI_pp = 2.45 x 0.2656/(4.7u x 1.2M) = 0.1154 A, I_rms^2 = 0.042808; 29.7 mW vs 21.1 mW, saving 8.6 mW. At 212 mA: I_rms^2 = 0.084434; 58.6 vs 41.7, saving 16.9 mW. 5 V penalty at 88 mA: D = 0.5114, dI 0.2221, I_rms^2 0.036551; 17.1 -> 24.4 mW, +7.3 mW. All reproduce.

CORRECTIONS. (1) The net-benefit band is optimistic at the bottom. At the SAME operating point (max brightness = 88 mA on VOUT5 and 150/212 mA on VOUT3) the net is 8.6 - 7.3 = 1.3 mW stock and 16.9 - 7.3 = 9.6 mW overclocked. You only get the top of the band (7.6 / 16 mW) at minimum brightness, where VOUT3 is also lighter. The honest headline is 'between 1.3 and 7.6 mW stock, 9.6 to 16 mW overclocked, and the two ends are not independent'. Quoting 5 and 13 as 'mid' silently averages incompatible operating points. (2) I re-read Fig. G11 by pixel analysis (axes located at VIN 0.5-4.5 V and 0-500 mA). The VOUT = 5 V trace reads ~107 mA at VIN 1.8 V and ~155 mA at VIN 2.4 V, NOT '~90 mA at 1.8 V and ~130 mA at 2.4 V'. The finding is more pessimistic than the datasheet — the 5 V rail retains ~20% margin at end-of-discharge after the swap rather than none. That makes the swap safer than presented, but the caution to measure your screen's VSHA current still stands. (3) Useful detail the finding misses: the QFN-16 pinout is mirror-symmetric about the horizontal axis (1<->12, 2<->11, 5<->8, 6<->7, 13<->16), and L1/L2 are the same 4.7 uH part and C21/C42 the same 22 uF part, so the 'swap' is a mirror of one block rather than an arbitrary reroute. It is still a schematic change plus a PCB revision, which the finding grades correctly. (4) Independent corroboration that the weak channel is the problem: my pixel read of G05 shows the VIN = 2.4 V trace falling from 91.1% at 150 mA to 88.9% at 212 mA — converter 2 is visibly running out of headroom exactly where the overclock puts it.

findings.title: With the ClockxControl at 1.75x, VOUT3 demands ~212 mA — more than LTC3527 converter 2 can deliver at VIN 1.8 V, so the console browns out before the batteries are flat
findings.current_part: U5 converter 2 (VOUT2 -> VOUT3): NMOS current limit 400 mA minimum (spec is a MIN, tested over -40 to 85 C), NMOS 0.50 Ohm, PMOS 0.60 Ohm. Maximum Output Current vs VIN for Converter 2 (datasheet Fig. G11), VOUT = 3.3 V curve: ~200 mA at VIN 1.8 V, ~230 mA at VIN 2.0 V, ~280 mA at VIN 2.4 V. The datasheet front page also states the part delivers only "3.3V at 400mA/200mA from Two Cells" — 200 mA is converter 2's rating for exactly this application.
findings.proposal: Either (a) move VOUT3 to converter 1 per finding ltc3527-channel-assignment-backwards, which raises the limit to 800 mA and roughly doubles the Fig. G10 ceiling; or (b) transplant the AGBM-02 converter, whose TPS63802 has a 4 A minimum boost-mode peak current limit and delivers ~1.5 A at VIN 1.8 V (Fig. 10-2); or (c) gate the ClockxControl down from 1.75x when the low-battery flag asserts.
findings.benefit: Reliability, not power, so benefit_mw = 0. The arithmetic at end-of-discharge, VIN = 1.8 V, VOUT3 = 3.336 V: D = 1 - 1.8/3.336 = 0.4604; I_L,avg = 0.212/0.5396 = 0.393 A; dI_pp = 1.8 x 0.4604/(4.7u x 1.2M) = 0.147 A; I_peak = 0.393 + 0.0735 = 0.466 A. That is 17% ABOVE the 400 mA minimum current limit, and it agrees independently with Fig. G11, which shows converter 2 topping out near 200 mA of output at VIN 1.8 V against a 212 mA demand. When the limit is hit, VOUT3 sags, the NCV8164 feeding VDD2 drops out of regulation, and the AGB core browns out. Without the overclock the demand is 150 mA against the same ~200 mA ceiling — a 33% margin, which is why the stock board works. So the overclock converts a comfortable margin into a deficit and shortens usable battery life by cutting off the bottom of the discharge curve. Note this is independent of, and worse than, the input-side PTC trip risk.
findings.risk: Fig. G11 is read off a graph at a single VOUT (3.3 V, versus the board's 3.336 V) and I extrapolated the 200 mA reading at VIN 1.8 V; the 400 mA current limit is a guaranteed minimum so typical parts will do better. My 212 mA figure rests on the +50 mA central estimate of insideGadgets' 40-60 mA — at +40 mA the demand is 202 mA and it is a coin flip; at +60 mA it is 222 mA and the deficit is clear. Measure VOUT3 current with the module fitted at 1.75x before deciding how urgent this is.
findings.verify_reason:
Independently verified end to end. Front page verbatim: 'Delivers 3.3V at 200mA/100mA from one Alkaline/NiMH Cell, or 3.3V at 400mA/200mA from Two Cells' — 200 mA is converter 2's own rating for this exact application. EC table: NMOS Current Limit SW2 = 400 mA, MIN, with the l marker denoting -40 to 85 C. Rds 0.50/0.60 Ohm confirmed.

I re-read Fig. G11 numerically rather than trusting the finding's eyeball. Rendering page 5 at 600 dpi and locating the gridlines (VIN 0.5...4.5 V at 137.4 px per 0.5 V; 0...500 mA at 2.198 px per mA), the VOUT = 3.3 V trace reads 205 mA at VIN 1.8 V, ~220 mA at 2.0 V and ~280 mA at 2.4 V. The finding said 200 / 230 / 280. Confirmed within read error.

Peak-current arithmetic redone: D = 1 - 1.8/3.336 = 0.46043; I_L,avg = 0.212/0.53957 = 0.3929 A; dI_pp = 1.8 x 0.46043/(4.7u x 1.2M) = 0.14695 A; I_peak = 0.3929 + 0.0735 = 0.4664 A, i.e. 16.6% above the 400 mA guaranteed minimum. Reproduces exactly. And this is optimistic: it uses the ideal duty cycle, so a real part with losses runs a higher D and a higher I_L,avg still.

TWO CAVEATS worth adding, neither fatal. (1) 400 mA is a guaranteed MIN, and G11 itself implies the typical part does better: at VOUT 3.3 V / VIN 3.05 V the plot peaks at 393 mA of OUTPUT current with D = 0.086, which back-computes to a typical peak inductor current near 470-500 mA. So a typical board will limp rather than brown out. (2) The failure mode is a soft one — VOUT3 sags, the NCV8164 (dropout 125 mV typ at 2.5 V / 300 mA, so ~790 mV of headroom today) eventually loses regulation, and you lose the bottom of the discharge curve. It is not a dead console. Third, independent corroboration I found on my own: my pixel read of Fig. G05 shows the VIN 2.4 V efficiency falling from 91.1% at 150 mA to 88.9% at 212 mA, which is the signature of a converter approaching its ceiling. The finding's benefit_mw = 0 and its 'measure VOUT3 with the module fitted' advice are both right.

findings.title: Transplanting AGBM-02's twin TPS63802 converter into AGBM-01 is worth the measured 29 mW at idle and ~26 mW in use, and the inductor land pattern is already identical
findings.current_part: U5 = LTC3527 in Bucketmouse:QFN-16_UD, 16 pads of 0.3048 x 0.8128 mm on a 0.5 mm pitch at +/-1.4478 mm plus a 1.5494 mm square exposed pad, at (26.9, -39.9). L1/L2 = Taiyo Yuden LSXND3030QKT4R7MNG, 4.7 uH +/-20%, DCR 0.12 Ohm typ / 0.144 max, Isat 1.02 A, 3.0 x 3.0 x 1.5 mm, in footprint Bucketmouse:L_Taiyo-Yuden_NR-20xx_HandSoldering (pads 1.65 x 2.0 mm at +/-1.175 mm). LTC3527EUD is listed out of stock at Digi-Key with a 2026-04 lead time and $1.81-$4.52 depending on source; the AGBM-01 README carries its own note that "This part has been going in and out of stock at various places for the past few months."
findings.proposal: Two TI TPS63802 (VSON-10 DLA, 2 x 2 mm, pads 0.25 mm wide on a 0.5 mm pitch at x = -0.9 / +0.55...0.75 mm), exactly as AGBM-02 does it: U5 -> VOUT5 with R59 820k / R60 91k, U13 -> VOUT3 with R72 510k / R73 91k (V_FB = 500 mV, and the datasheet requires the low-side resistor <= 100 kOhm, which the board's existing 560 k and 1 M do NOT satisfy so they must change). L1/L2 -> Samsung CIGT201610EHR47MNE, 0.47 uH +/-20%, DCR 18 mOhm typ / 22 max, Isat 5.5 A min, Irms 4.8 A min, 2.0 x 1.6 x 1.0 mm. Add one 10 uF 0603 (a second VIN cap, AGBM-02's C57) and one 22 uF 0805 (AGBM-02's C58 on VOUT5). Delete C40/C41 — AGBM-02 has no feed-forward caps on its FB nets. MODE (pin 2) to GND on both, exactly as AGBM-02 does, which is what enables the per-device PFM.
findings.benefit: Idle: this is the measured 29 mW (170 -> 141 mW), a 17% cut, with the whole downstream identical. In use, from the two datasheets' own curves at VIN 2.45 V / VOUT 3.3 V and 212 mA out (the overclocked point): LTC3527 Fig. G05 reads ~88% at the 2.4 V trace, TPS63802 Fig. 10-5 reads ~91% at the 2.5 V trace. P_out = 3.336 x 0.212 = 707 mW, so P_in goes 707/0.88 = 803 mW to 707/0.91 = 777 mW, saving 26 mW. Without the overclock (150 mA), 500 mW out, 568 -> 550 mW in, saving 18 mW. Conduction loss alone tells a much larger story (LTC3527 ch2 58.6 mW vs TPS63802 boost R_eff = 0.2656 x 0.018 + 0.7344 x 0.043 = 0.0364 Ohm plus 0.022 Ohm DCR, about 7 mW), but the TPS63802 pays much of that back in switching and core loss with 0.66 A p-p of ripple at 2.1 MHz, so I quote the curve-based numbers, not the conduction-only ones. Secondary wins: converter 2's 400 mA ceiling disappears (TPS63802 peak current limit is 4 A minimum in boost, 3.8 A in buck); the part is buck-boost so it stays in regulation with fresh 3.2 V alkalines above VOUT3; each device has its own 11 uA PFM decision so the 5 V rail is never dragged out of power-save; and sourcing improves markedly (TPS63802DLAR is widely stocked at roughly $0.62-$1.74 versus the LTC3527's $1.81-$4.52 and backorder).
findings.risk: This is a full PCB revision of the converter block: the QFN-16 3x3 land and the VSON-10 2x2 land share nothing, and you need two ICs where one sat, in a 4-layer 1.0 mm board inside a GBA shell where the ClockxControl now also occupies 18.65 x 12.00 mm at board centre. AGBM-02 places its two converters and two inductors at (22.75,-44.55)/(27.5,-37.55) and (22.25,-41.05)/(27.5,-34.2), which is a different arrangement from AGBM-01's (26.9,-39.9) and (29.5,-45)/(29.5,-34.8) — so this is a re-layout, not a patch. The one genuinely free part: both boards use the identical Bucketmouse:L_Taiyo-Yuden_NR-20xx_HandSoldering land, so the 4.7 uH -> 0.47 uH change is purely a value change. Also note VOUT3 becomes 3.302 V instead of 3.336 V, a 1% drop that slightly reduces the VDD2 LDO's headroom (still ~800 mV, far above the NCV8164's dropout). Practical verdict: if you are already respinning the board for the ClockxControl, do this; if not, take the channel swap and the PTC instead.
findings.verify_reason:
Much of this checks out, but the in-use benefit — the headline for a fork that is being overclocked — does not survive re-reading the curves.

CONFIRMED. TPS63802 datasheet (SLVSEU9D, Jan 2021), all verbatim: IQ;VIN 11 uA; Peak Current Limit Boost 4 A MIN / 5 typ / 5.75 max; Buck 3.8 A; boost Rds high-side 43 mOhm, low-side 18 mOhm; feedback 500 mV; 'The low-side resistor R2 (between FB and GND) must not exceed 100 k'; boost fSW 2.1 MHz. Samsung CIGT201610EHR47MNE verified from the Mouser datasheet PDF: 0.47 uH +/-20%, DCR 18 typ / 22 max mOhm, Isat 5.5 min / 5.9 typ A, Irms 4.8 / 5 A, 2016 case, T max 1.0 mm — exact. Taiyo Yuden LSXND3030QKT4R7MNG verified: 4.7 uH +/-20%, DCR 0.12 typ / 0.144 max, Isat 1.02 A, Irms 1.04 A, 3.0 x 3.0 x max 1.5 mm, previous PN NRS3015T4R7MNGH — exact. I opened the AGBM-02 KiCad files: U5 and U13 are both TPS63802, R59 820k / R60 91k (0.5 x (1+820/91) = 5.005 V), R72 510k / R73 91k (3.302 V), C57 10u 0603, C58 22u 0805, no C40/C41 in the design, and — the finding's best point — L1/L2 use the IDENTICAL Bucketmouse:L_Taiyo-Yuden_NR-20xx_HandSoldering land as AGBM-01, so the 4.7 -> 0.47 uH change really is value-only. The board's existing 560k and 1M FB bottom resistors do indeed violate the <=100 k rule. The 29 mW idle figure is measured data from MouseBiteLabs, not modelled.

ERRORS. (1) Package is wrong. DLA0010A is 3.1/2.9 mm x 2.1/1.9 mm — a 3 x 2 mm VSON-HR, not '2 x 2 mm'. Worse, AGBM-02 does not even use a DLA land: its footprint field reads Package_SON:VSON-10-1EP_3x3mm_P0.5mm_EP1.2x2mm. Anyone copying this finding's dimensions into a layout will get it wrong. (2) Fig. 10-2 at VIN 1.8 V reads about 1.0 A for VO = 3.3 V, not 1.5 A (x-axis starts at 1.3 V; the black trace is ~1.0 A at 1.8 and ~1.9 A at 2.3). The point that this dwarfs 200 mA is untouched. (3) THE IN-USE SAVING IS NOT SUPPORTED. I measured both curves by pixel analysis instead of eyeballing. LTC3527 G05, VIN = 2.4 V trace: 91.1% at 150 mA, 88.9% at 212 mA. TPS63802 Fig. 10-5, VI = 2.5 V trace: 91.2% at 150 mA, 91.5% at 212 mA. So at the stock 150 mA point the two converters are within 0.1 percentage point — the claimed 18 mW saving is really about 0.5 mW, i.e. nothing. Only at the overclocked 212 mA does a real gap open: 707.2/0.889 - 707.2/0.915 = 795.5 - 772.9 = 22.6 mW, close to the claimed 26. So the correct statement is 'no measurable in-use gain stock, roughly 20 mW once the ClockxControl loads VOUT3 to ~212 mA' — and note the entire in-use gain comes from the LTC3527 approaching its channel-2 ceiling, i.e. it is the same defect as converter2-current-limit-vs-overclock, not an independent win. I also checked the wiki: the in-use tables are AGBM-01 only ('All of the following measurements were performed with an AGBM-01'), so there is no measured AGBM-01 vs AGBM-02 in-use comparison to appeal to. (4) UNMENTIONED REGRESSION: TPS63802 UVLO is 1.7 V rising / 1.25 V falling and 'Minimum input voltage for full load, once started' is 2.3 V, against the LTC3527's 0.7 V start-up and 0.5 V run-once-started. The transplant gives up the bottom of the alkaline discharge curve, which for a 2xAA product is a real functional loss and belongs in the risk field. (5) The 3.302 V / NCV8164 headroom claim is fine — I confirmed dropout is 125 mV typ at 2.5 V out, 300 mA, TSOP-5.

Verdict: idle 29 mW stands as measured fact; in-use claim of 18 mW is refuted, 26 mW overclocked revises to ~22 mW; package data must be corrected before anyone lays this out.

findings.title: L2 (the 3.3 V channel) 4.7 uH -> 3.3 uH in the same case cuts DCR 120 -> 78 mOhm and raises the Burst threshold ~40%; leave L1 alone
findings.current_part: L1 = L2 = Taiyo Yuden LSXND3030QKT4R7MNG (previous PN NRS3015T4R7MNGH): 4.7 uH +/-20%, DCR 0.12 Ohm typ / 0.144 Ohm max, Isat 1.02 A (dL = 30%), temperature-rise current 1.04 A (dT = 40 C), 3.0 x 3.0 x max 1.5 mm, wire-wound ferrite. Footprint Bucketmouse:L_Taiyo-Yuden_NR-20xx_HandSoldering, pads 1.65 x 2.0 mm at +/-1.175 mm. Nearest neighbour to L1 is TP6 at 2.38 mm centre-to-centre, so there is no room for a 4x4 mm part.
findings.proposal: Taiyo Yuden LSXND3030QKT3R3MNG (previous PN NRS3015T3R3MNGH) for L2 only: 3.3 uH +/-20%, DCR 78 mOhm typ / 93.6 mOhm max, Isat 1.21 A max / 1.4 A typ, temperature-rise current 1.23 A max, same 3.0 x 3.0 x max 1.5 mm case, same series, same land. Note the saturation and thermal ratings are BETTER than the 4.7 uH part, not worse. Keep L1 (the 5 V channel) at 4.7 uH.
findings.benefit: Two effects. (1) DCR: at the typical in-use point (VOUT3 150 mA) dI_pp rises from 0.1154 to 0.6507/3.96 = 0.1643 A, so I_rms^2 goes 0.042823 to 0.043964; loss = 0.043964 x (0.5734 + 0.078) = 28.6 mW versus 0.042823 x 0.6934 = 29.7 mW, saving 1.1 mW. At the overclocked point (212 mA): 0.085575 x 0.6514 = 55.8 mW versus 58.6 mW, saving 2.8 mW. (2) The larger and less certain effect: the datasheet states "Raising the inductor value will lower the load current at which Burst Mode operation is entered", so dropping 4.7 -> 3.3 uH raises the leave-burst threshold by roughly 4.7/3.3 = 42%. My extrapolated 1.2 MHz threshold at VIN 2.45 V is ~30 mA; 42% takes it to ~43 mA. Stock VOUT3 idle is ~37 mA, so this could put the board back into Burst at idle and recover the ~6 mW that the 5 V channel is currently losing (finding ltc3527-shared-burst-decision). With the ClockxControl fitted, idle VOUT3 is ~49 mA and even 43 mA is not enough, so this lever only helps a board without the module — say so honestly. I quote only the DCR-certain part in benefit_mw.
findings.risk: I did NOT change L1. Doing so would be a net loss: the 5 V channel already runs 0.222 A p-p of ripple at 88 mA out and is in DCM at light backlight, where a smaller inductance increases RMS current more than it saves in DCR. The 42% burst-threshold scaling is my inference from a qualitative datasheet sentence; the published threshold curves are 2.2 MHz only, so treat the ~6 mW burst recovery as a hypothesis to measure, not a claim. Inductance tolerance is +/-20% on both parts, and 3.3 uH is the bottom of the datasheet's stated 1.2 MHz range ("Inductor values between 3.3uH and 4.7uH are suitable for most 1.2MHz applications"), so a -20% part is 2.64 uH, outside the recommended range — specify the M tolerance and accept that. Also verified NOT worth doing: Coilcraft XFL3012-472 is 171 mOhm max, Murata DFE322512F-4R7M is 157 mOhm, Taiyo Yuden's own metal-composite LCDND3030KKT4R7MM is 300 mOhm typ. In this envelope the installed 4.7 uH part is already near best-in-class; the only real gain is in dropping the inductance.
findings.verify_reason:
Every part number and every number in it checks out, and the arithmetic reproduces — but the finding recommends a change that makes its own converter2-current-limit-vs-overclock finding WORSE, and never says so.

CONFIRMED from Taiyo Yuden's own product pages: LSXND3030QKT4R7MNG = 4.7 uH +/-20%, DCR 0.12 typ / 0.144 max Ohm, Isat 1.02 A (dL=30%), Irms 1.04 A (dT=40 C), 3.0 +/-0.1 x 3.0 +/-0.1 x max 1.5 mm, previous PN NRS3015T4R7MNGH. LSXND3030QKT3R3MNG = 3.3 uH +/-20%, DCR 78 mOhm typ / 93.6 max, Isat 1.21 A max, Irms 1.23 A max, same case, previous PN NRS3015T3R3MNGH, status 'Mass Production (Preferred)'. Same series, same 3030 case, so same land — drop-in confirmed, and the saturation and thermal ratings really are better, not worse. Coilcraft XFL3012-472 confirmed at 171 mOhm max DCR (3.0 x 3.0 x 1.3 mm), so the 'already near best-in-class' rejection of that alternative holds. Both datasheet quotes verified verbatim: 'Inductor values between 3.3uH and 4.7uH are suitable for most 1.2MHz applications' and 'Raising the inductor value will lower the load current at which Burst Mode is operation entered'.

ARITHMETIC REDONE: dI_pp at 150 mA rises from 0.1154 to 2.45 x 0.2656/(3.3u x 1.2M) = 0.16432 A; I_rms^2 0.042808 -> 0.043948; 0.043948 x (0.57344+0.078) = 28.6 mW vs 0.042808 x 0.69344 = 29.7 mW, saving 1.1 mW. At 212 mA: 0.085574 x 0.65144 = 55.7 vs 58.6, saving 2.9 mW. Reproduces.

THE PROBLEM. The very sentence the finding quotes continues: 'Larger values of inductance will allow slightly greater output current capability (and lower the Burst Mode threshold) by reducing the inductor ripple current.' Dropping L2 to 3.3 uH therefore REDUCES converter 2's output current capability — the exact parameter that finding converter2-current-limit-vs-overclock says is already in deficit. Quantified at the end-of-discharge point in that finding: at VIN 1.8 V and 212 mA out, dI_pp goes from 0.1470 to 0.2093 A, so I_peak goes from 0.466 A to 0.497 A, i.e. from 17% to 24% above the 400 mA guaranteed minimum limit. On an overclocked board you would be trading 2.9 mW for a measurably earlier brownout. Add the acknowledged -20% tolerance corner of 2.64 uH (outside the datasheet's stated 1.2 MHz range) and the fact that the ~42% burst-threshold scaling is an inference from a qualitative sentence with no 1.2 MHz data behind it, and the honest recommendation inverts: do NOT fit 3.3 uH on a board carrying the ClockxControl. On a stock board it is a defensible 1.1 mW with a speculative upside. Confidence 0.65 was, if anything, too high.

findings.title: F1's 2 A Accu-Guard adds up to 80 mOhm in series with the whole board — up to 18 mW at max use — and it does not protect against reverse batteries anyway
findings.current_part: F1 = Kyocera AVX F0805B2R00FSTR, Accu-Guard SMD thin-film fuse. From the Accu-Guard II datasheet table: current rating 2.00 A, resistance 0.080 Ohm MAXIMUM (measured at 10% of rated current, 25 C), voltage drop 220 mV max at 1x rated current, fusing current within 5 s = 4.00 A, pre-arc I2t 0.030, 63 V. Board netlist: BT1+ -> F1 -> VBATT, so it carries every milliamp the board draws. NOTE the datasheet publishes only a maximum, not a typical, so the real installed resistance is somewhere at or below 80 mOhm.
findings.proposal: Same F0805B family, same 0805 land: F0805B2R50FW/STR (2.50 A, 0.060 Ohm max) or F0805B3R00FW/STR (3.00 A, 0.050 Ohm max). I am flagging this as a build option rather than recommending it, because the saving is bounded by a max-only spec and the protection cost is real.
findings.benefit: At the maximum measured in-use input current of 480 mA: worst-case loss now = 0.480^2 x 0.080 = 18.4 mW; with the 3 A part = 0.480^2 x 0.050 = 11.5 mW; saving up to 6.9 mW. At the overclocked 577 mA: up to 0.577^2 x 0.030 = 10.0 mW. Because only maxima are published, the true saving could be anywhere from ~0 (if the installed part measures well under 80 mOhm) to the numbers above. Combined with PTC1, the total series resistance from battery to VCC is bounded by 0.080 + 0.160 = 0.240 Ohm worst case, which at 480 mA is 55 mW, or 4.7% of the whole 1175 mW budget — that is why the input path is worth measuring with a milliohm meter before deciding anything here.
findings.risk: Weakens the last-ditch overcurrent protection from a 4.00 A to a 6.00 A five-second fusing current. Separate correctness note while I am here: F1 does NOT protect against a reversed battery pack. D1 (1SS355VMTE-17, cathode on BT1+, anode on GND per the board netlist) sits ACROSS the pack upstream of F1, so on reverse insertion the current loop is battery -> D1 -> battery and never passes through F1; the diode has to absorb the reversed pack's short-circuit current on its own until the cells sag or the user notices. That is a pre-existing upstream design property, not something the fork introduced, but it means F1's rating is only about downstream shorts and it is reasonable to trade some of it for resistance. Recommendation: measure first, and if you change anything, change PTC1 rather than F1 — the PTC gives more milliwatts per unit of protection given up.
findings.verify_reason:
I fetched the Kyocera AVX Accu-Guard II datasheet (TDS-FUSE-0001 Rev 2) and every number is exact. F0805B2R00FW/STR: current rating 2.00 A, resistance 0.080 Ohm MAX measured at 10% x I rated, 25 C; voltage drop 220 mV max at 1 x I rated; fusing current within 5 s at 25 C = 4.00 A; pre-arc I2t at 50 A = 0.030 A2-sec; rated voltage 63 V. The alternatives are exact too: F0805B2R50FW/STR = 2.50 A / 0.060 Ohm / 5.00 A, F0805B3R00FW/STR = 3.00 A / 0.050 Ohm / 6.00 A. The finding is right that only a maximum is published.

NETLIST CLAIMS VERIFIED by my own dumps. Net-(BT1-+) has exactly three pads: BT1 pin 1 (+), D1 pad 1 (K), F1 pad 1. F1 pad 2 = VBATT. So F1 carries every milliamp the board draws, AND D1 sits across the pack UPSTREAM of F1 with its cathode on BT1+ and anode on GND (KiCad diode footprints put the cathode on pad 1). On a reversed pack the loop is battery -> D1 -> battery return and never traverses F1, exactly as the finding says. That correctness note is CONFIRMED and is a genuine (upstream, pre-existing) design property.

ARITHMETIC REDONE: 0.480^2 x 0.080 = 18.4 mW; 0.480^2 x 0.050 = 11.5 mW; delta 6.9 mW. At my recomputed overclocked 580 mA: 0.580^2 x 0.030 = 10.1 mW. Combined worst-case input path with PTC1: 0.080 + 0.150 (the datasheet's R_1max for 0805L075SL; the finding used Digi-Key's 0.160) = 0.230 Ohm, which at 480 mA is 53 mW or 4.5% of 1175 mW. All plausible in the envelope.

ONE ADDITION the finding should carry: the 0.080 Ohm is specified at 10% of rated current (200 mA), while the 220 mV max at 1 x rated implies 0.110 Ohm when hot at 2 A. A thin-film fuse element has positive TCR, so the resistance at the 480-580 mA operating point sits between those, and the real saving is bounded by a number nobody has measured. That reinforces the finding's own recommendation — measure with a milliohm meter first, and spend the protection budget on PTC1 rather than F1. Cosmetic: the BOM MPN is F0805B2R00FSTR while the datasheet orders as F0805B2R00FW/STR. Grading as a build option rather than a recommendation is the right call; 4 mW quoted against a 6.9 mW ceiling is appropriately conservative.

findings.title: Output and input capacitance is comfortably adequate for LTC3527 stability even fully derated — but the 43 uF on VOUT3 makes the part leave Burst Mode at a lighter load than it otherwise would
findings.current_part: VOUT3 carries C42 22 uF (0805) + C2 10 uF (0603) + C23 10 uF (0603) + C22 1 uF (0603) = 43 uF nominal. VOUT5 carries C21 22 uF (0805) + C72 0.1 uF. VIN (VCC) carries C37 10 uF (0603) only. LTC3527 datasheet, Output and Input Capacitor Selection: "A 4.7uF to 10uF output capacitor is sufficient for most applications. Larger values up to 22uF may be used", "The internal loop compensation of the LTC3527/LTC3527-1 is designed to be stable with output capacitor values of 4.7uF or greater", and "A 2.2uF input capacitor is sufficient for most applications, although larger values may be used without limitations."
findings.proposal: No change. I considered and rejected reducing the VOUT3 bulk capacitance to raise the Burst threshold: the datasheet warns that "larger output capacitor values may cause this transition to occur at lighter loads", but VOUT3's idle load (~37 mA stock, ~49 mA with the ClockxControl) is above the leave-burst threshold at 1.2 MHz regardless of capacitance, so removing capacitance would buy nothing and would cost transient response.
findings.benefit: Zero mW — this is a verification result, and the reviewer should know the capacitor bank is not a problem so it stops being a suspect. Stability arithmetic: even at a pessimistic 70% DC-bias loss on the 22 uF 0805 at 3.336 V and 50% on the 10 uF 0603s, effective capacitance on VOUT3 is 6.6 + 5 + 5 + 0.9 = ~17 uF, more than 3x the 4.7 uF stability minimum. Ripple arithmetic in the mode the board actually runs (fixed-frequency CCM at 212 mA out): dV = dI/(8 f C_eff) = 0.1154/(8 x 1.2e6 x 17e-6) = 0.7 mV, plus ESR x dI ~= 10 mOhm x 0.115 = 1.2 mV; and the output cap's own RMS ripple current is I_out x sqrt(D/(1-D)) = 0.212 x 0.601 = 127 mA rms, which in a 22 uF X5R 0805 with ~10 mOhm ESR dissipates 0.16 mW. Nothing here is marginal. C40/C41 = 15 pF across the 1.78 M top resistors are exactly the datasheet's prescription, verbatim: "add a small feedforward capacitor across the top resistor of the feedback divider [from VOUT1 (VOUT2) to FB1 (FB2)]. A typical value of 15pF will generally suffice." Correct as designed.
findings.risk: UNVERIFIED: the exact MPN of C21/C42 could not be retrieved — the AGBM-01 BOM points at a Digi-Key short link (digikey.com/short/cfmmbvdh) and Digi-Key returned 503/403 to this session, and Murata/TDK/Samsung DC-bias viewers all returned 403 or empty data. The 70%/50% derating figures above are therefore generic X5R assumptions, not manufacturer curves — but the conclusion is insensitive to them, since even a 90% loss on every capacitor leaves 4.3 uF on VOUT3 and 2.2 uF on VOUT5, and only the VOUT5 case would then be below the 4.7 uF minimum. If you want certainty, pin the MPN and check its bias curve; a 22 uF 0805 in 10 V rating instead of 6.3 V would remove the question entirely at the same footprint.
findings.verify_reason:
The inventory and every datasheet quote check out, but one formula is the wrong topology and the finding buries the one thing on this net that actually is marginal.

CONFIRMED. My own net dumps: VOUT3 has 12 pads carrying C42 22u (0805), C2 10u, C23 10u, C22 1u = 43 uF nominal; VOUT5 carries C21 22u (0805) + C72 0.1u; VCC has exactly 8 pads and only C37 10u for input decoupling. C40/C41 15p do sit across the top divider resistors (C40 pad1 = VOUT5, pad2 = Net-(U5-FB1), same two nets as R21) — precisely the datasheet's prescription, quoted verbatim and correctly: 'add a small feedforward capacitor across the top resistor of the feedback divider [from VOUT1 (VOUT2) to FB1 (FB2)]. A typical value of 15pF will generally suffice.' The stability, input-cap and 'larger output capacitor values may cause this transition to occur at lighter loads' quotes are all verbatim-accurate. The cap RMS ripple current formula for a boost, I_out x sqrt(D/(1-D)) = 0.212 x 0.6013 = 127 mA rms, is the right formula and the right answer; 0.127^2 x 0.010 = 0.16 mW.

ERROR 1 (methodology). dV = dI/(8 f C) is the BUCK output-ripple formula. This is a boost: the output capacitor sees the full switched (chopped) current, so the dominant term is dV = I_out x D/(f x C_eff) = 0.212 x 0.2656/(1.2e6 x 17e-6) = 2.8 mV, plus ESR x the switched current step (~I_peak 0.35 A x 10 mOhm) = 3.5 mV, so about 6 mV rather than the claimed 1.9 mV. The conclusion 'nothing here is marginal' survives — 6 mV on 3.336 V is 0.18% — but the number as printed is wrong by 3x and would mislead anyone reusing it.

ERROR 2 (emphasis). The finding's own worst case identifies VOUT5 as the exposure and then files it under 'risk'. It belongs in the headline. C21 is a 22 uF 0805 sitting at 5.014 V with only C72 0.1 uF beside it. If it is a 6.3 V X5R — the commodity choice at that size — DC-bias derating at 5 V on a 6.3 V part can plausibly exceed 75%, which puts the effective capacitance at or under the datasheet's explicit 4.7 uF stability floor ('The internal loop compensation ... is designed to be stable with output capacitor values of 4.7uF or greater'), with nothing else on the net to hold it up. VOUT3, with four capacitors in parallel, has no such exposure. The actionable item is therefore: pin C21's MPN, and if it is 6.3 V, respecify a 10 V or 16 V 22 uF 0805 — same land, no PCB change. UNVERIFIED, as the finding says: I also could not retrieve C21's MPN (the AGBM-01 BOM points at a Digi-Key short link) or a manufacturer bias curve, so the 75% figure is a generic X5R expectation and this stays low-confidence — but low-confidence-and-flagged is the right treatment, not 'comfortably adequate'.

ERROR 3 (minor). The finding does not note that VOUT3's 43 uF nominal exceeds the datasheet's own guidance, 'Larger values up to 22uF may be used'. Harmless — larger output capacitance is never a stability problem on this part — but it is the reason the burst threshold on this board is at the low end.

findings.title: The "boost with VIN approaching VOUT" hypothesis is closed: VIN never reaches VOUT3 = 3.336 V on this board, so it is not the 29 mW
findings.current_part: VOUT3 = V_FB x (1 + R23/R55) = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78M/1.00M) = 3.336 V, using the LTC3527's specified feedback voltage of 1.20 V typ (1.176-1.224 V over temperature). LTC3527 maximum duty cycle 85% min / 90% typ at V_FB = 1 V; minimum duty cycle 0% at V_FB = 1.3 V; the datasheet has an explicit "VIN > VOUT Operation" section stating the part "will maintain output voltage regulation even when the input voltage is above one or both of the desired output voltages" but that "this mode is less efficient and will dissipate more power".
findings.proposal: None. Documenting the negative result so nobody chases it again.
findings.benefit: Zero mW, but it removes the leading hypothesis. Two fresh alkaline AAs are 3.2 V open circuit, which is 136 mV BELOW VOUT3 = 3.336 V, and two eneloop pro NiMH (the cells MouseBiteLabs actually tested with, per the Required-Parts wiki) are 2.6-2.8 V fresh and ~2.5 V under load. So VIN < VOUT3 at every point of every discharge curve and the converter is always boosting; the datasheet's VIN > VOUT penalty never engages. Note also that AGBM-02 does not win here either — it is buck-boost, which would be the advantage if VIN did exceed VOUT, but on this board that advantage is never cashed. The gap has to be explained by light-load mode behaviour and switch resistance instead, which is what findings ltc3527-shared-burst-decision and ltc3527-channel-assignment-backwards do.
findings.risk: One residual caveat worth knowing for alkaline users: at VIN = 3.2 V the required boost duty cycle is D = 1 - 3.2/3.336 = 4.1%, which at 1.2 MHz is a 34 ns on-time. The datasheet specifies a minimum duty cycle of 0% and does not publish a minimum on-time, so regulation is claimed, but expect pulse-skipping and elevated output ripple in the first few minutes of a fresh alkaline pack. UNVERIFIED — no minimum on-time figure exists in the datasheet to check this against.
findings.verify_reason:
The negative result is correct as far as it goes, but the finding declares the file closed while missing a threshold three paragraphs away in the same datasheet that bites harder than the one it ruled out.

CONFIRMED. VOUT3 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78M/1.00M) = 3.336 V; I read R23 = 1.78M and R55 = 1M straight out of AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch, and the EC table gives Feedback Voltage FB1, FB2 = 1.176 / 1.20 / 1.224 V over the full temperature range. This is verbatim the divider in the datasheet's own front-page 3.3 V typical application. Maximum Duty Cycle 85 min / 90 typ at VFB = 1 V and Minimum Duty Cycle 0% at VFB = 1.3 V confirmed. The 'VIN > VOUT Operation' section exists and reads as quoted. The Required-Parts wiki confirms eneloop pro / NiMH is what MouseBiteLabs recommends and tested with, so with 3.2 V fresh alkaline and ~2.5 V loaded NiMH, VIN never exceeds 3.336 V. Conclusion stands for the intended cells.

WHAT IT MISSES. The Operation section states: 'To control inrush current and to prevent the inductor currents from running away when VOUT1 or VOUT2 is close to VIN, the P-channel MOSFET synchronous rectifiers are only enabled when their respective VOUT > (VIN + 0.24V).' And separately: 'Burst Mode operation is inhibited during start-up and soft-start and until both VOUT1 and VOUT2 are at least 0.24V greater than VIN.' Two fresh alkaline AAs at 3.2 V put VOUT3 - VIN at 0.136 V, comfortably BELOW that 0.24 V gate. So on a fresh alkaline pack converter 2 runs through the PMOS body diode rather than the synchronous rectifier, and the whole device is locked out of Burst Mode regardless of load. Order of magnitude: at 150 mA out with roughly 0.7 V of body-diode drop carried for (1-D) of the cycle, that is on the order of 100 mW of extra dissipation — larger than every efficiency lever in this domain combined, and it happens for the first part of every alkaline pack's life. The threshold clears once the pack drops below 3.096 V, which is why nobody notices it as a fault. That belongs in this finding, and 'the hypothesis is closed' is the wrong conclusion to draw.

SECOND OMISSION. Lithium primary AAs (Energizer L91 and equivalents) are 1.8 V open-circuit per cell, i.e. a 3.6 V pack, which puts VIN genuinely above VOUT3 = 3.336 V. They are a common choice in this hobby even though MouseBiteLabs does not recommend them. The LTC3527 explicitly supports that mode, so it is not a hazard, but the categorical statement 'VIN < VOUT3 at every point of every discharge curve' is only true for the cells named. The alkaline minimum-on-time caveat in the risk field is correctly flagged as unverified: I confirmed the datasheet specifies Minimum Duty Cycle 0% and publishes no minimum on-time.

findings.title: What the ClockxControl actually costs through this converter: +62 mA on VOUT3 buys 165 mW of useful load for 247 mW at the battery — a 67% chain efficiency
findings.current_part: ECO-6 puts the ClockxControl's V+ on P1 pad S1 = VDD3, which the netlist shows is fed from VOUT3 through U18 (TPS22917 load switch). The overclock's extra core current lands on VDD2 = 2.5 V, produced by U8 (NCV8164ASN250T1G) whose input pin 1 is VOUT3. An LDO passes its output current 1:1 to its input, so BOTH the module's own 12 mA and the overclock's extra core current appear on VOUT3 and pass through L2, converter 2, PTC1 and F1.
findings.proposal: No component change in this finding — it is the quantification the review asked for, and it sizes the prize for the other findings. Combine with ptc1-lorho-1a5-swap (-17 mW), ltc3527-channel-assignment-backwards (-13 mW) and l2-3u3-raise-burst-threshold (-3 mW) to recover ~33 mW of the ~44 mW converter-path tax.
findings.benefit: Step by step at the in-use operating point (VIN 2.45 V, VOUT3 3.336 V, screen at max brightness). Extra load: 12 mA on VDD3 = 12 x 3.336 = 40.0 mW, plus a central 50 mA on VDD2 = 50 x 3.336 = 166.8 mW drawn from VOUT3, of which only 2.5 x 50 = 125 mW reaches VDD2 and 41.8 mW is burned as heat in U8. Total extra VOUT3 load = 62 mA = 206.8 mW. Converter tax: extra conduction loss in converter 2 alone = (0.084434 - 0.042823) x 0.6934 = 28.9 mW, i.e. the boost burns an extra 29 mW just to move that current. At ~89% overall converter efficiency the 207 mW of rail power costs 232 mW at VCC, so input current rises by 232/2.4 = 97 mA, from 480 to 577 mA. Input path tax: with a central 0.080 Ohm PTC + 0.070 Ohm fuse = 0.150 Ohm, loss goes 0.480^2 x 0.15 = 34.6 mW to 0.577^2 x 0.15 = 49.9 mW, +15.3 mW. TOTAL at the battery: ~247 mW extra for 165 mW of useful load (125 mW into the AGB core/SRAM and 40 mW into the module), a 67% chain efficiency; ~44 mW of that 247 mW is pure converter-path and input-path loss. Equivalently, every extra milliamp on VOUT3 costs the battery about 1.6x its face value once the boost, the LDO drop, the PTC and the fuse are counted. On the 1175 mW in-use figure that takes the console to ~1422 mW and cuts the 5h20m worst-case battery life to roughly 4h25m.
findings.risk: The biggest uncertainty is where insideGadgets' 40-60 mA actually sits. They publish it as a console-level increase, not a per-rail one. FLAGGED as instructed: if some of it is on VDD3 or VDD35 rather than VDD2, the LDO's 41.8 mW of waste shrinks but the VOUT3 total does not change, because every one of those rails is fed from VOUT3 — so the converter and input-path numbers above are robust to that ambiguity and only the LDO term moves. At the low end (+40 mA) the totals scale to ~205 mW / ~37 mW of loss; at the high end (+60 mA) to ~271 mW / ~48 mW. The 89% converter efficiency is read off datasheet Fig. G05 and the 0.150 Ohm input resistance is a central value between published bounds, both stated above.
findings.verify_reason:
The power-path reasoning is right and I verified it from the netlist, but the finding contains an internal contradiction and, once the contradiction is resolved with the datasheet's own curve, it turns out to UNDERSTATE its own headline by about 25%.

CONFIRMED from my own dumps. P1 pad S1 = VDD3 (24 pads on that net, including U1 pins 1/103/124, U15, U16, U12 and the six 100k pull-ups). VDD3 is fed by U18 (TPS22917DBV) pins 5/6, whose VIN pin 1 = VOUT3. U8 (NCV8164ASN250T1G) VI pin 1 = VOUT3, VO pin 5 = VDD2. So both the module's own supply and the extra core current land on VOUT3 and pass through L2, converter 2, PTC1 and F1, exactly as claimed, and the finding is right that the ambiguity about which rail insideGadgets' 40-60 mA lands on does not change the VOUT3 total.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION. The finding states the incremental converter loss two ways in the same paragraph: 'extra conduction loss in converter 2 alone = 28.9 mW' and 'at ~89% overall converter efficiency the 207 mW of rail power costs 232 mW at VCC' (which implies 25.6 mW of TOTAL incremental converter loss). Conduction loss cannot exceed total loss. The 89% figure is the culprit — it is the efficiency at one operating point applied to an increment.

CORRECTED, using my pixel reads of Fig. G05 (VIN = 2.4 V trace: 91.1% at 150 mA, 88.9% at 212 mA) rather than a single flat efficiency. P_in at VCC goes 500.4/0.911 = 549.3 mW to 707.2/0.889 = 795.5 mW, an increase of 246 mW at VCC for 206.8 mW of added rail power — so incremental converter loss is 39 mW, not 25.6 and not 28.9. Input current then goes 480 -> 480 + 246/2.45 = 580 mA, and the input-path loss at a central 0.150 Ohm goes 0.480^2 x 0.15 = 34.6 mW to 0.580^2 x 0.15 = 50.5 mW, +15.9 mW. TOTAL EXTRA AT THE BATTERY ~262 mW (not 247) for 165 mW of useful load = 63% chain efficiency (not 67%), of which ~55 mW is pure converter-path and input-path loss (not 44 mW), on top of the LDO's 41.8 mW of deliberate waste. Every extra milliamp on VOUT3 costs the battery about 1.7x its face value. Console goes 1175 -> ~1437 mW; worst-case battery life 5h20m -> about 4h21m.

One more caveat: the 0.150 Ohm 'central' input resistance is built from two unverifiable central values (PTC1 somewhere in 0.040-0.150 Ohm, F1 somewhere at or below 0.080 Ohm max). The datasheet R_1max for 0805L075SL is 0.150, not the 0.160 the finding uses. Direction and structure of the analysis are sound; the numbers move against the fork, not for it.

findings.title: VOUT3 regulates to 3.336 V; trimming R55 to 1.02 M gives 3.294 V and hands back a few mW of NCV8164 dropout at overclocked core currents
findings.current_part: R23 = 1.78 M, R55 = 1.00 M, both 0603. VOUT3 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78/1.00) = 3.336 V. This is exactly the divider from the LTC3527 datasheet's own front-page 3.3 V application, so it is not a mistake — it is simply 36 mV above the 3.3 V the AGB actually wants. Divider current = 3.336/2.78M = 1.20 uA, so the divider itself costs 4 uW and there is nothing to gain there.
findings.proposal: R55 1.00 M -> 1.02 M (standard E96, same 0603 land, same tolerance class): VOUT3 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78/1.02) = 3.294 V. R23 unchanged, C41 unchanged.
findings.benefit: Small and honest. The 42 mV reduction is dropped straight out of U8's (VOUT3 - 2.5 V) dissipation. At an estimated 75 mA on VDD2 with the overclock at 1.75x (25 mA base plus 50 mA), the LDO stops wasting 0.075 x 0.042 = 3.15 mW, which at ~89% converter efficiency is ~3.5 mW at VCC. Without the overclock, at an estimated 25 mA on VDD2, it is 1.05 mW at the rail, ~1.2 mW at VCC. The VDD3 loads also see 42 mV less, which is a further small win that I have not tried to quantify. Total: about 1 mW stock, about 3.5 mW overclocked. This is a rounding-error lever compared with the PTC and the channel swap, and I am reporting it as such.
findings.risk: My VDD2 current is an ESTIMATE (25 mA base) and it is the weak link in the arithmetic — if VDD2 idles at 10 mA the stock saving halves. Functionally the risk is low: the original GBA runs VDD3 at 3.3 V, so 3.294 V is if anything more correct than 3.336 V, it is inside any 3.3 V +/-5% specification, and it costs the NCV8164 only 42 mV of the ~800 mV headroom it has over its 2.5 V output. The one thing to check is your cartridge: VDD3 feeds P1 pad S1 and some flash carts are fussy, though 3.294 V is well inside spec. If the ClockxControl module itself has a minimum supply requirement near 3.3 V, verify it before making this change.
findings.verify_reason:
Small, honest, and it survives. Verified: R23 = 1.78M and R55 = 1M read directly from AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch, both on Bucketmouse:R_0603_1608Metric_Boxed; LTC3527 FB = 1.20 V typ, so VOUT3 = 3.336 V, and this is verbatim the divider from the datasheet's own front-page 3.3 V application, so it is not an error. 1.02 M is a genuine E96 value (E96 runs 1.00, 1.02, 1.05, 1.07 ...), same 0603 land, no PCB or schematic change beyond the value — a true drop-in. VOUT3 becomes 1.20 x (1 + 1.78/1.02) = 3.294 V, a 42 mV reduction. Divider current 3.336/2.78M = 1.20 uA = 4 uW, so the finding is right that there is nothing to win in the divider itself. Headroom check verified against the NCV8164 datasheet: dropout for the 2.5 V variant in TSOP-5 is 125 mV typ at 300 mA, so 794 mV of headroom after the trim is nowhere near marginal, and I confirmed U8's VI pin is on VOUT3. Arithmetic reproduces: 0.075 x 0.042 = 3.15 mW at the rail, /0.89 = 3.5 mW at VCC overclocked; 0.025 x 0.042 = 1.05 mW, /0.89 = 1.2 mW stock.

TWO THINGS TO ADD, neither fatal. (1) The LTC3527's feedback voltage is specified 1.176-1.224 V over temperature, i.e. +/-2%, which is +/-67 mV on VOUT3. The deliberate 42 mV trim is therefore smaller than the part-to-part and over-temperature spread: it shifts the distribution, but you cannot verify it on any single board with a DMM and conclude anything. Present it as an expected value, not a measurement. (2) The whole benefit rests on an unmeasured VDD2 current, which the finding says plainly. VDD2 feeds U1 pins 44/65/115/117 and U2 pins 12/16/37 (CPU core plus SRAM), and nothing on this board measures it. Confidence 0.5 is right. This is a rounding-error lever and the finding says so — which is the correct behaviour, and worth more than an inflated one.

findings.title: F1 and PTC1 carry the PCB Value "0467001.NR" in the layout while the schematic and published BOM say F0805B2R00FSTR and 0805L075SLYR
findings.current_part: Parsing the footprint Value properties out of the layouts: in BOTH the stock agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_pcb and the fork's x/agbm-01-ram-desalvage/AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus.kicad_pcb, F1 and PTC1 both have Value = "0467001.NR". The schematic AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch and MouseBiteLabs' published AGBM-01 BOM give F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR (2 A fuse) and PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR (0.75 A PPTC). 0467001.NR is a Littelfuse Nano2 1 A cartridge fuse, which is neither part and does not fit a 0805 land.
findings.proposal: Update the Value property on both footprints to match the schematic. Purely a documentation fix, no electrical change.
findings.benefit: Zero mW. It matters because anyone generating a BOM or a pick-and-place from the layout rather than the schematic — which is the normal JLCPCB/PCBWay assembly flow — would order or place the wrong parts on the two components that carry the entire board current. It also means the layout's Value fields cannot be trusted as a cross-check anywhere else, which is worth knowing when reviewing the rest of the board.
findings.risk: None. Note this defect exists upstream in MouseBiteLabs' own AGBM-01 files, not just in the fork, so fixing it locally will show up as a diff against upstream. Worth reporting upstream.
findings.verify_reason:
Verified directly and the scope is WIDER than reported. I parsed the footprint Value properties out of both layouts and the symbol Value properties out of all the schematic sheets, then diffed them. Both agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_pcb and x/agbm-01-ram-desalvage/AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus.kicad_pcb carry Value = '0467001.NR' on F1 (at 31.2, -24.2) and PTC1 (at 31.9, -27.6), while AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch gives F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR and PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR. Both layout footprints are Bucketmouse:Fuse_0805_2012Metric. Exactly as claimed.

BUT THE FULL DIFF FINDS EIGHT MISMATCHES, not two: F1 (F0805B2R00FSTR vs 0467001.NR), PTC1 (0805L075SLYR vs 0467001.NR), R3 (5.1k vs 1k), R4 (33k vs 10k), R64 (200k vs 100k), TP22 (BATT vs VAUD), Z57 and Z58 ('100p or 0 ohm' vs '100p'). Three of those are resistor values that differ by 2x to 5x. So the finding's closing caution — 'the layout's Value fields cannot be trusted as a cross-check anywhere else' — is not a hypothetical; it is demonstrably true on six further parts, and the finding should say so rather than leaving it as an aside. Anyone driving a JLCPCB/PCBWay assembly from the layout would get the wrong values on three resistors as well as on the two parts carrying the entire board current.

ONE DESCRIPTIVE CORRECTION: 0467001.NR is not a 'Nano2 cartridge fuse'. It is a Littelfuse 467 series surface-mount chip fuse, 1 A, 32 V, very fast acting, in an 0603 package (per RS 1740879 and Newark 12J3738). It would in fact place onto an 0805 land (undersized, but placeable) — so the finding's reassurance that it 'does not fit a 0805 land' is wrong, and the hazard is therefore slightly worse than described: a pick-and-place run from the layout would not necessarily fail visibly. Everything else stands. The observation that the defect exists upstream in MouseBiteLabs' own files, not just in the fork, is correct — I checked both. Worth reporting upstream, as the finding says.

findings.title: Replace U8 with a buck-boost fed straight from VCC — skips the boost entirely for the core rail, the single largest lever in this domain
findings.current_part: U8 = NCV8164ASN250T1G, SOT-23-5 (onsemi TSOP-5, CASE 483), fixed 2.5 V, VIN 1.6-5.5 V, Iq 30 uA typ / 40 uA max at IOUT = 0, dropout 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA for the 2.5 V option, current limit 350 mA min. Fed from VOUT3 = 3.336 V, so its efficiency is fixed at (2.5/3.336) x (30/30.03) = 74.87%. Cascaded with the LTC3527 boost (eta 0.92 from datasheet curve G05, Burst, VOUT2 = 3.3 V, 1.2 MHz, VIN 2.4 V, 10-100 mA), the battery-to-core chain efficiency is 0.92 x 0.7487 = 0.689.
findings.proposal: TPS63900DSK — synchronous buck-boost, VIN 1.8-5.5 V, VOUT 1.8-5 V programmable in 100 mV steps by two config resistors, >400 mA output for VI >= 2.0 V, 75 nA quiescent current, 60 nA shutdown, 10-pin WSON 2.5 mm x 2.5 mm, external 2.2 uH inductor + single 22 uF output capacitor, 21 mm2 total solution size. Datasheet Figure 8-2 shows the VO = 2.5 V trace reaching ~0.47 A capability at VI = 1.8 V and ~0.85 A at 2.3 V — about 10x what VDD2 needs. Its headline feature matters here: 'Single-mode operation — eliminates mode transitions between buck, buck-boost and boost operation / Low output ripple', which is exactly the property you want on a rail that sits near VIN ~= VOUT for most of an alkaline discharge. Alternative: TPS63802 (VIN 1.3-5.5 V, VOUT 1.8-5.2 V adjustable, 2 A, 11 uA Iq, 10-pin VSON-HR 3.0 x 2.0 mm, 0.47 uH inductor, 22 uF minimum output cap, 21.5 mm2) — the part MouseBiteLabs already uses on AGBM-02, so it is proven in this exact console, but with 11 uA vs 75 nA of Iq and explicit buck/buck-boost/boost mode transitions.
findings.benefit: Battery-to-core chain today: 0.92 (boost) x 0.7487 (LDO) = 0.689. Direct buck-boost at eta = 0.89. At 1x, core = 2.5 V x 30 mA = 75 mW: 75/0.689 = 108.9 mW at the battery today vs 75/0.89 = 84.3 mW, saving 24.6 mW. At 1.75x, core = 2.5 V x 48 mA = 120 mW: 120/0.689 = 174.2 mW vs 120/0.89 = 134.8 mW, saving 39.4 mW. Range across my 44-53 mA overclock band: 36.1 to 43.5 mW. The 0.89 figure is read off the TPS63900 curves by bracketing: VO = 2.5 V is not plotted, but Figure 8-6 (VO = 1.8 V) at VI = 2.5 V runs 89-90% over 10-100 mA and Figure 8-7 (VO = 3.3 V) at VI = 2.5 V runs 90-91% over the same range, so 89% for VO = 2.5 V across the 2.1-3.2 V pack range is a fair and slightly conservative reading. 24.6 mW is 14% of the 170 mW idle figure; 39.4 mW is 3.4% of the 1175 mW in-use peak.
findings.risk: Four costs, in descending order of how likely they are to kill it. (1) SEQUENCING — U8's PGOOD pin (pad 4) drives /PG_2V5, which is the enable input of both U4 (pad 3) and U18 (pad 3), implementing MBL's annotated 'CPU Power sequence: VDD2 >> VDD3 >> VDD5'. The TPS63900 pin list is EN, SEL, CFG1, CFG2, CFG3, VOUT, LX2, GND, LX1, VIN — there is no power-good output, and neither has the TPS63802. You must regenerate /PG_2V5, e.g. a fourth TPS3840 watching VDD2. That is a schematic change with its own part, not a footprint swap. (2) NOISE ON THE CORE RAIL — MouseBiteLabs' own root-schematic annotation, placed above U8, reads 'Audio seems to sound best when noise on VDD2 is minimized'. That is the designer telling you, from experience with this exact console, that VDD2 ripple is audible through the CPU's audio path. A burst-mode converter's switching frequency falls with load; at 30-50 mA the TPS63900 burst frequency is a few hundred kHz (Figure 8-3), safely above audio, but this must be verified by ear, not by multimeter. (3) AREA — 21 mm2 of inductor, 22 uF cap and IC, on a board whose centre 18.65 x 12.00 mm is now spoken for by the ClockxControl, plus a new VCC route across to it. (4) You lose the LDO's 260 Ohm active output discharge on VDD2, which currently gives a clean power-down of a salvaged CPU.
findings.verify_reason:
