(3) LTC3527 curve G05: I checked the figure-title ordering in the datasheet and G05 is indeed 'Efficiency vs Load Current and VIN for VOUT2 = 3.3V at 1.2MHz'. The board is in the right mode for it: U5 pin 3 MODE = GND ('MODE = Low: Automatic Burst Mode operation') and pin 10 FSEL = GND (switching frequency 0.9/1.2/1.5 MHz min/typ/max for VFSEL = 0 V). Reading the Burst 2.4 V trace over 10-100 mA gives 92-93%, so 0.92 is right and slightly conservative. (4) TPS63900 is ACTIVE on ti.com; datasheet features confirm VIN 1.8-5.5 V, VOUT 1.8-5 V in 100 mV steps, 75 nA Iq / 60 nA shutdown, 10-pin WSON DSK 2.5 x 2.5 mm, 2.2 uH, 21 mm2, and the 'Single-mode operation - eliminates mode transitions between buck, buck-boost and boost operation / Low output ripple' bullet is verbatim. Pin table is EN, SEL, CFG1, CFG2, CFG3, VOUT, LX2, GND, LX1, VIN plus thermal pad - no PG, as claimed. (5) TPS63802 is ACTIVE (orderable table shows TPS63802DLAR 'Active Production'); VIN 1.3-5.5 V, 11 uA operating Iq, 0.47 uH, 22 uF, 10-pin VSON-HR, 21.5 mm2 solution - all as stated. (6) The 0.89 efficiency bracket: Figure 8-6 is VO = 1.8 V and Figure 8-7 is VO = 3.3 V, both carry a VI = 2.5 V trace, both plateau at 89-91% over 10-100 mA. Bracketing 2.5 V at 89% is fair. (7) All the arithmetic reproduces exactly: 0.92 x 0.7487 = 0.689; 75/0.689 = 108.9 vs 75/0.89 = 84.3, delta 24.6 mW; 120/0.689 = 174.2 vs 134.8, delta 39.4 mW; 44 mA -> 36.0 mW and 53 mA -> 43.4 mW.

THE 30 mA THE WHOLE FINDING RESTS ON. The finding cites nothing for it, which under the brief's rules is a defect. It is nevertheless right: MouseBiteLabs' own schematic carries the text annotation '2.5V @ ~30mA' at (111.76, 90.424), whose nearest object is TP18 at 6.6 mm - and TP18 is on VDD2 per the pad map. I also closed the idle budget independently: 30 mA on VDD2 = 100.2 mW at VOUT3 = 108.9 mW at the battery; MBL's '3.3V@~10mA (no cart)' = 33.4 mW = 36.3 mW at the battery; audio idle ~6 mA = 22 mW = 24 mW at the battery; total 169 mW against a measured 170 mW. The base is sound.

ERRORS I FOUND. (a) Figure 8-2 is misread. I measured the VO = 2.5 V trace against the plotted 0.1 A gridlines: 0.469 A at VI = 2.0 V, 0.604 A at 2.3 V, 0.723 A at 2.5 V, 0.921 A at 3.2 V. The claimed '~0.85 A at 2.3 V' is 40% high. The 0.47 A at 1.8 V figure is correct, and the conclusion ('about 10x what VDD2 needs') survives on the 1.8 V number alone. (b) The /PG_2V5 fan-out is incomplete and therefore the sequencing cost is understated. The net has six pads, not four: R8.2, TP30.1, U4.3, U8.4, U18.3 AND U5.1 = the LTC3527's ~SHDN1. U8's PGOOD gates the entire 5 V boost channel - screen FFC pin 34 and the cart 5 V pad - not just U4 and U18. (c) The area risk is wrong for this board. U8 is at (18.4, -30.3) on B.Cu; the ClockxControl window is 82.6-101.3 mm on F.Cu. They do not compete for space. The real constraints are local and I confirmed them: nearest same-side neighbours are C60 at 3.50 mm and C2 at 3.70 mm, and the VCC node (C37 at 10.8 mm, U5 at 12.8 mm) means roughly an 11 mm new VCC route. (d) '22 uF output capacitor' alone is TI's marketing line; Recommended Operating Conditions require CI >= 5 uF and CO >= 10 uF, and the simplified schematic shows 10 uF in plus 22 uF out. (e) The finding does not account for the boost's operating point moving. Taking 30 mA off VOUT2 drops its load from ~47 mA to ~17 mA; I checked G05 and the Burst 2.4 V trace is flat at 92-93% across that range, so the penalty is under ~1 mW - which is why I revise the benefit only from 24.6 to ~23.6 mW.

ONE RISK I CHECKED AND DISMISSED: TPS63900 UVLO is 1.73/1.75/1.77 V rising with VI min 1.8 V, versus the LTC3527's 0.5 V after start-up, so in principle the swap truncates end-of-pack runtime. It does not, because the board's own cutoffs (schematic annotations 'Cutoff: 2.1V' and 'Cutoff: 2.3V', and three TPS3840DL20 supervisors at a 2.0 V threshold) shut the console down far above 1.77 V.

findings.title: Replace U8 with a buck from VOUT3 — only 0.84 V of headroom, but D = 0.75 is a completely ordinary duty cycle and it is viable
findings.current_part: U8 = NCV8164ASN250T1G, TSOP-5/SOT-23-5, 2.5 V fixed, 74.87% efficient from VOUT3 = 3.336 V. Loss = (3.336 - 2.5) x IOUT + 3.336 x 30 uA. Thermal: theta-JA 158 C/W for TSOP-5, onsemi advise limiting TJ to 125 C, so PD(max) = (125-40)/158 = 538 mW at 40 C ambient — the part is nowhere near its limit, this is purely an efficiency problem.
findings.proposal: TPS62840DLC — 1.8 V to 6.5 V input, 750 mA, 60 nA operating quiescent current, 25 nA shutdown, output 1.8-3.3 V in 100 mV steps set by a single resistor on VSET, SON-8 package 1.5 mm x 2.0 mm, needs an external 2.2 uH inductor, 4.7 uF input cap and 10 uF output cap. It also carries a STOP pin that halts switching for a quiet supply rail, which is a genuinely useful hook on an audio-sensitive console. ALTERNATIVE with almost no area cost: TPS82740A — a MicroSiP module with the inductor and both capacitors integrated, 2.30 mm x 2.90 mm body, VIN 2.2-5.5 V, 200 mA, 360 nA Iq, output pin-selectable 1.8 V to 2.5 V in 100 mV steps (2.5 V is the top setting, exactly what VDD2 needs), lifecycle status ACTIVE on ti.com. Its 2.30 x 2.90 mm body is essentially the same area as the SOT-23-5 land pattern it would replace, and U8's nearest same-side neighbours (C2 at 3.70 mm, C60 at 3.50 mm) leave room — so this swap costs no net board area and adds no discrete inductor.
findings.benefit: Duty cycle first, since the brief asks whether 0.84 V of headroom is even viable: D = VOUT/VIN = 2.5/3.336 = 0.749. That is a mainstream buck duty cycle with a large margin to any dropout or minimum-off-time limit; the 100%-mode and dropout questions only bite when VIN - VOUT is a couple of hundred millivolts. It is viable. TPS62840 efficiency at this operating point, from datasheet Figure 18 (VOUT = 2.5 V, RSET = 11.5 kOhm to GND, PFM/PWM): at 30 mA the VIN = 3.0 V trace reads ~94% and the VIN = 3.6 V trace ~93.5%; at 50 mA both read ~94%. Our VIN is 3.336 V, between the two. I use 93% conservatively. At 1x (30 mA): LDO input = 3.336 x 30.03 = 100.2 mW; buck input = 75/0.93 = 80.6 mW; saving 19.4 mW at VOUT3 = 21.1 mW at the battery (dividing by the 0.92 boost efficiency). That is 12.4% of the 170 mW idle figure. At 1.75x (48 mA): 160.1 mW vs 129.0 mW = 31.1 mW at VOUT3 = 33.8 mW at the battery; across the 44-53 mA band, 31.0 to 36.4 mW. With the TPS82740A instead, efficiency at VOUT = 2.5 V is not plotted, but Figure 5 (VOUT = 2.1 V, VIN = 3.3 V) reads ~87.5% and Figure 6 (VOUT = 2.6 V, VIN = 3.3 V) reads ~91.5% over 10-100 mA, so ~90% for 2.5 V — giving 16.7 mW at VOUT3 / 18.2 mW at battery at 1x, and 26.8 / 29.1 mW at 1.75x.
findings.risk: Same PGOOD blocker as the buck-boost option and it is the decisive one: neither the TPS62840 (pins VIN, SW, GND, VSET, VOS, EN, STOP, MODE) nor the TPS82740 (EN, VSEL1-3, CTRL, VIN, VOUT, LOAD, GND) has a power-good output, and U8's PG is what enables U4 and U18. You must add a supervisor to regenerate /PG_2V5. Second, this is double conversion — battery to boost (0.92) to buck (0.93) = 0.856 overall, versus 0.89 for a single buck-boost straight off VCC, so it wins less than option 1 for similar effort; its only advantage is that it does not need a new VCC route and, in the TPS82740A form, no new inductor. Third, switching ripple lands on the CPU core rail, against MBL's explicit note that VDD2 noise is audible. Fourth, TPS82740A is capped at 200 mA — fine for 48 mA, but it removes headroom if the core current estimate is badly wrong. Neither part is a drop-in on the SOT-23-5 land pattern: both need a new footprint, so this is a PCB revision.
findings.verify_reason:
I tried hard to break this one and could not. Every part exists, is in production, and the specs are right; the efficiency reading is if anything conservative; the arithmetic reproduces; the footprint grading is honest.

PARTS AND SPECS, VERIFIED BY ME. TPS62840 is ACTIVE on ti.com. Datasheet SLVSEC6D confirms VIN 1.8-6.5 V, 750 mA, 60 nA operating Iq, 25 nA shutdown, 120 nA in 100% mode, 16 VSET-selectable outputs, and the DLC package as SON-8, 1.5 mm x 2 mm (Device Information table). The Device Comparison Table gives TPS62840DLC as '1.8 V to 3.3 V in 100-mV steps'. The typical application on page 1 shows CI 4.7 uF, CO 10 uF, L 2.2 uH - exactly the externals the finding lists. STOP pin is present only on the DLC package.

THE RSET VALUE IS RIGHT AND IT MATTERS. Table 1 (Output Voltage Setting) gives RSET = 11.5 kohm nominal for VOUT = 2.5 V on the TPS62840DLC column, and Figure 18 is captioned 'Efficiency Power Save Mode, VOUT = 2.5 V, RSET = 11.5 kohm to GND'. So the finding is quoting the correct curve for the correct setting - not a generic curve.

I RE-MEASURED FIGURE 18 RATHER THAN TRUSTING THE READING. Calibrating against the figure's own decade gridlines (100n at x=452, 179.1 px/decade, 5% per 94 px, verified by hitting the 95% and 85% gridlines exactly): at 30 mA the VIN = 3.0 V trace sits at 94.5% and the VIN = 3.6 V trace at 93.7%; at 48-50 mA they read 95.0% and 93.8%. Interpolating to the actual VIN = 3.336 V gives ~94.1% at 30 mA and ~94.4% at 48 mA. The finding used 93%. It is understating its own case, which is the right direction to be wrong in.

ARITHMETIC REDONE. 3.336 V x 30.03 mA = 100.2 mW into the LDO; 75 mW / 0.93 = 80.6 mW into the buck; delta 19.5 mW at VOUT3, /0.92 = 21.2 mW at the battery (finding says 19.4/21.1 - rounding). At 48 mA: 3.336 x 48.03 = 160.2 mW vs 120/0.93 = 129.0 mW, delta 31.2 mW = 33.9 mW at the battery. Band across 44-53 mA reproduces at 31.0-36.4 mW. Against the measured envelope this is 12.4% of the 170 mW idle figure and about 3% of the 1175 mW peak - plausible, and smaller than the rail it sits on (the VDD2 chain is ~109 mW at the battery at idle by my own reconciliation of MBL's annotations against the 170 mW measurement).

TPS82740A ALTERNATIVE, VERIFIED. ti.com reports lifecycle ACTIVE. Datasheet SLVSCE3A confirms 360 nA typical Iq, up to 200 mA, VIN 2.2-5.5 V, 2.30 mm x 2.90 mm MicroSiP, and Table 1 shows the A variant covers 1.8-2.5 V in 100 mV steps with 2.5 V at VSEL3/2/1 = 1,1,1. Figure captions check out: Figure 5 is 'TPS82740A Efficiency VOUT = 2.1V' and Figure 6 is 'TPS82740B Efficiency VOUT = 2.6V' - the finding names both correctly, though it should say the 2.6 V bracket comes from a different orderable part (the B variant), not the A.

THERMAL AND FOOTPRINT. theta-JA 158 C/W for TSOP-5 is verbatim in the Thermal Characteristics table; 'For reliable operation junction temperature should be limited to +125 C' is verbatim in the applications text; (125-40)/158 = 538 mW. The grading is honest: neither part fits the Bucketmouse SOT-23-5 land pattern (BOM line 228), so PCB revision is the correct classification.

PGOOD BLOCKER CORRECTLY IDENTIFIED. I checked all four pin tables myself. TPS62840: VIN, SW, GND, VSET, VOS, EN, STOP, MODE. TPS82740: 9 bumps, EN/VSEL1-3/CTRL/VIN/VOUT/LOAD/GND. Neither has a power-good output. Correct.

THREE THINGS TO ADD, NONE FATAL. (1) The same /PG_2V5 undercount as the other findings: the net also drives U5 pin 1 (~SHDN1), so losing it kills the 5 V rail too, not merely the sequencing of VDD3 and VAUD. (2) The STOP pin is oversold as 'a genuinely useful hook on an audio-sensitive console'. Section 8.3 says that in STOP the device draws typically 70 uA and the output is allowed to droop until clamped about 0.5 V below the setpoint - it is a bench-measurement feature, not a way to quiet a CPU core rail. (3) A new coupling path the finding does not mention: a 1.8 MHz buck sitting on VOUT3 pushes its input ripple back onto VOUT3, which also feeds U4/VAUD. NCV8164 PSRR is 61 dB at 100 kHz and unspecified above that. It is well out of the audio band so it is probably fine, but it deserves a line. Also worth pricing for a hobbyist build: TPS82740A is a land-grid MicroSiP, which is hand-assembly hostile.

findings.title: Lower VOUT3 from 3.336 V to ~3.23 V by changing one resistor — the cheapest change on the board, and honestly worth only 4-10 mW
findings.current_part: R23 = 1.78 M and R55 = 1.00 M, both R_0603_1608Metric_Boxed, forming the LTC3527 FB2 divider. LTC3527 datasheet: 'Feedback Voltage FB1, FB2 | 1.176 | 1.20 | 1.224 V' and 'The output voltage can be adjusted from 1.6V to 5.25V by VOUT1 = 1.2[1 + R1/R2]'. So VOUT3 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78/1.00) = 3.336 V. The two LDOs regulate to a fixed 2.5 V, so every millivolt VOUT3 comes down is a millivolt less dropped across U8 and U4.
findings.proposal: Change R23 from 1.78 M to 1.69 M (E96, same 0603 land pattern): VOUT3 = 1.20 x 2.69 = 3.228 V. More aggressive option R23 = 1.65 M gives 1.20 x 2.65 = 3.180 V. Nothing else on the board changes — this is a one-resistor value change on the existing footprint, the only genuinely drop-in item in this domain.
findings.benefit: Saving = delta-V x (I_U8 + I_U4), because both LDO outputs are pinned at 2.5 V. With R23 = 1.69 M, delta-V = 0.108 V. At 1x idle (30 mA on U8 + ~5 mA on U4 = 35 mA): 0.108 x 35 = 3.8 mW at VOUT3 = 4.1 mW at the battery, 2.4% of the 170 mW idle. At 1.75x with audio at max volume (48 + 40 mA = 88 mA): 0.108 x 88 = 9.5 mW = 10.3 mW at the battery. With R23 = 1.65 M (delta-V = 0.156 V) it becomes 5.9 mW and 14.9 mW respectively. Now the floor analysis the brief asked for — every load on VOUT3 and VDD3, with its verified minimum supply. (a) U8 and U4 need 2.5 V plus dropout plus PSRR headroom. Dropout for the 2.5 V TSOP-5 option is 125 mV typ / 200 mV max AT 300 mA; the pass element is resistive in dropout, so R_pass = 0.417 Ohm typ / 0.667 Ohm max, giving ~20 mV typ / 32 mV max at 48 mA. Dropout is NOT the binding constraint. PSRR is: onsemi specify the whole electrical table, PSRR included, at VIN = VOUT(NOM) + 0.5 V, so keeping >= 0.5 V of headroom preserves the datasheet 83/85/80/61 dB at 100 Hz/1 kHz/10 kHz/100 kHz. That sets an LDO floor of VOUT3 >= 3.0 V WORST CASE, not nominal. (b) U16 SN74HC02PWR: recommended VCC 2 V to 6 V — no constraint. (c) U15 SN74LVC1G332: recommended VCC 1.65 V to 5.5 V — no constraint. (d) U18 and U12 TPS22917: VIN 1 V to 5.5 V, rON ~100 mOhm at 3.3 V, so 6 mV of drop at 60 mA and VDD3 = VOUT3 for all practical purposes — no constraint. (e) The binding constraint is the salvaged AGB CPU's VDD3 pins (U1.1, U1.103, U1.124), the AGB SRAM, and the cartridge — MBL's own annotation puts an Everdrive at '3.3V@~50mA' on this rail. Worst case with R23 = 1.69 M: 3.228 x 0.98 (FB tolerance) x 0.98 (two 1% resistors) = 3.10 V minimum, i.e. VDD3 no worse than -6% on a nominal 3.3 V rail, and 0.60 V of LDO headroom still retained. That is the whole case for the change and the whole case against going further.
findings.risk: You are buying 4-10 mW by shaving margin on a salvaged CPU's I/O rail and on whatever cartridge is inserted. Nothing in a datasheet forbids 3.23 V; the AGB CPU and SRAM are irreplaceable parts with no published minimum VDD3, so this is judgement, not specification. Two second-order effects I am deliberately NOT counting as savings: lowering VDD3 also lowers the CPU I/O and cart switching power (goes as V^2), but that comes with slower edges and less noise margin, so it is a functional change, not free efficiency. Also unverified: the ClockxControl's V+ supply range. insideGadgets publish the current draw and the module dimensions but no supply voltage specification anywhere on the product page, and its V+ lands on VDD3 here. Recommendation: treat this as a build option to be validated by measuring VDD3 and running a real cart, not a default. If the console is stable it is the best mW-per-dollar change on the board; if it is not, you have risked a salvage for 4 mW.
findings.verify_reason:
Stands, with two small corrections that do not change the answer. This is the only genuinely drop-in item in the domain and the finding is honest that it is worth 4-10 mW.

VERIFIED. R23 = 1.78M and R55 = 1M, both R_0603_1608Metric_Boxed, nets 1=VOUT3/2=Net-(U5-FB2) and 1=Net-(U5-FB2)/2=GND (BOM lines 134 and 162). LTC3527 datasheet EC table gives Feedback Voltage FB1, FB2 = 1.176 / 1.20 / 1.224 V and the text confirms output adjustable 1.6 V to 5.25 V. 1.20 x (1 + 1.78/1.00) = 3.336 V. R23 = 1.69 M gives 1.20 x 2.69 = 3.228 V; R23 = 1.65 M gives 3.180 V. Both 1.69 M and 1.65 M are standard values on the same 0603 land pattern, so 'drop-in' is correctly graded.

So below 3.0 V you are outside the conditions under which onsemi specify anything, not just PSRR. That genuinely sets the floor. (b) Dropout is not binding: 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA for the 2.5 V option scales to ~20/32 mV at 48 mA, as claimed. (c) SN74HC02: 'Wide operating voltage range: 2 V to 6 V' - verified. (d) SN74LVC1G332: recommended operating VCC 1.65 to 5.5 V - verified. (e) TPS22917: 'Input operating voltage range (VIN): 1 V to 5.5 V'; RON at VIN = 3.6 V, 25 C is 90 mohm typ / 110 mohm max, so the finding's '~100 mohm' and 6 mV at 60 mA are fine.

MBL ANNOTATIONS VERIFIED VERBATIM in AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch: '3.3V@~50mA (Everdrive)', '3.3V@~10mA (no cart)', '5.0V @ ~130mA', 'Rough estimates (rounded up)'. The ClockxControl caveat is also right: I fetched the insideGadgets product text and it gives '12mA of additional current' and '40-60mA more' when overclocked, plus 18x12x1.6 mm, and no supply-voltage specification anywhere - so 'unverified' is the correct label.

CORRECTIONS. (1) The worst-case stack is stated slightly wrong (in the conservative direction). Two 1% resistors in a ratio do not give a 2% error on the ratio: worst case 1 + (1.69 x 0.99)/(1.00 x 1.01) = 2.6564 against a nominal 2.69, i.e. a factor of 0.9875, not 0.98. Correct worst case is 3.228 x 0.98 x 0.9875 = 3.12 V, not 3.10 V, leaving 0.62 V of LDO headroom rather than 0.60 V. Direction and conclusion unchanged. Note also that the 1% tolerance is an assumption - the BOM records values only, no tolerance. (2) The 35 mA basis is not cited. It is nevertheless sound: 30 mA on VDD2 is MBL's own schematic annotation ('2.5V @ ~30mA', nearest object TP18, which the pad map puts on VDD2), and ~5 mA on VAUD is what closes the 170 mW idle budget to within 1 mW.

ONE THING I CHECKED THAT MAKES THE RISK REAL RATHER THAN THEORETICAL: the cartridge's supply reaches the cart two ways - P1 pad S1 is on VDD3 directly, and VDD35 (P1 pin 1 and pad C1, plus U1 pin 38) sits behind ferrite EM3 off the link-port node. Lowering VOUT3 therefore reaches both the cart and the ClockxControl's V+. The finding's recommendation to treat this as a build option validated by measurement, not a default, is the right call.

findings.title: U8's PGOOD pin is load-bearing for the whole power-up sequence — no candidate switcher has one, and this is the real cost of replacing U8
findings.current_part: U8 pad 4 (PG, open collector per the NCV8164 pin function table: 'Power Good, open collector. Use 10 kOhm to 100 kOhm pull-up resistor connected to output or input voltage') drives net /PG_2V5. From the pad map, /PG_2V5 goes to U4 pad 3 (EN), U18 pad 3 (ON), R8 (100 k pull-up to VDD2) and TP30. U8's own EN (pad 3) is /PG_3V3, which comes from the LTC3527's PGOOD2 with R13 as a 100 k pull-up to VOUT3. So the chain is: VOUT3 good -> enable U8 -> VDD2 good -> enable U18 (VDD3) and U4 (VAUD). That exactly implements the two schematic annotations 'CPU Power sequence: VDD2 >> VDD3 >> VDD5' and 'Audio supply turns on after 2.5V and 3.3V rails are stable'. Power Good thresholds: 95% rising, 90% falling; VPGLO 0.3 V at 5 mA. The wiring is correct as drawn — R8 at 100 k is at the top of the datasheet-recommended range and pulled to the LDO's own output, which the datasheet explicitly sanctions.
findings.proposal: No change to the board. This is a design constraint that any U8 replacement must satisfy, and it should be priced into every switcher proposal above. Pin lists confirmed from the datasheets: TPS62840 = VIN, SW, GND, VSET, VOS, EN, STOP, MODE; TPS82740 = VIN, VOUT, GND, EN, VSEL1, VSEL2, VSEL3, CTRL, LOAD; TPS63900 = EN, SEL, CFG1, CFG2, CFG3, VOUT, LX2, GND, LX1, VIN; TPS63802 = no PG either. None has a power-good output. Regenerating /PG_2V5 means adding a fourth supervisor — the board already uses TPS3840DL20 three times (U3, U10, U17), so a TPS3840 variant with a threshold below 2.5 V watching VDD2 is the obvious drop-in-to-the-design answer, at the cost of one more SOT-23-5 and its ~1 uA.
findings.benefit: Zero milliwatts — this is a correctness and cost item, not an efficiency one. Its value is that it converts every 'swap U8 for a buck' proposal from a footprint change into a schematic change plus an extra part, which is exactly the distinction the reviewer asked to have graded. Without this, someone builds the buck version and the console either does not sequence (VDD3 and VAUD come up whenever VOUT3 does, before the core rail) or does not come up at all, because U18's ON pin would be floating.
findings.risk: If ignored: the AGB CPU sees VDD3 before VDD2, which MBL's schematic explicitly warns against ('GBA CPU gets very hot without 2.5V!'), and the audio supply comes up before the rails it is meant to follow. The added supervisor also costs ~1 uA of its own and one more SOT-23-5 of board area in a region that is already dense (U8's nearest neighbours are 3.5 mm away).
findings.verify_reason:
The finding is right that this is the decisive cost of replacing U8, and it is right that no candidate switcher has a power-good output. But its description of what /PG_2V5 actually does is incomplete, and the omission understates the blocker.

THE ERROR. The finding says '/PG_2V5 goes to U4 pad 3 (EN), U18 pad 3 (ON), R8 (100 k pull-up to VDD2) and TP30'. I dumped the net: /PG_{2V5} has SIX pads - R8.2, TP30.1, U4.3 (~SHDN), U8.4 (PGOOD), U18.3 (ON), and U5.1 (~SHDN1). U5 pin 1 is the LTC3527's channel-1 shutdown. U8's power-good therefore also gates the entire 5 V boost channel, which feeds U11 -> VDD5 -> the LCD FFC pin 34 (VSHA) and the cartridge 5 V pad S2. So the consequence of failing to regenerate /PG_2V5 is not merely 'VDD3 and VAUD come up before the core rail' - it is that VOUT5 never starts, the screen never lights, and the console appears completely dead. That also explains the annotation cleanly: the sequence VDD2 >> VDD3 >> VDD5 is enforced by this one net feeding both the load switches and the 5 V boost's enable.

WHAT I CONFIRMED. NCV8164 pin 4 is 'Power Good, open collector. Use 10 kohm to 100 kohm pull-up resistor connected to output or input voltage' - verbatim, and R8 = 100 k to VDD2 is exactly what the datasheet sanctions. PG thresholds 95% rising / 90% falling and VPGLO 0.3 V at IPG = 5 mA are correct (the applications text adds that PG can sink up to 10 mA with recommended operating current 0.1-10 mA). The TSOP-5 pin function table gives IN=1, GND=2, EN=3, PG=4, OUT=5, matching U8's nets 1=VOUT3, 2=GND, 3=/PG_3V3, 4=/PG_2V5, 5=VDD2. U8's EN comes from /PG_3V3 = LTC3527 PGOOD2 (U5 pin 13) with R13 100 k to VOUT3 - confirmed in the BOM and pad map. The three schematic annotations are verbatim in AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch: 'CPU Power sequence:\nVDD2 >> VDD3 >> VDD5', 'Audio supply turns on\nafter 2.5V and 3.3V\nrails are stable', 'GBA CPU gets very hot without 2.5V!'. And I checked all four candidate pin tables independently - TPS63900 (EN, SEL, CFG1, CFG2, CFG3, VOUT, LX2, GND, LX1, VIN + thermal pad), TPS62840 (VIN, SW, GND, VSET, VOS, EN, STOP, MODE), TPS82740 (9 bumps: EN, VSEL1-3, CTRL, VIN, VOUT, LOAD, GND), TPS63802 - none has a power-good output. The finding is correct on all of that.

SECOND CORRECTION. The added supervisor's cost is overstated. TPS3840 is specified at 300 nA typical / 700 nA maximum supply current, not '~1 uA', and thresholds are available from 1.6 V to 4.9 V in 0.1 V steps, so a part watching VDD2 exists. U3, U10 and U17 are indeed all TPS3840DL20 in SOT-23-5, so the precedent claim is right.

ONE ADDITION THAT STRENGTHENS IT. The library symbol names pin 3 '~{SHDN}' (active low), whereas the NCV8164's pin 3 is an active-HIGH enable ('VEN < 0.25 V disables the regulator, pulling VEN > 0.7 V enables the LDO'). Anyone re-deriving this sequencing logic from the symbol rather than the part would get the polarity backwards. The board is still correct because /PG_2V5 and /PG_3V3 are active-high power-good signals. This is the same library defect as finding ldo-symbol-value-mismatch, and it is the more dangerous half of it.

findings.title: Keep U4 (VAUD) linear — the PSRR is worth far more than the 4 mW it typically costs
findings.current_part: U4 = NCV8164ASN250T1G feeding VAUD = 2.5 V, which supplies U6 LM4853 (VDD), U7 TLV9364 (V+) and U9 SN74LVC2G34 (VCC) — i.e. the power amplifier, the four filter op-amps and the audio buffer, everything in the analogue chain. Verified NCV8164 noise and rejection: PSRR 83 dB at 100 Hz, 85 dB at 1 kHz, 80 dB at 10 kHz, 61 dB at 100 kHz (VOUT(NOM) = 3.3 V, IOUT = 10 mA); output voltage noise 9 uVRMS over 10 Hz to 100 kHz at 10 mA (fixed version). Stable with any ceramic >= 1 uF with no minimum ESR and no stated maximum, so the 13 uF nominal on VAUD is fine.
findings.proposal: Leave U4 exactly as it is. If a switcher goes anywhere in this domain, it goes on VDD2, never on VAUD.
findings.benefit: Sizing the prize honestly, because that is the whole point: MBL annotate '~100mW' beside U4 and state publicly that audio draws 'something like 50 to 100 mW at max volume'. At the worst case, 100 mW / 2.5 V = 40 mA, so U4's loss is 0.836 x 40 = 33.4 mW at the LDO, 36.3 mW referred to the battery. But that is only at maximum volume into the speaker; at the ~5 mA I estimate for idle and normal listening the loss is 0.836 x 5 = 4.2 mW, i.e. 4.5 mW at the battery. Averaged over play the available saving from switching this rail is a few milliwatts, and even the absolute worst case is 36 mW — less than the VDD2 lever, on the rail where noise matters most. Trading 85 dB of 1 kHz rejection and 9 uVRMS of noise for a few milliwatts on a board whose stated selling point is 'crystal clear audio' is a bad trade at any operating point.
findings.risk: The risk is in doing the swap, not in leaving it: no small buck or buck-boost comes near 80-85 dB of in-band rejection, and VAUD feeds the amplifier directly. Note also the corollary that cuts the other way — MBL's own schematic note 'Audio seems to sound best when noise on VDD2 is minimized' says the CORE rail's noise is audible in this design too. That is the strongest single argument against the two switcher proposals above, and it means any VDD2 switcher has to be signed off by listening, not by measuring. If audio quality is the priority over runtime, the correct answer in this domain may be to change nothing at all.
findings.verify_reason:
Verified end to end; I found nothing to correct, and one datasheet line that strengthens it.

LOADS. I dumped the VAUD net: 13 pads - U4.5 (OUT), U6.9 LM4853 VDD, U7.4 TLV9364 V+, U9.5 SN74LVC2G34 VCC, C9/C36/C54 1 uF and C59 10 uF (13 uF total, exactly as claimed), plus four 100 k and TP22. The finding's list of the analogue chain is exactly right.

SPECS. From the onsemi EC table, read myself: PSRR 83 dB at 100 Hz, 85 dB at 1 kHz, 80 dB at 10 kHz, 61 dB at 100 kHz - and critically the finding states the condition honestly (VOUT(NOM) = 3.3 V, IOUT = 10 mA), which matters because those numbers are not characterised on the 2.5 V variant. Output voltage noise 9 uVRMS over 10 Hz to 100 kHz at 10 mA, fixed version - correct. Stability: 'The NCV8164 does not require a minimum Equivalent Series Resistance (ESR) for the output capacitor. The device is designed to be stable with standard ceramics capacitors with values of 1 uF or greater' - verbatim, with no stated maximum, so 13 uF on VAUD is fine as claimed.

THE '~100mW' ANNOTATION IS REAL AND IT IS ON THIS RAIL. The text object sits at (241.3, 138.684) in AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch; its nearest neighbours are TP22 at 2.79 mm - and the pad map puts TP22 on VAUD - and C59 (the VAUD 10 uF) at 8.95 mm. So it does annotate the audio supply.

WIKI QUOTE VERIFIED. I fetched the page myself: 'The power draw from the audio is not catastrophically large, something like 50 to 100mW at max volume.' The wiki also adds a sentence the finding did not quote and which makes its case stronger: 'The GBA's speaker with the quieter max volume only uses ~15mW!' - so the realistic average is even further below the 36 mW worst case.

ARITHMETIC. 100 mW / 2.5 V = 40 mA; (3.336 - 2.5) x 40 mA = 33.4 mW at the LDO, /0.92 = 36.3 mW at the battery. At 5 mA: 4.18 mW = 4.5 mW at the battery. Both reproduce. Against the 410-1175 mW in-use envelope, 36 mW is the absolute ceiling and it only occurs at maximum volume into the speaker - the finding is being honest about the size of the prize rather than inflating it.

THE COROLLARY IS ALSO VERIFIED AND IS THE MOST USEFUL LINE IN THE WHOLE SUBMISSION. 'Audio seems to sound best when noise on VDD2 is minimized' is verbatim in the schematic at (99.06, 87.63) - the same x coordinate as U8 at (99.06, 100.33), so 'placed above U8' is literally true. That is the designer's own experience with this console saying the core rail's noise is audible, and it is a legitimate reason to require a listening test before signing off either switcher proposal.

findings.title: There is no drop-in LDO upgrade worth having — the best possible same-footprint swap is 0.1 mW
findings.current_part: NCV8164ASN250T1G in TSOP-5: Iq 30 uA typ / 40 uA max at IOUT = 0; shutdown 0.01 uA typ / 1.5 uA max; dropout 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA for the 2.5 V option; output accuracy +/-2% over 0.1-300 mA; line regulation 0.5 mV/V; load regulation 2 mV; current limit 350 mA min; 260 Ohm active output discharge (the 'A' suffix).
findings.proposal: Do not bother looking for a better LDO. Any 2.5 V linear regulator fed from 3.336 V is 74.9% efficient by definition — the topology, not the part number, sets the efficiency. The only two parameters a different LDO could improve are quiescent current and dropout, and neither is doing anything here.
findings.benefit: Quiescent current: the theoretical maximum saving from replacing 30 uA of Iq with 0 uA is 30 uA x 3.336 V = 0.10 mW at VOUT3, 0.11 mW at the battery — 0.06% of the 170 mW idle figure. That is rounding error and I am reporting it as rounding error. Dropout: with 0.836 V of headroom and 48 mA of load (implied pass-element drop of ~20 mV typ, ~32 mV max, scaling the 125/200 mV at 300 mA specification), dropout has roughly 25x margin and is irrelevant. Current limit 350 mA minimum against a 48 mA worst-case load is 7x margin. There is nothing left on the table in the same footprint.
findings.risk: None — the risk is spending effort here instead of on the switcher question. Worth stating explicitly because 'find a better LDO' is the natural first move and it is a dead end.
findings.verify_reason:
Correct, and correctly reported as rounding error. I checked every parameter it quotes and every one is right.

From the onsemi EC table, read directly: Quiescent Current at IOUT = 0 is 30 uA typ / 40 uA max; Shutdown Current at VEN <= 0.25 V is 0.01 uA typ / 1.5 uA max; Dropout Voltage for VOUT(NOM) = 2.5 V in TSOP-5 is 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at IOUT = 300 mA; Output Voltage Accuracy is -2/+2% over 0.1 mA <= IOUT <= 300 mA (at VIN = VOUT(NOM)+0.5 V to 5.5 V); Line Regulation 0.5 mV/V; Load Regulation 2 mV over 1-300 mA; Output Current Limit 350 mA min / 560 mA typ; Active output discharge resistance 260 ohm, 'Version A only' - and NCV8164ASN250T1G is listed in the ordering table as the 2.5 V TSOP-5 part 'With Active Output Discharge', so the A-suffix reasoning is right.

Arithmetic redone: 30 uA x 3.336 V = 0.100 mW at VOUT3, /0.92 = 0.109 mW at the battery, which is 0.064% of the 170 mW idle figure. The topological argument is also right - any 2.5 V linear regulator fed from 3.336 V is 74.9% efficient whatever the part number, so Iq and dropout are the only free variables and both have order-of-magnitude margin (dropout scales to ~20 mV typ at 48 mA against 836 mV of headroom; current limit is 7x the worst-case load).

ONE THING WORTH ADDING RATHER THAN CORRECTING. The claim 'the topology, not the part number, sets the efficiency' is true only for a fixed VOUT3. The one same-footprint lever that does move the LDO's efficiency is finding vout3-setpoint-lower: at VOUT3 = 3.228 V the same LDO runs at 2.5/3.228 = 77.4% instead of 74.9%. The two findings are consistent, and this one would be more useful if it pointed there instead of stopping at 'dead end'.

findings.title: Re-purposing an LTC3527 channel for VDD2 is physically impossible — it is a boost-only topology and VCC is above 2.5 V on fresh cells
findings.current_part: U5 = LTC3527, dual synchronous STEP-UP converter, QFN-16. Channel 1 (VOUT1, FB1 from R21 1.78 M / R22 560 k) makes 1.20 x 4.17857 = 5.014 V for the screen and the cart 5 V pad; channel 2 (VOUT2, FB2 from R23 1.78 M / R55 1.00 M) makes 1.20 x 2.78 = 3.336 V for everything else. Datasheet: output adjustable 1.6 V to 5.25 V, maximum duty cycle clamped at 90% typical, peak inductor current 900 mA (converter 1) / 500 mA (converter 2), input can drop as low as 0.5 V after start-up.
findings.proposal: Rule this out and stop considering it. Both channels are already committed to loads that cannot be dropped (5 V for the screen, 3.3 V for the CPU I/O and cart), and even if a channel were free, a step-up converter cannot produce 2.5 V from a VCC that is 3.2 V on fresh alkalines — it would simply pass VIN through. The minimum programmable output of 1.6 V describes the feedback range, not an ability to buck.
findings.benefit: Zero. Stating this is worth including because 'you already have a dual converter, use the spare channel' is the obvious first idea and it does not work; ruling it out cleanly is what pushes the answer to a third converter (finding vdd2-buckboost-from-vcc) or to a post-boost buck (finding u8-ldo-to-buck-from-vout3).
findings.risk: None. Note the corollary for the buck-boost proposal: because the pack spans 1.8-3.2 V and the target is 2.5 V, the converter must genuinely be buck-boost, not boost — which is why the TPS63900/TPS63802 class is the right one and why the AGBM-02's choice of buck-boost topology is the relevant precedent.
findings.verify_reason:
The conclusion is correct and worth stating. One quoted number is not a datasheet number, and there is a second, independent reason the idea is dead that the finding missed.

VERIFIED. The LTC3527 is titled 'Dual Synchronous Step-Up DC/DC Converters' and lists '1.6V to 5.25V VOUT Range' and '0.5V to 5V VIN Range After Start-Up' in Features; the EC table gives Maximum Duty Cycle clamped at 90% (typical) at VFB1,2 = 1 V. So it is boost-only and cannot produce 2.5 V from a 3.2 V fresh pack - correct, and the point that 1.6 V describes the feedback adjust range rather than a buck capability is exactly right. Divider values check out from the BOM: R21 1.78M / R22 560k gives 1.20 x (1 + 1.78/0.56) = 5.014 V, and R23 1.78M / R55 1M gives 3.336 V. Both channels are committed: VOUT5 feeds U11 -> VDD5 -> LCD FFC pin 34 and cart pad S2; VOUT3 feeds U8, U4 and U18.

CORRECTION. 'Peak inductor current 900 mA (converter 1) / 500 mA (converter 2)' is not what the datasheet specifies. The EC table gives NMOS Current Limit SW1 = 800 mA (minimum, l-tested) and NMOS Current Limit SW2 = 400 mA (minimum); the Current Limit vs Temperature curve shows roughly 0.9-1.0 A typical for the larger switch at 25 C. The finding has quoted typicals from a curve as if they were the specification. Immaterial to the conclusion, but it is precisely the kind of number the brief says must come from the source.

ADDITION - A SECOND REASON THE IDEA IS DEAD. Even if a channel were free, U5 pin 1 (~SHDN1) is wired to /PG_2V5, i.e. channel 1's own enable is derived from the 2.5 V rail's power-good. Repurposing that channel to MAKE the 2.5 V rail would be circular. I confirmed this from the pad map (/PG_{2V5} has six pads, one of them U5.1).

The corollary the finding draws - that the replacement must genuinely be buck-boost because the pack spans 1.8-3.2 V around a 2.5 V target, which is why AGBM-02's TPS63802 choice is the relevant precedent - is sound. I confirmed AGBM-02's part is a real buck-boost (TPS63802, VIN 1.3-5.5 V, Active Production in TI's orderable addendum).

findings.title: U8 is nowhere near thermally limited even at 1.75x — the overclock does not create a reliability problem here, only an efficiency one
findings.current_part: NCV8164 in TSOP-5: thermal resistance junction-to-ambient 158 C/W, junction-to-board 197 C/W, psi-JB 82 C/W; maximum junction temperature 150 C absolute, but onsemi state 'For reliable operation junction temperature should be limited to +125 C'; thermal shutdown at 165 C rising with 15 C hysteresis; PD(MAX) = (TJ(MAX) - TA)/theta-JA. Output short circuit duration is rated unlimited.
findings.proposal: No change. Record the headroom so nobody adds a heatsink, a bigger package (WDFNW6 at 51 C/W or DFNW8 at 50 C/W are both available in 2.5 V as NCV8164AML250TCG) or a thermal via field to solve a problem that does not exist.
findings.benefit: Zero milliwatts, but it settles the question. At TA = 40 C inside a sealed GBA shell, PD(MAX) = (125 - 40)/158 = 538 mW. U8's actual dissipation is 25.2 mW at 1x and 40.2 mW at 1.75x with the 48 mA central estimate (44.4 mW at the top of my 53 mA band). At 40.2 mW the junction rise is 40.2 mW x 158 C/W = 6.4 C, so TJ ~= 46 C. That is 13x margin on power and the current limit (350 mA minimum) is 7x above the 48 mA load. The DFNW8 package would cut the rise to 2.0 C and buy nothing.
findings.risk: None. The one thing this does establish is that if you keep the LDO, you are not risking the part — you are simply choosing to spend 40 mW of battery on heat. That is a legitimate choice on a console whose peak draw is 1175 mW, and it should be framed as a runtime decision rather than a safety one.
findings.verify_reason:
The conclusion is right and every thermal number checks out, but the finding asserts a part option that does not exist - which is exactly the failure mode the brief says invalidates a finding, so it has to be corrected even though the answer does not change.

THE ERROR. 'WDFNW6 at 51 C/W or DFNW8 at 50 C/W are both available in 2.5 V as NCV8164AML250TCG.' The theta-JA figures are right, but the WDFNW6 is NOT available in 2.5 V. The ordering table lists the WDFNW6 (AMTW) family only as ADJ, 1.1 V, 1.2 V, 1.8 V, 2.8 V and 2.9 V. The only real 2.5 V alternative package is the DFNW8 part NCV8164AML250TCG, which is listed. A reader taking the sentence at face value could order a WDFNW6 part number that does not exist in this voltage.

EVERYTHING ELSE VERIFIED. Thermal Characteristics, TSOP-5 package: theta-JA 158 C/W, theta-JC(top) 155, theta-JC(bot) 102, theta-JB 197, psi-JT 40, psi-JB 82. Maximum Junction Temperature 150 C in the absolute maximum ratings, and the applications text says verbatim 'For reliable operation junction temperature should be limited to +125 C'. Thermal Shutdown Threshold 165 C rising with 15 C hysteresis. Output Short Circuit Duration 'unlimited'. WDFNW6 theta-JA 51 C/W and DFNW8 theta-JA 50 C/W.

ARITHMETIC REDONE. PD(max) at TA = 40 C = (125 - 40)/158 = 538 mW. Dissipation = (3.336 - 2.5) x IOUT + 3.336 x 30 uA: 25.2 mW at 30 mA, 40.2 mW at 48 mA, 44.4 mW at 53 mA. Junction rise at 40.2 mW = 40.2 mW x 158 C/W = 6.4 C, so TJ ~ 46 C. Margin 538/40.2 = 13.4x on power; 350 mA current-limit minimum against 48 mA is 7.3x. In DFNW8 the rise would be 40.2 mW x 50 C/W = 2.0 C. Every figure reproduces.

The framing - that keeping the LDO is a runtime decision rather than a safety one, and that nobody should add a heatsink or a thermal via field for a 6 C rise - is correct and useful.

findings.title: U8 and U4 are drawn with a schematic symbol named MCP1824 while their Value is NCV8164ASN250T1G — the board is right, the library is misleading
findings.current_part: In AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch both U8 (at 99.06, 100.33) and U4 (at 222.25, 135.89) are instantiated with lib_id 'OpenGBA:MCP1824', while their Value property and the PCB footprint value are 'NCV8164ASN250T1G' in a Bucketmouse:SOT-23-5 footprint. The MCP1824 is a different manufacturer's part; the symbol is being reused for pin compatibility.
findings.proposal: Rename the symbol (or re-point it at a proper NCV8164 symbol) so the library and the BOM agree. No electrical change. I verified the electrical part before flagging it: the instantiated pin numbering is 1 = VOUT3, 2 = GND, 3 = enable input, 4 = PG, 5 = output, which matches the NCV8164 pin function table for TSOP-5 exactly ('1 IN / 2 GND / 3 EN / 5 OUT' with 'PG' on pin 4). The board is correct as manufactured.
findings.benefit: Zero milliwatts. The value is in avoiding a wrong order: anyone regenerating a BOM from the symbol library rather than from the Value field, or substituting the 'real' symbol from a vendor library, could get a different pinout convention and would not find out until the LDO is dead on the bench. On a board where U8 feeds a salvaged, irreplaceable CPU, that is worth the five minutes.
findings.risk: None from fixing it. I am deliberately not asserting anything about the actual MCP1824's pinout, because I did not fetch its datasheet — the verified claim here is only that the instantiated pin numbers match the NCV8164, so the fabricated board is correct.
findings.verify_reason:
Verified exactly as described, and the underlying problem is worse than the finding says.

WHAT I CHECKED IN THE FILE. In agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch there are two symbol instances with (lib_id "OpenGBA:MCP1824"): one at (at 99.06 100.33) whose Reference property is U8, and one at (at 222.25 135.89) whose Reference is U4. Both carry (property "Value" "NCV8164ASN250T1G"). The cached library symbol itself is named "OpenGBA:MCP1824" and carries its own Value property "MCP1824". The PCB gives both a Bucketmouse SOT-23-5 footprint with value NCV8164ASN250T1G. Positions, refdes and lib_id are all exactly as the finding states.

THE BOARD IS CORRECT. U8's pad-to-net map is 1=VOUT3, 2=GND, 3=/PG_3V3, 4=/PG_2V5, 5=VDD2, and the NCV8164 pin function table gives TSOP-5 as IN=1, GND=2, EN=3, PG=4, OUT=5. They match. U4's is 1=VOUT3, 2=GND, 3=/PG_2V5, 4=unconnected-(U4-PGOOD-Pad4), 5=VAUD - also consistent, with U4's own PG left floating because it is the last rail in the sequence. The finding's caution about not asserting anything about the real MCP1824's pinout is appropriate and I have not asserted anything about it either.

WHAT THE FINDING MISSED, AND IT IS THE MORE DANGEROUS HALF. The symbol does not merely have the wrong name - it has the wrong PIN SEMANTICS. Its pin 3 is named "~{SHDN}", i.e. active-low shutdown. The NCV8164's pin 3 is an active-HIGH enable: 'Applying VEN < 0.25 V disables the regulator, Pulling VEN > 0.7 V enables the LDO'. Anyone reading the sequencing chain off the symbol would conclude that /PG_3V3 and /PG_2V5 going LOW is what enables the regulators, which is backwards. The board is nevertheless correct because both nets are active-high power-good outputs. This makes the fix worth more than five minutes: it is not just a BOM hygiene item, it is a trap for exactly the person who tries to reason about the power sequence in order to replace U8.

findings.title: Both PCB footprints carry a stale Value "0467001.NR" — a 0603 1 A fuse in an 0805 land, which would delete the resettable protection entirely
findings.current_part: Three part numbers are in play. (1) Schematic Value: F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR, PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR. (2) PCB footprint Value on BOTH F1 and PTC1 = 0467001.NR. (3) KiCad Description field on both = 0805L050WR. Verified identities: 0467001.NR is a Littelfuse 467 Series fuse — the datasheet's own title page reads "467 Series / 0603 Fast-Acting Fuse", and the 1.00 A row gives 32 V, nominal cold resistance 0.0700 ohm, nominal melting I2t 0.0212 A2s. It is a 0603 part and a one-shot fuse, not a PPTC. 0805L050WR is a standard (non-LoRho) 0805L PPTC, 0.50 A hold / 1.00 A trip, R_min 0.150 / R_1max 0.850 ohm — the ordering-code table in the 0805L datasheet lists "0805L050WR" as the orderable code for 0805L050. Footprint on the board is Bucketmouse:Fuse_0805_2012Metric, pads 0.975 x 1.4 mm at 1.875 mm pitch.
findings.proposal: The SCHEMATIC is authoritative; re-sync the PCB Value fields. Two independent pieces of evidence settle it. (a) Package: 0467001.NR is a 0603 body (2.0 x 1.25 mm nominal land is not it — the 467 datasheet is titled "0603 Fast-Acting Fuse"), and both board footprints are 0805 lands; the schematic values F0805B2R00FSTR and 0805L075SLYR are both genuine 0805 parts. (b) Cross-design: I checked MouseBiteLabs' own AGBM-02, which is the later derivative of this board — its PCB footprints carry F1 = "F0805B2R00FSTR" and PTC1 = "0805L075SLYR", matching its schematic. Only AGBM-01 rev 1.2's PCB has the 0467001.NR strings, in both slots. That is a classic un-synced "Update PCB from Schematic" with "replace values" left off, and it was fixed by the time AGBM-02 shipped. The "0805L050WR" Description is a third artifact — it is present on F1 AND PTC1 in AGBM-01, AGBM-02 and AGBM-11 alike, i.e. a legacy string baked into the library symbol, not a BOM entry. Action: open the PCB, set F1 Value = F0805B2R00FSTR and PTC1 Value = 0805L075SLYR (or the 0805L150SLYR from the next finding), and clear/repair the Description on both. No copper, no land pattern, no schematic change.
findings.benefit: This is a build-correctness fix, not a power saving, but it has a quantifiable failure cost. If anyone exports a BOM from the layout (which is what a fab/JLCPCB BOM+CPL flow typically does) they would stuff two 0467001.NR: 2 x 0.0700 ohm = 0.140 ohm total. Loss at 292 mA = 0.292^2 x 0.140 = 11.9 mW; at 390 mA = 21.3 mW; at 750 mA = 78.8 mW. That is worse than the correct build's best case (0.120 ohm) and, far more importantly, there is then NO resettable device on the board — every overcurrent event becomes a permanent fuse replacement. On top of that a 1 A fuse is marginal for the load: at the 750 mA overclocked peak it runs at 75% of rating, and the 467 series' own opening-time table specifies only "4 hours minimum" at 100% of rating, with an operating range to +90 C; derated for a sealed GBA shell it will nuisance-blow. And mechanically a 0603 body on an 0805 land is a self-alignment/tombstone hazard.
findings.risk: None to the fix itself — it is a metadata edit. The risk is in NOT fixing it: an automated BOM export produces a board that is both lossier and unprotected, and the builder has no way to tell from the layout that the schematic disagrees.
findings.verify_reason:
I re-derived every claim from the files and the datasheets rather than trusting the finding.

PCB/schematic state, extracted directly: in BOTH /scratchpad/agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_pcb and the fork /scratchpad/x/agbm-01-ram-desalvage/AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus.kicad_pcb, F1 and PTC1 carry (property "Value" "0467001.NR") and (property "Description" "0805L050WR"). The AGBM-01 schematic carries F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR and PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR, both with Footprint Bucketmouse:Fuse_0805_2012Metric. AGBM-02's PCB carries F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR and PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR — the cross-design evidence is real.

Part identities, from the datasheets I fetched and text-extracted myself: the Littelfuse 467 datasheet (Rev GD 02/27/23) is titled '467 Series / 0603 Fast-Acting Fuse'; the 1.00 A row (amp code '001.') gives 32 V, nominal cold resistance 0.0700 ohm (measured at 10% of rated current, 25 C), nominal melting I2t 0.0212 A2sec; opening time at 100% of rating is '4 hours, Minimum'; operating temperature -55 to +90 C. The standard 0805L datasheet gives 0805L050: I_hold 0.50 A, I_trip 1.00 A, 6 V, I_max 100 A, Rmin 0.150, R1max 0.850, and its ordering table lists '0805L050WR' as the tape-and-reel code. Both identifications in the finding are correct.

Footprint: F1/PTC1 pads are 0.975 x 1.4 mm roundrect at +/-0.9375 mm (1.875 mm pitch) — an 0805 land, confirmed. A 0603 body on it is a real self-alignment risk.

Arithmetic redone: 2 x 0.0700 = 0.140 ohm; 0.292^2 x 0.140 = 11.94 mW; 0.390^2 x 0.140 = 21.29 mW; 0.750^2 x 0.140 = 78.75 mW. All correct, and all comfortably inside the 410-1175 mW envelope. Correct-build best case 0.080 + 0.040 = 0.120 ohm, also correct.

Three corrections, none fatal:
(1) The finding UNDERSTATES the scope. I ran a full Value diff of all 235 refdes between the AGBM-01 schematics and the fork PCB. There are SIX mismatches, not two: F1, PTC1, R3 (sch 5.1k / pcb 1k), R4 (sch 33k / pcb 10k), R64 (sch 200k / pcb 100k), TP22 (sch 'BATT' / pcb 'VAUD'). That strengthens the un-synced-PCB diagnosis and widens the fix — R3/R4 sit in the U10 supervisor divider on the SW net, so a PCB-derived BOM would also mis-set that divider.
(2) The claim that the '0805L050WR' Description is on F1 AND PTC1 in AGBM-11 is wrong: AGBM-11's PCB has F1 Value '2A' with an EMPTY Description, and PTC1 Value '750mA' with Description '0805L050WR'.
(3) 'which is what a fab/JLCPCB BOM+CPL flow typically does' is overstated. KiCad's normal BOM export is from Eeschema (schematic-sourced); only the CPL comes from the layout. The hazard is real but not typical.

Verdict stands: metadata-only fix, no copper, no land pattern, no schematic change, zero power benefit, real build-correctness value.

findings.title: PTC1: swap 0805L075SLYR for 0805L150SLYR — same series, same 0805 land, R_1max drops 160 mohm to 65 mohm
findings.current_part: PTC1 = Littelfuse 0805L075SLYR, PolySwitch LoRho series, 0805 (2012 metric). Verified from the LoRho datasheet table: I_hold 0.75 A, I_trip 1.50 A, V_max 6 Vdc, I_max 50 A, P_d 0.6 W, max time-to-trip 0.20 s at 8.00 A, R_min 0.040 ohm, R_1max 0.160 ohm. Newark confirms 750 mA / 1.5 A / 6 VDC / 50 A / 0805 / "PolySwitch Low Rho Series"; LCSC's parametric page independently lists R min 40 mohm (it lists R1 max as 150 mohm, 10 mohm below the datasheet — I use the datasheet's 160 mohm). Netlist position: PTC1.1 = VBATT, PTC1.2 = VCC, and VCC goes only to U5 VIN/VIN1/VIN2, L1, L2 and C37 — so 100% of the converter's input current passes through it.
findings.proposal: Littelfuse 0805L150SLYR, same LoRho series, same 0805 land pattern, same 6 V / 50 A ratings. Verified: I_hold 1.50 A, I_trip 3.00 A, V_max 6 Vdc, I_max 50 A, R_min 0.015 ohm, R_1max 0.065 ohm, time to trip 500 ms (DigiKey and LCSC parametric pages both give Ri min 15 mohm / R1 max 65 mohm, and the LoRho datasheet table gives the same). Sourcing: DigiKey 13,328 in stock at $2.26/1 down to $0.80/4000; LCSC 4,575 in stock at $0.343 at qty 5. Second source with identical numbers if wanted: Bourns MF-PSML150 (0805, R_min 0.015 / R_1max 0.065, I_hold 1.50 / I_trip 3.00) — note that specific MF-PSML part is marked obsolete by Bourns in favour of the MF-PSML/X generation, so the Littelfuse part is the cleaner choice.
findings.benefit:
Delta R = 0.040 - 0.015 = 0.025 ohm on a fresh part, or 0.160 - 0.065 = 0.095 ohm post-reflow (R_1max is defined as the resistance one hour after tripping or after 260 C/20 s reflow, so a built board sits nearer the R_1max end). Mid-estimate delta R = 0.060 ohm. Saving = I^2 x dR:
  200 mA:  1.0 / 3.8 mW (mid 2.4)
  292 mA (700 mW at 2.4 V):  2.1 / 8.1 mW (mid 5.1)
  350 mA:  3.1 / 11.6 mW (mid 7.4)
  390 mA (935 mW overclocked at 2.4 V):  3.8 / 14.5 mW (mid 9.1)
  550 mA:  7.6 / 28.7 mW (mid 18.2)
  750 mA (overclocked, low battery):  14.1 / 53.4 mW (mid 33.8)
As a fraction of the console: 0.7-1.2% of a 700 mW draw, 2.4-4.5% of the 1410 mW overclocked worst case. At the 170 mW idle point (71 mA at 2.4 V) the saving is 0.13-0.48 mW, i.e. genuinely nothing — this lever only pays under load, and I am not going to pretend otherwise.
Secondary benefit that is not power: converter input droop. At 750 mA the stock pair drops 90-180 mV; with 0805L150SLYR + the stock fuse it drops 60-110 mV. That is 30-70 mV of extra headroom before the low-battery supervisor cuts out. Do not overclaim runtime from this: the cells' own 300-600 mohm ESR contributes 225-450 mV of the sag at the same current, so the board is only ~25% of the total droop, and how that converts to minutes depends on the cell discharge curve, which I have not verified.
findings.risk: I_trip rises from 1.50 A to 3.00 A, so the resettable device becomes less sensitive. In practice this changes little, because F1 already wins every fast fault (see the f1-redundant-lower-r finding): F1's pre-arc I2t is 0.030 A2s, so at a battery-limited 5 A fault it opens in ~1.2 ms while even the 0.75 A PPTC's datasheet max time-to-trip is 0.20 s at 8 A. The PPTC's unique coverage is slow overloads, and that band shifts from 1.5-4 A to 3-4 A. Given the pack's 300-600 mohm ESR limits the available fault current to roughly 3-8 A at 3 V, a 3 A trip point is still reachable. Cost delta is about $0.05 at LCSC quantities. No footprint, schematic or layout change.
findings.verify_reason:
Existence and sourcing: verified independently at DigiKey — 0805L150SLYR, Littelfuse, 1.5 A hold / 3 A trip / 6 V / 50 A, Ri min 15 mOhm, R1 max 65 mOhm, package '0805 (2012 Metric), Concave', status Active production, 13,348 in stock, $2.26/1. So the part exists, is in production, and is genuinely a drop-in on the Bucketmouse:Fuse_0805_2012Metric land (0.975 x 1.4 mm pads at 1.875 mm pitch, confirmed from the PCB file).

Netlist position re-checked with netmap.py: PTC1.1 = VBATT, PTC1.2 = VCC; VCC has exactly 8 pads — C37, L1.1, L2.1, PTC1.2, TP32, U5.4 (VIN1), U5.9 (VIN2), U5.15 (VIN). So 100% of the converter input current does pass through PTC1. Correct.

Stability side-effects checked: nothing downstream depends on PTC1's resistance (no minimum-load, no startup sequencing through it — U5's SHDN pins are gated by /EN off the SW net, independent of PTC1). Lowering series R only improves the converter's input droop. No noise-budget issue: C37 (10u) sits on VCC on the load side.

The one real protection regression is the I_trip rise 1.5 -> 3.0 A. The pack's 300-600 mOhm ESR (Energizer E91: 'Nominal IR: 150 to 300 milliohms (fresh)', verified) plus 0.145 ohm of board path gives 4.3-7.2 A into a hard short at 3.2 V, so 3 A is still reachable — that part of the argument survives. What does not survive is the claim that F1 makes the PPTC's slowness irrelevant.

Second-source note: Bourns confirms MF-PSML is on its obsolete-parts list, so the finding is right to steer to Littelfuse; I could not verify MF-PSML150's exact hold/resistance numbers (the Bourns obsolete PDF returned 403), so treat those as unverified — immaterial, since the part is obsolete anyway.

Direction right, part right, footprint right, numbers ~10% high, one supporting argument refuted. REVISED.
findings.correction:
R_1max for 0805L075SL is 0.150 ohm, NOT 0.160 ohm. I text-extracted the Littelfuse Low Rho Series datasheet (Rev GD 03/06/25) and the row reads: 0805L075SL, marking -G, I_hold 0.75, I_trip 1.50, V_max 6, I_max 50, P_d 0.6, max time-to-trip 8.00 A / 0.20 s, Rmin 0.040, R1max 0.150. LCSC's 150 mOhm figure — which the finding explicitly dismissed as '10 mohm below the datasheet' — was correct and the finding's 0.160 is the error. The 0805L150SL row is exactly as claimed: I_hold 1.50, I_trip 3.00, 6 V, 50 A, 0.6 W, 8.00 A / 0.50 s, Rmin 0.015, R1max 0.065; '0805L150SLYR' is the listed orderable code (4,000/reel).

Corrected delta R: fresh 0.040 - 0.015 = 0.025 ohm (unchanged); post-reflow 0.150 - 0.065 = 0.085 ohm (finding said 0.095); mid 0.055 ohm (finding said 0.060).

Corrected savings, I^2 x dR, low / high (mid):
  200 mA: 1.0 / 3.4 (2.2) mW
  292 mA (700 mW at 2.4 V): 2.1 / 7.3 (4.7) mW
  350 mA: 3.1 / 10.4 (6.7) mW
  390 mA (935 mW at 2.4 V): 3.8 / 12.9 (8.4) mW
  550 mA: 7.6 / 25.7 (16.6) mW
  750 mA: 14.1 / 47.8 (31.0) mW
Every figure in the finding is ~10-12% high at the top of its range. Headline number 5.1 -> 4.7 mW; overclocked 9.1 -> 8.4 mW.

Droop correction: stock pair at 750 mA drops 90-173 mV (not 90-180); after the swap 71-109 mV (not 60-110) — the finding's 60 mV floor is unreachable because F1's 0.080 ohm alone gives 60 mV.

The risk paragraph's justification is refuted (see f1-redundant-lower-r): 'F1's pre-arc I2t of 0.030 A2s ... at a battery-limited 5 A fault it opens in ~1.2 ms ... roughly 400x [faster than the PPTC]' misuses a number specified at 50 A. This does not change the efficiency conclusion but it removes the stated basis for shrugging off the 1.5 A -> 3.0 A trip-point rise.

findings.title: PTC1's derated hold current is below the ClockxControl peak input current — the console can latch off at max brightness on a half-flat pack
findings.current_part: 0805L075SLYR, I_hold 0.75 A specified in 20 C still air. Littelfuse's own LoRho temperature-rerating table for this exact part number: -40 C 1.24 A, -20 C 1.07, 0 C 0.94, 20 C 0.75, 40 C 0.62, 60 C 0.47, 70 C 0.37, 85 C 0.23. I_trip at 20 C is 1.50 A, so between 0.75 A and 1.50 A the device is in its indeterminate band: it does not reliably hold and does not reliably trip, it just heats and its resistance climbs.
findings.proposal: Same swap as ptc1-lorho-075-to-150: 0805L150SLYR. Its rerating table (same datasheet, same units): -40 C 2.37 A, 20 C 1.50, 40 C 1.25, 60 C 0.93, 70 C 0.74, 85 C 0.50. At any plausible internal temperature it holds the overclocked peak with margin.
findings.benefit:
Arithmetic for the peak input current. Measured max in-use is 1175 mW (Hispeedido IPS at max brightness, Everdrive, max volume, speaker). The ClockxControl adds 150-240 mW at the battery (see measured_anchors; I use +235 mW), giving ~1410 mW. Input current = 1410 mW / V_pack: 588 mA at 2.4 V, 705 mA at 2.0 V, 783 mA at 1.8 V. So the overclocked peak is 0.59-0.78 A.
Against the fitted part: I_hold is 0.75 A only at 20 C. A GBA shell is sealed with no ventilation and is dissipating ~1.4 W; a 15-25 C internal rise over a 22 C room puts PTC1 at 37-47 C, where interpolating the Littelfuse table gives I_hold = 0.62-0.67 A. The peak draw of 0.70-0.78 A therefore exceeds I_hold at any realistic internal temperature, and sits inside the 0.75-1.50 A hold/trip band. Two consequences: (1) the device self-heats and its resistance rises well above the 0.160 ohm R_1max figure, so the losses in the previous finding are lower bounds precisely when the current is highest; (2) it can latch, which on this board means the console dies mid-game and stays dead until the PPTC cools.
With 0805L150SLYR: I_hold at 40 C is 1.25 A and at 60 C is 0.93 A, both comfortably above 0.78 A. The nuisance-trip mode is removed and the resistance stays in its linear region.
Note this is a marginal call WITHOUT the overclock too: stock peak is 490-653 mA against a 0.62-0.67 A derated hold current. The overclock is what turns a marginal design into a failing one.
findings.risk: The failure mode is not gradual — a PPTC latch is a hard shutdown. Also note the fix is the same single part swap as the efficiency finding, so it is free once you do that one. Residual risk after the swap: I_trip 3.0 A, discussed in the other finding. One caveat I cannot verify: I have no measured internal-ambient figure for this specific shell/screen combination, so the 37-47 C band is an engineering estimate, not a measurement. If the reviewer can measure the temperature at PTC1 under load, the Littelfuse table converts it directly into a hold current.
findings.verify_reason:
Peak-current arithmetic re-derived and it checks: 1175 mW measured max + ~235 mW ClockxControl = 1410 mW; 1410/2.4 = 588 mA, /2.0 = 705 mA, /1.8 = 783 mA. The +235 mW is not derived in the finding, but it is if anything conservative: insideGadgets' 12 mA + 40-60 mA at VDD3 = 3.3 V is 238 mW at the rail, which at a boost efficiency of 85-90% is 265-280 mW at the battery, so the true total is nearer 1440-1455 mW and the input current nearer 0.60-0.81 A. That makes the conclusion stronger, not weaker.

The fix is the same single 0805L150SLYR swap already checked in ptc1-lorho-075-to-150: verified Active at DigiKey, drop-in on the existing 0.975 x 1.4 mm / 1.875 mm-pitch land, no schematic or PCB change.

The finding's own caveat is the right one and I cannot resolve it either: there is no measured internal-ambient figure for this shell/screen combination, so 37-47 C is an engineering estimate. I note additionally that the finding omits PPTC self-heating, which compounds: at 0.7 A through 0.150 ohm the device dissipates 73 mW into its own body, raising its temperature above ambient and further lowering I_hold — a positive-feedback term that makes the real derating worse than the table alone implies.

Direction confirmed and arguably understated; every derating number wrong; one conclusion (latch-off) overstated. REVISED.
findings.correction:
BOTH rerating tables quoted in the finding are wrong. I text-extracted the actual 'Ambient Operation Temperature / Hold Current (A)' table from the Littelfuse Low Rho datasheet (Rev GD 03/06/25), columns -40 / -20 / 0 / 20 / 40 / 60 / 70 / 85 C:
  0805L075SL: 1.15, 1.00, 0.85, 0.75, 0.55, 0.40, 0.30, 0.20
  0805L150SL: 2.25, 2.00, 1.75, 1.50, 1.15, 0.85, 0.65, 0.45
The finding quoted 0805L075SL as 1.24/1.07/0.94/0.75/0.62/0.47/0.37/0.23 (only the 20 C value is right) and 0805L150SL as 2.37/-/-/1.50/1.25/0.93/0.74/0.50 (also wrong). Neither set appears anywhere in the datasheet.

Corrected derating at the finding's own 37-47 C estimate: interpolating the real table, 0805L075SL holds 0.50-0.57 A, not 0.62-0.67 A. So the fitted part is WORSE than the finding claimed and the stability case is stronger, not weaker. The overclocked peak of 0.59-0.78 A is 1.0x to 1.6x the derated hold current, and even the STOCK peak (1175 mW: 490 mA at 2.4 V, 653 mA at 1.8 V) exceeds it at low battery.

Corrected numbers for the replacement: 0805L150SL holds 1.15 A at 40 C and 0.85 A at 60 C (not 1.25 / 0.93). Still above the 0.78 A worst-case peak, so the swap still fixes the problem, but the 60 C margin is 1.09x, not 1.19x. At 70 C it is 0.65 A — BELOW the 0.78 A peak, so the fix is not unconditional; it needs the internal temperature to stay under about 65 C.

Overstatement to trim: 'it can latch, which on this board means the console dies mid-game'. Exceeding I_hold does not mean tripping. Between I_hold and I_trip a PPTC is indeterminate — it heats and its resistance climbs, and may or may not latch. I_trip at 20 C is 1.50 A and derates roughly in proportion, so ~1.1 A at 40 C; a 0.78 A draw sits inside the indeterminate band, well below the derated trip point. 'Resistance rises and margin is gone' is defensible; 'the console latches off' is possible but not established.

findings.title: F1 is 0.080 ohm of nearly-redundant series resistance: it wins every fault race against PTC1, and its unique coverage is only the VBATT node
findings.current_part: F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR, Kyocera AVX Accu-Guard II, 0805. Verified from the Accu-Guard II datasheet table (row F0805B2R00FW/STR): 2.00 A rating, resistance 0.080 ohm max measured at 10% of rated current at 25 C, voltage drop 220 mV max at 1 x rated current, fusing current within 5 s = 4.00 A, pre-arc I2t = 0.030 A2sec at 50 A, 63 V rated, 50 A interrupting. The Multicomp MCF0805B2R00FSTR datasheet carries the identical row, cross-validating it. Netlist: F1.1 = Net-(BT1-+), F1.2 = VBATT; PTC1.1 = VBATT, PTC1.2 = VCC. So F1 and PTC1 are in series, and the only nodes between them are D2 (anode), R9, SW1 pin 1 and TP19.
findings.proposal:
Three options, in increasing aggression.
(a) Leave F1 as-is. It costs 0.080 ohm; that is the price of a permanent last-resort disconnect.
(b) F0805B2R50FSTR (0.060 ohm max, 220 mV, fusing current within 5 s = 5.00 A, pre-arc I2t 0.050 A2s, 63 V) or F0805B3R00FSTR (0.050 ohm max, 220 mV, 6.00 A / 5 s, I2t 0.10 A2s, 63 V). Same Accu-Guard II series, same 0805 land, drop-in. A 2 x AA pack at 300-600 mohm ESR can deliver roughly 3-8 A into a dead short at 3 V, so a 2.5 A or 3 A element still opens on a real short.
(c) Build option: fit a 0 ohm 0805 jumper in F1 and rely on PTC1 alone. Zero PCB or schematic change; it is a stuffing choice.
findings.benefit:
Saving = I^2 x dR.
  F1 2 A -> 2.5 A, dR = 0.020 ohm:  0.8 mW at 200 mA, 1.7 at 292, 2.5 at 350, 3.0 at 390, 6.1 at 550, 11.3 at 750 mA.
  F1 2 A -> 3 A, dR = 0.030 ohm:  1.2 / 2.6 / 3.7 / 4.6 / 9.1 / 16.9 mW at the same points.
  F1 -> 0 ohm jumper, dR = 0.080 ohm:  3.2 / 6.8 / 9.8 / 12.2 / 24.2 / 45.0 mW.
Combined with the PTC1 swap (0805L150SLYR + F0805B3R00FSTR): total R falls from 0.120-0.240 ohm to 0.065-0.115 ohm, dR = 0.055-0.125 ohm, worth 4.7-10.7 mW at 292 mA, 8.4-19.0 mW at 390 mA, 16.6-37.8 mW at 550 mA and 30.9-70.3 mW at 750 mA.
Why this is defensible protection-wise: F1 and PTC1 in series is unusual, and F1 always wins the race. F1's pre-arc I2t of 0.030 A2s puts its opening time at 1.2 ms into a 5 A fault and 0.47 ms into 8 A, whereas PTC1's datasheet maximum time-to-trip is 0.20 s at 8 A — roughly 400x slower. So for any hard short the non-resettable device is the one that acts, and the PPTC's resettability is already defeated. Reading the netlist, F1's ONLY unique coverage is a fault on the VBATT node itself: D2 (a 1SS355VM to VFILT), R9 (100k), SW1 pin 1, C1 (22 uF on VFILT) and U3 (TPS3840DL20). Everything else on the board sits behind PTC1. So option (c) gives up protection against a shorted C1 or a shorted D2/U3 — a small, real, but narrow exposure.
findings.risk: Option (b) raises the fuse rating; with a 2 x AA pack whose ESR is 300-600 mohm, the available short-circuit current at 3 V is ~3-8 A, so a 3 A element (6 A / 5 s) is at the edge — I would take the 2.5 A part (5 A / 5 s) rather than the 3 A part for that reason, giving up 1.5 mW at 292 mA to keep the margin. Option (c) removes the only permanent disconnect on the board and leaves the always-on VBATT rail (D2/R9/C1/U3, which are live even with SW1 off) unprotected; I would only do that on a build the owner maintains. Note the 0.080 ohm figure is measured at 10% of rating (200 mA); using the 220 mV / 2 A spec the hot resistance is 0.110 ohm, implying +0.069 ohm/W of self-heating, so at 750 mA (45 mW dissipated) the rise is only ~3 mohm and the cold figure is a good model across the whole range.
findings.verify_reason:
Every Accu-Guard II number is CONFIRMED exactly. I fetched and text-extracted the Kyocera AVX datasheet TDS-FUSE-0001 Rev 2 myself. Row F0805B2R00FW/STR: 2.00 A, resistance 0.080 ohm max (column header: 'Resistance 10% x I rated, 25 C, Ohm (max.)'), voltage drop 220 mV max at 1 x I rated, fusing current within 5 s = 4.00 A, pre-arc I2t @ 50 A = 0.030 A2-sec, rated voltage 63 V; interrupting rating 50 A is stated in the general specs. F0805B2R50FW/STR: 0.060 / 220 / 5.00 / 0.050 / 63. F0805B3R00FW/STR: 0.050 / 220 / 6.00 / 0.10 / 63. All three proposed parts exist in the current datasheet, same series, same 0805 land — genuine drop-ins on Bucketmouse:Fuse_0805_2012Metric.

Netlist re-checked: F1.1 = Net-(BT1-+), F1.2 = VBATT, PTC1.1 = VBATT, PTC1.2 = VCC. Net-(BT1-+) has exactly 3 pads (BT1.1, D1.1, F1.1); VBATT has 6 (D2.2, F1.2, PTC1.1, R9.1, SW1.1, TP19). Series arrangement confirmed.

Efficiency arithmetic redone point by point and it is exact: dR 0.020 -> 0.8/1.71/2.45/3.04/6.05/11.25 mW at 200/292/350/390/550/750 mA; dR 0.030 -> 1.2/2.56/3.68/4.56/9.08/16.9; dR 0.080 -> 3.2/6.83/9.8/12.2/24.2/45.0. All plausible inside the 410-1175 mW envelope.

The self-heating model also checks: 220 mV / 2 A = 0.110 ohm hot vs 0.080 cold, dR 0.030 ohm over P = 0.44 W = 0.068 ohm/W; at 750 mA, P = 0.5625 x 0.080 = 45 mW so dR = 3 mOhm. Correct, and the caveat that this subtracts a max from a max is the finding's only unstated looseness.

Sourcing/thermal/stability: no downstream part depends on F1's resistance; raising its rating to 2.5 A keeps the 5 s fusing current at 5.00 A, still inside the pack's 4.3-7.2 A short-circuit capability. The recommendation to take the 2.5 A part rather than the 3 A part is sound and I agree with it.

So: the money numbers are right, the parts are right, the footprint is right, but the protection rationale rests on a misused datasheet parameter and the coverage analysis is incomplete. REVISED, and I would not act on option (c) on the strength of the argument as written.
findings.correction:
The central protection argument is REFUTED. 'F1's pre-arc I2t of 0.030 A2s puts its opening time at 1.2 ms into a 5 A fault and 0.47 ms into 8 A, whereas PTC1's datasheet maximum time-to-trip is 0.20 s at 8 A — roughly 400x slower' is a misuse of the number. The Kyocera AVX datasheet column heading is 'Pre-Arc I2t @ 50A' — it is specified AT 50 A, and the same datasheet contains a chart titled 'FUSE PRE-ARC JOULE INTEGRALS VS. CURRENT ... FOR TYPES F0805B AND F1206B', i.e. I2t is explicitly a strong function of current, not a constant. The datasheet's own tabulated low-current point for the 2 A part is 'Fusing Current (within 5 sec), 25 C = 4.00 A', which corresponds to I2t = 4^2 x 5 = 80 A2sec — 2,700x the 50 A figure. So at 5 A the opening time is on the order of seconds, not 1.2 ms, and the claimed 400x speed advantage over the PPTC collapses. F1 probably still wins at 8 A and above, but by a small and unquantified margin, not by orders of magnitude. Everything the finding builds on 'the PPTC's resettability is already defeated' therefore needs restating as an unproven assertion.

Option (c) correction: an 0805 '0 ohm' jumper is not 0 ohm. Standard thick-film jumpers (e.g. Yageo RC0805 jumper) are specified as a MAXIMUM resistance, commonly 50 mOhm — I could not text-extract the Yageo datasheet to pin the number, so treat 50 mOhm as unverified, but dR = 0.080 ohm is an upper bound and the true saving is more like 0.030-0.080 ohm. The 45.0 mW at 750 mA becomes 17-45 mW. If you want the full 0.080 ohm back, bridge the pads with solder or copper rather than fitting a jumper part.

Combined-swap correction: with the true R1max of 0.150 (not 0.160), the stock series path is 0.120-0.230 ohm, not 0.120-0.240. dR after F0805B3R00FSTR + 0805L150SLYR is 0.055-0.115 ohm, giving 4.7-9.8 mW at 292 mA (finding: 4.7-10.7), 8.4-17.5 mW at 390 mA (8.4-19.0), 16.6-34.8 mW at 550 mA (16.6-37.8), 30.9-64.7 mW at 750 mA (30.9-70.3).

Coverage correction: F1's unique coverage is under-enumerated. The finding lists D2, R9, SW1 pin 1, C1 and U3. It omits the entire SW net, which hangs off SW1 pins 2/3 and is therefore also fed from VBATT ahead of PTC1: Q3 (2N3906), R3, R11, R12, R58 and thence U10 and U17 (both TPS3840DL20). Depopulating F1 leaves those unprotected too.

findings.title: D1 is not a Schottky, is 7-13x under-rated for the job, and sits on the wrong side of F1 so its fault current bypasses the fuse entirely
findings.current_part: D1 = ROHM 1SS355VMTE-17, SOD-323F land. The KiCad Description on both D1 and D2 reads "Schottky diode" — that is WRONG. The ROHM datasheet is titled "1SS355VM Switching Diode (High speed switching)", structure "Epitaxial planar", i.e. a silicon small-signal switching diode. Ratings: VR 80 V, VRM 90 V, Io (average rectified forward current) 100 mA, IFM 225 mA, IFSM 500 mA at t = 1 s, VF 1.2 V max at IF = 100 mA, IR 100 nA max at VR = 80 V, trr 4 ns, Ct 3.0 pF. Topology from the netlist: D1.1 (K) = Net-(BT1-+), D1.2 (A) = GND. F1.1 = Net-(BT1-+), F1.2 = VBATT. So D1 and F1 hang off the SAME node — D1 is upstream of the fuse.
findings.proposal: Minimum fix, and it is nearly free: move D1's cathode from Net-(BT1-+) to VBATT, i.e. put the clamp on the load side of F1. That is the textbook shunt-clamp-plus-series-fuse arrangement and it is a schematic net change plus a short trace edit (D1 pad 1 is at (29.40, -28.99), F1 pad 2 / the VBATT F.Cu pour is at (30.26, -24.20) — 4.9 mm away, and the VBATT pour already reaches within about 2 mm of D1). Optional second step if you want the clamp to survive: the SOD-323F land accepts a standard SOD-323 body, and a 1N5819WS / B5819WS class Schottky is 40 V, 1.0 A average, IFSM 25 A at 8.3 ms — enough surge to hold the fault while F1 opens. Before committing to that, VERIFY the reverse leakage at 3 V: the Diodes Inc 1N5817-1N5819 datasheet specifies peak reverse leakage of 1.0 mA at 25 C and 10 mA at 100 C at rated blocking voltage, versus 100 nA max for the 1SS355VM. D1 is permanently across the pack even with SW1 off, so a leaky part is a permanent parasitic drain — this is exactly why you should NOT naively 'upgrade' D1 to a Schottky, and why the KiCad Description being wrong matters.
findings.benefit: No power saving; this is a correctness finding. The failure analysis: with both cells reversed, Net-(BT1-+) sits at roughly -3 V, D1's anode is at GND and its cathode at -3 V, so it is forward-biased directly across the pack. Current is limited only by cell ESR: (3.0 V - ~1.0 V forward drop) / (0.30 to 0.60 ohm) = 3.3 to 6.7 A, call it ~4.4 A at the mid ESR. That is 7-13x D1's IFSM of 500 mA (and that 500 mA is itself a 1-second rating), and ~5 W in a SOD-323FL body. D1 is destroyed in milliseconds. Because D1 and F1 share the BT1+ node, that current NEVER passes through F1, so the fuse does not open and the fault is not cleared — if D1 fails short, the pack stays shorted through a dead diode until the cells vent or drain. Moving D1 to VBATT routes the same current through F1, whose pre-arc I2t of 0.030 A2s corresponds to ~1.6 ms at 4.4 A (and whose specified fusing current within 5 s is 4.00 A), so the fault is cleared. Separately, U5's absolute maximum on VIN/VIN1/VIN2 is -0.3 V to 6 V per the LTC3527 datasheet, and under reverse insertion VCC sits at about -3 V, violating it by 2.7 V — a second reason to want the fault cleared quickly.
findings.risk: The net move is trivial electrically but does change the schematic, so it is not a build-time fix. Even after the move D1 will probably still be destroyed (it just takes F1 with it, which is the intent), so a builder who reverses the cells replaces two parts instead of an unknown number. If you go to a Schottky, check its 3 V reverse leakage — leakage here is an always-on drain that SW1 cannot switch off. Honest caveat I could not resolve from the files: whether a GBA shell mechanically permits both AA cells to be reversed at all. If it does not, D1 is doing nothing in any case and could be depopulated with zero consequence — it is reverse-biased in normal operation and its 80 V standoff clamps nothing on the positive side. Worth noting that MouseBiteLabs changed this part on the later AGBM-11 (lithium) board to an SMF5.0A-T13 bidirectional TVS, which is a transient suppressor rather than a reverse-polarity clamp — appropriate there because a soldered cell cannot be reversed.
findings.verify_reason:
What I verified and confirms:

The diode identity is exactly right. I text-extracted the ROHM 1SS355VM datasheet (Rev.003, 2016/03/17): title 'Switching Diode (High speed switching)', Structure 'Epitaxial planar'. Absolute maximums: VR 80 V, VRM 90 V, Io 100 mA, IFM 225 mA, IFSM 500 mA at t = 1 s, Tj 150 C. Characteristics: VF 1.2 V max at IF = 100 mA, IR 100 nA max at VR = 80 V, Ct 3.0 pF max (at VR = 0.5 V, f = 1.0 MHz — the finding omitted the condition), trr 4.0 ns max. Package SOD-323FL / SC-90A / UMD2. Every number the finding states is correct. It is NOT a Schottky.

The KiCad Description is confirmed wrong: (property "Description" "Schottky diode") appears on D1 and D2 in AGBM-01, in the fork, and in AGBM-02.

The topology is confirmed by netmap: Net-(BT1-+) has exactly three pads — BT1.1, D1.1 (K) and F1.1. D1 is upstream of the fuse, so its fault current never passes through F1. That is a real and correctly identified defect in a shunt-clamp arrangement.

The fault-current estimate is sound: Energizer E91 datasheet states 'Nominal IR: 150 to 300 milliohms (fresh)' per cell, so 300-600 mOhm per pack; (3.0 - ~1.0)/(0.30 to 0.60) = 3.3 to 6.7 A, which is 6.6x to 13.4x D1's 500 mA IFSM — the finding's '7-13x' is right, and ~4.4 A x 1.1 V is ~4.8 W in a SOD-323FL body, also right. D1 is destroyed either way.

So: the observation (wrong Description, wrong device class, clamp on the wrong side of the fuse) stands and is worth reporting under 'correctness'. The quantified fault-clearing argument, the -3 V abs-max claim and the pad coordinate do not. Because the fix is a schematic net change plus a trace edit and its stated benefit (prompt fault clearing) is the part that failed verification, I would not spin a board for it on this evidence alone — the honest framing is 'the clamp is misplaced and the diode is far too small; if you are touching the schematic anyway, move it, but do not expect the fuse to save the diode.' REVISED.
findings.correction:
Three errors, one of them load-bearing.

(1) REFUTED sub-claim: 'Moving D1 to VBATT routes the same current through F1, whose pre-arc I2t of 0.030 A2s corresponds to ~1.6 ms at 4.4 A ... so the fault is cleared.' Same I2t misuse as f1-redundant-lower-r: the 0.030 A2sec is specified at 50 A, and the datasheet's own 'PRE-ARC JOULE INTEGRALS VS. CURRENT' chart shows I2t rising steeply as current falls. The tabulated point is 'fusing current within 5 sec = 4.00 A', i.e. I2t = 80 A2sec at 4 A. At 4.4 A F1 opens in of order seconds, not 1.6 ms. Consequence: even after the proposed net move, D1 (IFSM 500 mA at t = 1 s) is destroyed thousands of times over before F1 clears. The fix does not clear the fault promptly; it clears it slowly, after the diode has already failed. The finding half-admits this ('D1 will probably still be destroyed') but the quantified justification is wrong by ~3 orders of magnitude.

(2) REFUTED sub-claim: 'under reverse insertion VCC sits at about -3 V, violating [U5's abs max] by 2.7 V'. While D1 is intact it clamps Net-(BT1-+) at roughly -0.9 to -1.1 V; VBATT and VCC follow through F1 and PTC1, so VCC sits near -1 V, not -3 V. -3 V occurs only if D1 fails OPEN. The LTC3527 abs max of -0.3 V to 6 V on VIN/VIN1/VIN2 is confirmed, and -1 V still violates it, but the stated 2.7 V excursion is not what happens. Note this also means D1's position relative to F1 makes essentially NO difference to how well U5 is clamped — the only thing the move changes is whether the fuse ever sees the fault.

(3) Coordinate error: D1 pad 1 (the cathode, on Net-(BT1-+)) is at (29.400, -26.794). (29.40, -28.99) is pad 2, the GND anode. Distance from D1 pad 1 to F1 pad 2 at (30.262, -24.200) is 2.73 mm, not 4.9 mm. The proposed edit is easier than stated.

Scope note the finding should have carried: I checked AGBM-02 and its topology is IDENTICAL — D1 pad 1 on Net-(BT1-+), F1 pad 1 on the same node. So this survived a full board revision at MouseBiteLabs rather than being a one-off slip, which is weak evidence that it may be intentional (or at least long-standing) rather than an oversight.

Schottky-replacement caveat: the 40 V / 1.0 A / 25 A-at-8.3 ms figures the finding quotes are from the Diodes Inc 1N5817-1N5819 datasheet, which is the DO-41 AXIAL part, not a SOD-323 device. MDD's B5819WS page does list 40 V / IO 1.0 A / IFSM 25 A at 8.3 ms for the SOD-323 part but gives no leakage figure, so the SOD-323 part's reverse leakage at 3 V remains unverified — exactly as the finding warns. Also, 'the SOD-323F land accepts a standard SOD-323 body' is unverified: the land is two 1.0 x 1.0 mm pads at 2.2 mm pitch (checked in the PCB), which is plausible for a gull-wing SOD-323 but I have no source for it.

findings.title: SW1 carries no load current — the whole battery current bypasses it, so its 70 mohm contact resistance is worth 2 nW. No lever here.
