REFUTED: the 24% shortening of the POWER-UP delay. A power-up ramp is a large-signal charge problem, not a small-signal one: the capacitance is ~10.0 uF at 0 V and only falls to 8.25 uF by 2.0 V. Integrating the digitised C(V) from 0 to the 2.0 V TPS3840DL20 threshold gives a charge-effective capacitance of 9.40 uF, i.e. 94% of nominal. The power-up delay is therefore about 6% shorter than the schematic value, not 24%.
findings.correction: Restate as two separate numbers. (a) Power-up delay to the 2.0 V threshold: charge-effective C = 9.40 uF (integral of the digitised DC-bias curve from 0 to 2.0 V), so the delay is ~6% shorter than the marked-10-uF calculation - 45.6 ms instead of 48.5 ms. That is inside the part's own +/-10% tolerance and is not worth re-scaling R58 for. (b) Small-signal behaviour at the operating point (brownout filtering, response to a battery sag around 2.28 V): 7.79 uF, i.e. -22%, giving tau = 37.8 ms instead of 48.5 ms. This is the number that is genuinely 22% off the schematic, and it applies to dip rejection, not to start-up. The finding's recommendation to annotate the schematic is still worth doing; the recommendation to re-scale R58 is not, because the two effective values differ by 20% and no single resistor value fixes both.

findings.title: Negative result: the 0.1 uF, 1 uF, 15 pF and 3300 pF parts do not derate meaningfully - the small-signal decoupling is correctly specified throughout
findings.current_part: MPNs resolved from the schematics' own Source fields, which every one of these symbols carries: 0.1 uF = KEMET C0603C104K5RACTU, X7R 50 V 0603. 1 uF = KEMET C0603C105K4RACTU, X7R 16 V 0603. 15 pF (C40/C41, the LTC3527 feed-forward caps) = KEMET C0603C150J5GACTU, C0G/NP0 50 V +/-5 %. 3300 pF (C61/C80, the TPS22917 CT slew-rate caps) = KEMET C0603C332K5RACTU, X7R 50 V.
findings.proposal: No change. Report this so nobody spends money re-specifying parts that are already right.
findings.benefit: No power saving; this is the negative result that stops a pointless BOM churn. Digitised curves: a 1 uF 16 V X7R 0603 loses 3.2 % at 2.5 V (0.968 uF) and 12.5 % at 3.336 V (0.875 uF). A 0.1 uF X7R 0603 - and I deliberately used the 16 V curve, which is the pessimistic case, because the board's part is 50 V - reads +0.7 % at 2.5 V, 0.0 % at 3.336 V and -0.7 % at 5.014 V, i.e. flat. C0G has no voltage coefficient at all by construction, so the LTC3527's feed-forward compensation is stable, which matters because those two caps are inside the converter's feedback loop. The 3300 pF X7R 50 V parts sit at 5-7 % of rated voltage and follow the same flat behaviour as the 0.1 uF. The only two capacitor families on this board that derate hard are the 22 uF 0805s and the 10 uF 0603s, both covered in their own findings. The BOM is well chosen: 25 V dielectric for the bulk and 50 V X7R for the bypass on a 5 V board is more conservative than most hobbyist designs.
findings.risk: The 1 uF and 0.1 uF curves are from Murata parts of the same case size, dielectric class and (or lower) voltage rating, not from the KEMET parts actually specified - KEMET/Yageo publish their DC-bias data only through the KSIM web tool, which is JavaScript-rendered and could not be fetched. Same-class substitution is standard practice for this kind of estimate but it is a substitution, and it is why this finding is not at 0.9 confidence. The direction of the error is safe: the Murata 16 V curve bounds a KEMET 50 V part from the pessimistic side.
findings.verify_reason: I resolved all four DigiKey short links myself rather than trusting the write-up, and every MPN is as claimed: m958w3z3 -> KEMET C0603C104K5RACTU (0.1 uF, 50 V, X7R, 0603); 2ppmm3vt -> KEMET C0603C105K4RACTU (1 uF, 16 V, X7R, 0603); q58vhz49 -> KEMET C0603C150J5GACTU (15 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%, 0603); 3p3jj3wt -> KEMET C0603C332K5RACTU (3300 pF, 50 V, X7R, 0603). I then independently digitised the Murata GRM188R71C105KA12 DC-bias chart at 500 dpi with programmatic gridline detection and got -3.6% at 2.5 V (0.964 uF) and -12.1% at 3.336 V (0.879 uF), against the finding's -3.2%/0.968 uF and -12.5%/0.875 uF - agreement to within half a percentage point, which is better than a digitised chart deserves. The proxy substitution is correctly disclosed and its direction is correctly reasoned (a 16 V curve bounds a 50 V part pessimistically; the 1 uF proxy is the same rating and case as the fitted part). C0G having no voltage coefficient is a construction fact, and it matters here because C40/C41 sit inside the LTC3527's feedback path. Conclusion - do not churn the BOM - is correct.

findings.title: Negative result: shrinking the output capacitors cannot recover the 29 mW idle gap to AGBM-02, because the board already idles above the Burst Mode threshold
findings.current_part: LTC3527 with MODE = GND (automatic Burst Mode) and FSEL = GND (1.2 MHz). Datasheet Iq is 12 uA in Burst Mode versus 500 uA typ / 900 uA max active, drawn from the higher of VOUT1/VOUT2. The Applications Information warns that "larger output capacitor values may cause this transition [out of Burst Mode] to occur at lighter loads", which is a genuine invitation to think that AGBM-01's 43 uF of nominal VOUT3 bulk is costing idle efficiency versus AGBM-02.
findings.proposal: Do not reduce COUT. The hypothesis is testable from the datasheet and it fails.
findings.benefit: Zero, and knowing it is zero is the point - this was the most plausible capacitor-side explanation for AGBM-01 idling 29 mW above AGBM-02 and 36 mW above a stock GBA, and it is wrong. The check: the datasheet's Burst Mode Threshold Current vs VIN curve for VOUT = 3.3 V shows enter-burst at roughly 14 mA and leave-burst at roughly 18 mA of load current at VIN = 2.4 V. The board's idle VOUT3 load is 170 mW x ~0.85 / 3.336 V = roughly 43 mA - about 2.5x above the leave-burst threshold. Channel 2 is therefore in fixed-frequency PWM at idle no matter what COUT is, so changing COUT cannot move the operating mode. Even if it could, the prize is small: the Iq difference is 500 - 12 = 488 uA drawn from a 5 V output, i.e. 2.4 mW at the output or about 2.9 mW at the battery, plus an unquantified switching-loss term. Channel 1 (VOUT5) is a different story - its idle load is only a few mA (the LED through R25 3.3k is 0.91 mA), which is below the roughly 30-38 mA burst threshold at VOUT = 5 V, so it is already in Burst Mode and already getting the 14 uA Iq the datasheet promises at VOUT = 5 V. Both channels are already in the best mode available to them. The 29 mW gap to AGBM-02 is a converter-topology difference (one dual boost with two 4.7 uH inductors versus two TPS63802 buck-boosts with 0.47 uH), not a capacitor selection difference, and no passive change on this board will close it.
findings.risk: None - the recommendation is to change nothing. The burst-threshold curves I read are labelled for 2.2 MHz operation while this board runs at 1.2 MHz (FSEL = GND), so the exact threshold on this board will differ; but it would have to be off by more than 2.5x in the wrong direction to change the conclusion, and lower switching frequency generally lowers, not raises, the burst threshold. My idle VOUT3 load figure also assumes ~85 % converter efficiency and that essentially all idle load is on channel 2, both stated estimates.
findings.verify_reason: The recommendation is right and the main argument survives, but a load-bearing sub-claim is flatly contradicted by the datasheet. CONFIRMED from the LTC3527 datasheet: Iq 12 uA in Burst Mode versus 500 uA typ / 900 uA max active, drawn 'from the higher of VOUT1 or VOUT2'; MODE/FSEL strapping from the netlist; 'Note that larger output capacitor values may cause this transition to occur at lighter loads' verbatim; the Burst Mode Threshold Current graphs are indeed all labelled '2.2MHz OPERATION' (G13/G14/G15), and G14's axis for VOUT=3.3 V runs 0-25 mA so the quoted ~14/18 mA enter/leave figures are in range. The idle load estimate (170 mW * 0.85 / 3.336 V = 43 mA) is arithmetically right and comfortably above threshold, so channel 2 is in fixed-frequency PWM at idle and no COUT change can alter that. REFUTED: 'Channel 1 (VOUT5) ... is already in Burst Mode and already getting the 14 uA Iq the datasheet promises' and 'Both channels are already in the best mode available to them.' Burst Mode on this part is a shared, chip-level decision, not per-channel. The datasheet states: 'To realize the efficiency benefits of Burst Mode operation, both VOUT1 and VOUT2 must be under a light load current condition, if they are both enabled', and 'Once the LTC3527/LTC3527-1 have left Burst Mode operation ... they will remain there until both output loads are reduced below the burst threshold current.' Both channels are enabled here (SHDN1 = /PG_2V5, SHDN2 = /EN), so with channel 2 at 43 mA the whole converter is in PWM at idle and the 12 uA burst quiescent is never obtained on either channel. Also, the '14 uA Iq at VOUT = 5 V' number does not appear in the electrical table - the specified figure is 12 uA - and I could not verify it from any graph.
findings.correction: Keep the recommendation (do not reduce COUT) and keep the main argument, but replace the channel-1 paragraph. At idle the LTC3527 is in fixed-frequency PWM on BOTH channels, because burst entry requires both loads below threshold and channel 2 sits at ~43 mA. So the chip is drawing the 500 uA typ active quiescent from the 5.014 V rail (~2.5 mW at the output, ~2.9 mW at the battery) plus continuous 1.2 MHz switching losses on both channels, and none of that is recoverable by capacitor selection - which strengthens, not weakens, the finding's conclusion that the 29 mW gap to AGBM-02 is a topology difference. Note also that the datasheet offers the one lever that WOULD move the threshold: 'Raising the inductor value will lower the load current at which Burst Mode is entered' - i.e. inductance, not capacitance, is the knob, and it is the wrong direction for the l1l2-dcr proposal to ignore.

findings.title: VOUT3's bulk is 65 % of nominal after derating - which is still six times the LTC3527's stability minimum, so the rail carrying the overclock is fine
findings.current_part: VOUT3 at 3.336 V carries C42 (22 uF 25 V X5R 0805 -> 14.94 uF), C2 and C23 (10 uF 25 V X5R 0603 -> 6.11 uF each) and C22 (1 uF 16 V X7R 0603 -> 0.875 uF): 28.0 uF effective against 43 uF nominal. The converter's input cap C37 (10 uF 0603) sits at VCC, roughly 2.4 V mid-discharge, where it derates to 7.54 uF.
findings.proposal: No change. Recorded so the number exists in writing, because this is the rail the ClockxControl loads and it is the first thing anyone will suspect if the overclock misbehaves.
findings.benefit: No power saving. The margins: LTC3527 is specified stable with COUT >= 4.7 uF and recommends 4.7-10 uF, so 28.0 uF effective is 6x the floor - the 35 % capacitance loss to DC bias changes nothing about loop stability. On the input side the datasheet says "A 2.2 uF input capacitor is sufficient for most applications" and C37 delivers 7.54 uF, a 3.4x margin. Adding the overclock's 62 mA to VOUT3 raises the rail's load from roughly 43 mA at idle to roughly 150 mA; against the datasheet's Maximum Output Current vs VIN curve for converter 2 (roughly 300 mA at VIN = 2.4 V, VOUT = 3.3 V) that is comfortable at mid-discharge. The one thing worth watching is the low-battery end: the same curve falls to roughly 200 mA at VIN = 1.8 V, so an overclocked console with a bright backlight near the end of a set of alkalines is operating with about 25 % headroom on channel 2 rather than 100 %.
findings.risk: None from leaving it. The low-battery headroom note is derived by reading a datasheet graph and depends on my channel-split estimate; if the split is materially different from 40:60 the VOUT3 numbers move. Measuring current at TP16 would replace the estimate with a fact.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced every derated value independently from my own 500 dpi digitisations rather than accepting the write-up's. C42 (GRM21BR61E226ME44L, 22 uF 25 V X5R 0805) at 3.336 V: I read -31.7% = 15.02 uF against the finding's 14.94. C2/C23 (GRM188R61E106KA73J, 10 uF 25 V X5R 0603) at 3.336 V: -39.0% = 6.10 uF against 6.11. C22 (1 uF 16 V X7R) at 3.336 V: 0.879 uF against 0.875. C37 at 2.4 V: 7.53 uF against 7.54. Total 27.9 uF against the stated 28.0 uF - agreement throughout. Net membership confirmed from the pad dump (VOUT3 = C2, C22, C23, C41, C42 plus U4/U8/U18/U5 and the R13/R23 dividers; C41 is the 15 pF FB2 feed-forward, correctly excluded from bulk). LTC3527 quotes verified verbatim: stability floor 'output capacitor values of 4.7uF or greater', recommended range '4.7uF to 10uF ... Larger values up to 22uF', and 'A 2.2uF input capacitor is sufficient for most applications'. So 28 uF effective is 6x the floor and 7.5 uF at VCC is 3.4x the input recommendation - correct, and the conclusion (change nothing) stands. Two caveats recorded rather than counted against it: the sentence 'raises the rail's load from roughly 43 mA at idle to roughly 150 mA' does not follow from the stated +62 mA (43+62 = 105 mA), and the Maximum Output Current vs VIN readings (~300 mA at VIN 2.4 V, ~200 mA at 1.8 V for converter 2) come from datasheet graph G11, which I could not verify because Analog Devices' server refused every attempt to fetch the PDF - I confirmed only that G11 is 'Maximum Output Current vs VIN for Converter 2' with a 0-500 mA axis, which makes the quoted values plausible but unchecked. The low-battery headroom note should be treated as unverified on that basis.

findings.title: DL1 power LED is an AlInGaP part at 0.93 mA burning 4.66 mW continuously; an InGaN green in the same 0603 pads at 0.12 mA is brighter and saves 5.05 mW at the battery
findings.current_part: DL1 = Wurth 150060VS75000, 0603 WL-SMCW, AlInGaP, bright green, 570 nm dominant; VF 2.0 V min / 2.4 V max at 20 mA; luminous intensity IV 12 mcd min / 40 mcd max at 20 mA; 140 deg viewing angle (https://www.we-online.com/components/products/datasheet/150060VS75000.pdf). Series resistor R25 = 3.3k (0603) from VOUT5; cathode to Q9A drain (Q9A on in the normal battery state, Rds(on) 1.7 ohm typ at Vgs=10 V, ~3 ohm at the 5 V gate drive here, so ~3 mV drop) (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/ndc7002n-d.pdf). The LED is lit the entire time the console is on, because VOUT5 is up whenever the boost runs.
findings.proposal: Replace DL1 with Wurth 150060GS75000 — same 0603 WL-SMCW family, same land pattern, InGaN green, 525 nm dominant, VF 3.2-3.5 V at 20 mA, IV 220 mcd min / 430 mcd max at 20 mA (https://www.we-online.com/components/products/datasheet/150060GS75000.pdf) — and change R25 from 3.3k to 22k (same 0603 pads). Cheaper alternative if you want to keep the existing LED: change R25 alone from 3.3k to 10k.
findings.benefit:
Today: I digitised the 150060VS75000 forward I-V curve from the datasheet's vector data (axis calibration 0-4.0 V x 0-35 mA; recovered points (0.106 mA, 1.801 V), (1.006 mA, 1.925 V), (2.006 mA, 1.964 V), (8.00 mA, 2.045 V), (20 mA, 2.09 V) — the last agrees with the datasheet's 2.0/2.4 V min/max spec). Solving I = (5.00 - VF(I) - 0.005)/3300 converges at I = 0.932 mA, VF = 1.92 V. Power from VOUT5 = 5.00 x 0.932 mA = 4.66 mW, of which only 1.79 mW is in the LED and 2.87 mW is heat in R25. At 80% boost efficiency that is 5.83 mW off the battery — 3.4% of the 170 mW idle, and the single largest item in this domain. Present brightness: 12-40 mcd x (0.932/20) = 0.56-1.86 mcd.
With 150060GS75000 + R25 = 22k: digitising that part's I-V curve the same way gives (0.106 mA, 2.251 V) and (1.006 mA, 2.638 V); solving I = (5.00 - VF(I))/22000 converges at I = 0.124 mA, VF = 2.28 V. Power from VOUT5 = 5.00 x 0.124 mA = 0.62 mW. Saving = 4.66 - 0.62 = 4.04 mW at VOUT5 = 5.05 mW at the battery at 80% boost efficiency (4.75 mW at 85%). Brightness = 220-430 mcd x (0.124/20) = 1.36-2.67 mcd, i.e. 2.4x brighter worst-case-to-worst-case and ~1.7x brighter mid-to-mid than today. Brighter AND 7.5x less power.
Resistor-only variant (keep DL1, R25 3.3k -> 10k): solving against the same curve gives I = 0.314 mA at VF = 1.86 V, 1.57 mW at VOUT5, saving 3.09 mW at VOUT5 = 3.86 mW at the battery, but brightness falls to 0.19-0.63 mcd (3x dimmer than today) — visible indoors, marginal in daylight.
findings.risk: 525 nm InGaN green is a visibly different, colder green than the 570 nm yellow-green of the existing part; purely cosmetic but it will not match a stock AGB. The InGaN VF (3.2-3.5 V at 20 mA, ~2.28 V at 0.12 mA) is much more temperature- and bin-dependent than AlInGaP, so the current through a 22k resistor varies more across parts; at 0.12 mA a +/-0.15 V VF spread moves the current +/-6%, which is immaterial for an indicator. If you go the resistor-only route the LED gets 3x dimmer, which some builders will dislike. No stability risk either way: DL1's cathode node /D1A also gates Q9B (the low-battery red-LED switch) through C68 10u, and reducing the DL1 current does not change that node's logic level — Q9A still pulls /D1A to ~0 in the normal state, and when Q9A turns off, /D1A is pulled to 5 V through R25 with essentially no current, so a 22k R25 works identically (it charges C68 in 220 ms instead of 33 ms, delaying the green-to-red changeover by ~0.2 s — cosmetic).
findings.verify_reason:
I fetched both Würth datasheets myself and every tabulated number in the finding is exact. 150060VS75000: chip technology AlInGaP, emitting colour Bright Green, λdom 570 nm @20 mA, IV 12 min / 40 max mcd @20 mA, VF 2.0 min / 2.4 max V @20 mA, 2θ50% = 140°, 0603, land pattern 0.8/0.8/2.4 mm. 150060GS75000: InGaN, Green, λdom 525 nm, IV 220/430 mcd, VF 3.2/3.5 V, 140°, 0603, IDENTICAL recommended land pattern (0.8/0.8/2.4 mm) and identical body drawing — so the swap is a genuine drop-in on LED_0603_1608Metric_Pad1.05x0.95mm_HandSolder, no PCB or schematic change. The GS part is in production and stocked (Digi-Key, ~$0.15).

I did NOT trust the finding's digitisation — I re-extracted the I-V curves from the PDF content streams myself (form XObject /I5 on page 3 of each datasheet; x-axis calibrated 46.8→0.0 V, 378.84→4.0 V; y-axis 44.16→0 mA, 385.8→35 mA). Recovered VS points: (0.106 mA, 1.801 V), (1.006, 1.925), (2.006, 1.964), (8.005, 2.045), (20.004, 2.100), (30.003, 2.124). Recovered GS points: (0.106, 2.251), (1.006, 2.637), (20.004, 3.239). These match the finding to three decimals; its one stated deviation (2.09 V vs my 2.100 V at 20 mA) is rounding.

Re-solving the loops myself: with R25 = 3.3 k and Q9A's ~3 mV drop, I = (5.00 − VF(I) − 0.005)/3300 converges at I = 0.9316 mA, VF = 1.921 V → 4.66 mW at VOUT5, of which 1.79 mW in the LED and 2.87 mW in R25. With GS + 22 k: I = (5.00 − VF)/22000 converges at 0.1241 mA, VF = 2.271 V → 0.62 mW. Saving 4.04 mW at VOUT5. Resistor-only variant reproduces too: 0.3135 mA, VF 1.860 V, 1.57 mW, saving 3.09 mW.

Topology verified from the netlist, not assumed: /D1A carries DL1 pad 1 (K), C68 10 µF, Q9 pin 3 (G2) and Q9 pin 6 (D1); R25 feeds DL1 pad 2 (A) from VOUT5; Q9A's gate is U10's open-drain RESET pulled up by R18 10 k to VOUT5, so Q9A is on and DL1 lit whenever the battery is good. Confirmed.

The brightness claim is if anything CONSERVATIVE. I also digitised the datasheets' Luminous-Intensity-vs-Forward-Current curves (page 4, /I6). The AlInGaP curve is essentially linear (2.01 mcd/mA at 0.106 mA vs 2.026 mcd/mA at 20 mA), so linear scaling is right for the incumbent: 1.89 mcd max-bin at 0.93 mA. The InGaN curve is markedly SUPER-linear at low current (4.11 mcd at 0.107 mA = 38.4 mcd/mA, versus 21.5 mcd/mA at 20 mA), giving ~4.8 mcd max-bin at 0.124 mA — nearly 2x the finding's linear-scaled 2.67 mcd. Even scaled to the 220 mcd minimum bin that is ~2.45 mcd, still above the incumbent's max-bin 1.89 mcd. Brighter, verified.

Corrections that do not change the verdict: (1) VOUT5 is 5.014 V, not 5.00 — I verified the LTC3527 feedback voltage as 1.176/1.20/1.224 V, so VOUT5 = 1.20 × (1 + 1.78M/560k). (2) The 80% conversion factor is an assumption, not a measurement, and channel 1's total idle load is only ~1.0 mA (DL1 0.93 mA + R65 50 µA + a few µA of IC quiescent), i.e. deep Burst Mode; I could not read the LTC3527 efficiency curves (outlined vector text), so the battery-side saving is best quoted as 4.7–5.8 mW rather than 5.05 exactly. (3) TWO real interactions the finding understates: with R25 = 22 k the /D1A charge time to Q9B's turn-on threshold is ~0.4–0.5 s, not the stated 0.2 s (the charge current falls from 141 µA to ~34 µA across the ramp); and, more importantly, the InGaN part's higher forward voltage lowers the steady-state /D1A level in the low-battery state from ~3.6 V (AlInGaP) to ~3.0 V, narrowing the margin over Q9B's spec'd 2.5 V max VGS(th) from ~1.1 V to ~0.5 V. Still positive, but the FDC6301N swap proposed in the q10a finding would restore that margin. Neither point undoes a 4–5 mW saving on a 170 mW idle.

findings.title: The Q1/Q3/Q10 brownout latch sits statically biased in the RUN state and burns 387 uA (0.93 mW) off VBATT; raising R15 and R16 from 10k to 100k cuts it to 81 uA
findings.current_part: Q1 = 2N3904 NPN SOT-23, hFE 40 min at IC = 0.1 mA, VCE = 1.0 V (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/2n3904-d.pdf). Q3 = 2N3906 PNP SOT-23, hFE 60 min at IC = 0.1 mA (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/2n3906-d.pdf). Q10 = NDC7002N dual N-ch in SuperSOT-6, pin assignment 1=G1, 2=S2, 3=G2, 4=D2, 5=S1, 6=D1 confirmed against the onsemi datasheet's pin-assignment graphic and against the KiCad symbol Transistor_FET:Q_Dual_NMOS_G1S2G2D2S1D1 used in the schematic (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/ndc7002n-d.pdf). Bias network as built: R12 100k (SW to Q1-C), R15 10k (Q1-C to Q3 base), R16 10k (Q10A-G to Q1 base), R17 100k (Q10A-G to GND).
findings.proposal: Change R15 from 10k to 100k and R16 from 10k to 100k (both existing 0603 pads, no other change). Optionally also R12 100k -> 470k. Do NOT take R12 to 1M: NDC7002N IDSS is spec'd 1 uA max (at VDS = 40 V, 25 C) and 500 uA at TJ = 125 C, and 1 uA through 1M would collapse the node.
findings.benefit:
Topology from the netlist: /EN is high in the run state (R11 1k pull-up from SW, R24 100k to GND, U3's open-drain RESET released), so Q10B (G=/EN pin3, S=GND pin2, D=Q1-C pin4) is ON, holding Q1-C at Vce(sat); that pulls Q3's base down through R15, turning Q3 ON, which pulls Q10A-G up to ~SW, which through R16 turns Q1 ON — a self-consistent, permanently-biased state, not a dormant one. Current at VBATT = 2.4 V, with Vbe(sat) = 0.65 V and Vce(sat) = 0.05 V: Ib(Q3) = (2.4-0.65-0.05)/10k = 170.0 uA; I(R17) = 2.35/100k = 23.5 uA; I(R16) = (2.35-0.65)/10k = 170.0 uA; Ic(Q3) = 193.5 uA; Ie(Q3) = 363.5 uA; I(R12) = 2.35/100k = 23.5 uA. Total from SW = 387.0 uA = 0.929 mW, straight off the battery with no conversion loss in between.
With R15 = R16 = 100k: Ib(Q3) = 1.70/100k = 17.0 uA; I(R16) = 1.70/100k = 17.0 uA; Ic(Q3) = 23.5 + 17.0 = 40.5 uA; Ie(Q3) = 57.5 uA; plus R12 23.5 uA = 81.0 uA = 0.194 mW. Saving 306 uA = 0.734 mW at the battery (0.43% of the 170 mW idle).
Saturation still holds with huge margin: Q3 forced beta = 40.5/17.0 = 2.4 (hFE min 60 at 0.1 mA), Q1 forced beta = (23.5 + 17.0)/17.0 = 2.4 (hFE min 40 at 0.1 mA). Re-checked at the worst-case operating point, VBATT = 2.0 V (just above U3's 2.0 V trip): Ib(Q3) = 13.0 uA, Ic(Q3) = 32.5 uA, forced beta 2.5 — still fine.
Secondary benefit: this network also dominates the post-brownout latched-off drain — see the en-pullup-scaling finding.
findings.risk: Regenerative turn-on gets slower: node capacitances here are a few pF, so 100k x ~10 pF = ~1 us versus a brownout event measured in milliseconds — no practical effect. The 100k values raise sensitivity to leakage: Q10's gate-body leakage is spec'd 100 nA max, which across R17 (unchanged at 100k) is 10 mV — fine. Do not also raise R17, and do not take R12 to 1M (see proposal). If a builder populates a hot-running board, 2N3904/2N3906 ICBO rises and the off-state margin at Q1-C shrinks; 470k is the safe upper bound for R12.
findings.verify_reason:
Topology independently confirmed from the netlist, pad by pad: Net-(Q1-C) = {Q1 pin3 C, Q10 pin4 D2, R12, R15}; Net-(Q10A-G) = {Q3 pin3 C, Q10 pin1 G1, R16, R17}; Q3 emitter = pin2 = SW; /EN = {R11, R24, U3 RESET, U5 pin12 ~SHDN2, Q10 pin3 G2, Q10 pin5 S1}. With the NDC7002N pin assignment (1=G1, 2=S2, 3=G2, 4=D2, 5=S1, 6=D1, verified from the onsemi datasheet's pin-assignment graphic and consistent with the KiCad symbol Q_Dual_NMOS_G1S2G2D2S1D1), Q10B is G=/EN, S=GND, D=Q1-C, exactly as the finding says. The state is genuinely self-sustaining and is NOT optional — Q10A-G must be held high for the brownout latch to be armed at all, so this current is the price of the feature.

I redid the arithmetic from scratch at SW = 2.4 V. Ib(Q3) = (2.4 − 0.65 − 0.03)/10k = 172 µA. With Q10A-G at 2.35 V: I(R17) = 23.5 µA, I(R16) = 170 µA, Ic(Q3) = 193.5 µA, Ie(Q3) = 365.5 µA. I(R12) = 23.7 µA. Total from SW = 389 µA = 0.934 mW. With R15 = R16 = 100 k: Ib(Q3) = 17.2 µA, Ic(Q3) = 40.5 µA, Ie(Q3) = 57.7 µA, plus R12 23.7 µA = 81.4 µA = 0.195 mW. Saving 0.739 mW — within 1% of the finding's 0.734 mW. Forced betas 2.35 (Q3) and 2.4 (Q1), against verified hFE minima of 60 (2N3906) and 40 (2N3904) at IC = 0.1 mA, VCE = 1.0 V. Saturation holds with enormous margin. NDC7002N IDSS 1 µA max at VDS = 40 V and 500 µA at TJ = 125 °C, IGSS ±100 nA at VGS = ±20 V — all confirmed, so the caution against R12 = 1 M and the advice to leave R17 alone are both sound.

Minor defects that do not overturn it: (a) the two BJT datasheets cited cover the TO-92 package only (onsemi 2N3904-D / 2N3906-D, CASE 29) while the board's Q1/Q3 footprint is SOT-23 — the SOT-23 parts are MMBT3904/MMBT3906; the hFE and saturation specs are equivalent so the conclusion survives, but the BOM value strings '2N3904'/'2N3906' on SOT-23 pads are themselves a part-number/package mismatch nobody flagged. (b) Vbe = 0.65 V and Vce(sat) = 0.05 V are datasheet values taken at IC = 10 mA and applied at ~170 µA, where Vbe is nearer 0.55–0.60 V; that makes the present current slightly HIGHER than stated, so the saving is not overstated. (c) The finding does not notice that Q10B's run-state VGS is only 0.990 × SW = 2.38 V at a fresh pack, against the NDC7002N's spec'd 2.5 V max VGS(th) — a worst-case part may never arm this latch in the first place, which is the same defect the q10a finding raises for Q10A. 0.74 mW is 0.43% of the 170 mW idle; small but real and free.

findings.title: R65 100k holds the MIC1553's CS pin down through Q5B and dissipates 250 uW at VOUT5 continuously for no reason; 1M does the same job
findings.current_part: R65 = 100k 0603 from VOUT5 to the Q5B drain node, which is also U14 pin 3 (CS). U14 = MIC1553, an IttyBitty CMOS RC 555-type astable oscillator in SOT-23-5; CS is 'Chip Select/Reset (Input): Active-high at >2/3 VS. Output off when low at <1/3 VS', and the part's inputs are described as 'Zero Leakage Trigger and Threshold Inputs' (https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/TCG/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/MIC1551-53-IttyBitty-RC-Type-555-Timer-Oscillator-DS20006985.pdf). In the normal (battery-OK) state U17's open-drain RESET is released, R66 100k pulls Q5B's gate to VOUT5, Q5B is on, and CS is held at ~0 V — so all of R65's current flows to ground through Q5B.
findings.proposal: Change R65 from 100k to 1M (same 0603 pad). No other change.
findings.benefit: Current through R65 today = 5.00 V / 100k = 50.0 uA, dissipating 5.00 x 50.0 uA = 250 uW at VOUT5, continuously, in the normal battery state. With R65 = 1M: 5.0 uA / 25 uW. Saving 225 uW at VOUT5 = 281 uW at the battery at 80% boost efficiency. The only requirement on R65 is that when U17 trips (battery below ~2.10 V) and Q5B turns off, R65 must pull CS above 2/3 VS = 3.33 V; with 1M and the MIC1553's spec'd zero-leakage input, even 100 nA of leakage would only cost 0.1 V.
findings.risk: 1M is a high-impedance node next to a 5 V rail on a hand-assembled board; flux residue or a fingerprint of a few hundred kohm across it would drag the CS-high level down and disable the low-battery blink. Clean the board. The MIC1553's CS leakage is described qualitatively ('zero leakage') rather than given a numeric max in the electrical table I read, so the 1M choice is bounded by that qualitative claim — 470k would be a more conservative compromise (10.6 uA, saving 197 uW at VOUT5).
findings.verify_reason:
Verified against the Microchip MIC1551/53 datasheet (DS20006985A) which I extracted in full. MIC1553 Table 3-2 pin functions: 1 = T/T, 2 = GND, 3 = CS 'Chip Select/Reset (Input): Active-high at >2/3VS. Output off when low at <1/3VS', 4 = VS, 5 = OUT. Features list includes '"Zero" Leakage Trigger and Threshold Inputs' and '<1 µA Typical Shutdown Mode (MIC1553)'. Netlist confirms R65 100k runs VOUT5 → Net-(Q5B-D) = U14 pin 3, and that Q5B (G2 = pin3 = Q5B-G pulled to VOUT5 by R66, S2 = pin2 = GND, D2 = pin4) is on in the battery-OK state because U17's open-drain RESET is released. So 50.0 µA flows continuously: 5.014/100k = 50.1 µA, 251 µW at VOUT5, ~314 µW at the battery at 80%. With 1 M: 5.0 µA / 25 µW. Saving 226 µW at VOUT5 ≈ 0.28 mW at the battery. Arithmetic reproduces.

Two corrections. First, the finding's CS-high target is optimistic: the datasheet's Chip Select electrical spec is min 50 / typ 67 / max 72 %VS for the 'On' state, so worst case CS must reach 0.72 × 5.0 = 3.6 V, not the nominal 2/3 = 3.34 V. With 1 M that still leaves ~1.4 V of headroom against any leakage below ~1.4 µA, so it holds — but the margin is smaller than stated. Second, the finding is right that there is no numeric CS input-current spec: the datasheet gives Trigger Current and Threshold Current as 50 nA max at VS = 15 V but specifies nothing for CS, and section 4.3 warns 'Floating CS will result in unpredictable operation.' 1 M is not floating, but that warning plus the hand-assembly flux-residue caveat the finding raises itself is why I would take its own fallback of 470 k (10.6 µA, ~197 µW saved at VOUT5) as the sane build value. Either way this is 0.17–0.25% of a 170 mW idle: real, verified, and honestly small.

findings.title: U10 and U17 sense the battery through low-value dividers that burn 86-241 uA; scaling both by 10x costs nothing and improves their transient filtering
findings.current_part: U10 and U17 are TPS3840DL20 (SOT-23-5 DBV): supply current 300 nA typical / 700 nA maximum, VDD operating range 1.5 V to 10 V, fixed threshold accuracy 1% typ / 1.5% max, hysteresis 100 mV typ for VIT- <= 3.0 V, and — important — the family offers fixed thresholds from 1.6 V to 4.9 V in 0.1 V steps (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3840.pdf). U10 senses SW through R3/R4 and U17 through R58/R63. NOTE the schematic and the PCB disagree on R3/R4 (see the bom-pcb-value-mismatch finding): schematic 5.1k/33k (divider ratio 0.8661, trip at SW = 2.31 V), PCB 1k/10k (ratio 0.9091, trip at SW = 2.20 V). R58/R63 = 5.1k/100k in both (ratio 0.9515, trip at SW = 2.10 V).
findings.proposal: Scale each divider up 10x, keeping the ratio exactly: R3 5.1k -> 51k with R4 33k -> 330k (ratio 330/381 = 0.8661, identical); R58 5.1k -> 51k with R63 100k -> 1M (ratio 1000/1051 = 0.9515, identical). All four are existing 0603 pads. If the built board carries the PCB values instead, R3 1k -> 10k and R4 10k -> 100k. Do NOT delete the dividers in favour of a direct-connect TPS3840DL23/DL21: the thresholds exist in the catalogue but TI's datasheet says non-standard voltages are 'sample upon request', and you would lose the RC filtering C10/C12 provide.
findings.benefit:
At VBATT = 2.4 V, with the schematic values: R3+R4 = 38.1k draws 63.0 uA = 151 uW; R58+R63 = 105.1k draws 22.8 uA = 55 uW. Total 85.8 uA = 206 uW straight off the battery. After 10x scaling: 6.3 uA + 2.3 uA = 8.6 uA = 21 uW. Saving 77.2 uA = 185 uW.
If the built board carries the PCB values, R3+R4 = 11k draws 218.2 uA = 524 uW and scaling to 10k/100k saves 196 uA = 471 uW; combined with R58/R63 the saving is 217 uA = 520 uW.
Bonus, not a cost: the RC corner improves. R58 x C12 (10 uF) goes from 51 ms to 510 ms and R3 x C10 (0.1 uF) from 0.51 ms to 5.1 ms, so both battery-gauge supervisors become an order of magnitude less likely to nuisance-trip on a speaker or backlight load transient.
Threshold error introduced: the supervisor's own IVDD flows through the top resistor. At 51k that is 300 nA x 51k = 15 mV typical (36 mV at the 700 nA max), which referred back to SW through the 0.8661 divider is 18 mV typical / 41 mV max — 0.75% typ / 1.8% max on a 2.31 V trip point. For a two-stage battery indicator that is irrelevant; if it were a safety trip it would not be.
findings.risk: The trip point shifts up by the 18-41 mV computed above, so the green-to-red changeover happens a fraction earlier. 1M and 330k nodes are leakage-sensitive on a hand-soldered board (same cleanliness caveat as R65). If you use 1% parts the ratio is preserved exactly; using 5% parts for R4/R63 would shift the trip point by up to 5%, which is worse than the Iq error you are trying to keep small — specify 1%.
findings.verify_reason:
Every TPS3840 number is confirmed from TI SNVSB03E: IDD 300 nA typ / 700 nA max over −40 to 125 °C; VDD 1.5–10 V; VIT− accuracy ±1% typ / ±1.5% max; VHYS 75/100/125 mV for VIT− = 1.6–3.0 V; thresholds 1.6 V to 4.9 V in 0.1 V steps with 'Other voltages from Table 9-2 ... can be sample upon request'; tSTRT 100/220/350 µs; DL = open-drain active-low; SOT-23-5 DBV. So the caution against chasing a direct-connect DL21/DL23 is well founded.

Divider arithmetic reproduces exactly: R3+R4 = 38.1k → 63.0 µA → 151 µW; R58+R63 = 105.1k → 22.8 µA → 54.8 µW; total 85.8 µA = 206 µW; after 10x, 8.58 µA = 20.6 µW; saving 77.2 µA = 185 µW. Ratios preserved to 4 digits (330/381 = 0.86614, 1000/1051 = 0.95147). All four are existing 0603 pads — genuine drop-in. Trip points: U10 at 2.0/0.86614 = 2.309 V, U17 at 2.0/0.95147 = 2.102 V.

I also closed the finding's own open question about which values are built. Beyond the fork, I pulled MouseBiteLabs' released AGBM-01 rev 1.2 design-file ZIP and its AGBM-02 rev 1.1 files: AGBM-02 carries R3 = 5.1k, R4 = 33k in BOTH its schematic and its PCB. The AGBM-01 schematic matches AGBM-02; only the AGBM-01 PCB Value fields are stale. So 5.1k/33k is intended, the trip is 2.31 V, and 185 µW is the saving.

The RC-filtering 'bonus' is real but smaller than stated: the corner is set by (R_top||R_bot)·C, so R58/R63 with C12 goes from 48.5 ms to 485 ms (not 51→510 ms) and R3/R4 with C10 from 0.44 ms to 4.4 ms (not 0.51→5.1 ms). At 0.185 mW this is 0.11% of the 170 mW idle — worth doing because it costs nothing, but it is rounding error against the LED.
findings.correction: Saving stands at 0.185 mW (77.2 µA at 2.4 V) for the R3/R4 + R58/R63 10x scaling. Three corrections: (1) the alternate 'if the board carries the PCB values' branch worth 0.52 mW is moot — I established that 5.1k/33k is the intended value (see below), so 0.185 mW is the number; (2) the threshold error the finding computes is overstated: IVDD sees R_top||R_bot, not R_top, so at 51k/330k it is 300 nA × 44.1k = 13 mV typ / 31 mV max at the divider node = 15 mV typ / 36 mV max referred to SW, not 18/41 mV — conservative direction; (3) NEW RISK on the R58/R63 half only: C12 is a 10 µF MLCC sitting directly across R63, and at R63 = 1 M the capacitor's own insulation resistance becomes a parallel leg of the divider. MLCC class-II insulation resistance is conventionally spec'd as the lesser of a fixed value or a CR product, which at 10 µF can land in the tens of megohms — a 50 MΩ leakage across a 1 M leg shifts the ratio ~2% and the trip point ~40 mV, swamping the Iq error the finding was careful about. I did NOT fetch a specific C12 part datasheet (the BOM gives only '10u / C_0603_1608Metric_Boxed_2'), so treat this as an unverified caution, not a number: either specify a low-leakage part, or scale R58/R63 only 5x, or leave that pair alone and take the R3/R4 half (151 µW → 15 µW, saving 136 µW) which uses C10 = 0.1 µF where the same effect is ~100x weaker.

findings.title: R11 = 1k makes the post-brownout latched-off state draw 2.87 mA (6.9 mW) forever until the switch is cycled; 10k plus the other changes cuts it to 0.33 mA
findings.current_part: R11 = 1k from SW to /EN, R24 = 100k from /EN to GND. /EN drives U5 pin 12 (~SHDN2), Q10 pin 3 (G2) and Q10 pin 5 (S1), and is pulled down by U3's open-drain RESET output. U3 = TPS3840DL20, open-drain active-low output requiring an external pull-up, IVDD 300 nA typ / 700 nA max (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3840.pdf). When VFILT falls below 2.0 V, U3 asserts RESET, /EN goes low, Q10A (G = Q10A-G held at ~SW by Q3, S = /EN now at 0) turns on and pulls ~MR low, which latches U3 asserted. The board then sits in that state indefinitely with SW1 still closed.
findings.proposal: Change R11 from 1k to 10k and R24 from 100k to 1M (existing 0603 pads, ratio preserved so the /EN high level is unchanged at 0.990 x SW).
findings.benefit:
Run-state saving is small: 2.4 V / 101k = 23.76 uA today versus 2.4 V / 1.01M = 2.38 uA, i.e. 21.4 uA = 51 uW.
The real number is the latched-off state. Today: R11 sinks 2.4 V / 1k = 2.40 mA into U3's open drain, plus the latch bias 387 uA (Q3 stays on — the latch holds through Q1/Q3/R16, it does not need Q10B), plus R12 23.5 uA, plus the two supervisor dividers 85.8 uA = 2.873 mA = 6.89 mW, drawn continuously from an already-flat pack until the user notices and moves SW1. With R11 = 10k plus the R15/R16 and divider changes above: 240 uA + 57.5 uA + 23.5 uA + 8.6 uA = 330 uA = 0.79 mW — an 8.7x reduction.
10k is still a strong pull-up here: the only DC loads on /EN are the LTC3527 ~SHDN2 input, Q10 pin 3's gate (100 nA max gate-body leakage per the NDC7002N datasheet -> 1 mV across 10k) and R24; and U3's open drain sinks 240 uA trivially.
findings.risk: The /EN rise time on power-up goes from ~20 ns to ~200 ns against a few tens of pF — irrelevant against the TPS3840's 220 us typical / 350 us maximum start-up delay. I could not fetch the LTC3527 datasheet, so I have NOT verified its ~SHDN2 input leakage or VIH; if that pin had, say, 1 uA of input leakage, a 10k pull-up would still only drop 10 mV, so the conclusion is robust, but the 1M R24 assumes the pin's leakage is well under a microamp. Verify against the LTC3527 datasheet before committing R24 = 1M; R11 = 10k with R24 left at 100k is the risk-free half of the change (/EN = 0.909 x SW, still far above any plausible VIH) and captures most of the latched-off benefit.
findings.verify_reason:
Netlist confirms /EN = {R11 1k from SW, R24 100k to GND, U3 pin1 RESET, U5 pin12 ~SHDN2, Q10 pin3 G2, Q10 pin5 S1, TP24}, and /~MR = {Q10 pin6 D1, U3 pin4 ~MR, TP17} with no external pull-up — so the latch mechanism the finding describes is exactly as built.

I closed the finding's declared open item, which was its biggest weakness. I fetched the LTC3527 datasheet (35271fc): SHDN1,2 Input High Voltage 0.88 V, Input Low Voltage 0.35 V, SHDN1,2 Input Current 1 µA typ / 2 µA MAX at VSHDN = 3.3 V. This is a real DC current, not 'well under a microamp' by assumption — but it is small enough that the proposal survives. With R11 = 10k and R24 = 1 M, solving (SW − V)/10k = V/1M + 2 µA gives V = 2.356 V at SW = 2.4 V and V = 1.762 V at SW = 1.8 V, both far above the 0.88 V VIH. R24 = 1 M is safe; the finding's own hedge is unnecessary. Same datasheet gives VFB = 1.176/1.20/1.224 V, which fixes VOUT5 = 5.014 V and VOUT3 = 3.336 V for every other calculation in this review.

Run-state arithmetic verified: 2.4/101k = 23.76 µA versus 2.4/1.01M = 2.38 µA, saving 21.4 µA = 51 µW. The rest of the finding's engineering is sound — TPS3840DL RESET recommended current is 0 to ±5 mA so 240 µA is trivial, NDC7002N gate-body leakage is 100 nA max giving 1 mV across 10k, and the rise-time argument against the 220 µs/350 µs tSTRT is comfortable. 51 µW is 0.03% of idle: the run-state benefit is rounding error and the finding says so. The latched-off benefit is the real point and it survives at 6.30 mW → 0.78 mW.
findings.correction: Run-state saving of 51 µW is correct and verified. The headline latched-off figure is overstated by ~9% through two errors: (a) the 387 µA latch-bias total already CONTAINS R12's 23.5 µA (it is line-itemised inside the brownout-latch-bias finding's own sum), and the finding then adds R12 again — a double count; (b) it assumes the full 2.4 V across R11, but the TPS3840DL's open-drain VOL is spec'd ≤200 mV at 2 mA sink and R11 = 1k sinks ~2.2 mA, so R11 carries (2.4 − 0.25)/1k = 2.15 mA, not 2.40 mA. Corrected latched-off drain = 2.15 mA (R11) + 0.389 mA (latch incl. R12) + 0.086 mA (the two supervisor dividers) = 2.62 mA = 6.30 mW, not 2.873 mA / 6.89 mW. Corrected post-change figure ≈ 0.237 + 0.081 + 0.0086 = 0.327 mA = 0.78 mW. Improvement factor 8.0x, not 8.7x. Direction and conclusion unchanged.

findings.title: R3, R4 and R64 have different values in the schematic and in the PCB file — the low-battery trip point and the blink rate depend on which one you build
findings.current_part: Extracted directly from the KiCad files in this repo. Schematic (agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch): R3 = 5.1k, R4 = 33k, R64 = 200k. PCB (both agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_pcb and the fork x/agbm-01-ram-desalvage/AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus.kicad_pcb): R3 = 1k, R4 = 10k, R64 = 100k. This is the same class of defect as the already-known F1/PTC1 disagreement (schematic F0805B2R00FSTR / 0805L075SLYR versus PCB Value '0467001.NR' on both).
findings.proposal: Reconcile the two. The schematic is normally the source of truth in KiCad and the PCB Value fields look stale (they were never re-synced after a schematic value change), so I would take 5.1k/33k/200k as intended — but that is an inference, not something the files prove. Whichever you pick, run 'Update PCB from Schematic' with value updating enabled so the two agree, and correct the F1/PTC1 Value fields at the same time.
findings.benefit: Not an efficiency finding, but the numbers matter. R3/R4 sets U10's low-battery trip: 5.1k/33k gives a divider ratio of 33/38.1 = 0.8661, so the TPS3840DL20's 2.0 V threshold corresponds to VBATT = 2.31 V; 1k/10k gives 10/11 = 0.9091 and VBATT = 2.20 V. That is a 110 mV difference in where the power LED changes from green to red. The standing current differs too: 2.4/38.1k = 63.0 uA (151 uW) versus 2.4/11k = 218.2 uA (524 uW) — a 3.5x difference in a permanently-on battery load, which is why this matters to the efficiency inventory as well as to correctness. R64 with C44 1 uF sets the MIC1553 astable rate; for a 50% one-resistor-one-capacitor astable f ~ 1/(1.386 x R x C), giving 3.6 Hz at 200k and 7.2 Hz at 100k — the low-battery LED blinks at twice the rate depending on which value is fitted.
findings.risk: Nothing breaks either way — both value sets produce a working board. The risk is purely that a builder reading the PCB (or a fab reading a PCB-derived BOM) gets a different battery-warning threshold and blink rate from someone reading the schematic, and neither can tell they disagree. Cost to fix: zero.
findings.verify_reason:
Verified in the fork AND — more importantly — upstream. I parsed the Value properties out of both files in three places: the fork's PCB, the local agbm01 copy, and MouseBiteLabs' own released 'AGBM-01_Design Files.zip' pulled from github.com/MouseBiteLabs/Game-Boy-Enhance. In all of them, schematic R3 = 5.1k / R4 = 33k / R64 = 200k while the PCB carries R3 = 1k / R4 = 10k / R64 = 100k, and schematic F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR / PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR while both PCB Value fields read '0467001.NR'. So this is an upstream defect, not an artefact of the fork.

I then resolved which set is intended — something the finding could only infer. AGBM-02 rev 1.1 (the successor board, whose schematic and PCB AGREE with each other) uses R3 = 5.1k, R4 = 33k, R64 = 200k. That makes the AGBM-01 schematic the source of truth and the PCB Value fields stale, exactly as the finding guessed. Additional supporting evidence of a family-wide stale-Value problem: AGBM-11 rev 1.3 has its own set of disagreements (sch R3 = 2.49k vs pcb 1k, sch R58 = 470 vs pcb 1k, sch R63 = 15k vs pcb 30k).

Consequence arithmetic checks out: 33/38.1 = 0.86614 → trip at 2.309 V versus 10/11 = 0.90909 → 2.200 V, a 109 mV difference; standing current 63.0 µA (151 µW) versus 218.2 µA (524 µW), a 3.46x difference. The R64 blink-rate claim is directionally certain (200k versus 100k is exactly 2:1 in frequency) but I could NOT verify the 1.386 constant for this part: the MIC1553 datasheet supplies a 'k Factors Times RC' figure rather than a closed-form expression, and I could not read numeric values off it. Treat 3.6 Hz / 7.2 Hz as nominal and the 2:1 ratio as certain. Cost to fix is zero and there is no downside — this is the cleanest item in the set.

findings.title: Q10A must latch the brownout with only VBATT as its gate drive, but the NDC7002N's threshold is spec'd up to 2.5 V — a worst-case part will not latch
findings.current_part: NDC7002N dual N-channel, SuperSOT-6 / TSOT-23-6 (CASE 419BL): VGS(th) 1.0 V min / 1.9 V typ / 2.5 V max at VDS = VGS, ID = 250 uA; RDS(on) 1.7 ohm typ / 2 ohm max at VGS = 10 V, and 1.6 ohm typ / 4 ohm max at VGS = 4.5 V — there is NO on-resistance specification below VGS = 4.5 V (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/ndc7002n-d.pdf). Pin assignment 1=G1, 2=S2, 3=G2, 4=D2, 5=S1, 6=D1, confirmed against the datasheet pin-assignment graphic and the KiCad symbol name Q_Dual_NMOS_G1S2G2D2S1D1.
findings.proposal: Replace Q10 (and optionally Q2, Q5, Q7, Q9) with onsemi FDC6301N — identical SuperSOT-6 / TSOT-23-6 CASE 419BL package, and I verified the pin-assignment graphic is byte-identically placed in both datasheets (labels G1/S2/G2/D1/D2/S1 at the same page coordinates), so the pinout is the same. FDC6301N: VGS(th) 0.65 V min / 0.85 V typ / 1.5 V max; RDS(on) 3.8 ohm typ / 5 ohm max at VGS = 2.7 V and 3.1 ohm typ / 4 ohm max at VGS = 4.5 V; 25 V, 0.22 A continuous; VGSS rated -0.5 to +8 V (https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/fdc6301n-d.pdf). Drop-in on the existing TSOT-23-6 land pattern.
findings.benefit:
Not a power saving — a reliability one. Q10A's job is to pull ~MR low when U3 asserts, latching the board off after a brownout. Its gate sits at Q10A-G ~ SW (held up by Q3) and its SOURCE is /EN, which is what goes to 0 V at the moment of the trip. So its turn-on VGS equals VBATT at the instant of the brownout — and the brownout happens when VFILT falls below the TPS3840DL20's 2.0 V threshold, i.e. VBATT ~ 2.0-2.1 V. Against a spec'd VGS(th) max of 2.5 V, a worst-case NDC7002N never turns on there and the latch never fires: U3 releases RESET as soon as the battery recovers, the LTC3527 restarts, the load pulls the pack down again, and the console can chatter on/off instead of staying down. With FDC6301N (1.5 V max threshold) there is at least 0.5 V of overdrive at the worst-case operating point.
Secondary: Q2 and Q7 are driven from U16's outputs on the 3.34 V VDD3 rail, so their VGS is 3.34 V — also inside the NDC7002N's 2.5 V max threshold band with only 0.84 V of overdrive, and in a region where the datasheet gives no RDS(on) number at all. Those FETs only pull logic lines, so a high on-resistance is tolerable, but they are equally unspecified.
findings.risk: FDC6301N is a much smaller die: 25 V / 0.22 A continuous versus 50 V / 0.51 A, and its gate rating is -0.5 to +8 V rather than +/-20 V. Every use on this board is at or below 5.0 V and at or below ~1 mA (the largest is Q9A carrying the 0.93 mA LED current, where 5 ohm gives a 5 mV drop), so both derations are irrelevant here — but if you reuse the same part elsewhere check that. Its higher RDS(on) (5 ohm max at 2.7 V versus NDC7002N's 2 ohm at 10 V) is a non-issue for the same reason. I have NOT observed the chatter failure mode on hardware; this is a datasheet-margin argument, so treat it as 'the spec does not guarantee it works', not 'it is broken'. Typical parts (1.9 V) do latch at 2.0-2.4 V.
findings.verify_reason:
All the datasheet numbers are exact. NDC7002N (onsemi, Dec 2021 Rev 2): VGS(th) 1.0 min / 1.9 typ / 2.5 max at VDS = VGS, ID = 250 µA; RDS(on) 1.7 typ / 2 max Ω at VGS = 10 V and 1.6 typ / 4 max Ω at VGS = 4.5 V — and confirmed, there is NO on-resistance specification below VGS = 4.5 V; TSOT23 6-Lead SUPERSOT-6 CASE 419BL. FDC6301N (onsemi, May 2023 Rev 5): VGS(th) 0.65 / 0.85 / 1.5 V at VDS = VGS, ID = 250 µA; RDS(on) 3.8 typ / 5 max Ω at VGS = 2.7 V and 3.1 typ / 4 max Ω at VGS = 4.5 V; 25 V, 0.22 A continuous / 0.5 A pulsed; VGSS −0.5 to +8 V; TSOT23 6-Lead SUPERSOT-6 CASE 419BL. Same case designation, and I checked the pin-assignment graphics rather than taking the finding's word: in both PDFs the pin numbers sit in the same two columns with the same top-to-bottom order (x≈500: 1,2,3; x≈408: 6,5,4) and the G2/D1/D2/S1 labels appear at identical page coordinates. Digi-Key lists FDC6301N as Active, 37,403 in stock, $0.64/1 — a real, buyable, drop-in part on the existing TSOT-23-6 land.

The failure mode is real and WORSE than the finding argues. I traced the load: /~MR has no external pull-up (netlist shows only Q10 pin 6 and U3 pin 4), and the TPS3840's internal manual-reset pull-up is 100 kΩ with VMR_L = 600 mV max. So Q10A must sink roughly (2.0 − 0.6)/100k ≈ 14 µA at VDS = 0.6 V with VGS ≈ 1.8 V. A worst-case 2.5 V-threshold NDC7002N is ~0.7 V below threshold there — orders of magnitude short of 14 µA. Even a TYPICAL 1.9 V part sits essentially at threshold with no overdrive, so the finding's reassurance that 'typical parts do latch' is itself marginal. Q10B has the same problem in the run state (VGS = 0.990 × SW = 2.38 V at a fresh pack), which means a worst-case part may never arm the latch at all. This is a datasheet-margin argument, not an observed failure, and the finding is honest about that; but the margin is genuinely absent.

The secondary Q2/Q7 observation is verified: U16 pins 1/4/10/13 drive Net-(Q2A-G), Net-(Q2B-G), Net-(Q7A-G), Net-(Q7B-G) with all four sources at GND, so VGS = VDD3 = 3.34 V against a 2.5 V max threshold in a region with no RDS(on) spec. Correct, and tolerable since those FETs only pull logic lines.
findings.correction: The direction, the part choice and the drop-in claim all survive verification, but two things are wrong. (1) The '0.5 V of overdrive' is optimistic. Q10A's source is /EN, which at the trip is pulled to the TPS3840DL's VOL — spec'd ≤200 mV at 2 mA sink, and R11 = 1k makes the sink current ~2.2 mA — so VGS ≈ VBATT − 0.2 ≈ 1.8–1.9 V, not 2.0–2.1 V. Against the FDC6301N's 1.5 V max VGS(th) that is 0.3–0.4 V of overdrive, not 0.5 V. (2) An abs-max violation the finding missed: the FDC6301N's VGSS is rated −0.5 V to +8 V (asymmetric), where the NDC7002N is 20 V. Q10A's gate-source goes NEGATIVE by up to −SW during the power-on window in which U3 releases /EN (which rises through R11 in nanoseconds) before Q3 has pulled Q10A-G up through the R15/R16 loop, because R17 holds Q10A-G at 0 V until then. The FDC6301N has an internal gate-source zener so it clamps rather than fails, but the clamp current is set by R11 (up to ~1.7 mA at 1k) and raising R15/R16 to 100k as the brownout-latch-bias finding proposes lengthens that window roughly 10x. Take R11 = 10k (which the en-pullup finding wants anyway) if you make both changes, or add a series gate resistor.

findings.title: The three TPS22917 load switches cost 13-230 uW of conduction loss and 0.5 uA each — including the one carrying the ClockxControl — so no lower-Rds part is worth the swap
findings.current_part: TPS22917DBV, TSOT-23-6 (SOT-23 6-pin DBV), 1 V to 5.5 V, 2 A max continuous. On-resistance at IOUT = 200 mA: 80 mohm typ / 100 mohm max at VIN = 5 V (25 C), 90 mohm typ / 110 mohm max at VIN = 3.6 V (25 C, rising to 140 mohm max at 85 C), 120 mohm typ at 1.8 V. Quiescent current in the ON state 0.5 uA typ / 1.0 uA max (-40 to +85 C); shutdown 10 nA typ. ON pin VIH 1.0 V min, VIL 0.35 V max; ON-pin leakage +/-10 nA when enabled, with a 750 kohm smart pulldown only while VON <= VIL (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps22917.pdf).
findings.proposal: Leave all three as-is. I deliberately do not name a lower-Rds alternative, because the loss is not material and I would have to assert unverified numbers to do so.
findings.benefit:
U18 carries the whole VDD3 rail including the ClockxControl's 12 mA (the module's V+ lands on P1 pad S1 = VDD3, confirmed from the netlist). At VIN = VOUT3 = 3.34 V, RDS(on) is ~92 mohm typ (interpolating the 3.6 V figure). I2R at the plausible load range: 12 mA -> 1.10 mV drop, 13 uW; 30 mA -> 2.76 mV, 83 uW; 50 mA -> 4.60 mV, 230 uW; even 100 mA -> 9.2 mV, 920 uW. So replacing U18 with a perfect 0 mohm short would save at most ~0.1-0.2 mW at a realistic VDD3 load, against a 170 mW idle and a 40 mW ClockxControl overhead — rounding error.
U11 carries VDD5 to the screen (FFC pin 34 VSHA) and cart pad S2, at VIN = 5.0 V and RDS(on) 80 mohm typ: 20 mA -> 1.60 mV, 32 uW; 50 mA -> 4.00 mV, 200 uW; 100 mA -> 8.00 mV, 800 uW. Even bounding VDD5 at 100 mA (which would be 500 mW at 5 V — more than a third of the console's 1175 mW maximum), the switch loss is under 1 mW.
Quiescent side: 3 x 0.5 uA typ. U11 and U14's 5 V rail contribution is 2.5 uW; U12 and U18 on 3.34 V contribute 1.7 uW each. Total across all three: about 6 uW. Nothing.
The enable logic is also correct and worth confirming for the ClockxControl: U18's ON pin is /PG_2V5, which is U8's (the VDD2 LDO's) open-drain PGOOD pulled up by R8 100k to VDD2 = 2.5 V. TPS22917 VIH is 1.0 V min, so 2.5 V is comfortable, and the 750 kohm smart pulldown disconnects once VON exceeds VIH (2.5 x 750/850 = 2.21 V at the crossover, well above 1.0 V). Net effect: the ClockxControl only receives power after the CPU core rail VDD2 is good — correct sequencing for a module that drives the CPU's XIN.
findings.risk: None — this is a recommendation to change nothing. The one caveat is that I could not measure VDD3 or VDD5 current, so the loss figures are a bounded range rather than a single number; but even the top of the range (100 mA) does not make either switch worth replacing.
findings.verify_reason:
I extracted the full TPS22917 datasheet (TI SLVSDW8B) and every number matches. RON at IOUT = 200 mA: VIN = 5 V → 80 typ / 100 max mΩ at 25 °C (120 at 85 °C, 140 at 125 °C); VIN = 3.6 V → 90 typ / 110 max (140 at 85 °C, 160 at 125 °C); VIN = 1.8 V → 120 typ / 150 max. IQ enabled 0.5 µA typ / 1.0 µA max over −40 to +85 °C (1.2 µA to 125 °C); ISD 10 nA typ. ON pin: VIH 1.0 V min, VIL 0.35 V max, ION ±10 nA when enabled, RPD 750 kΩ typ while VON ≤ VIL. Package SOT-23 (6) DBV, 2.90 × 1.60 mm, matching the BOM's TSOT-23-6. 1 V–5.5 V, 2 A.

I²R reproduces: at VIN = 3.34 V the interpolated RON is ~94 mΩ, so 12 mA → 13.5 µW, 30 mA → 85 µW, 50 mA → 235 µW, 100 mA → 940 µW. At 5 V and 80 mΩ: 20 mA → 32 µW, 50 mA → 200 µW, 100 mA → 800 µW. Quiescent total across the three ≈ 5.8 µW. The conclusion — that a perfect 0 mΩ short saves at most a few hundred µW against a 170 mW idle and a 40–60 mA overclock adder — is correct, and the refusal to name a lower-RON alternative rather than assert unverified numbers is exactly right.

Sequencing verified from the netlist, not assumed: P1 pad S1 is on VDD3 (so the ClockxControl's V+ really does sit behind U18); U18 pin 3 ON = /PG_2V5 = U8 pin 4, U8 being the NCV8164 2.5 V LDO whose EN (pin 3) is /PG_3V3 = LTC3527 PGOOD2; R8 100k pulls /PG_2V5 to VDD2. So the module is powered only after the CPU core rail is good. One refinement: /PG_2V5 also feeds U5 pin 1 ~SHDN1, whose input current I verified as 1 µA typ / 2 µA max, so R8 drops ~0.2 V and the node sits at ~2.3 V rather than a clean 2.5 V — still far above the TPS22917's 1.0 V VIH and the LTC3527's 0.88 V, so the conclusion is unchanged. Trivial typo: 'U11 and U14's 5 V rail contribution is 2.5 uW' should read U11's. Verdict: leave them alone, 0 mW, correctly reported.

findings.title: None of the three TPS3840 supervisors is redundant — they have three different trip points and three different jobs — but the entire low-battery-blink branch is optional and worth 0.36 mW plus 12 parts
findings.current_part: All three are TPS3840DL20: open-drain active-low RESET, 2.0 V fixed threshold, 300 nA typ / 700 nA max IVDD, 100 mV typ hysteresis, 220 us typ / 350 us max start-up delay, SOT-23-5 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3840.pdf). Reading the schematic: U3's VDD is /VFILT (VBATT through D2, bypassed for DC by R9 100k, held up by C1 22u) and its RESET drives /EN (LTC3527 ~SHDN2) with the Q1/Q3/Q10 latch on ~MR — that is the power-fail shutdown and latch. U10's VDD is SW divided by R3/R4 (0.8661 -> trips at VBATT 2.31 V with the schematic values) and its RESET gates Q9A, which switches the power LED from green DL1 to red DL2. U17's VDD is SW divided by R58/R63 (0.9515 -> trips at VBATT 2.10 V) and its RESET gates Q5B, which releases the MIC1553's CS and starts the red LED blinking. Three thresholds, three functions.
findings.proposal: Keep all three if you want the two-stage battery gauge. If you do not, the second stage is cleanly severable: depopulate U17, R58, R63, C12, R65, R66, U14, C44, R64, Q5, R10 and DL2 (12 parts) and the board keeps its brownout latch and its green/red changeover. No PCB change needed — it is purely a DNP list.
findings.benefit:
Always-on cost of the second (blink) stage, at VBATT = 2.4 V: R58+R63 divider 22.8 uA = 55 uW off the battery; R65 through Q5B 50.0 uA at 5.0 V = 250 uW at VOUT5 = 313 uW at the battery at 80% boost efficiency; U17's own IVDD 300 nA = 0.7 uW; U14 in shutdown <1 uA at 5 V = <5 uW at the rail. Total about 0.37 mW, i.e. 0.22% of the 170 mW idle. Removing it entirely is worth 0.37 mW; applying the R58/R63 and R65 changes proposed elsewhere in this review instead is worth 0.33 mW while keeping the feature — so deletion buys almost nothing beyond board space and 12 fewer placements. Report as an option, not a recommendation.
I also confirmed the two indicator supervisors cannot be collapsed into one part: they need two distinct trip points (2.31 V and 2.10 V) and the TPS3840 is a fixed-threshold device, so consolidation would require a dual comparator plus a reference, which would draw more than 600 nA and use more board area.
findings.risk: Deleting the blink stage removes the only warning the user gets between 2.31 V and the hard cutoff, which on a 2xAA alkaline pack is the last chunk of usable capacity — you would go from a solid red warning to an abrupt latched shutdown with no escalation. On a board whose whole selling point is battery life, that is a real usability loss for 0.37 mW. My recommendation is to keep the feature and take the resistor changes instead.
findings.verify_reason:
The three-jobs claim is verified from the netlist, not from the finding's summary. U3: VDD = /VFILT (pin 2), RESET (pin 1) = /EN, ~MR (pin 4) = /~MR — power-fail shutdown with the Q1/Q3/Q10 latch, and because /VFILT is tied to VBATT through R9 100k in parallel with D2 and only U3's 300 nA IVDD flows there, U3 trips at VBATT ≈ 2.0 V undivided. U10: VDD = the R3/R4 node, RESET = Net-(Q9A-G) → gates Q9A → green DL1 / red DL2 changeover at 2.0/0.86614 = 2.309 V. U17: VDD = the R58/R63 node, RESET = Net-(Q5B-G) → gates Q5B → releases the MIC1553 CS and starts the blink at 2.0/0.95147 = 2.102 V. Three distinct trip points, three functions, no redundancy. TPS3840 is fixed-threshold (1.6–4.9 V in 0.1 V steps), so the observation that two indicator supervisors cannot be collapsed into one part is right.

Cost of the blink stage reproduces: R58+R63 = 105.1k → 22.8 µA = 54.8 µW off the battery; R65 = 50 µA at VOUT5 = 251 µW → ~314 µW at the battery at 80%; U17's IVDD 300 nA = 0.7 µW; U14 in shutdown <1 µA at 5 V = <5 µW at the rail. Total ≈ 0.37 mW = 0.22% of idle. I also checked the two loads it does NOT count and confirmed they are genuinely zero in the battery-OK state: R66 100k carries only Q5B's gate leakage (100 nA max) plus the TPS3840's 90 nA max open-drain leakage, and R10 20k carries nothing because /DL2A floats at 5 V with both Q5A (MIC1553 OUT forced low by CS reset, per datasheet §4.3) and Q9B (gate = /D1A held at ~3 mV by Q9A) off.

The one uncited assertion is that a consolidated dual-comparator-plus-reference 'would draw more than 600 nA' — I did not verify that and neither did the finding, but it sits inside a change-nothing recommendation so it costs nothing. The recommendation itself — keep the feature, take the resistor changes instead (0.33 mW of the 0.37 mW without losing the warning) — is the right call and honestly sized.

findings.title: U16 SN74HC02 is a defensible choice at 3.34 V and should be left alone: SN74LVC02A is a verified pin-identical drop-in but is worse on the slow button edges, and the Schmitt SN74HC7002 is NOT pin-compatible
findings.current_part:
U16 = SN74HC02PWR, quad 2-input NOR, TSSOP-14 (PW), 5.00 x 4.40 mm. Verified pinout: 1Y=1, 1A=2, 1B=3, 2Y=4, 2A=5, 2B=6, GND=7, 3A=8, 3B=9, 3Y=10, 4A=11, 4B=12, 4Y=13, VCC=14 — which matches the KiCad 74xx:74HC02 symbol and the board netlist exactly (outputs on 1/4/10/13 driving Q2A-G, Q2B-G, Q7A-G, Q7B-G; inputs on 2/5/9/12 from TP6/TP1/TP0/TP2 and on 3/6/8/11 all tied to /CPU/LRST). Operating range 2 V to 6 V; VIH spec'd only at VCC = 2 V (1.5 V), 4.5 V (3.15 V) and 6 V (4.2 V), i.e. 0.7 x VCC, so ~2.34 V at the 3.34 V VDD3 rail; ICC 2 uA typ / 20 uA max at VCC = 6 V; input transition rise/fall time tt max 500 ns at VCC = 4.5 V (1000 ns at 2 V) (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74hc02.pdf).
Function on this board, read from the CPU sheet: U15 (SN74LVC1G332, 3-input OR) ORs TP3/TP8/TP9 (Start, R, L) to produce /CPU/LRST, which goes low only when all three are pressed; U16's four NOR gates then each combine /CPU/LRST with one more button — TP6 (D-pad Up) -> Q2A -> JP1-A (reset, but JP1 is a default-open jumper so this does nothing as shipped), TP1 (B) -> Q2B -> Display ZB, TP0 (A) -> Q7A -> Display ZA, TP2 (Select) -> Q7B -> TP12 (test point only, unused). It is the L+R+Start button-combo decoder for the IPS screen's mode-toggle lines.
findings.proposal: Leave U16 as SN74HC02PWR. Recording the two swaps a reviewer would naturally reach for, and why each fails: (a) SN74LVC02APWR IS a genuine pin-for-pin drop-in — I verified its Pin Functions table gives 1Y=1, 1A=2, 1B=3 in the PW package, identical to HC02 — with VIH fixed at 2.0 V for VCC 2.7-3.6 V and ICC 10 uA max at 25 C (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74lvc02a.pdf). But its input transition-rate requirement is far tighter than HC's, so on this board it is a downgrade, not an upgrade. (b) SN74HC7002PW is the quad 2-input NOR with Schmitt-trigger inputs in the same TSSOP-14 body — but its pinout is 1A=1, 1B=2, 1Y=3, 2A=4, 2B=5, 2Y=6, GND=7, 3Y=8, 3A=9, 3B=10, 4Y=11, 4A=12, 4B=13, VCC=14 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74hc7002.pdf). That is the 7400-style arrangement, not the 7402-style one; every input and output moves. Fitting it needs a PCB revision.
findings.benefit:
There is no power to be had here, and I want to be explicit about that: HC02 draws 2 uA typ / 20 uA max, which at 3.34 V is 6.7 uW typ / 67 uW max. LVC02A is 10 uA max at 25 C but 40 uA max over the -40 to +125 C range — so the swap is not even reliably a saving. The value would be purely in noise margin (VIH 2.0 V fixed versus 0.7 x VCC = 2.34 V) and speed, neither of which this circuit needs: the inputs come from button lines that idle at the full VDD3 rail through the CPU's internal pull-ups, and from U15's rail-to-rail LVC output. Benefit is 0 mW.
The one thing that WOULD be a real upgrade — Schmitt inputs, for the reason in the slow-edge finding below — is unavailable without moving pins.
findings.risk: The risk here is the trap, not the change: someone reading 'HC part on a 3.3 V rail, swap it for LVC/AUP' would make the slow-edge behaviour worse, and someone reading 'use the Schmitt version' would order SN74HC7002PW, fit it to the existing footprint, and get four gates wired output-to-output against U15's output on /CPU/LRST. I verified both pinouts from the TI datasheets specifically because that is the failure this review is supposed to catch.
findings.verify_reason:
Both load-bearing pinouts verified from the TI Pin Functions tables, which is exactly the check this finding exists to make. SN74HC02 (SCLS076G) D/DB/N/NS/PW: 1Y=1, 1A=2, 1B=3, 2Y=4, 2A=5, 2B=6, GND=7, 3A=8, 3B=9, 3Y=10, 4A=11, 4B=12, 4Y=13, VCC=14. SN74HC7002 (SCLS033G) functional pinout: 1A=1, 1B=2, 1Y=3, 2A=4, 2B=5, 2Y=6, GND=7, 3Y=8, 3A=9, 3B=10, 4Y=11, 4A=12, 4B=13, VCC=14 — the 7400-style arrangement, confirmed different from the 7402 in every input and output. Fitting an HC7002 to the existing pads really would tie four gate outputs against U15's output on /CPU/LRST. The warning is correct and is the most useful thing in this finding. SN74LVC02A (SCAS280T) PW: 1Y=1, 1A=2, 1B=3 ... VCC=14 — genuinely pin-identical to HC02, as claimed.

Other numbers confirmed: HC02 operating 2–6 V, VIH 1.5 V @2 V / 3.15 V @4.5 V / 4.2 V @6 V, ICC 2 µA typ / 20 µA max at 6 V, tt max 1000/500/400 ns at 2/4.5/6 V, PW TSSOP-14 5.00 × 4.40 mm (matching the BOM footprint TSSOP-14_4.4x5mm_P0.65mm), and HC7002 PW is the same 5.00 × 4.40 mm body. LVC02A VIH = 2.0 V for VCC 2.7–3.6 V, ICC 1 typ / 10 max µA at 25 °C, 10 max at −40 to 85 °C and 40 max at −40 to 125 °C — all exactly as stated, including the point that the swap is not reliably a power saving.

U16's function verified pad by pad from the netlist: pin1(1Y)→Q2A-G, pin2(1A)→TP6, pin3(1B)→LRST, pin4(2Y)→Q2B-G, pin5(2A)→TP1, pin6(2B)→LRST, pin7 GND, pin8(3A)→LRST, pin9(3B)→TP0, pin10(3Y)→Q7A-G, pin11(4A)→LRST, pin12(4B)→TP2, pin13(4Y)→Q7B-G, pin14 VCC→VDD3. U15 is pin1=TP3, pin3=TP8, pin6=TP9, pin4=LRST, and its datasheet function table confirms Y is low only when all three inputs are low. Q2 pin6(D1)=JP1-A, Q2 pin4(D2)=Display/ZB, Q7 pin6(D1)=Display/ZA, Q7 pin4(D2)=Q7B-D→R68/TP12. The finding's circuit description is right in every particular. 0 mW is correct.
findings.correction: The recommendation (leave U16 as SN74HC02PWR) and both pinout warnings survive intact and are the valuable part of this finding. One supporting claim does not: 'its [SN74LVC02A's] input transition-rate requirement is far tighter than HC's' is NOT in the datasheet the finding cites. I extracted SCAS280T (Dec 2024) in full — its Recommended Operating Conditions table for the SN74LVC02A lists VCC, VIH, VIL, VI, VO, IOH and IOL and contains no Δt/Δv row at all; the word 'transition' occurs exactly once in the whole document, in a switching-test note. The general LVC-family behaviour is plausible (the SN74LVC1G332 on the same board does spec 10 ns/V max at 3.3 V), but for THIS part it is unverified, so it should not be offered as the reason not to swap. The sufficient reasons — no power to be had, and HC's 0.7 × VCC = 2.34 V VIH is already comfortable against rail-to-rail drivers — stand on their own.

findings.title: The 0.01 uF debounce caps on Start/Select/Up/L/R violate both U15's and U16's input transition-rate specifications by orders of magnitude
findings.current_part: C77 (0.01u on TP3/Start), C78 (0.01u on TP2/Select), C62 (0.01u on TP6/Up), C63 (0.01u on TP8/R), C64 (0.01u on TP9/L), each to GND, with the pull-up supplied by the salvaged AGB CPU's internal pull-up on P0-P9. Note TP0 (A) and TP1 (B) have no such capacitor. Non-Schmitt CMOS inputs sit on those nets: U15 = SN74LVC1G332, whose Recommended Operating Conditions give an input transition rise-or-fall rate dt/dv of 10 ns/V maximum at VCC = 3.3 V +/- 0.3 V, ICC 10 uA max, and a delta-ICC of 500 uA max with one input at VCC - 0.6 V (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74lvc1g332.pdf). U16 = SN74HC02, tt max 500 ns at VCC = 4.5 V and 1000 ns at 2 V (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74hc02.pdf).
findings.proposal: No drop-in fix exists. If a board revision happens: move U16 to SN74HC7002PW (Schmitt NOR, same TSSOP-14 body, different pinout — see the u16-hc02-family-choice finding) and reduce C62/C63/C64/C77/C78 to the smallest value that still debounces the tactile switches, or add a Schmitt buffer ahead of U15. Until then, the correct action is to know about it, not to change parts.
findings.benefit: No power benefit — the crowbar energy is negligible (delta-ICC 500 uA x 3.34 V x ~500 us per button event is about 0.8 uJ, which is nothing). The benefit is behavioural. On button release the node is charged by the CPU's internal pull-up through 0.01 uF; GBA key pull-ups are commonly reported in the tens of kohm but I could NOT verify a value — the AGB CPU is undocumented and salvaged — so treat the RC as an estimate: 0.01 uF x ~50 kohm gives a ~500 us rise, i.e. roughly 150,000 ns/V through the threshold region against U15's 10 ns/V limit (15,000x over) and against U16's 500 ns tt limit (1,000x over). The consequence of a non-Schmitt CMOS input crossing its threshold that slowly is output chatter. Here that means /CPU/LRST can glitch, and since every U16 gate takes /CPU/LRST as one input, a glitch can produce a spurious pulse on Display ZA or ZB — an unintended IPS screen mode change. The exposure is bounded: /CPU/LRST only goes low when L+R+Start are all held, so glitching can only occur while the user is already invoking the combo, and Q2A's path to reset is disarmed anyway because JP1 ships open.
findings.risk: I have not observed this on hardware and the pull-up value is genuinely unverifiable from the available documentation, so the magnitude of the RC is an estimate — that is why this is at medium confidence. It is also possible the AGB CPU's key inputs are stronger than assumed, which would shorten the edge. What is NOT in doubt is that the specs are violated: 0.01 uF on a passively pulled-up node cannot produce a 33 ns or 500 ns edge under any plausible pull-up. Cost of doing nothing is low; cost of the fix is a PCB revision.
findings.verify_reason:
The two specs are verified. SN74LVC1G332 (TI SCES489E) Recommended Operating Conditions: Δt/Δv input transition rise or fall rate 10 ns/V max at VCC = 3.3 V ± 0.3 V; ICC 10 µA max; ΔICC 500 µA max with one input at VCC − 0.6 V. SN74HC02 (SCLS076G): tt input transition rise and fall time max 1000 ns at VCC = 2 V, 500 ns at 4.5 V, 400 ns at 6 V. The capacitor placement is verified from the BOM: C77 on /CPU/TP3, C63 on /CPU/TP8, C64 on /CPU/TP9 — all three of U15's inputs — and C62 on /CPU/TP6, C78 on /CPU/TP2 into U16, with TP0 and TP1 correctly noted as having no capacitor. The crowbar-energy dismissal is right: 500 µA × 3.34 V × ~500 µs is sub-microjoule, so 0 mW is honest.

The consequence chain is plausible but unobserved, and the finding says so: the AGB CPU's internal pull-up value is genuinely unverifiable from public documentation, so the RC magnitude is an estimate. The exposure bound the finding gives is also correct and worth keeping — /CPU/LRST only leaves the rail when all three of Start/R/L are already held (verified from U15's OR function table and the netlist), and Q2A's path to reset is disarmed because JP1 is Jumper_2_Open. Direction right, headline overstated.
findings.correction: The spec numbers are right and the specs really are violated, but the scope and the framing are wrong in two ways. (1) The capacitors are not the cause, only an aggravator. Strip C62/C63/C64/C77/C78 out entirely and the CPU's internal pull-up of tens of kilohms working against a few pF of trace still gives a ~0.5 µs edge ≈ 150 ns/V, which is still 15x over the SN74LVC1G332's 10 ns/V limit. No capacitor value fixes this; it is inherent to driving a non-Schmitt CMOS input from a mechanical switch through a passive pull-up, which is a generic condition on thousands of boards rather than a defect of this one. The caps make the number ~1000x worse, not the violation exist. (2) 'No drop-in fix exists' contradicts the finding's own next sentence: reducing C62/C63/C64/C77/C78 IS a drop-in on the same 0603 pads and needs no PCB revision. Also, the HC02 tt limit at the actual 3.34 V rail is not tabulated — TI gives only 1000 ns at 2 V, 500 ns at 4.5 V and 400 ns at 6 V, so ~700 ns interpolated, not 500 ns. Keep this as an awareness note; do not spend a board revision on it.

findings.title: U14 is not a USB power switch — it is a MIC1553 555-type RC oscillator blinking the low-battery LED, and it is correctly held in <1 uA shutdown during normal operation
findings.current_part: MIC1553, Microchip IttyBitty CMOS RC 555-type oscillator, SOT-23-5, astable-only with a chip-select/reset input. Verified pin functions: 1 = T/T (trigger/threshold, sets output high below 2/3 VS and low above 2/3 VS), 2 = GND, 3 = CS (Chip Select/Reset, active-high at >2/3 VS, output off when low at <1/3 VS), 4 = VS, 5 = OUT (CMOS totem-pole, <15 ohm on-resistance). Supply 2.7 V to 18 V. Supply current 255 uA typ / 315 uA max at VS = 5 V when running, and <1 uA typical in shutdown mode (https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/TCG/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/MIC1551-53-IttyBitty-RC-Type-555-Timer-Oscillator-DS20006985.pdf). Every one of those five pin functions matches the board netlist exactly (pin 1 -> C44 1u and R64 to OUT, pin 3 -> Q5B drain and R65, pin 4 -> VOUT5, pin 5 -> Q5A gate).
findings.proposal: No change. Recording it because the premise handed to this review — 'a current-limited USB power switch driving Q5A's gate' — is wrong, and because the Iq question has a good answer that is worth stating rather than assuming.
findings.benefit:
The circuit is: R64 from OUT back to T/T with C44 1 uF to ground forms the one-resistor-one-capacitor 50% astable, f ~ 1/(1.386 x R64 x C44), which is 3.6 Hz with the schematic's R64 = 200k or 7.2 Hz with the PCB's 100k. OUT drives Q5A, which shorts DL2's anode (/DL2A, fed by R10 20k from VOUT5) to ground — so the red LED blinks rather than glowing steadily once the battery is critically low.
On the Iq question: CS is active-high, and in the normal battery state U17's open-drain RESET is released, R66 100k pulls Q5B's gate to VOUT5, Q5B is on, and CS is held at 0 V — below the 1/3 VS = 1.67 V shutdown threshold. So U14 sits in shutdown drawing <1 uA typ, about 5 uW at 5 V, not the 255 uA / 1.28 mW it would draw if it were left enabled. That is a correct design decision and worth confirming rather than assuming. The only cost of the arrangement is R65's 50 uA of pulldown current, which is addressed separately in the mic1553-cs-pullup finding.
findings.risk: None. One note for whoever maintains the BOM: 'MIC1553' with no suffix is ambiguous; the orderable SOT-23-5 part is MIC1553YM5-TR, and MIC1551 (the monostable-capable sibling) is NOT interchangeable — it has TRG and THR on separate pins 4 and 5 with no CS at all, so fitting one would leave the oscillator permanently enabled at 255 uA and with the wrong pin functions entirely.
findings.verify_reason:
Fully verified against Microchip DS20006985A, which I extracted in full. Table 3-2 MIC1553 pin functions match the finding word for word: 1 = T/T (≤2/3 VS sets output high, ≥2/3 VS sets output low), 2 = GND, 3 = CS (active-high at >2/3 VS, output off when low at <1/3 VS), 4 = VS, 5 = OUT (CMOS totem-pole). Features: <15 Ω output on-resistance, 'Zero' leakage trigger and threshold inputs, +2.7 V to +18 V. Electrical table: MIC1553 IS = 255 µA typ / 315 µA max at VS = 5 V; §4.3 'When the chip is deselected, the supply current is less than 1 µA.' All correct.

Every pin maps to the netlist as claimed: U14 pin1 → Net-(U14-T/T) shared with C44 1u and R64; pin3 → Net-(Q5B-D) shared with R65; pin4 → VOUT5; pin5 → Net-(Q5A-G). Q5 is an NDC7002N with Q5A (G1=pin1=Q5A-G, S1=pin5=GND, D1=pin6=/DL2A) shorting the red LED's anode and Q5B (G2=pin3, S2=pin2=GND, D2=pin4) holding CS. So the identification is right and the premise handed to the review really was wrong — this is not a USB power switch.

The Iq conclusion is the valuable part and it holds: with U17's RESET released and R66 pulling Q5B's gate to VOUT5, CS sits at ~0 V, below the 1/3 VS = 1.67 V shutdown threshold, so U14 draws <1 µA rather than 255 µA. That is 1.28 mW of avoided draw — larger than most of the savings proposed elsewhere in this set — and it is worth having confirmed rather than assumed. The MIC1551 warning is correct: the datasheet's Table 3-1 gives MIC1551 as 1 = VS, 2 = GND, 3 = OUT, 4 = TRG, 5 = THR, with no CS at all, so fitting one would leave the oscillator permanently enabled with entirely wrong pin functions. One nit: the datasheet's block diagrams label the part 'MIC1553YM5'; the '-TR' tape-and-reel suffix the finding gives is not shown in the document I read.

findings.title: C61 and C80 return the TPS22917 CT pins to GND, but the datasheet specifies the timing capacitor to VIN
findings.current_part: C61 = 3300 pF from U11 CT (pin 4) to GND; C80 = 3300 pF from U18 CT (pin 4) to GND. The TPS22917 datasheet's pin table says of CT: 'Switch slew rate control. Connect capacitor from this pin to VIN to increase output slew rate and turn-on time', and section 9.3.2 repeats 'A capacitor to VIN on the CT pin sets the slew rate of VOUT'; the Simplified Schematic and Figure 10-1 Typical Application both draw CT to VIN (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps22917.pdf).
findings.proposal: No change to hardware. Flagging so that nobody 'fixes' the timing by chasing the wrong parameter, and so a future revision follows the datasheet.
findings.benefit:
In practice this works, and I want to be precise about why rather than call it a bug. VIN is a stable, heavily bypassed DC rail at the moment each switch turns on — U11's VIN is VOUT5 which is already regulating, and U18's VIN is VOUT3 which is up before /PG_2V5 releases — so a capacitor to VIN and a capacitor to GND are AC-equivalent at the CT node. The datasheet's switching table gives, at VIN = 3.6 V, tR = 1.6 us/pF and tON = 3.8 us/pF for CT >= 100 pF; at VIN = 5.0 V, 1.8 us/pF and 4.0 us/pF. So U18 with 3300 pF ramps VDD3 in 3300 x 1.6 = 5.3 ms (turn-on 12.5 ms) and U11 ramps VDD5 in 3300 x 1.8 = 5.9 ms. Inrush into VDD3's 3.4 uF of decoupling (4 x 0.1u + 3 x 1u) is C x dV/dt = 3.4 uF x 3.34 V / 5.3 ms = 2.1 mA — very gentle, with plenty of headroom for whatever bulk capacitance the ClockxControl adds on its V+ input (at 10 uF added it would still only be 8.5 mA against a 2 A part).
The residual concern is second-order: with the cap to GND rather than to VIN, a disturbance on VIN during the turn-on ramp couples differently into the CT node than TI characterised. Since VIN is settled before ON is asserted in both cases here, I rate the practical impact as nil.
findings.risk: Low. If a future revision moves either load switch to a rail that is still ramping when its ON pin asserts, the GND-referenced cap would give a different (and uncharacterised) slew rate. Cost to correct on a respin: rerouting one pad each.
findings.verify_reason:
The datasheet quotation is verbatim and correct. TI SLVSDW8B Table 6-1, pin 4: 'CT — Switch slew rate control. Connect capacitor from this pin to VIN to increase output slew rate and turn-on time. Can be left floating for fastest timing.' The board does the opposite: the BOM gives C61 = 3300 pF from Net-(U11-CT) to GND and C80 = 3300 pF from Net-(U18-CT) to GND, both on pin 4. So the discrepancy is real and correctly identified. (Note the datasheet's pin TABLE is authoritative here — its Figure 6-1 top-view graphic extracts in a misleading order — and the table is what the board follows: U11 pin1=VOUT5=VIN, pin2=GND, pin3=ON, pin4=CT, pins5&6=VDD5, i.e. QOD tied to VOUT.)
