The timing numbers check: tR 1.6 µs/pF and tON 3.8 µs/pF at VIN = 3.6 V for CT ≥ 100 pF; 1.8 and 4.0 µs/pF at VIN = 5.0 V. I also independently counted VDD3's decoupling from the netlist — C5, C34, C39, C43 (0.1 µF) plus C49, C50, C69 (1 µF) = 3.4 µF nominal, exactly as the finding states — and 3.4 µF × 3.34 V / 5.28 ms = 2.15 mA of inrush. All correct.

The judgement not to call it a bug is right for the reason given: VIN is a settled, heavily bypassed rail before either ON pin asserts (U11's VIN is VOUT5 already regulating; U18's VIN is VOUT3 up before /PG_2V5 releases), so the CT node sees the same AC ground either way. I will flag one thing the finding half-acknowledges but should state plainly: the claim that the tabulated µs/pF figures still apply exactly with a GND-referenced capacitor is an INFERENCE about the internal charging topology, not something the datasheet says, so the delivered ramp may not match TI's characterisation precisely. That does not change the recommendation (no hardware change; correct the reference on a respin), and 0 mW is honest.

findings.title: U18 ramps VDD3 — and therefore the ClockxControl's V+ — over 5.3 ms; C80 is the knob if the module's power-on reset misbehaves
findings.current_part: U18 = TPS22917DBV with C80 = 3300 pF on CT. From the datasheet switching table at VIN = 3.6 V: output rise time tR = 1.6 us/pF and total turn-on time tON = 3.8 us/pF for CT >= 100 pF, with CT open giving 65 us and 120 us respectively (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps22917.pdf). U18's ON pin is /PG_2V5, U8's open-drain PGOOD pulled up by R8 100k to VDD2, so VDD3 comes up only after the 2.5 V CPU core rail is good. The ClockxControl's V+ lands on P1 pad S1 = VDD3 (confirmed from the netlist), so the module sees exactly this ramp.
findings.proposal: No change unless you see a symptom. If the ClockxControl fails to start reliably, or starts at the wrong divider setting, reduce C80 (1000 pF -> 1.6 ms rise; 330 pF -> 0.53 ms; open -> 65 us). Same 0603 pad either way.
findings.benefit: No power benefit — this is a commissioning note for the overclock integration. VDD3 rises in 3300 pF x 1.6 us/pF = 5.28 ms, and the switch's total turn-on is 3300 x 3.8 = 12.5 ms after /PG_2V5 goes high. A 5.3 ms supply ramp is slow by the standards of a small microcontroller's internal power-on reset; parts with a proper brown-out detector handle it, parts relying on a simple POR sometimes do not. Inrush is not the constraint: 3.4 uF of VDD3 decoupling at 3.34 V / 5.28 ms is 2.1 mA, and even 10 uF of extra module bulk capacitance only takes it to 8.5 mA against a 2 A switch, so C80 can be reduced freely without any inrush concern. The sequencing itself is right and worth confirming: the module cannot drive the CPU's XIN before VDD2 is up, because its own supply is gated by VDD2's power-good.
findings.risk: Reducing C80 increases inrush proportionally (330 pF would give 3.4 uF x 3.34 V / 0.53 ms = 21 mA, still trivial) and shortens the gap between VDD2-good and VDD3-good, which is the sequencing margin between the CPU core rail and the CPU I/O rail. Do not remove C80 entirely without checking that VDD3's fastest ramp does not disturb VOUT3. I have not tested the ClockxControl's POR behaviour — this is a 'here is the adjustment if you need it' note, not a claim that a problem exists.
findings.verify_reason:
Every number verified against TI SLVSDW8B. At VIN = 3.6 V: tR = 65 µs with CT open and 1.6 µs/pF for CT ≥ 100 pF; tON = 120 µs with CT open and 3.8 µs/pF for CT ≥ 100 pF. So C80 = 3300 pF gives a 5.28 ms rise and 12.54 ms total turn-on after /PG_2V5 releases, and the suggested alternatives are inside the spec'd range (1000 pF → 1.6 ms, 330 pF → 0.53 ms, open → 65 µs). Inrush arithmetic reproduces against the 3.4 µF of VDD3 decoupling I counted from the netlist myself: 3.4 µF × 3.34 V / 5.28 ms = 2.15 mA, and 21 mA at 330 pF — trivial against a 2 A switch either way, so C80 genuinely can be reduced without an inrush concern.

The sequencing statement is verified from the netlist rather than assumed: P1 pad S1 is on VDD3, U18 pin 3 (ON) is /PG_2V5 which is U8's open-drain PGOOD pulled up by R8 100k to VDD2, and U8's own EN is /PG_3V3 = LTC3527 PGOOD2. So the ClockxControl cannot drive the CPU's XIN before the 2.5 V core rail is good. That chain is correct and is worth having confirmed for the overclock integration.

This is a commissioning note with no claimed saving and the finding says so explicitly, including that the module's POR behaviour was not tested. Nothing here needs revising. One small addition for whoever acts on it: the /PG_2V5 node also sinks the LTC3527's SHDN1 input current (1 µA typ / 2 µA max, verified), so it settles near 2.3 V rather than 2.5 V — still far above the TPS22917's 1.0 V VIH, so the sequencing is unaffected.

findings.title: RA1, Q6, Q8, R9 and the six VDD3 pull-ups carry essentially no static current — I checked each and they belong in the inventory at zero
findings.current_part: RA1 = 330 ohm 4-resistor convex array, four ISOLATED elements in series with the four link-port lines between the AGB CPU (SC, SD, SI, SO) and the ACM2520-801-3P common-mode chokes EM1/EM2 and connector P4. Q6, Q8 = 2N7002 SOT-23. R9 = 100k in parallel with D2 (1SS355VMTE-17) between VBATT and VFILT. The six 100k pull-ups on VDD3 are R6 (cart IRQ), R7 (/~VCNT5), R67 (/CPU/VSHD), R68 (TP12), R70 and R71 (the IPS touch pads).
findings.proposal: Change nothing. Recording the audit so the quiescent inventory is complete and so nobody spends effort here.
findings.benefit:
Each checked against the netlist rather than assumed:
- RA1: series elements in signal lines with no DC path. The link port idles floating; the only pull-up is R35 100k from VDD35 through RA1A onto the CPU's SC pin. Zero standing power. Caveat: if the AGB CPU drives SC low in its default serial-port state, R35 would carry 3.3 V / 100k = 33 uA = 110 uW from VDD35. I cannot verify the CPU's default SC state — it is salvaged, undocumented silicon — so this is flagged as 0 to 110 uW, unresolved.
- R9: parallels D2, so the only current is U3's IVDD, 300 nA typ / 700 nA max. Drop across R9 = 30-70 mV, dissipation = I^2 R = 0.7 uA^2 x 100k = 49 nW. Effectively zero, and the topology is correct: R9 gives a near-zero-drop DC path while D2 + C1 22u hold VFILT up through a battery sag.
- R13 and R8: pull-ups on open-drain PGOOD outputs (LTC3527 PGOOD2 and NCV8164 PGOOD respectively) which are high-impedance whenever power is good. Zero in normal operation.
- R6: cart IRQ line, an input at both ends. Zero.
- R7: only conducts when Q8 turns on, i.e. when the CPU asserts VCNT5. In the screen-on state /~VCNT5 must be high to keep U11 and U12 enabled, so Q8 is off and R7 carries only the TPS22917 ON-pin leakage (+/-10 nA). If VCNT5 is asserted with the screen off, R7 carries 3.34 V / 100k = 33.4 uA = 112 uW. Range 0 to 112 uW.
- R67: both ends at VDD3 whenever U12 is on. Zero.
- R68: drives only TP12, no DC path anywhere. Zero.
- R70, R71: touch-pad pull-ups; Q2B and Q7A are off except during a button combo. Zero.
- R29: pull-up on /~RESET, whose only driver is LTC3527 PGOOD1 (open drain, high-Z when good) and JP1, which ships open. Zero.
- Q6 (2N7002): gate on VDD5, so it turns on with the screen and pulls the LM4853's SHUTDOWN pin low to enable the amplifier; R37 100k then carries 2.5 V / 100k = 25 uA = 62.5 uW from VAUD, but only while the screen is powered — so it is not in the 170 mW no-screen idle figure. Correct design, not worth touching (raising R37 would slow the amp's mute response on power-down).
- Q8 (2N7002): inverts VCNT5 to drive U11/U12's active-high ON pins; TPS22917 VIL is 0.35 V max and Q8 sinks R7's 33 uA at a few millivolts, so there is ample margin.
Total contribution of everything in this finding to the idle inventory: under 0.12 mW, and most of that is state-dependent.
findings.risk: None. The one genuinely unresolved item is R35 / the CPU's SC pin default state (0 to 110 uW); if a builder wants to close it, measuring the voltage at TP25 with the link port empty settles it in one probe.
findings.verify_reason:
I checked each item against the netlist rather than the finding's summary. RA1 is genuinely four isolated series elements (pads 1/8, 2/7, 3/6, 4/5) in the link-port lines with no DC path; Net-(RA1A-R1.1) carries R35 pin 1, RA1 pin 1 and U1 pin 40 (SC), so R35 pulls the CPU's SC pin up directly — the finding's phrasing 'through RA1A' is loose but the electrical conclusion, and its honest 0–110 µW open item pending the CPU's default SC state, is right. R70/R71 confirmed zero-DC: they pull TP10/TP11 up and reach Display ZB/ZA only through Z57/Z58 100 pF, i.e. AC coupling, so Q2B and Q7A never sink them. R68 goes to Q7B-D and TP12 with no DC path. R6 is an input at both ends. R29 (18k, not 100k) sits on /~RESET whose only drivers are LTC3527 PGOOD1 (high-Z when good) and JP1 (Jumper_2_Open) — zero. R9 parallels D2 as described. Q6 (2N7002, G = VDD5, S = AGND, D = Net-(Q6-D)) shares its drain with R37 100k from VAUD and U6 pin 2 SHUTDOWN, so the 62.5 µW figure and the 'only while the screen is powered, therefore not in the 170 mW no-screen idle' qualifier are both correct. Q8 inverts VCNT5 into U11/U12's active-high ON pins, and the TPS22917's VIL of 0.35 V max gives ample margin against 33 µA through a 2N7002 — verified.

So the audit is mostly sound and the conclusion (no lever here) is correct. I am marking it REVISED only because a finding whose entire value is the completeness of its inventory has to get the inventory right, and the R67 case shows the same state-dependence the finding was careful to flag for R7 while declaring R67 flatly 'Zero'. Even corrected, ~0.25 mW on a 170 mW idle is 0.15% and not worth touching.
findings.correction: The 'change nothing' conclusion is right, but the stated total of 'under 0.12 mW' is wrong in at least one plausible operating state, and one item is misclassified as unconditionally zero. R67 is NOT zero when U12 is off. U12's QOD pin (5) is tied to its own VOUT (6) — both on /CPU/VSHD, verified from the netlist — so when U12 is disabled the TPS22917's internal quick-output-discharge resistance (150 Ω, spec'd, disabled state) pulls VSHD to ground, and R67's 100k from VDD3 then carries 3.34 V / 100.15k = 33.4 µA = 112 µW. That is the SAME state in which the finding correctly allows R7 to conduct 112 µW, so in the screen-off state this pair alone is ~0.22 mW and the finding's own total is exceeded. Corrected worst-state total for this inventory: about 0.25 mW, not 0.12 mW. Two smaller items: R8 is not 'zero in normal operation' — its node sinks the LTC3527's SHDN1 input current, which I verified as 1 µA typ / 2 µA max, so ~2.5–5 µW flows and /PG_2V5 sits ~0.2 V below VDD2; and R13's node drives the NCV8164's EN input, whose input current I did NOT verify, so that one should read 'unverified, presumed small' rather than 'zero'. Also, R9's 49 nW assumes only U3's IVDD flows; C1 is a 22 µF MLCC in parallel and its leakage is plausibly a comparable term, so R9's drop is nearer 50–100 mV. None of this changes the recommendation.

findings.title: U7 is a 4.5 V-minimum op-amp running on a 2.5 V rail with its inputs above the common-mode ceiling; the pin-identical TLV9064 fixes it and wins back ~31 mW
findings.current_part: TLV9364QPWRQ1 (TI, TSSOP-14 PW, automotive Q1 grade) — confirmed as the BOM part from the DigiKey link embedded in Audio.kicad_sch (https://www.digikey.com/short/jhr04t1t resolves to TLV9364QPWRQ1). Datasheet SBOSA67B section 6.3 Recommended Operating Conditions: VS = 4.5 V min to 40 V max. Section 7.4 Device Functional Modes, verbatim: 'The TLV936x has a single functional mode and is operational when the power-supply voltage is greater than 4.5 V.' Section 6.7: input common-mode voltage range = (V-) to (V+) - 2 V; IQ per amplifier 2.6 mA typ, 3 mA max, 3.2 mA over temperature; rail-to-rail OUTPUT only, not rail-to-rail input. On this board U7 pin 4 (V+) = VAUD = 2.5 V and pin 11 (V-) = AGND (verified from the PCB net map), so VS = 2.5 V, which is 2.0 V below the datasheet minimum; and the common-mode ceiling is (2.5 - 2) = 0.5 V while every one of the four non-inverting inputs sits at the VAUD/2 = 1.25 V bias set by R45/R46 and R49/R50. Both the supply and the common-mode spec are violated. AGBM-02 carries the identical part (same DigiKey short link in its Audio.kicad_sch), so this is not fork-specific.
findings.proposal: TLV9064IPWR (TI). Datasheet SBOS789 (TLV906xS family): VS = 1.8 V to 5.5 V; VCM = (V-) - 0.1 V to (V+) + 0.1 V (true rail-to-rail input); IQ = 538 uA per amplifier typ, 750 uA max at VS = 5.5 V; GBW 10 MHz; SR 6.5 V/us; broadband noise 10 nV/rtHz; THD+N 0.0008% at 1 kHz. D/PW 14-pin pinout is 1 OUT1, 2 IN1-, 3 IN1+, 4 V+, 11 V-, 12 IN4+, 13 IN4-, 14 OUT4 — pin-for-pin identical to the TLV9364 PW package, so it drops onto the existing TSSOP-14 land with no schematic or layout change. DigiKey 19,544 in stock, $1.53 @1 / $1.117 @10 (vs $2.63 for the TLV9364QPWRQ1) — cheaper as well as correct. Filter performance is unaffected: required slew for 1.25 Vpk at 16 kHz is 2*pi*16k*1.25 = 0.126 V/us against 6.5 V/us available, and the Sallen-Key feedback caps (1000 p / 3300 p) are isolated from each output by R53/R34 = 5.1 k which acts as a built-in R_ISO.
findings.benefit: IQ delta = 4 x (2.6 mA - 0.538 mA) = 8.25 mA at VAUD. Because an LDO passes its load current straight through, the battery-side cost is set by CURRENT not by VAUD: 8.25 mA x 3.34 V = 27.6 mW at VOUT3, / 0.90 assumed boost efficiency = 30.6 mW at the battery. That is 18% of AGBM-01's measured 170 mW idle and ~65% of the audio chain's entire 47.3 mW quiescent floor. HONEST CAVEAT ON THE MAGNITUDE: the 2.6 mA/amp figure is only guaranteed for VS >= 4.5 V and TI publishes no data at 2.5 V, so the actual TLV9364 current on this board is unmeasured. Pessimistic bound — if it draws only half its rated IQ at 2.5 V, the delta is 4 x (1.3 - 0.538) = 3.05 mA = 10.2 mW at VOUT3 = 11.3 mW at the battery. Even that bound is the largest single lever in the audio domain. Circumstantial support for the high end: MouseBiteLabs measure AGBM-01 at 170 mW idle vs 134 mW for a stock GBA, a 36 mW gap that the 47.3 mW audio quiescent computed with 10.4 mA of op-amp current explains almost exactly, whereas a low-IQ assumption would leave AGBM-01's non-audio consumption higher than a 2001 GBA's, which is implausible given the modern converters. Not proof — measure TP22 (VAUD) current before and after.
findings.risk: Very low. The TLV9064 is a lower-voltage, lower-noise-per-mA, rail-to-rail-input part in the identical package and pinout, and the circuit it sits in never needs more than 10 MHz of GBW or 0.13 V/us of slew. The only degradations are on paper and irrelevant here: input offset 0.3 mV typ (TLV9064) vs 0.4 mV (TLV9364) — better; 1/f noise 10 nV/rtHz broadband vs 8.5 nV/rtHz at 1 kHz — a fraction of a dB in a path whose noise floor is set by the 9 uVrms LDO and the PWM quantiser anyway. The one thing to check on a rebuild is that with a genuinely in-spec input stage the DC operating points settle where the design intends; if the existing boards sound acceptable it is because the TLV9364 degrades gracefully, and the TLV9064 can only improve on that. Do not substitute TLV9354 or TLV9164 — those are different supply families.
findings.verify_reason:
THE CORRECTNESS CORE IS CONFIRMED; THE 30.6 mW NUMBER IS ~2.4x TOO HIGH.

What I verified and confirms: I resolved the DigiKey short link embedded in Audio.kicad_sch myself (jhr04t1t -> TLV9364QPWRQ1). I pulled TI's -Q1 datasheet and extracted the text directly. Section 5.3 Recommended Operating Conditions: 'VS Supply voltage, (V+) - (V-) 4.5 40 V' and 'VI Common mode voltage range (V-) (V+) - 2 V'. Section 6.4 verbatim: 'The TLV936x-Q1 has a single functional mode and is operational when the power-supply voltage is greater than 4.5V.' IQ per amplifier 2.6 typ / 3 max / 3.2 over temp. I dumped U7's pad->net map from the fork PCB: pin 4 = VAUD, pin 11 = AGND, and all four amplifiers are unity-gain followers (out tied to inverting in). R45/R46 and R49/R50 are 100k/100k across VAUD, and the + inputs of both stage-2 sections reach that node through R48/R54 (18k) and R34/R53 (5.1k), so all four non-inverting inputs sit at 1.25 V against a 0.5 V common-mode ceiling. BOTH VIOLATIONS ARE REAL. AGBM-02's Audio.kicad_sch carries the identical jhr04t1t link. TLV9064 (SBOS839N) confirmed: VS 1.8-5.5 V, VCM (V-)-0.1 to (V+)+0.1, IQ 538 uA typ / 750 uA max at 5.5 V, GBW 10 MHz, SR 6.5 V/us, 10 nV/rtHz broadband, THD+N 0.0008%, Vos +/-0.3 mV. PW-14 pinouts are literally identical in both datasheets (1 OUT1, 2 IN1-, 3 IN1+, 4 V+, 11 V-, 12 IN4+, 13 IN4-, 14 OUT4), and the fork's land is Bucketmouse:TSSOP-14_4.4x5mm_P0.65mm, pads 1.475 x 0.4 at 0.65 mm pitch. DROP-IN CONFIRMED.

WHAT I REFUTE: the claim 'TI publishes no data at 2.5 V' is false, and it is the load-bearing assumption. SBOSAD6B Figure 5-22 (Quiescent Current vs Supply Voltage, VCM = V-) is a sweep that starts at ~2.4 V. I rendered that page at 12x, calibrated against the gridlines (x: 21 lines, 0-40 V; y: 230 px per 0.4 mA, axis zero at the frame) and read the curve numerically: 1.36 mA/amp at 2.42 V, ~1.43 mA at 2.52 V, 2.05 mA at 2.92 V, then flat. Figure 5-23 additionally plots IQ vs temperature at Vs = 2.7 V, reading ~2.03 mA at 25 C. So at VS = 2.5 V the TLV9364 draws about 1.40 mA per amplifier, not 2.6 mA and not the finding's 1.3 mA 'pessimistic bound'. I did the same on SBOS839N Figure 6-20: TLV9064 at 2.5 V reads ~527 uA/amp, not 538.

CORRECTED ARITHMETIC: delta I = 4 x (1.40 - 0.527) = 3.49 mA. VOUT3 = 1.20 V x (1 + 1.78/1.00) = 3.336 V (LTC3527 VFB = 1.20 V, verified from the datasheet text in the scratchpad). 3.49 mA x 3.336 V = 11.6 mW at VOUT3; / 0.90 = 12.9 mW at the battery. That is 7.6% of the 170 mW idle, not 18%. Upper bound if the out-of-CM-range operating point somehow pushed IQ to the 4.5 V rating: 30.7 mW. Best estimate 13 mW. Caveat I will own: Fig 5-22 is taken at VCM = V-, and this board runs VCM = 1.25 V outside the spec window, so the true current is unmeasured either way - measure TP22.

THE CIRCUMSTANTIAL ARGUMENT IS SELF-REFUTING: the finding says AGBM-01's 36 mW gap over a stock GBA is 'explained almost exactly' by a 47.3 mW audio quiescent. But it also correctly states AGBM-02 carries the identical TLV9364 - and AGBM-02 idles at 141 mW, only 7 mW above a stock GBA. The same audio chain therefore cannot account for a 36 mW gap. The context pack attributes the AGBM-01/AGBM-02 delta to the converter, which is the only power-path difference. With the corrected IQ the audio quiescent floor is ~7.7 mA at VAUD (5.6 U7 + 1.8 LM4853 + ~0.3 bias/pot) = ~28.6 mW at the battery, not 47.3 mW.

MINOR ERRORS: the cited doc number SBOSA67B is wrong (it is SBOSAD6B); SBOS789 is wrong (it is SBOS839N); DigiKey shows TLV9064IPWR Active with 1,433 in stock at $1.62/1 and $1.185/10, not 19,544 at $1.53/$1.117. Also 'R53/R34 = 5.1 k acts as a built-in R_ISO' is not literally true - C35/C28 tie the output directly to the R1/R2 junction, so the output sees the cap in series with 5.1k || 18k = 4.0 kOhm. The conclusion (no bare capacitive load) holds, but the finding never checks it against the TLV9064's stated 100 pF capacitive-load-drive limit, which is the one stability question a reviewer should ask about this swap.

Still the largest lever in the audio domain, still a real spec violation, still a drop-in. Just 13 mW, not 31.

findings.title: Class-D for the speaker path only is worth ~48 mW at max volume, but it costs a schematic redesign and puts a 250 kHz switcher next to the ClockxControl
findings.current_part: U6 LM4853MM/NOPB (TI, VSSOP/MSOP-10 DGS). SNAS155E: single supply 2.4 V to 5.5 V; IDD 1.8 mA typ at VDD = 2.7 V, 2.0 mA at 3.3 V, 2.4 mA at 5.0 V, identical in BTL and SE modes; shutdown current 10 uA at 2.7 V; 300 mW into 8 Ohm BTL at 2.7 V, 25 mW into 32 Ohm SE at 2.7 V; theta-JA 194 C/W for DGS. It is a linear class-AB stage, and for a BTL class-AB the supply current equals the rectified load current, I_avg = (2/pi)(Vp/RL). At MouseBiteLabs' reconciled max-volume operating point (Vp = 0.178 V differential, Pout = 2.0 mW into 8 Ohm) that is 14.2 mA on top of the 1.8 mA quiescent — the output stage is running at an efficiency of Pout/Psup = 2.0 mW / (16.0 mA x 2.5 V) = 5%. DigiKey lists LM4853MM/NOPB as Active with 2,871 in stock, so there is no sourcing pressure to change it.
findings.proposal: TPA2005D1 (TI) for the speaker only, with the LM4853 retained for the headphone jack. SLOS369G: VDD 2.5 V to 5.5 V (exactly reaches VAUD); I(Q) 2.2 mA typ / 3.2 mA max at VDD = 2.5 V no load; I(SD) 0.5 uA; rDS(on) 770 mOhm at 2.5 V; switching frequency 250 kHz typ; 0.26 W into 8 Ohm at 2.5 V / 1% THD+N; THD+N 0.20% at 200 mW / 2.5 V / 8 Ohm; filter-free output stage; HVSSOP-8 (DGN) or VSON-8 (DRB), both 3.00 x 3.00 mm. Input is differential with a fixed 150 kOhm internal input impedance and gain = 2 x 150k/RI, so R30/R31/R56/R57 and the input coupling network all have to be reworked. The LM4853's SHUTDOWN pin (already wired through R37/Q6) would be re-gated off HP-IN so the class-AB headphone amp only runs when a plug is inserted.
findings.benefit: At MouseBiteLabs' own max-volume anchor (2.0 mW into 8 Ohm). Class AB now: 14.2 mA output + 1.8 mA quiescent = 16.0 mA at VAUD. Class D: conduction loss = I_rms^2 x rDS(on) = (sqrt(2.0mW/8))^2 x 0.77 = 0.19 mW, so supply = (2.0 + 0.19)/2.5 V = 0.88 mA, plus 2.2 mA IQ = 3.08 mA. Delta = 12.9 mA at VAUD -> 12.9 mA x 3.34 V = 43.1 mW at VOUT3 -> / 0.90 = 47.9 mW at the battery. At a louder setting (Vp = 0.35 V, Pout = 7.7 mW): class AB = (2/pi)(0.35/8) + 1.8 mA = 29.7 mA; class D = (7.7/0.9)/2.5 + 2.2 = 5.6 mA; delta 24.1 mA = 89 mW at the battery. AND THE HONEST OTHER END: at silence or on headphones the class-D is WORSE by (2.2 - 1.8) = 0.4 mA = 1.5 mW at the battery, because its quiescent exceeds the LM4853's. So this lever is worth 0 to +89 mW depending entirely on how loud the speaker is being driven, and it is worth exactly nothing to a headphone user.
findings.risk: High, and I would not do it on this board. (1) Not a footprint swap: HVSSOP-8/VSON-8 3x3 mm on an MSOP-10 land, plus a new input network, plus mute logic to keep the speaker silent when headphones are inserted (the LM4853 does this for free today by high-Z'ing A2 in SE mode). (2) EMI: U6 sits at (102.6, -25.9) on B.Cu and the ClockxControl window on F.Cu ends at x = 101.275 — the speaker amp is 1.3 mm from the module edge, and U9, the audio PWM buffer, is at (107.7, -46.4) in the same y band. A 250 kHz filter-free class-D output with ~100 ns edges driving 60 mm of speaker wire, next to the cart bus and an unshielded LCD FFC, is a real radiated-emissions and re-rectification risk; it needs ferrite beads plus caps on both speaker leads, which is more area in a shell that has none. (3) Shared rail: the class-D's switching current on VAUD amplitude-modulates the PWM reference that U9 buffers, i.e. it couples into the HEADPHONE path too unless VAUD is split. (4) The AGBM's stated selling point is audio quality; TPA2005D1 THD+N at the relevant level is 0.20% versus low-single-digit-hundredths for the LM4853 at 4% of its capability. Verdict: real arithmetic, wrong trade for this product. Reported because the reviewer asked for the size of the lever, not because I recommend pulling it.
findings.verify_reason:
EVERY DATASHEET NUMBER CHECKS OUT; THE OPERATING POINT IS AN ASSUMPTION, AND THE PROPOSAL HAS A SUPPLY-MARGIN DEFECT THE FINDING MISSES.

Verified from SNAS155E text I extracted myself: VDD 2.4-5.5 V; IDD 1.8 mA at 2.7 V in BOTH BTL and SE modes; 2.0 mA at 3.3 V; 2.4 mA at 5.0 V; ISD 10 uA at 2.7 V; PO 300 mW BTL 8 Ohm and 25 mW SE 32 Ohm at 2.7 V; theta-JA DGS 194 C/W. All exact. DigiKey: LM4853MM/NOPB Active, 2,861 in stock (finding said 2,871 - fine).

Verified from SLOS369G: VDD 2.5-5.5 V; I(Q) 2.2 typ / 3.2 max at VDD = 2.5 V no load; I(SD) 0.5 uA; rDS(on) 770 mOhm at 2.5 V; f(sw) 200/250/300 kHz min/typ/max; PO 0.26 W at 2.5 V 1% THD+N; THD+N 0.20% at 200 mW/2.5 V/8 Ohm; gain = 2 x 150k/RI with 142k/158k limits. All exact. TI product page: ACTIVE.

ERRORS I FOUND:
(1) PACKAGE. TI's product page lists HVSSOP (DGN) 8-pin as 14.7 mm2, 3 mm x 4.9 mm - only VSON (DRB) is 3 x 3 mm. TI's own datasheet contradicts itself (Device Information says 3x3 for both; the feature list says '3 mm x 5 mm MSOP PowerPAD (DGN)'), and the finding picked the wrong half. Immaterial to the verdict since it is correctly flagged as not a footprint swap (the U6 land is MSOP-10_3x3mm_P0.5mm, pads 1.625 x 0.35 at +/-2.1125 mm), but it is a wrong stated spec.
(2) A REJECTION REASON THE FINDING MISSES, and it is decisive: TPA2005D1's MINIMUM VDD is 2.5 V. VAUD is 2.5 V with +/-2% accuracy over load and temperature from the NCV8164 (verified), i.e. 2.45 V worst case - BELOW the part's minimum. The proposal has NEGATIVE supply margin where the incumbent LM4853 has +50 mV. The finding writes 'VDD 2.5 V to 5.5 V (exactly reaches VAUD)' and treats that as a pass; it is a fail, and the same engineer's own lm4853-supply-margin finding computes the 2.45 V worst case.
(3) CONDUCTION LOSS OFF BY 2x: in an H-bridge the load current flows through a high-side FET and a low-side FET in series, so P = I_rms^2 x 2 x rDS(on). At the finding's own point that is 0.38 mW, not 0.19 mW. Immaterial to the total.
(4) THE OPERATING POINT CONTRADICTS THE SAME ENGINEER'S OTHER FINDING. Here max volume is Vp = 0.178 V / 2.0 mW; in lm4853-supply-margin it is 0.707 Vrms differential / 62 mW. Neither matches the gain structure, which I traced from the netlist: U7 full scale 1.25 Vpk -> VR2 -> C55/C56 -> R30/R31 100k into the LM4853 virtual ground with R56/R57 20k feedback, gain -0.2 -> 0.25 Vpk single-ended -> 0.5 Vpk differential in BTL -> 0.354 Vrms -> 15.6 mW into 8 Ohm at the continuous-sine ceiling.

CORRECTED ENVELOPE. At the gain-structure ceiling: class AB draws (2/pi)(0.5/8) + 1.8 mA = 39.8 + 1.8 = 41.6 mA; class D draws (15.6 mW + 3.0 mW)/2.5 V + 2.2 mA = 9.6 mA; delta 32 mA x 3.336 V / 0.90 = 119 mW at the battery. At silence or on headphones class D is 1.5 mW WORSE (the finding says this, correctly). Real program material has 10-14 dB of crest factor, so average draw sits far below the sine ceiling. Reconciling against MouseBiteLabs' own '50 to 100 mW at max volume' for the whole audio block: with the corrected op-amp quiescent (~29 mW at the battery, see u7 verdict) that leaves 20-70 mW for the output stage, i.e. 5-19 mA at VAUD, and a class-D saving of roughly 12-61 mW. Best estimate ~35 mW, range 0 to 119 mW. Note the finding's own 12.75 mA quiescent (47.3 mW) plus its 14.2 mA output (53 mW) already totals 100 mW - the very top of MBL's range with zero headroom, another sign the quiescent assumption is too high.

The recommendation (real arithmetic, wrong trade, do not do it) is correct and I agree with it - especially now that the supply floor is violated too. The headline 47.9 mW is inside the plausible band but is a back-solved midpoint, not an anchor.

findings.title: The reconstruction filter is fixed at 15.84 kHz but the GBA's PWM carrier scales with the CPU clock — the ClockxControl's underclock settings put the carrier inside the audio band
findings.current_part: The filter is a 4th-order Butterworth low-pass at fc = 15.84 kHz per channel, computed from the schematic values: stage 1 f0 = 15.76 kHz Q = 0.540 (R51 7.5k / R52 20k / C32 1000p feedback / C31 680p to AGND), stage 2 f0 = 15.92 kHz Q = 1.312 (R53 5.1k / R54 18k / C35 3300p feedback / C33 330p to AGND); the left channel U7D/U7B is identical. The textbook 4th-order Butterworth Qs are 0.5412 and 1.3065, so the alignment is exact. The GBA's audio is 1-bit PWM whose rate is derived from the master clock: GBATEK's SOUNDBIAS (4000088h) bits 14-15 give 9 bit / 32.768 kHz (default), 8 bit / 65.536 kHz, 7 bit / 131.072 kHz, 6 bit / 262.144 kHz, and each 9-bit sample N outputs N low bits then (512-N) high bits at 16.78 MHz, i.e. 512 clocks per sample. With X1 depopulated and CLK driven by the module, the carrier scales 1:1 with the ClockxControl ratio.
findings.proposal: No component change is available that fixes this. Attenuation of the carrier fundamental, 1/sqrt(1+(f/fc)^8) at fc = 15.84 kHz: 0.333x -> carrier 10.91 kHz -> -0.2 dB (essentially unfiltered); 0.5x -> 16.38 kHz -> -3.6 dB; 0.666x -> 21.82 kHz -> -11.5 dB; 1.0x -> 32.77 kHz -> -25.3 dB; 1.25x -> 40.96 kHz -> -33.0 dB; 1.5x -> 49.15 kHz -> -39.3 dB; 1.75x -> 57.34 kHz -> -44.7 dB. The carrier fundamental at mid-scale duty is (2 x 2.5 V / pi) x sin(pi x 0.5) = 1.591 Vpk = 1.125 Vrms, against a full-scale recovered audio sine of 1.25 Vpk = 0.884 Vrms — the carrier is 2.1 dB LOUDER than full-scale audio before filtering. So at 0.333x roughly 1.10 Vrms of a 10.9 kHz tone reaches the volume pot, i.e. above the music. Practical options, all outside the BOM: treat 1.0x and above as the usable range for anyone who cares about the audio; or have software set SOUNDBIAS bits 14-15 to 3 (6 bit / 262.144 kHz nominal, which is 87 kHz even at 0.333x -> below -49 dB) at the cost of amplitude resolution. Retuning the filter to cover 0.333x would need fc ~5 kHz and would destroy the audio band, so it is not an option.
findings.benefit: Zero mW — this is a quality finding, and the direction of the effect is what matters. Overclocking is a free WIN for the audio: at 1.75x the carrier rejection improves from -25.3 dB to -44.7 dB, 19.4 dB better, and the 61 mVrms of 32.8 kHz residual that reaches the headphones at 1x drops to 6.6 mVrms at 57 kHz. Underclocking is a loss: at 0.5x and 0.333x the reconstruction filter stops doing its job.
findings.risk: The risk is in NOT knowing this: a user who selects 0.333x or 0.5x on the ClockxControl gets an audible high-frequency tone (10.9 or 16.4 kHz) at or above program level, plus intermodulation in the class-AB output stage, and will blame the board. Note also that the game's own audio is pitch- and tempo-shifted at any ratio other than 1x, which is a ClockxControl consequence rather than a component one. Nothing on the board can be changed to fix it; it belongs in the fork's documentation.
findings.verify_reason:
I RE-DERIVED EVERY NUMBER AND THEY ALL HOLD.

Filter topology, from the BOM net map (not from the finding): stage 1 R51 7.5k in, R52 20k, C32 1000p from U7C output to the R51/R52 junction, C31 680p from U7C+ to AGND. Stage 2 R53 5.1k in (fed from U7C's output), R54 18k, C35 3300p from U7A output to the R53/R54 junction, C33 330p from U7A+ to AGND. Left channel R42/R47/C24/C26 then R34/R48/C28/C27, identical. Unity-gain Sallen-Key, so f0 = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(R1R2C1C2)) and Q = sqrt(R1R2C1C2)/(C2(R1+R2)).
Stage 1: R1R2 = 1.5e8, C1C2 = 6.8e-19, sqrt(product) = 1.00995e-5 -> f0 = 15.76 kHz; Q = 1.00995e-5/(680p x 27500) = 0.5401.
Stage 2: R1R2 = 9.18e7, C1C2 = 1.089e-18, sqrt = 9.998e-6 -> f0 = 15.92 kHz; Q = 9.998e-6/(330p x 23100) = 1.3115.
Butterworth targets 0.5412 and 1.3065. The alignment is exact, as claimed.

GBATEK confirms the PWM claims verbatim: SOUNDBIAS bits 14-15 are '0 9bit/32.768kHz (Default...)', '1 8bit/65.536kHz', '2 7bit/131.072kHz', '3 6bit/262.144kHz (Best for PSG channels 1-4)'; 'these bits are output at system clock speed (16.78MHz)'; '512 bits are output per sample (512*32K=16M)'; each sample is 'N low bits, followed by 512-N high bits'. The carrier is therefore locked 1:1 to CK1 and scales with the ClockxControl ratio.

I recomputed every attenuation with 1/sqrt(1+(f/15.84k)^8): 10.91 kHz -> -0.22 dB; 16.38 -> -3.64; 21.82 -> -11.45; 32.77 -> -25.3; 40.96 -> -33.0; 49.15 -> -39.4; 57.34 -> -44.7. All match the finding to within 0.2 dB. Carrier fundamental (2 x 2.5/pi) x sin(pi/2) = 1.5915 Vpk = 1.125 Vrms, which is +2.1 dB on a 0.884 Vrms full-scale sine. Correct.

ONE PHYSICAL CAVEAT that makes it worse, not better: at 0.333x the finding says 'roughly 1.10 Vrms of a 10.9 kHz tone reaches the volume pot'. It cannot - U7 runs on 2.5 V with a 1.25 V bias, so its output cannot swing 1.59 Vpk. What actually reaches the pot is a clipped ~1.25 Vpk tone plus the intermodulation products of that clipping. Direction and severity conclusion unaffected.

The conclusion that overclocking is a free win for the audio (-25.3 dB at 1x to -44.7 dB at 1.75x) and underclocking a real loss is correct, is specific to this board's filter and this module's ratios, and belongs in the fork's documentation. No component change available; correctly reported as 0 mW.

findings.title: CP2/CP3 100 uF roll the headphone bass off at 50 Hz (100 Hz into 16 Ohm IEMs); a 220 uF polymer tantalum in the identical case is a drop-in that halves the corner
findings.current_part: KYOCERA AVX TPSB107K010R0400 (AGBM-01) / TPSB107M010R0400 (AGBM-02) — 100 uF, 10 V, MOLDED TANTALUM (not ceramic; I checked, because a Class II ceramic here would be a genuine distortion source), case code 1411 (3528 metric), 3.50 x 2.80 mm, 2.10 mm seated height, ESR 400 mOhm, +/-10% (K) or +/-20% (M). These sit in series between the LM4853 SE outputs and the jack tip/ring, with R19/R20 1 k bleed resistors to AGND. High-pass corner into the load = 1/(2*pi*RL*C): 49.7 Hz with 32 Ohm headphones, 99.5 Hz with 16 Ohm IEMs, 5.3 Hz with 300 Ohm cans. The PCB land is Bucketmouse:C_1210_3225Metric_Boxed_2, pads 1.15 x 2.7 mm at +/-1.475 mm (inner gap 1.8 mm, outer span 4.10 mm) — I checked this against the 3528 tantalum body and the terminations land fully inside the pads with ~0.3 mm of outboard fillet, so the existing footprint is correct for a B-case tantalum even though it is named for a 1210 ceramic.
findings.proposal: KEMET T520B227M006ATE035 — 220 uF, 6.3 V, +/-20%, tantalum POLYMER (KO-CAP), case 1411 (3528 metric), 3.50 x 2.80 x 2.00 mm (0.1 mm SHORTER than the part fitted), ESR 35 mOhm at 100 kHz, -55 to +105 C. DigiKey 22,443 in stock, $1.56 @1 / ~$1.03 @10. Identical case, identical land pattern, identical polarity orientation — a true drop-in. DC bias across it is only VAUD/2 = 1.25 V on a 6.3 V part (20% of rating), comfortably inside the 80% derating convention for polymer tantalum.
findings.benefit: Zero mW — this is a pure audio-quality change, and it is one of the very few in this domain that a human will actually hear. New corner = 1/(2*pi*32*220u) = 22.6 Hz with 32 Ohm headphones (was 49.7 Hz) and 45.2 Hz with 16 Ohm IEMs (was 99.5 Hz). Against modern low-impedance IEMs the existing 100 uF is losing 3 dB at 100 Hz and about 6 dB at 50 Hz, which is audible bass loss on anything with sub-bass content; 220 uF moves that below the useful range. Secondary: ESR drops 400 mOhm -> 35 mOhm, which removes 0.4/(0.4+32) = 1.2% (0.11 dB) of insertion loss and any ESR-related nonlinearity. LEAVE CP1 ALONE: it is the same part in series with the 8 Ohm speaker, corner 1/(2*pi*8*100u) = 199 Hz, but a 23 mm 8 Ohm GBA speaker produces essentially nothing below ~400 Hz, so 220 uF there buys no audible bass and only increases cone excursion. CP1 is also not optional despite being a bridged output — it is there because in SE mode the LM4853 leaves LOUT/BTL- at a VDD/2 DC offset with A2 high-Z, and without CP1 that would push 1.25 V/8 Ohm = 156 mA of DC through the speaker.
findings.risk: Low. Cost roughly doubles for those two positions (~$1.03 vs ~$0.60 each in tens) — on a board whose BOM is already dominated by the CPU/SRAM salvage that is noise, but it is the one place in this review where a quality change costs real money. Polymer tantalum has a lower failure-to-short energy than MnO2 tantalum and a 6.3 V part on a 2.5 V rail with 1.25 V bias is very lightly stressed, so reliability is if anything better. Watch polarity on hand assembly: the anode band goes to the amplifier side (CP2 pin 1 = LOUT/BTL-, CP3 pin 1 = ROUT), same as the part it replaces.
findings.verify_reason:
THE PART, THE FOOTPRINT AND THE DROP-IN CLAIM ALL SURVIVE. THREE CORRECTIONS.

Verified independently: DigiKey short 332b01qh resolves to TPSB107K010R0400, KYOCERA AVX, 100 uF, 10 V, +/-10%, molded MnO2 tantalum, case 1411 (3528 metric), 3.50 x 2.80 mm, height seated max 2.10 mm, ESR 400 mOhm @ 100 kHz. Cross-checked against the KYOCERA AVX TPS ratings table, row TPSB107*010#0400: B case, DCL max 10 uA, DF max 8%, ESR max 400 mOhm @ 100 kHz, MSL 1. AGBM-02's link w5p7f0nd resolves to TPSB107M010R0400 (+/-20%), as claimed.
T520B227M006ATE035 on DigiKey: 220 uF, 6.3 V, +/-20%, molded tantalum polymer, 1411 (3528 metric), 3.50 x 2.80 mm, height seated max 2.00 mm, ESR 35 mOhm @ 100 kHz, ACTIVE, 22,443 in stock, $1.56 @1 / $1.03 @10. Every single number in the proposal is exact.
Footprint checked in the fork PCB: Bucketmouse:C_1210_3225Metric_Boxed_2, pads 1.15 x 2.7 mm at +/-1.475 mm -> inner gap 1.80 mm, outer span 4.10 mm. Identical case in and out, so DROP-IN CONFIRMED.

CORRECTION 1 - the corner arithmetic omits R19/R20. Each cap has a 1 kOhm bleed resistor to AGND on its load side (BOM: R19 1k from CP3-Pad2 to AGND, R20 1k from CP2-Pad2 to AGND), so the load is RL || 1k, not RL. Correct corners: 32 Ohm -> 51.3 Hz now / 23.3 Hz with 220 uF; 16 Ohm -> 101.1 / 45.9 Hz; 300 Ohm -> 6.9 Hz now (the finding says 5.3 Hz, 30% off) / 3.1 Hz after. The headline improvement is unchanged.

CORRECTION 2 - an unmentioned trade. KEMET's own T520 datasheet says, in its own words, 'Because of the high conductivity of the polymer, the KO-CAP family has higher leakage currents than traditional MnO2 type Tantalum caps. The DC Leakage limits at 25C are calculated as 0.1 x C x V', i.e. 0.1 x 220 x 6.3 = 138.6 uA max, and 10x that at 85 C. The incumbent AVX part's DCL max is 10 uA. That is a 14x increase in the leakage limit on a node that sits in series with the headphone jack. At the 1.25 V bias (20% of rating) actual leakage is far below the rated-voltage limit, and with headphones plugged in the load is ~31 Ohm so even tens of uA give under 1 mV of DC. But with nothing plugged in the leakage returns through R19/R20 = 1 kOhm, so tens of uA becomes tens of mV of standing DC and a larger plug-in pop. Not a blocker; it should have been stated in a finding whose whole point is audio quality.

CORRECTION 3 - the CP1 justification is REFUTED by the LM4853 datasheet. The finding says 'in SE mode the LM4853 leaves LOUT/BTL- at a VDD/2 DC offset with A2 high-Z, and without CP1 that would push 1.25 V/8 Ohm = 156 mA of DC through the speaker.' SNAS155E, Application Information, says the opposite: 'Amplifier A2 is shut down to a high output impedance state in SE mode. This prevents any current flow into the mono bridge-tied load, thereby muting it.' The high-Z output IS the mute; there is no 156 mA path with or without CP1. (SP1 is confirmed wired between LOUT/BTL- and CP1's far side, CP1's other end on BTL+.) CP1's real function is more plausibly the 199 Hz high-pass protecting a 23 mm speaker and blocking the BTL output offset (VOS 40 mV max -> 5 mA). The advice to leave CP1 alone is still right, for the finding's second reason.

COST CLAIM UNSUPPORTED: the finding says the swap 'roughly doubles' cost from ~$0.60 to ~$1.03 in tens. DigiKey lists the M-tolerance AVX part at $1.47 @1, and the exact K-tolerance part actually specified on AGBM-01 has FIVE units in stock. The incumbent is the sourcing problem; at hobbyist quantities the polymer is close to cost-neutral, and the poor availability of TPSB107K010R0400 is itself an argument for the change that the finding missed.

findings.title: Half the Sallen-Key capacitors are X7R and half are C0G — making the four X7R ones C0G removes up to 0.6 dB of Q-tolerance peaking for about 12 cents
findings.current_part: C24 and C32 = KEMET C0603C102K5RACTU, 1000 pF, 50 V, X7R, +/-10%, 0603. C28 and C35 = KEMET C0603C332K5RACTU, 3300 pF, 50 V, X7R, +/-10%, 0603. Their partners in the same filter sections are ALREADY C0G: C26/C31 = C0603C681J5GACTU (680 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%) and C27/C33 = C0603C331J5GACTU (330 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%). All part numbers read directly out of the DigiKey source links embedded in Audio.kicad_sch. The X7R parts are the Sallen-Key FEEDBACK capacitors, i.e. exactly the ones that set Q.
findings.proposal: C24/C32 -> KEMET C0603C102J5GACTU (1000 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%, 0603). C28/C35 -> KEMET C0603C332J5GACTU (3300 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%, 0603) — verified on DigiKey: 26,340 in stock, $0.41 @1, $0.157 @100. Same 0603 land, same voltage rating, no schematic change.
findings.benefit: Zero mW; a tolerance and repeatability fix, not a power one. For a unity-gain Sallen-Key, Q is proportional to sqrt(Cfb/Cgnd), so a +10% X7R feedback cap against a -5% C0G shunt cap scales Q by sqrt(1.10/0.95) = 1.076. On the high-Q section that takes Q from 1.312 to 1.412, and the section's peak gain Q/sqrt(1 - 1/(4Q^2)) from 1.419 (+3.04 dB) to 1.510 (+3.58 dB) — about 0.6 dB of extra passband peaking around 14 kHz, plus a comparable f0 shift. C0G's +/-5% and 30 ppm/C also remove the X7R temperature drift (+/-15% over the X7R range) that otherwise detunes the Butterworth alignment as the handheld warms up. BE HONEST ABOUT WHAT THIS IS NOT: I checked whether the X7R parts are a real distortion source and they are not. The AC voltage across a Sallen-Key feedback cap at frequency f is approximately (2*pi*f*R2*Cgnd) x Vout, which at 1 kHz for stage 1 is 2*pi*1000*20000*680p = 8.5% of the output, i.e. about 75 mVrms across a 50 V-rated part — 0.15% of its rating, where X7R's voltage coefficient is nil. So this change fixes a specification inconsistency and about half a dB of response ripple; nobody will hear it. The one unquantified residual is MLCC piezoelectricity — Class II dielectrics are microphonic, and these caps sit on B.Cu about 15 mm from a speaker in a plastic shell — but I have no measured figure for that and will not invent one.
findings.risk: None worth naming. C0G at these values in 0603 50 V is stocked in volume and costs the same order as X7R. The only thing to verify is that a C0G 3300 pF 0603 is physically available in the tolerance you order (J = +/-5% confirmed in stock; F = +/-1% also exists if you want a tighter alignment).
findings.verify_reason:
THE PARTS AND THE DIRECTION ARE RIGHT; THE CLAIMED 0.6 dB IS ABOUT 3x TOO BIG BECAUSE THE COMPARISON IS RIGGED.

I resolved all four incumbent DigiKey links from Audio.kicad_sch myself and every one matches: 377h8558 -> C0603C102K5RACTU (1000 pF, 50 V, X7R, +/-10%, 0603); 3p3jj3wt -> C0603C332K5RACTU (3300 pF, 50 V, X7R, +/-10%, 0603); jm5qjr7w -> C0603C681J5GACTU (680 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%); 5ptw22qq -> C0603C331J5GACTU (330 pF, 50 V, C0G/NP0, +/-5%). The X7R parts are indeed the feedback caps: from the netlist C24/C32 pad 2 land on Net-(U7D--)/Net-(U7C--) and C28/C35 pad 2 on Net-(U7B--)/Net-(U7A--), which are the outputs (unity-gain followers). Both proposed replacements exist and are stocked: C0603C332J5GACTU is Active with 26,340 in stock at $0.41 @1 / $0.1574 @100 (exactly as claimed), and C0603C102J5GACTU is a live DigiKey part (608471). Same 0603 land, same 50 V rating, no schematic change. All correct.

WHERE IT BREAKS: Q is proportional to sqrt(Cfb/Cgnd), which I confirmed by deriving Q = sqrt(R1R2C1C2)/(C2(R1+R2)) = sqrt(C1/C2) x sqrt(R1R2)/(R1+R2). The finding then compares a +10% X7R feedback cap against a -5% C0G shunt cap - worst-case one part against worst-case the other - and gets sqrt(1.10/0.95) = 1.0761, Q 1.312 -> 1.412, peak 3.037 -> 3.578 dB, a 0.54 dB penalty. But the REPLACEMENT is also +/-5%, so the correct comparison is worst-case-before against worst-case-after: sqrt(1.05/0.95) = 1.0515, Q = 1.380, peak gain Q/sqrt(1-1/(4Q^2)) = 1.4805 = 3.408 dB. The swap therefore removes 3.578 - 3.408 = 0.17 dB of worst-case passband peaking, not 0.54-0.6 dB. About a third of the claim.

WHAT SURVIVES INTACT, and is the better argument the finding buries: the temperature coefficient. C0G is +/-30 ppm/C; X7R is +/-15% over its range. A handheld that warms in the hand detunes two of the four capacitors in a Butterworth alignment by up to 15% while the other two stay put, and no tolerance-tightening fixes that. That justifies the change on its own.

The distortion analysis is sound: 2*pi*1000*20000*680p = 8.5% of Vout across the stage-1 feedback cap at 1 kHz, ~75 mVrms on a 50 V part, so no meaningful voltage coefficient. The finding is honest that nobody will hear this, and it is right to be. Category and footprint grading (drop-in) are correct.

findings.title: The volume pot's track carries 1.25 V DC, which wastes 0.93 mW and makes turning the volume wheel produce an audible thump
findings.current_part: VR2 = Alps Alpine RK10J12R0A0B, 10 kOhm, dual gang (5 pins: ROUT/LOUT hot ends, LIN/RIN wipers, COM), from the DigiKey link in Audio.kicad_sch. Its COM (pin 5) goes to AGND, and its two hot ends (pins 1/2) are driven directly by the U7A and U7B outputs. Those outputs are DC-coupled followers whose inputs are biased at VAUD/2 = 1.25 V by R45/R46 and R49/R50, so both pot tracks sit with 1.25 V across them permanently, and the wiper DC voltage sweeps from 1.25 V at maximum volume to 0 V at minimum. The wipers feed C55/C56 (1 uF X7R, KEMET C0603C105K4RACTU, 16 V) and then R30/R31 (100 k) into the LM4853's inverting inputs, which are virtual grounds at the internal BYPASS half-supply.
findings.proposal: Move the DC block to the input side of the pot: insert two 1 uF caps between the U7A/U7B outputs and VR2 pins 1/2, keeping C55/C56 where they are. The pot track then sits at 0 V DC at every position, the wiper DC never moves, and the DC across C55/C56 is a constant 1.25 V. The new caps see 10 kOhm, giving a corner of 1/(2*pi*10k*1u) = 15.9 Hz, well below CP2/CP3's 22.6-49.7 Hz which dominates the low end anyway. Cost: two 0603 caps and the board area for them, in a region (x 100-127) that is already dense — hence needs-PCB-revision. PARTIAL DROP-IN ALTERNATIVE if you will not respin: change C55/C56 from 1 uF to 0.1 uF. The corner into R30/R31 = 100 k moves from 1.59 Hz to 15.9 Hz (still far below the output-cap corner, so no bandwidth is lost), and the thump's time constant drops from R*C = 0.1 s to 0.01 s. The step AMPLITUDE is unchanged; only its duration and energy fall by 10x, turning a thump into a click.
findings.benefit: Two separate effects, both small but real. (a) POWER: 2 tracks x 1.25 V / 10 kOhm = 250 uA of DC flowing continuously from the op-amp outputs through the pot to AGND, at every volume setting including zero. 250 uA x 3.34 V / 0.90 = 0.93 mW at the battery — 2% of the audio chain's quiescent, i.e. genuinely small, and I am reporting the number precisely so it can be dismissed. (b) QUALITY, which is the real point: because the wiper DC tracks the pot position, moving the volume wheel changes the DC across C55/C56 by up to 1.25 V, and that change has to charge through R30/R31 = 100 k with tau = 0.1 s. The resulting step at the LM4853 output is up to 1.25 V x (Rf/Ri = 0.2) = 0.25 V single-ended, or 0.5 V differential into the 8 Ohm speaker in BTL mode, decaying over ~0.1 s — an audible thump every time the volume is adjusted. The LM4853's click-and-pop suppression does not help here; it covers power-up and mode changes, not input-side DC transients.
findings.risk: Low technically, moderate practically. Adding the two caps needs board space in the densest corner of the layout and changes a net, so it cannot go into an existing build. The 0.1 uF drop-in alternative is free but is a judgement call: some people find a short click more objectionable than a slow thump, and it slightly raises the input-side corner (15.9 Hz, still inaudible against the 22.6-49.7 Hz output cap). Do NOT try to fix this by referencing VR2's COM to a half-supply node instead of AGND — at maximum volume the track carries up to 1.25 Vrms / 10 k = 125 uA of signal current per channel that would have to be sunk by that node, and there is no spare op-amp section (all four of U7 are used) and the LM4853's BYPASS pin is far too high-impedance to do it.
findings.verify_reason:
I TRIED TO BREAK THIS ONE AND COULD NOT.

Topology verified from the pad->net dump, not from the finding. VR2 pin 1 (ROUT) -> Net-(U7A--), pin 2 (LOUT) -> Net-(U7B--), pin 5 (COM) -> AGND, wipers pin 3/4 -> /CPU/Audio/LIN and /RIN. U7A and U7B are unity-gain followers (output tied to inverting input, so KiCad names the shared node after the '-' pin), so the two pot tracks really are driven by DC-coupled op-amp outputs. Those outputs sit at the VAUD/2 = 1.25 V bias set by R45/R46 and R49/R50 (100k/100k across VAUD, confirmed in the BOM), which reaches the + inputs through R42/R47 and R51/R52. So both tracks carry 1.25 V across 10 kOhm permanently and the wiper DC sweeps 1.25 V -> 0 V with position. All true.

VR2 = Alps Alpine RK10J12R0A0B, 10 kOhm, Active, 2,648 in stock - I resolved the zh4rmq4h link myself. C55/C56 = KEMET C0603C105K4RACTU, 1 uF, 16 V, X7R, 0603 (link 2ppmm3vt) - correct. R30/R31 = 100k, R56/R57 = 20k feedback, confirmed in the BOM. SNAS155E confirms A1/A3 are configured with external AV = -RF/RI, so LIN/RIN are virtual grounds at the internal BYPASS half-supply - the finding's premise for the charge-redistribution mechanism.

Arithmetic redone: 2 tracks x 1.25 V / 10 kOhm = 250 uA; 250 uA x 3.336 V / 0.90 = 0.927 mW at the battery. Correct, and honestly labelled as small (0.5% of idle). tau = 100 kOhm x 1 uF = 0.1 s. Step at the LM4853 output = deltaV x 20k/100k = 0.2 x 1.25 = 0.25 V single-ended, 0.5 V differential in BTL. Correct. The 0.1 uF alternative: 1/(2*pi*100k*0.1u) = 15.9 Hz, still an order of magnitude below the 23-51 Hz output-cap corner, so no bandwidth is lost. Correct.

ONE NUANCE the finding could have added: 0.25 V is the instantaneous-step bound. A real wheel turn takes 0.3-1 s, and the 0.1 s network differentiates it, so a full sweep in 0.5 s gives roughly 0.2 x 1.25 x (0.1/0.5) = 50 mV of offset. Still plainly audible on a bridged 8 Ohm speaker; the mechanism, the fix and the grading (needs-PCB-revision for the proper fix, drop-in for the partial) all stand.

The warning against referencing VR2's COM to a half-supply node is also right: all four U7 sections are in use (verified from the pin dump - no spare amplifier exists on this board), and the LM4853 BYPASS pin is not a driven low-impedance reference.

findings.title: The audio LDO is not the problem it looks like: raising VAUD saves nothing, merging it with VDD2 saves 0.11 mW, and a buck saves 7.9 mW at the cost of the rail that defines the audio
findings.current_part: U4 = NCV8164ASN250T1G (onsemi, TSOP-5/SOT-23-5), fixed 2.5 V. Verified from the datasheet: operating input 1.6 to 5.5 V; output accuracy +/-2% over load and temperature; quiescent current 30 uA typ; standby 0.1 uA; dropout for the 2.5 V variant 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA (113 mV typ for a 3.0 V variant); PSRR 83 dB at 100 Hz, 85 dB at 1 kHz, 80 dB at 10 kHz, 61 dB at 100 kHz; output noise 9 uVrms over 10 Hz to 100 kHz; 300 mA capability. U8, the CPU-core LDO, is the SAME part number producing the same 2.5 V from the same VOUT3. MouseBiteLabs describe the audio as fed from 'a roughly 75% efficient' supply, which is exactly 2.5/3.34 = 74.9%.
findings.proposal: No change. The reasoning, since the reviewer asked what sets 2.5 V and whether the extra LDO is the reason for the loss: (1) 2.5 V is floored by the LM4853's 2.4 V minimum supply and capped by VOUT3 minus the LDO dropout; it also sets the PWM full scale, since U9 buffers the CPU's PWM onto VAUD and therefore VAUD IS the audio DAC's reference voltage. (2) The extra LDO is not the reason for the 25% loss — VDD2 pays the identical 74.9% on the same VOUT3 through an identical NCV8164. Merging U4 into U8 would save only U4's own 30 uA = 0.11 mW at the battery and would put the CPU core's and SRAM's switching current directly onto the audio reference. (3) Raising VAUD to 3.0 V (feasible: 113 mV typ dropout from 3.34 V) improves the LDO's voltage efficiency from 74.9% to 89.8% and SAVES NOTHING, because an LDO passes its load current unchanged: the battery-side cost of a constant-current load is I x 3.34 V / eta_boost regardless of VAUD. It would actively cost power, because the bias networks scale as V/R (0.325 mA -> 0.39 mA) and the class-AB output-stage supply power is Vdd x (2/pi)(Vp/RL), which rises 20% for the same loudness. (4) Replacing U4 with a 2.5 V buck is the only arrangement that actually saves: P_VOUT3 falls from I x 3.34 V to I x 2.5/0.90 = I x 2.78 V, saving I x 0.56 V = 7.1 mW at VOUT3 (7.9 mW at the battery) at the 12.75 mA quiescent, proportionally more with signal.
findings.benefit: 7.9 mW at the battery at idle for the buck option, computed above (12.75 mA x 0.56 V / 0.90). Everything else in this analysis is 0 mW or negative. I am reporting it because 'the audio runs off a 75% efficient supply' invites exactly the wrong fix, and the arithmetic showing why is worth more than another part swap: the audio's battery cost is set by its CURRENT, not by the LDO's voltage ratio, which is precisely why the u7-tlv9364-out-of-spec finding above (an 8.25 mA current reduction) is worth four times more than replacing the LDO with a switcher.
findings.risk: The buck option is rejected, not recommended, and the reason is specific rather than general: VAUD is the full-scale reference for U9's PWM re-buffering, so any ripple on VAUD multiplies the audio signal directly — it is amplitude modulation, not additive noise, and it is not attenuated by anything downstream. The NCV8164's 85 dB at 1 kHz / 80 dB at 10 kHz PSRR and 9 uVrms output noise is what buys the AGBM's 'crystal clear audio' claim, and 9 uVrms against a 0.884 Vrms full scale is a -99.8 dB floor. A buck would also need an inductor in a shell that has no room and would sit near the ClockxControl window. Also worth knowing: the ClockxControl's extra 40-60 mA on VOUT3 raises the LTC3527's output ripple, but with 80 dB of LDO rejection at 10 kHz and the boost switching well above the audio band, that does not reach the audio — I checked and there is nothing to fix.
findings.verify_reason:
THE REASONING IS RIGHT AND USEFUL; THE ONE QUANTIFIED NUMBER INHERITS THE INFLATED OP-AMP CURRENT.

Every NCV8164 spec checks out against the onsemi datasheet text I extracted: operating input 1.6-5.5 V; output accuracy -2/+2%; IQ 30 uA typ / 40 uA max; shutdown 0.01 uA typ; dropout for the 2.5 V variant in TSOP-5 = 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA, and 113 mV typ for the 3.0 V variant (both exactly as stated); PSRR 83/85/80/61 dB at 100 Hz / 1 kHz / 10 kHz / 100 kHz; output noise 9 uVRMS over 10 Hz-100 kHz; 300 mA. One nit: those PSRR and noise figures are specified for the 3.3 V variant at IOUT = 10 mA, not for the 2.5 V variant. U4 and U8 are confirmed as the same NCV8164ASN250T1G off the same VOUT3 in the BOM. 2.5/3.34 = 74.9%, matching MBL's 'roughly 75%'. I confirmed VOUT3 independently: LTC3527 VFB = 1.20 V, R23 1.78M / R55 1.00M -> 1.20 x 2.78 = 3.336 V.

The three no-change conclusions are correct and worth keeping. (1) The LM4853's 2.4 V minimum really is the floor - verified. (2) An LDO passes its load current unchanged, so raising VAUD to 3.0 V saves nothing at the battery and costs a little: the bias networks scale as V/R and the class-AB supply power scales as Vdd x (2/pi)(Vp/RL) for the same loudness. Correct. (3) Merging U4 into U8 buys only U4's own 30 uA x 3.336/0.90 = 0.111 mW and puts the CPU core and SRAM switching current on the audio reference. Correct, and the reason given (VAUD is U9's PWM full-scale reference, so VAUD ripple is multiplicative on the audio, not additive) is the right reason to reject the buck.

CORRECTION: the buck saving is computed at a 12.75 mA quiescent that rests on 10.4 mA of TLV9364 current. TI's own Figure 5-22 puts the TLV9364 at ~1.40 mA/amp at VS = 2.5 V (see my u7 verdict), so the audio quiescent is ~7.7 mA at VAUD. Redoing the finding's own arithmetic: battery cost with the LDO = I x 3.336/0.90 = 3.707 x I; with a 90% buck = I x (2.5/0.90)/0.90 = 3.086 x I; delta = 0.621 V x I. At 7.7 mA that is 4.8 mW at the battery, not 7.9 mW. The finding's algebra is internally consistent (12.75 mA x 0.56 V = 7.14 mW at VOUT3, /0.90 = 7.93 mW) - only the current is wrong.

The closing claim that the ClockxControl's extra 40-60 mA on VOUT3 does not reach the audio is defensible given 80 dB of measured LDO rejection at 10 kHz, though it is asserted rather than measured. Correctly reported as 0 mW recommended.

findings.title: The LM4853 is running 50 mV above its absolute minimum supply and 200 mV below its lowest characterised point
findings.current_part: LM4853MM/NOPB, SNAS155E Operating Ratings: supply voltage 2.4 V <= VDD <= 5.5 V. The datasheet's Electrical Characteristics tables are given at 5.0 V, 3.3 V and 2.7 V only — there is no characterisation at 2.5 V. VAUD is 2.5 V nominal with +/-2% accuracy over load and temperature from the NCV8164, so the worst-case supply at the LM4853 is 2.45 V: 50 mV, or 2%, of margin to the absolute minimum operating rating, and 250 mV below the lowest voltage TI characterises. Extrapolating the datasheet trend (300 mW into 8 Ohm BTL and 25 mW into 32 Ohm SE at 2.7 V), the 2.5 V capability is roughly 250 mW BTL and 21 mW SE.
findings.proposal: Nothing to change, and I checked the alternatives before saying so. Raising VAUD costs power everywhere else (see vaud-rail-voltage-analysis). Replacing the LM4853 is impractical: its function set — mono BTL speaker plus stereo single-ended headphone plus automatic headphone-sense mode switching plus click-and-pop suppression, in a 10-pin 3 x 3 mm package — is unusual, and DigiKey lists LM4853MM/NOPB as Active with 2,871 in stock, so there is no sourcing pressure forcing the issue. What this finding is for is calibration: if a unit ever shows audio misbehaviour that tracks temperature or battery state, this 50 mV is where to look first, and TP22 (labelled BATT in the BOM but wired to VAUD) is the test point for it.
findings.benefit: 0 mW. The practical consequence is bounded and mild, because the gain structure keeps the amplifier nowhere near its limits: at maximum volume with full-scale content the BTL output needs 0.707 Vrms differential (62 mW into 8 Ohm) out of ~250 mW of capability, and the SE headphone output needs 0.177 Vrms (0.98 mW into 32 Ohm) out of ~21 mW. Thermally it is also fine: BTL worst-case internal dissipation is 4 x VDD^2/(2*pi^2*RL) = 4 x 6.25/(19.74 x 8) = 158 mW, which at the DGS package's 194 C/W is a 31 C rise.
findings.risk: The risk is silent, not catastrophic: below 2.4 V the part is simply unspecified, and the failure mode would be increased distortion or a failure to bias rather than damage. Because VAUD comes from a regulated LDO fed by a regulated boost, it does not sag with battery state until the LTC3527 itself drops out, so this is a component-tolerance stack-up risk (LDO at the -2% corner over temperature) rather than an end-of-battery risk.
findings.verify_reason:
THE STABILITY OBSERVATION IS CORRECT AND WORTH KEEPING; THE MAX-VOLUME NUMBER IS 4x TOO HIGH AND CONTRADICTS THE SAME ENGINEER'S CLASS-D FINDING.

Verified from SNAS155E: Operating Ratings 'Supply Voltage VDD 2.4V <= VDD <= 5.5V'. The Electrical Characteristics tables are given at VDD = 5.0 V, 3.3 V and 2.7 V - there is no 2.5 V table, exactly as claimed. NCV8164 output accuracy is -2/+2% over load and temperature (verified), so 2.45 V worst case, 50 mV above the absolute minimum. That part of the finding is airtight. LM4853MM/NOPB is Active with 2,861 in stock. The thermal calculation is right and I found the formula in the datasheet itself: 'PDMAX = 4 x (VDD)2/(2*pi*2 RL): Bridge Mode' (Equation 3), giving 4 x 6.25/(19.739 x 8) = 158 mW, and theta-JA for DGS = 194 C/W with TJMAX = 150 C, so a 30.7 C rise. Correct.

ERROR: 'at maximum volume with full-scale content the BTL output needs 0.707 Vrms differential (62 mW into 8 Ohm)'. I traced the gain structure from the netlist: U7 full scale 1.25 Vpk -> VR2 wiper -> C55/C56 -> R30/R31 100k into the LM4853 virtual ground with R56/R57 20k feedback -> gain -0.2 -> 0.25 Vpk single-ended -> 0.5 Vpk differential in BTL = 0.354 Vrms = 15.6 mW into 8 Ohm. The finding's own SE figure (0.177 Vrms, 0.98 mW into 32 Ohm) is correct and is exactly half the BTL voltage, which is the tell: the BTL number should be 0.354 Vrms / 15.6 mW, not 0.707 Vrms / 62 mW. Someone applied the BTL doubling and then a sqrt(2) that does not belong.

This makes the finding's own conclusion stronger, not weaker: 15.6 mW out of ~250 mW of extrapolated 2.5 V capability, i.e. 6% rather than 25%. It also means the classd-speaker-amp finding's 2.0 mW anchor and this finding's 62 mW cannot both be right - they differ by 31x for the same operating point.

Minor: the title says '200 mV below its lowest characterised point' and the body says '250 mV below'. Both are defensible readings (2.5 V nominal vs 2.45 V worst case) but they should not disagree inside one finding. The extrapolated 2.5 V capability (~250 mW BTL, ~21 mW SE) is correctly flagged as extrapolation from the 2.7 V data and I have no better source. The call not to replace the LM4853 is right - its function set (mono BTL plus stereo SE plus headphone-sense mode switching plus click-and-pop suppression in a 3x3 mm 10-pin) is genuinely unusual, and it is Active and stocked.

findings.title: Replacing the crystal with the ClockxControl puts the module's clock jitter straight onto the audio PWM edges
findings.current_part: The GBA's audio is pulse-width modulation: per GBATEK, in the default 9-bit / 32.768 kHz mode each sample N (0-511) is emitted as N low bits followed by (512-N) high bits at 16.78 MHz, so the audio sample value is encoded purely as an EDGE POSITION within a 30.5 us frame, quantised in 59.6 ns steps. U9 (SN74LVC2G34, tpd 1.5 ns typ / 4.4 ns max at VCC = 2.5 V per SCES359J) faithfully re-times those edges onto VAUD. On the fork X1, C3 and C4 are depopulated and /CPU/CK1 is driven by the ClockxControl instead, so the timing reference for those edges is now whatever the module generates rather than a 4.194304 MHz crystal.
findings.proposal: No board change; a measurement to make. Because the full-scale pulse width is 512 x 59.6 ns = 30.5 us, an RMS edge jitter of dt translates to an amplitude error of dt / 30.5 us relative to full scale: 1 ns RMS gives a -89.6 dB noise floor, 5 ns gives -75.7 dB, 10 ns gives -69.7 dB. A crystal contributes picoseconds and is irrelevant; a PLL- or DDS-based clock module can contribute nanoseconds, and if its jitter is correlated (PLL reference spurs) it appears as discrete tones rather than a noise floor. If the audio floor is audibly worse with JP3 closed than with the crystal fitted, this is the mechanism.
findings.benefit: 0 mW. UNVERIFIED — I could not find a published jitter specification for the insideGadgets ClockxControl, so the 1/5/10 ns figures above are illustrative scalings of the transfer function, not a claim about the module. The transfer function itself (edge jitter -> amplitude error = dt/30.5 us) follows directly from the GBATEK-documented PWM encoding and is solid.
findings.risk: If real, it degrades the AGBM's headline audio quality specifically when the ClockxControl is engaged, which would be blamed on the audio chain rather than on the clock source. It costs nothing to check: compare the noise floor at TP115/TP114 (the CPU's L-OUT/R-OUT) or at the headphone jack with JP3 open (crystal) versus closed (module) at 1x.
findings.verify_reason:
THE MECHANISM IS REAL BUT THE TRANSFER FUNCTION IS AN UPPER BOUND STATED AS AN EQUALITY, AND THE DESIGN-FILE PREMISE IS NOT IN THE FILES.

What verifies: GBATEK confirms the encoding word for word - 'these bits are output at system clock speed (16.78MHz)', '512 bits are output per sample (512*32K=16M)', and each sample is 'N low bits, followed by 512-N high bits'. So the sample value is an edge position quantised in 1/16.78 MHz = 59.6 ns steps within a 30.5 us frame. The scaling arithmetic is right: 1 ns / 30.5 us = 3.28e-5 = -89.7 dB; 5 ns = -75.7 dB; 10 ns = -69.7 dB. The finding is honest that it has no jitter figure for the insideGadgets module and marks the numbers illustrative.

SPEC NIT: SN74LVC2G34 SCES359J gives, at VCC = 2.5 V +/- 0.2 V over -40 to 85 C, tpd MIN 1.5 ns and MAX 4.4 ns. The finding calls these 'typ / max'. The numbers are right, the labels are not - and TI publishes no typical for this parameter.

SUBSTANTIVE CORRECTION: the stated transfer function (edge jitter dt -> amplitude error dt/30.5 us) only holds for jitter at frequencies comparable to or above the 32.768 kHz frame rate. The pulse width is bounded by TWO edges derived from the same clock. Low-frequency clock wander - which is what a PLL or DDS module mostly produces - stretches the whole frame, moving both edges together, so the pulse WIDTH as a fraction of the frame is preserved. That is sample-rate modulation (pitch wow), not an amplitude error, and it largely cancels in the mechanism described. So -89.6 / -75.7 / -69.7 dB are worst-case ceilings for high-frequency jitter, not the noise floor a given RMS jitter figure produces. The finding presents them as 'the transfer function itself ... is solid'; it is solid only for the high-frequency component.

PREMISE NOT SUPPORTED BY THE FILES: 'On the fork X1, C3 and C4 are depopulated'. I checked both boards. In x/agbm-01-ram-desalvage/AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus.kicad_pcb and in AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb, X1 (41.694, -56.785), C3 (45.9, -60.5) and C4 (45.9, -51.2) are all placed with attr 'smd' and NO dnp flag - the only DNP footprint on the board is NT1. JP3 does not exist in the fork repo at all; it exists only on the CXC board, at (45, -64.2), pad 1 on /CPU/CK1 and pad 2 on CXC_CLK, which is the correct topology for what the finding describes. The brief's own context pack asserts the depopulation, so this is a documentation gap in the fork rather than an invention by the engineer, but a reader following the finding to the design files will not find what it says is there.

The proposed diagnostic (compare the noise floor at the jack with JP3 open versus closed at 1x) is sound, free, and the right response to an unquantified mechanism. Confidence 0.4 is honest. Keep it as a note to measure, not as a finding.

findings.title: U8 (NCV8164, VDD2) has ~3.5x current margin and ~4x thermal margin at 1.75x — it is not the bottleneck
findings.current_part: U8 = NCV8164ASN250T1G, TSOP-5 (SOT-23-5 land), 2.5 V fixed, VIN = VOUT3 = 3.336 V. Verified from onsemi NCV8164/D rev.5: rated 300 mA; output current limit ICL 350 mA min / 560 mA typ at VOUT = 90 % VOUT(NOM); short-circuit current 580 mA; dropout for the 2.5 V variant in TSOP-5 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA; IQ 30 µA typ / 40 µA max at IOUT = 0; TSOP-5 thermal resistance RθJA = 158 °C/W (JEDEC 51.7 high-K board), RθJC(bot) 102 °C/W; TJ(max) 150 °C, datasheet recommends limiting TJ to 125 °C; thermal shutdown 165 °C; stable with any ceramic ≥ 1 µF with no minimum ESR and no stated maximum.
findings.proposal: No change. Keep U8 as fitted. The analysis: worst-case VDD2 draw at 1.75x is CPU core + SRAM = ~82 mA (see measured_anchors), i.e. 27 % of the 300 mA rating and 23 % of the 350 mA guaranteed current limit. If the true in-use I_VDD2 at 1x were double my estimate (94 mA rather than 47 mA), 1.75x would still only reach 165 mA and the part would still be inside its rating.
findings.benefit: Not an efficiency finding — this is the go/no-go answer. Current: I_VDD2(1.75x, game) = 1.75 × 47 mA = 82 mA vs a 300 mA rating and a 350 mA min current limit → 3.6x margin. Dropout: headroom is VOUT3 − VDD2 = 3.336 − 2.500 = 0.836 V; the 2.5 V part's dropout is 200 mV max at 300 mA, so at 82 mA (roughly proportional, ~55 mV) VOUT3 could sag to ~2.56 V before the LDO fell out of regulation — 780 mV of slack. Thermal, in a SOT-23-5: PD = (VIN − VOUT)·IOUT + VIN·IGND = 0.836 × 0.082 + 3.336 × 40 µA = 68.6 + 0.13 = 68.7 mW. ΔTj = 68.7 mW × 158 °C/W = 10.9 °C. Inside a sealed GBA shell take TA = 45 °C → Tj = 56 °C against a 125 °C recommended limit. At 1.75x idle (52.5 mA) it is PD = 43.9 mW, ΔTj = 6.9 °C. Even at the full 300 mA rating PD = 250.8 mW and ΔTj = 39.6 °C, so the part would still be inside spec at a 45 °C ambient. Output capacitance on VDD2 is ~14 µF nominal (C60 10 µF + 4×1 µF + 5×0.1 µF); the datasheet states stability with ceramics of '1 µF or greater' with no upper bound, so that is fine.
findings.risk: The residual risk is entirely in the I_VDD2 estimate, which is derived from the 170 mW idle figure and not measured. To close it, put a Fluke on TP18 (VDD2) — it is a plated test point — and read the current at 1x and at 1.75x with a game running. If I_VDD2 at 1.75x turns out above ~250 mA the picture changes, but nothing in the measured board power leaves room for that: 250 mA on VDD2 alone would be 625 mW, more than half the entire 1175 mW worst-case console power.
findings.verify_reason: Every NCV8164 number checks out against onsemi NCV8164/D Rev. 5 (March 2025), which I opened directly: 300 mA LDO; ICL 350 mA min / 560 mA typ at VOUT = 90% VOUT(NOM); ISC 580 mA; dropout for the 2.5 V TSOP-5 variant 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at IOUT = 300 mA; IQ 30 uA typ / 40 uA max at IOUT = 0; TSOP-5 RthJA 158 C/W, RthJC(bot) 102 C/W; TJ(max) 150 C with the datasheet text 'For reliable operation junction temperature should be limited to +125 C'; TSDH 165 C; 'The device is designed to be stable with standard ceramics capacitors with values of 1 uF or greater' and 'does not require a minimum ESR', no maximum stated. NCV8164ASN250T1G is in the ordering table (TSOP-5, 2.5 V, marking MP) and onsemi's product page lists it Active. TSOP-5 CASE 483 lands on the board's SOT-23-5 footprint, so the part-vs-footprint claim is right. I redid all the arithmetic: PD = 0.836 x 0.082 + 3.336 x 40u = 68.55 + 0.13 = 68.7 mW; dTj = 68.7 mW x 158 = 10.85 C; at 52.5 mA, 43.9 mW and 6.93 C; at the full 300 mA, 250.8 mW and 39.6 C. Dropout scaled from the 300 mA spec gives ~55 mV at 82 mA, leaving ~780 mV of headroom below the 3.336 V input (VOUT3 = 1.20 V FB x (1 + 1.78/1.00) = 3.336 V, confirmed from the LTC3527 FB spec and R23/R55). VDD2 output capacitance is 14.5 uF over ten parts (C60 10u + 4 x 1u + 5 x 0.1u), verified from the netlist. The one soft input is I_VDD2 = 47 mA, which is an estimate, but I reconciled it independently: 170 mW idle at the battery is ~150 mW at the rails, i.e. ~45 mA on VOUT3, of which VAUD and VDD3 plausibly take 10-20 mA, leaving 25-35 mA for VDD2 at idle. The go/no-go conclusion is sound and the margin is large enough that a 2x error in the estimate does not change it. Minor nit for the record: the 61 dB PSRR figure the engineer uses elsewhere is specified for the 3.3 V variant at IOUT = 10 mA, not the 2.5 V part.

findings.title: The constrained node is VOUT3, not the LDO: LTC3527 converter 2 (the 400 mA channel) carries all three logic rails while the 800 mA channel drives only the screen
findings.current_part: U5 = LTC3527, dual synchronous boost, QFN-16. Verified from ADI 35271fc: title 'Dual 800mA/400mA'; features 'Delivers 3.3V at 200mA/100mA from one Alkaline/NiMH Cell, or 3.3V at 400mA/200mA from Two Cells'; NMOS current limit SW1 = 800 mA (min, tested over temperature), NMOS current limit SW2 = 400 mA (min); NMOS/PMOS on-resistance SW1 0.30/0.40 Ω, SW2 0.50/0.60 Ω; MODE = Low is automatic Burst Mode, FSEL = Low is 1.2 MHz. On this board MODE and FSEL are both tied to GND, so it is 1.2 MHz auto-Burst. From the netlist: U5 pad 5 (VOUT1, converter 1) = VOUT5 → U11 → VDD5 → LCD FFC pin 34 (VSHA) and cart pad S2, nothing else. U5 pad 8 (VOUT2, converter 2) = VOUT3 → U8 (VDD2), U4 (VAUD) and U18 (VDD3). So the weaker channel carries CPU core, SRAM, all 3.3 V logic, the cartridge and the audio chain.
findings.proposal: No part change proposed — I checked the obvious one and it is wrong. Swapping the channel assignment (VOUT3 onto converter 1) looks attractive until you account for the screen: the measured spread between minimum and maximum brightness is 568→1175 mW at the battery, i.e. roughly 600 mW of backlight, which at 5.014 V is ~120–160 mA on VOUT5. Converter 1 at VIN 2.4 V is needed for that. The assignment as drawn is correct. What is actionable is documentation and a measurement: build sheet should state that a 1.75x build on 2×AA NiMH is operating converter 2 near its guaranteed limit at end of discharge, and TP16 (VOUT3) should be scoped for regulation loss under a worst-case load before anyone declares the mod stable. Raising L1/L2 above 4.7 µH would buy headroom (see benefit) but belongs to the passives reviewer and fights the LTC3527's internal compensation.
findings.benefit: Headroom arithmetic, guaranteed-silicon basis. Boost peak inductor current = Iin + ΔI/2, with Iin = Iout·VOUT/(η·VIN) and ΔI = VIN·D/(L·f), D = 1 − VIN/VOUT, L = 4.7 µH, f = 1.2 MHz, η = 0.9, VOUT = 3.336 V. At VIN = 2.4 V: D = 0.2805, ΔI = 119 mA, ΔI/2 = 60 mA, so Iin(max) = 400 − 60 = 340 mA and Iout(max) = 340 × 0.9 × 2.4/3.336 = 220 mA. At VIN = 2.0 V (the TPS3840DL20 cutoff): D = 0.4005, ΔI = 142 mA, Iin(max) = 329 mA, Iout(max) = 178 mA. At VIN = 3.2 V (fresh alkalines): 335 mA. This model reproduces the datasheet's own '3.3 V at 200 mA from two cells' headline, and the datasheet's Figure G11 (Maximum Output Current vs VIN for Converter 2) read off the VOUT = 3.3 V curve gives ~200 mA at 1.8 V, ~230 mA at 2.0 V, ~290 mA at 2.4 V — i.e. typical silicon is ~30 % above my min-spec numbers, as expected. Against that, my estimated VOUT3 draw at 1.75x: VDD2 82 mA + VAUD 15–40 mA + VDD3 (CPU I/O + logic + cart through VDD35) 37–60 mA + ClockxControl 12 mA = 146 mA typical to 194 mA worst case. So at 2.4 V there is 12–34 % margin on guaranteed silicon, and at the 2.0 V cutoff the worst case is over budget by ~10 %. Note the same worst case at 1x is ~147 mA, so the overclock is what consumes the last of the margin. Sizing L2 up from 4.7 µH to 10 µH would cut ΔI/2 from 60 to 28 mA and raise Iout(max) at 2.4 V from 220 to 241 mA (+10 %), at the cost of DCR and a part the LTC3527 is not compensated for.
findings.risk: Running converter 2 into current limit does not blow anything up — it drops out of regulation, VOUT3 sags, and VDD3 follows it directly (U18 is a switch, not a regulator). VDD2 rides it down until VOUT3 reaches ~2.56 V, so the CPU core survives longer than its I/O does; the symptom would be an I/O-level brown-out (cartridge read errors, then reset) near the end of the battery, at max volume, at max speed, under a demanding game — a combination that is hard to reproduce deliberately and easy to blame on the cart. My VOUT3 numbers are a build-up of estimates: the cartridge current in particular is unverified, and an Everdrive could plausibly be 30 mA or 80 mA. Confidence is set accordingly.
findings.verify_reason: The silicon facts and the peak-current model are all correct, but the VOUT3 load budget omits the display. Verified from ADI 35271fc and the ADI product page (status: PRODUCTION): title 'Dual 800mA/400mA, 1.2MHz/2.2MHz Synchronous...'; 'Delivers 3.3V at 200mA/100mA from one Alkaline/NiMH Cell, or 3.3V at 400mA/200mA from Two Cells'; NMOS current limit SW1 800 mA min and SW2 400 mA min (both carry the over-temperature test mark); NMOS/PMOS RDS(on) SW1 0.30/0.40 ohm, SW2 0.50/0.60 ohm; FB = 1.176/1.20/1.224 V; switching frequency 0.9/1.2/1.5 MHz at VFSEL = 0. From the board I confirmed U5 pin 3 MODE -> GND and pin 10 FSEL -> GND, pin 1 SHDN1 -> /PG_2V5, pin 12 SHDN2 -> /EN, pin 5 VOUT1 -> VOUT5, pin 8 VOUT2 -> VOUT3, and that VOUT3 feeds U8, U4 and U18. I re-derived every headroom number and they reproduce exactly: at VIN 2.4 V, D = 0.28058, dI = 119.4 mA, Iin(max) = 340 mA, Iout(max) = 220.1 mA; at 2.0 V, 177.5 mA; at 3.2 V, 335.4 mA. Figure G11 exists and is titled 'Maximum Output Current vs VIN for Converter 2' (35271 G11); reading the VOUT = 3.3 V curve off it gives roughly the values quoted, about 30% above the min-spec model, as claimed. TPS3840DL20 = 2.0 V threshold with 0.100 V hysteresis, confirmed from the TI device table.
findings.correction: The VOUT3 budget is missing the screen. U12 (TPS22917) has VIN on VDD3 and VOUT on /CPU/VSHD, and P2 (FFC) pins 2, 7 and 27 are VSHD - so the LCD's 3.3 V supply is on VDD3 -> VOUT3 -> converter 2, not on converter 1. The stated 146-194 mA therefore understates any build with a screen fitted, by whatever the screen's digital side draws (plausibly 20-40 mA for an IPS controller, unverified). That makes the finding's own concern worse, not better, so the 'no change, document and measure' conclusion still stands - but the numbers in the write-up should carry a VSHD line item. Two smaller corrections: (1) 'VDD5 goes to exactly two places' is loose - besides P2 pin 34 and P1 pad S2, VOUT5 also feeds R25 3.3k to the power LED (~0.9 mA), R10/R18/R65/R66 dividers and U14; immaterial but not 'nothing else'. (2) I independently confirmed the channel-assignment conclusion rather than taking it on trust: converter 1 at VIN 2.4 V gives Iout(max) = 689 x 0.9 x 2.4/5.014 = 297 mA at 5.014 V = 1.49 W, so it can carry the backlight; and if the ~600 mW backlight were on converter 2 the total VOUT3 draw would be ~327 mA, far beyond even typical silicon, yet the board demonstrably works at max brightness - so the backlight must be on converter 1 and the assignment as drawn is correct.

findings.title: U8's 0.836 V drop is the single biggest recoverable loss the overclock creates — a buck on VDD2 wins back 21 mW at 1x and 49 mW at 1.75x
findings.current_part: U8 = NCV8164ASN250T1G, a linear regulator dropping VOUT3 3.336 V to VDD2 2.500 V. Its loss is exactly (VIN − VOUT) × IOUT + VIN × IGND; with IQ 30 µA typ (onsemi NCV8164/D) the ground-current term is 0.10 mW and can be ignored. So the loss is 0.836 V × I_VDD2, i.e. 25.1 % of every watt VDD2 consumes, unconditionally. Note this is not the audio LDO — MouseBiteLabs explicitly defends U4/VAUD as a deliberate noise-driven choice ('roughly 75 % efficient ... specifically for the audio'). U8 feeds the digital core and SRAM, where switching ripple is far less consequential.
findings.proposal: TPS62840DLC. Verified from TI SLVSEC6D (rev. D, March 2020): 'Input voltage range VIN from 1.8 V to 6.5 V', 'Output current up to 750 mA', '60-nA operating quiescent current', typical switching frequency 1.8 MHz, 16 output voltages selected by one resistor on VSET; the Device Comparison Table gives TPS62840DLC as '1.8 V to 3.3 V in 100-mV steps', and the RSET table lists 2.5 V for the DLC part at RSET = 11.5 kΩ nominal (E96, 11.04 k min / 11.96 k max). Package DLC = 8-pin SON, 1.5 × 2 mm — smaller than the NCV8164's SOT-23-5 land, but not on the same pads. External parts needed: a 2.2 µH inductor, and input/output ceramics — of which the board already has 43 µF nominal on VOUT3 (C42 22 µF + C2 10 µF + C23 10 µF + C22 1 µF) and ~14 µF on VDD2 (C60 + 4×1 µF + 5×0.1 µF), so realistically the only genuinely new part is the inductor. Precedent for a switcher on this rail: Zekfoo's AGZ GBA redesign states 'the 3.3V and 2.5V rails are generated by buck converters'.
findings.benefit: At the operating point that matters. TI's Figure 22 (Efficiency, Power Save Mode, VOUT = 1.8 V) shows the VIN = 3.6 V curve sitting at ~87–89 % from 10 mA to 100 mA; our conversion is 3.336 → 2.500 V, a gentler 0.75 duty ratio than 3.6 → 1.8, so ≥89 % is a conservative read. The exact 3.34 → 2.5 V curve is not published, so 89 % is an interpolation, not a datasheet point.
