Arithmetic, all at VOUT3 then referred to the battery at the boost's 88 %: (a) 1x, in use, I_VDD2 = 47 mA → LDO input 156.8 mW, loss 39.3 mW; buck output 117.5 mW, input 132.0 mW, loss 14.5 mW; saving 24.8 mW at VOUT3 = 28.2 mW at the battery. (b) 1x idle, I_VDD2 = 30 mA → LDO loss 25.1 mW, buck loss 9.3 mW, saving 15.8 mW = 18.0 mW at the battery, which is 10.6 % of the entire measured 170 mW idle figure and roughly half of AGBM-01's 36 mW idle gap to a stock GBA. (c) 1.75x idle, 52.5 mA → LDO loss 43.9 mW, buck loss 16.2 mW, saving 27.7 mW = 31.5 mW at the battery. (d) 1.75x in a game, 82 mA → LDO loss 68.6 mW, buck loss 25.3 mW, saving 43.3 mW = 49.2 mW at the battery. Against a total overclock cost of ~146 mW at the battery (module 45.5 mW + console ~100 mW), (d) recovers about a third of it. Second-order benefit: it also gives back 13 mA of VOUT3 current at the worst case, which is exactly the margin the previous finding says is running out.
findings.risk: This is the invasive one. It needs a schematic change (new part, new VSET resistor, an inductor, different pinout) and a PCB revision on a board with no free area — and the one component-free window on the front is now spoken for by the ClockxControl itself. It puts a 1.8 MHz switcher on the CPU core rail: with 11 decoupling caps already on VDD2 that should be fine, and AGZ does exactly this, but it is a change from a field-proven arrangement on an irreplaceable salvaged CPU. It also overlaps the passives/power-tree reviewer's territory — the same argument applies to the AGBM-01-vs-AGBM-02 converter question and should be resolved once, not twice. Sourcing: TPS62840DLC is a current TI part in a 1.5 × 2 mm SON, which is harder to hand-solder than a SOT-23-5 and is a real cost for a hobbyist build. My benefit numbers inherit the ±20 % uncertainty in I_VDD2 and the interpolated 89 % efficiency.
findings.verify_reason:
The physics and the direction are right and the loss arithmetic is correct, but the proposal as written would produce a console that does not boot, and the efficiency figure is both wrongly cited and too pessimistic.

What holds: U8's loss really is (VIN - VOUT) x IOUT + VIN x IGND with a 0.836 V drop, i.e. 25.1% of everything VDD2 consumes; IQ 30 uA typ confirmed. TPS62840 is a real, ACTIVE TI part (I fetched ti.com/product/TPS62840): VIN 1.8-6.5 V, up to 750 mA, 60 nA operating IQ, ~1.8 MHz, DLC = VSON-HR SON-8, 1.5 x 2 mm (3 mm^2). Table 1 of SLVSEC6D confirms RSET = 11.5 k nominal (11.04 k min / 11.96 k max) selects 2.5 V on the TPS62840DLC, and the Device Comparison Table confirms 'TPS62840DLC, 1.8 V to 3.3 V in 100-mV steps, 750 mA, SON-8'. The board really does carry 43 uF on VOUT3 (C42 22u + C2 10u + C23 10u + C22 1u) and 14.5 uF on VDD2. The Zekfoo AGZ precedent is verbatim correct - I fetched the README: 'A boost converter supplies the 5V rail while the 3.3V and 2.5V rails are generated by buck converters.' And it is correctly graded as needing both a schematic change and a PCB revision, not a drop-in.

What breaks it: U8 pin 4 is PGOOD, and net /PG_2V5 is driven by nothing else. I dumped the net: /PG_2V5 = R8 (100k pull-up to VDD2), TP30, U18 pin 3 ON, U4 pin 3 SHDN, U5 pin 1 SHDN1, U8 pin 4 PGOOD. So U8's power-good is the board's master sequencing signal - it enables the VDD3 load switch, the audio LDO, and the LTC3527's 5 V channel that feeds the screen. The TPS62840 has no power-good pin in any package: TI's pin-function table gives the DLC 8 pins as GND(1), VIN(2), MODE(3), EN(4), VSET(5), STOP(6), SW(7), VOS(8), and TI's product page lists no PG. Substituting it as described leaves /PG_2V5 pulled up by R8 with nothing to release it correctly - no VDD3, no VAUD, no VOUT5. The swap needs an added supervisor (a fourth TPS3840, which this board already uses three times) plus its pull-up before it is buildable.
findings.correction: Three corrections. (1) SCOPE: add a VDD2 supervisor to regenerate /PG_2V5 (U8's PGOOD, which drives U18.ON, U4.SHDN and U5.SHDN1 - verified from the netlist). Without it the board is dead. Also, 'the only genuinely new part is the inductor' is wrong: TI's pin table says VIN 'A 4.7-uF ceramic capacitor is required' close to the pin, and the board's 43 uF sits at U5, not at U8 - so the real add is inductor + 11.5 k VSET resistor + local 4.7 uF VIN ceramic + supervisor + pull-up. (2) FIGURE: Figure 22 is 'Efficiency Power Save Mode, VOUT = 1.8 V for the DGR device'. The exact curve the finding says is unpublished IS published - Figure 18, 'Efficiency Power Save Mode, VOUT = 2.5 V, RSET = 11.5 kOhm to GND', for the DLC part, with VIN = 2.5/3.0/3.6/4.2/5.0/6.5 V curves bracketing our 3.336 V. I read it: at 30-100 mA the VIN = 3.0 V and 3.6 V curves sit at ~93-95%, not 89%. (3) NUMBERS: at a conservative 93% the savings are LARGER than claimed, all referred to the battery at 88% boost efficiency - 1x idle (30 mA): LDO 25.1 mW vs buck 5.6 mW, saving 19.4 mW at VOUT3 = 22.1 mW at the battery (13% of the measured 170 mW idle); 1x in use (47 mA): 39.3 vs 7.5, saving 31.8 = 36.1 mW; 1.75x idle (52.5 mA): 43.9 vs 9.9, saving 34.0 = 38.6 mW; 1.75x in a game (82 mA): 68.6 vs 15.4, saving 53.2 = 60.5 mW. All of this still inherits the unverified I_VDD2 estimates, which I independently sanity-checked against the 170 mW idle figure and found defensible to about +/-30%.

findings.title: insideGadgets' 40–60 mA is a system-level figure with no rail attribution, no speed and no measurement point — and it is quoted identically for DMG, GBC and GBA
findings.current_part: insideGadgets' product page, verbatim and complete, is one sentence: 'Consumes about 12mA of additional current and when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more.' Grammatically 'it' is the console, not the module. There is no statement of where the current was measured, at what speed, with what cartridge or screen fitted, or on which rail. The same number is given for the DMG (whose firmware goes to 3x), the GBC (2x) and the GBA (1.75x) — three different CPUs on three different rails, which alone is enough to treat it as an order-of-magnitude figure. I fetched the page directly (WebFetch returns 403; a plain curl with a browser user-agent returns 200) rather than relying on a search snippet.
findings.proposal: Split it into the two rails it actually lands on, which the netlist settles unambiguously. (1) The module's own ~12 mA: V+ is specified as 'GBA SI', which is the pad silkscreened S1, and on all three AGBM variants P1 pad S1 is on net VDD3. So the module's 12 mA is on VDD3, switched by U18 off VOUT3. (2) The overclock's extra current is not the module's at all — it is the console's own dynamic power, which lives on VDD2 (CPU core pins 44/65/115/117 and SRAM pins 12/16/37) and on VDD3 (CPU I/O pins 1/103/124 plus the cartridge, which reaches the cart through the CPU's VDD35 pin). Both rails sit under VOUT3, so all of it is converter 2's problem. Nothing lands on VOUT5/VDD5 except through the screen.
findings.benefit: Reconciliation, which is the point of the finding. Module, at 1x: 12 mA × 3.335 V = 40.0 mW at VDD3; at the boost's 88 %, 45.5 mW at the battery = 19.0 mA at 2.4 V. That is +27 % on the measured 170 mW idle before a single clock is added. Overclock, from my own per-rail model: ΔI_VDD2 = 0.75 × 30 mA = 22.5 mA, which the LDO passes 1:1 to VOUT3 → 22.5 × 3.336 = 75.1 mW → 85.3 mW at the battery; plus VDD3 I/O dynamic ~3.6 mA → 12.0 mW → 13.6 mW; plus the clock net's own C·V²·f = 1.2 mW. Total ≈ 100 mW = 42 mA at 2.4 V, rising to ~63 mA if the in-use base is 1.5× idle. insideGadgets' 40–60 mA brackets that, which is the strongest evidence I have that the 30 mA VDD2 anchor is right. Whole-mod cost at 1.75x: 45.5 + 100 ≈ 146 mW idle-basis, ~195 mW in a demanding game. Consequences: idle goes 170 → 316 mW, i.e. past the 288 mW Funnyplaying GBA the AGBM is designed to beat; battery life at the measured extremes goes 15h15m → ~11h14m (410 → 556 mW) and 5h20m → ~4h34m (1175 → 1370 mW).
findings.risk: None — this is a flag, not a change. The risk is in *not* flagging it: 40–60 mA read as a per-rail number would suggest the VDD2 LDO is near its limit, which it is not, and would under-count what the boost has to supply, which is where the actual margin problem is. If anyone reuses insideGadgets' number, they should know it is a single un-conditioned sentence covering three consoles.
findings.verify_reason: I fetched the insideGadgets page myself (curl with a browser user-agent, HTTP 200) and stripped the markup. The sentence is verbatim and is the page's only statement of current: 'Consumes about 12mA of additional current and when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more.' There is no measurement point, no speed, no cartridge or screen condition, and the same range is given for all three consoles, whose firmware tops out at 3x (DMG), 2x (GBC) and 1.75x (GBA) - all confirmed in the same page's firmware lists. Grammatically 'it' is the console. The install instructions are also verbatim: 'Device V+ to GBA SI', 'Device V+ to VCC pad as shown' (GBC), 'Device V+ to Capacitor +' (DMG). The rail attribution is correct on the board: P1 pad S1 is on VDD3 (netlist), VDD3 comes from U18 (TPS22917) off VOUT3, and U1's ONLY supply pins are VDD2 (44, 65, 115, 117), VDD3 (1, 103, 124) and VDD35 (38) - I dumped all 128 pads to check - so every milliamp the overclock adds is on converter 2. I redid all the arithmetic and it reproduces: 12 mA x 3.335 V = 40.0 mW, /0.88 = 45.5 mW, /2.4 V = 19.0 mA, = 26.8% of 170 mW; 0.75 x 30 mA = 22.5 mA x 3.336 = 75.1 mW -> 85.3 mW; total ~100 mW = 41.7 mA at 2.4 V; 170 + 146 = 316 mW; 15h15m x 410/556 = 11h14m; 5h20m x 1175/1370 = 4h34m. Two nits that do not change the verdict: the clock net's C.V^2.f of 1.2 mW implies ~15 pF, while the same engineer's own capacitance build-up elsewhere is ~20 pF (1.6 mW); and treating insideGadgets' 40-60 mA as corroboration for the 30 mA VDD2 anchor is mildly circular given the finding's whole thesis is that the number is unconditioned. Also 'GBA SI' -> pad S1 is an inference, not something insideGadgets state - but it is the only reading that makes sense for a supply pin, and P1.S1 = VDD3 is verified on all AGBM variants I checked.

findings.title: ECO-6 has C4 and R41 the wrong way round: C4 is NOT dangling with the crystal removed — it is still on CK2 through R41, and it costs ~2 mW at 1.75x
findings.current_part: From the netlist: X1 pad 2, R41 pad 2 and C4 pad 1 all share net 'Net-(C4-Pad1)'; R41 pad 1 is /CPU/CK2; C4 pad 2 is GND. R41 = 2.2 k 0603, C4 = 33 p 0603, C3 = 27 p 0603 (CK1 to GND), R1 = 1.5 M (CK1 to CK2). The CPU symbol declares pin 113 CLK1 as an input and pin 114 CLK2 as an output — a textbook Pierce inverter. Depopulating X1 therefore removes the crystal from between C4 and CK1, but leaves C4 hanging on the CPU's still-driven XOUT pin through R41. ECO-6/README.md says 'C4 (33 p) — do not populate. Dangling once the crystal is gone' and 'R41 (2.2 k) ... ends up driving nothing'. Both statements are backwards: with X1 out, R41 is the part with a dead end on one side, and C4 is the part still being charged and discharged every clock edge.
findings.proposal: Keep the recommendation (depopulate X1, C3, C4) but fix the reason in the ECO text, and add the alternative: depopulating R41 *instead of* C4 achieves the same isolation with one part, since R41 is the only remaining path from C4 to CK2. Either way, note in the build sheet that leaving C4 fitted is not free. R1 (1.5 M) may stay as ECO-6 says — with CK1 driven, the feedback path carries at most 3.3 V/1.5 M = 2.2 µA.
findings.benefit: C3, on CK1, is charged by the module's output driver from VDD3: P = C·V²·f = 27 pF × 3.3² × 7.34 MHz = 2.16 mW at 1.75x (1.23 mW at 1x). This also confirms ECO-6's own figure — it quotes 0.37 mA at 4.19 MHz, and C·V·f = 27 pF × 3.3 V × 4.194 MHz = 0.374 mA, correct. C4, on CK2, is charged by the CPU's own XOUT driver through R41: the unloaded figure is 33 pF × 3.3² × 7.34 MHz = 2.64 mW, de-rated by the RC (τ = 2.2 k × 33 p = 72.6 ns against a 68.1 ns half-period at 7.34 MHz, so the cap only reaches ~61 % of the swing) to roughly 1.6–2.6 mW. Depopulating both is therefore worth ~4.3 mW on the 3.3 V domain at 1.75x → 4.9 mW at the battery, and ~2.4 mW → 2.8 mW at 1x. Small, but it is free, it was already planned, and it is one of only two genuine efficiency levers this domain has.
findings.risk: Almost none — depopulating is the mod's own requirement for X1 and is the obvious consequence for C3/C4. The one caveat is that I have assumed the AGB CPU's oscillator block runs from the 3.3 V domain; there is no public datasheet for the part. If XIN/XOUT are actually on VDD2 (2.5 V) the numbers scale by (2.5/3.3)² = 0.574, i.e. 2.5 mW rather than 4.3 mW at 1.75x. The RC de-rating on C4 is an approximation, not an exact integration.
findings.verify_reason: The topology claim is exactly right and I verified it from the board netlist and the footprint dump: X1 pad 2, R41 pad 2 and C4 pad 1 all sit on Net-(C4-Pad1); R41 pad 1 is /CPU/CK2 (which also carries U1 pin 114 CLK2, R1 pad 2 and TP81); C4 pad 2 is GND. /CPU/CK1 carries C3 pad 2, R1 pad 1, TP80, U1 pin 113 CLK1 and X1 pad 1. So with X1 depopulated, R41 is the part with a dead end and C4 is still hung on the CPU's driven XOUT pin through 2.2 k. I also verified the ECO text being corrected, verbatim, in clockxcontrol-integration/README.md lines 118-123: 'C4 (33 p) - do not populate. Dangling once the crystal is gone.' and 'R41 (2.2 k) ... ends up driving nothing.' Both are backwards, as claimed. The arithmetic reproduces: C3 27 pF x 3.3^2 x 7.34 MHz = 2.16 mW (1.23 mW at 4.194 MHz); the internal cross-check against the ECO's own 0.37 mA figure works (27 pF x 3.3 V x 4.194 MHz = 0.374 mA); C4 unloaded 33 pF x 3.3^2 x 7.34 MHz = 2.64 mW, RC-derated (tau = 72.6 ns vs a 68.1 ns half-period) to roughly 1.6-2.6 mW; total ~4.3 mW on the 3.3 V domain at 1.75x = 4.9 mW at the battery, ~2.4 -> 2.8 mW at 1x. R1's leakage bound (3.3 V / 1.5 M = 2.2 uA) is right. Two honest caveats the finding already declares: the AGB oscillator's supply rail is unverified (if XIN/XOUT are on VDD2 the numbers scale by 0.574), and the RC derate is an approximation. One thing worth saying plainly that the finding soft-pedals: the ECO already instructs the builder to depopulate C3 and C4, so the incremental saving over the planned build is zero - the 2.8/4.9 mW is what you lose by leaving them in, not a new lever. The correctness half of the finding (fix the reason in the ECO text; note that depopulating R41 alone achieves the same isolation) is the real content and it is right.

findings.title: The 67.5 mm B.Cu clock run is referenced to five different In2.Cu power islands in turn, and injects its return current into the LCD's own analogue rail for 32.6 mm of it
findings.current_part: Measured out of AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb. CXC_CLK is 73.5 mm total at 0.25 mm width: 6.0 mm on F.Cu, 67.5 mm on B.Cu, two F.Cu↔B.Cu vias at (47.45, −59.60) and (97.90, −38.60). The stackup in the board file is F.Cu / 0.100 mm prepreg / In1.Cu / 0.840 mm core / In2.Cu / 0.100 mm prepreg / B.Cu, so an F.Cu track is referenced to In1.Cu (which carries only GND and AGND zones) but a B.Cu track is referenced to In2.Cu, which carries GND, VDD2, VDD3, VDD35, VDD5, VOUT5, VAUD, VCC and /CPU/LGND zones. Sampling the B.Cu run at 0.25 mm intervals against the filled In2.Cu polygons: 32.6 mm sits over VDD5, 13.2 mm over VDD3, 8.8 mm over VDD35, 5.4 mm over no copper at all, 5.0 mm over VDD2 and only 2.4 mm over GND. The nearest GND via to either layer-change via is 2.44 mm and 2.47 mm away.
findings.proposal: Two options, in order of preference. (a) Re-reference: move as much of the run as possible onto F.Cu, where In1.Cu gives it a single continuous GND reference for its whole length. The router chose B.Cu because the cartridge keepout (which forbids pads and footprints but explicitly permits tracks) is empty; that is a routing convenience, not an electrical one. (b) If the run must stay on B.Cu, add 100 nF 0402/0603 stitching capacitors from the crossed rail to GND within ~2 mm of each In2.Cu boundary the run crosses, and add GND stitching vias adjacent to both layer-change vias so the return has a low-inductance hop between In1.Cu and In2.Cu. Either way, narrow the track from 0.25 mm to 0.15 mm while redrawing — it raises Z0 from 42 to 57 Ω and drops the run's capacitance from 10.9 to 7.8 pF, worth 0.25 mW at 1.75x, which is rounding error but free.
findings.benefit: Magnitude, honestly stated: the injected current is small but its spectral content is not. The run's capacitance to its reference is 0.148 pF/mm (Z0 = 42.0 Ω, εeff = 3.477, computed from the board's own stackup with εr 4.5), so the 32.6 mm over VDD5 presents 4.8 pF to the LCD's analogue rail. With a 3.3 V swing and an assumed 2 ns edge (dV/dt = 1.65 V/ns) that is 4.8 pF × 1.65 V/ns = 7.9 mA of peak displacement current into the VDD5 plane at every edge, twice per cycle; the time-average is only 4.8 pF × 3.3 V × 2 × 7.34 MHz = 0.23 mA, but the peak is what lands on the screen. VDD5 goes to exactly two places — P2 pin 34 (VSHA, the LCD's analogue supply) and cart pad S2 — so this is being coupled into the most display-sensitive rail on the board. That matters here specifically because insideGadgets already document screen trouble at speed: the FunnyPlaying laminated IPS 'fades to black' at 1.5x, and the OneChip IPS and GBC FP IPS are reported glitchy. I am not claiming the return path is the cause — but it is a mechanism the board is introducing that the field-proven flying-wire install does not have, and it costs nothing to avoid while the ECO is still on paper. Separately, the 5.4 mm stretch with no In2.Cu copper under it sees Z0 jump from 42 to 118 Ω (reference falls back to In1.Cu at 0.975 mm); electrically that is a 34 ps discontinuity and is irrelevant for timing, but it is 5.4 mm with nowhere local for the return to go.
findings.risk: The 2 ns edge is an assumption — insideGadgets publish no output characteristics for the module — and everything scales linearly with dV/dt, so a 5 ns edge cuts the peak to 3.2 mA. The coupling estimate assumes the In2.Cu island is the dominant return, which the 0.1 mm dielectric makes overwhelmingly likely. Option (a) may simply not be routable on a front side this congested; option (b) costs board area for capacitors in a band that is already tight, and the ECO has 0 new DRC violations today which any re-route has to preserve. This is a quality/EMI finding with no measurement behind it, hence the confidence.
findings.verify_reason: I re-measured everything from AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb rather than trusting the write-up, and it reproduces to the last decimal. CXC_CLK: 5.996 mm on F.Cu + 67.464 mm on B.Cu = 73.46 mm, all at 0.25 mm width, two F.Cu/B.Cu vias at exactly (47.45, -59.60) and (97.90, -38.60). Stackup as stated: F.Cu 0.035 / prepreg 0.100 (epsilon_r 4.5) / In1.Cu / core 0.840 / In2.Cu / prepreg 0.100 / B.Cu. In1.Cu carries exactly two zone nets (GND, AGND); In2.Cu carries exactly the nine listed (GND, VDD2, VDD3, VDD35, VDD5, VOUT5, VAUD, VCC, /CPU/LGND). I sampled the B.Cu centreline against the filled In2.Cu polygons at 0.05 mm and got VDD5 32.59, VDD3 13.13, VDD35 8.88, no copper 5.48, VDD2 5.02, GND 2.37 mm - versus the claimed 32.6/13.2/8.8/5.4/5.0/2.4. Nearest GND via to the two layer-change vias: 2.442 mm and 2.470 mm (claimed 2.44 and 2.47). Hammerstad reproduces: epsilon_eff 3.4766, Z0 42.05 ohm, 0.1479 pF/mm, 6.22 ps/mm; over the 0.975 mm fallback, epsilon_eff 3.042 and Z0 118.4 ohm; at 0.15 mm width, 57.14 ohm and 0.1066 pF/mm, so the narrowing saves 3.05 pF and 0.244 mW at 1.75x. The 32.6 mm over VDD5 is 4.82 pF, giving 7.95 mA peak at an assumed 1.65 V/ns and 0.23 mA time-average. VDD5's only real destinations are P2 pin 34 (VSHA) and P1 pad S2. The routing rationale is also verified: the B.Cu cart keepout (x 33.1-105.1, y -54.2 to -32.2) is (tracks allowed)(vias allowed)(pads not_allowed)(footprints not_allowed), so tracks are indeed permitted there.
findings.correction: Two corrections, neither fatal. (1) Proposal (a)'s premise is not exact. I sampled In1.Cu under the full 73.46 mm path: it is GND for 68.18 mm and absent for 5.28 mm. There is an all-layer rule area (F.Cu/In1.Cu/In2.Cu/B.Cu, x 40.4-130.0, y -48.6 to -33.6) with copperpour not_allowed around the cart slot, so the same gap exists on In1.Cu. Moving to F.Cu buys a single continuous GND reference for 68.2 of 73.5 mm, not 'its whole length' - still a large improvement over six reference changes, but say it accurately. (2) The 'most display-sensitive rail' framing is the weakest part. VDD5/VSHA is the stock AGB LCD's analogue bias; most IPS replacement kits regenerate their own rails and may leave FFC pin 34 unconnected, in which case VDD5 is a lightly-loaded island rather than the screen's supply, and the rhetorical link to insideGadgets' reported IPS glitches at speed weakens accordingly (the finding does concede it is not claiming causation). Also 'a 34 ps discontinuity' is loose phrasing: 33.6 ps is the transit time of that 5.4 mm stretch; the delay difference against the 42 ohm sections is about 2 ps. Immaterial, as stated.

findings.title: CXC_CLK is an unterminated 42 Ω, 73.5 mm line into a capacitive far end — add a series-resistor land at TP83 so overshoot into the salvaged CPU's XIN can be clamped
findings.current_part: CXC_CLK as routed: 73.5 mm of 0.25 mm track 0.1 mm over a plane. From the board's stackup, Hammerstad gives εeff = 3.477, Z0 = 42.0 Ω, 6.22 ps/mm — so one-way delay is 457 ps and the round trip is 914 ps. The far end is the CPU's XIN (U1 pin 113, declared 'CLK1 input' in the schematic symbol) plus the existing 22.9 mm of CK1 copper (3.4 pF) with C3 depopulated, so a capacitive load of roughly 8–9 pF including an assumed 5 pF of CPU input. There is no series element anywhere on the net — the only components on CK1 are R1 1.5 M to CK2 and, on a crystal build, X1/C3. The module's output impedance and edge rate are not published by insideGadgets.
findings.proposal: Add a 0603 land in series with CXC_CLK immediately adjacent to TP83 (the CLK wire pad at 97.900, −37.950), i.e. at the source end of the board's run — the wire from the module's CLK pad to TP83 is only 3.8 mm, so a resistor there really is at the source. Populate 0 Ω by default so the board is electrically identical to today's ECO, and specify in the build sheet: scope CK1 at TP80 with the module fitted and running at 1.75x; if the positive peak exceeds VDD3 + 0.3 V, fit 22–33 Ω. Source-series termination is the correct topology here because the driver is at one end and the only load is at the other.
findings.benefit: Stability, not power. The rule of thumb is that a line needs termination when the driver's rise time is shorter than twice the one-way delay, which here is 914 ps. If the module's edge is faster than that, the line behaves as a transmission line: with an assumed 15 Ω CMOS driver into 42 Ω the initial step is 3.3 × 42/(42+15) = 2.43 V, which doubles at the open/capacitive far end to 4.86 V — 1.56 V above VDD3, enough to forward-bias the CPU's input ESD clamp on an irreplaceable salvaged part. Adding Rs = 27 Ω makes the source impedance 42 Ω, the initial step 1.65 V, and the far-end sum exactly 3.3 V with no overshoot. The RC cost of doing so is negligible: 33 Ω into the line's 10.9 pF plus ~8 pF of load gives τ = 0.63 ns and a 10–90 % time of ~1.4 ns, against a 136 ns period at 7.34 MHz. Worth noting the board's route is capacitively *worse* than the stock install it replaces: 10.9 pF of PCB run against roughly 2.5–5 pF for 40–60 mm of flying wire (~0.5–1 pF/cm in air), so the on-board version costs about 0.5–0.7 mW more at 1.75x and presents a lower-impedance, more reflective line.
findings.risk: The whole case rests on an unpublished parameter — if the module's driver is slow (say 5 ns) or already has an internal series resistor, the line is electrically short and the resistor does nothing. That is precisely why the proposal is a 0 Ω land plus a measurement, not a specified value: the downside of the land is one 0603 footprint and a solder joint, the downside of getting it wrong is a damaged CPU that cannot be bought. The counter-evidence is that the stock 40–60 mm flying-wire install is field-proven and would have a *higher* line impedance (~100–150 Ω for a wire over a board) and therefore a larger initial step — which suggests either the driver is slow or people are living with overshoot they have never looked at.
findings.verify_reason: Every measurable input checks out. From the board file: Z0 = 42.05 ohm and 6.22 ps/mm from the actual stackup, so 457 ps one-way and 914 ps round trip on 73.46 mm; /CPU/CK1 copper on the ECO board is 22.91 mm (17.89 mm stock + the 5.0 mm ECO addition to JP3 pad 1) = 3.39 pF; TP83 is at exactly (97.900, -37.950) and the ECO's 3.8 mm wire length to the module's CLK pad is in the write-up's own table; there is no series element on CK1 - the net is C3 pad 2, R1 pad 1, TP80, U1 pin 113 CLK1, X1 pad 1, plus JP3 pad 1 on the ECO board. The termination arithmetic reproduces: 3.3 x 42/57 = 2.43 V initial step, 4.86 V at an open far end, 1.56 V of overshoot; Rs = 27 ohm gives a 42 ohm source, a 1.65 V step and a 3.3 V far-end sum; 33 ohm into ~18.9 pF gives tau = 0.62 ns and t(10-90) ~1.4 ns against a 136 ns period; the on-board route's extra ~7 pF over a flying wire costs 0.56 mW at 1.75x. So nothing here is factually wrong.
findings.correction: Scale it down and fix two things. (1) The far end is not open - it is roughly 8.4 pF (3.39 pF of CK1 copper + an assumed 5 pF CPU input), and Z0 x C = 42 x 8.4 pF = 353 ps is comparable to the 457 ps one-way delay. That damps and slews the reflection, so the ideal-open 4.86 V is an upper bound, not an expectation; the real overshoot is meaningfully smaller. (2) This finding and clk-return-path-patchwork contradict each other: one sizes Rs for a 42 ohm line, the other proposes narrowing the track to 0.15 mm / 57 ohm. If both are adopted the resistor must be ~42 ohm, not 27. (3) Substantively this is a generic transmission-line principle applied to an unpublished driver - the impedance, the edge rate and the CPU input capacitance are all assumptions, as the finding admits. The actionable residue is exactly what it proposes and no more: a 0603 land at TP83 populated 0 ohm by default, plus a build-sheet instruction to scope CK1 at TP80. That costs one footprint and is worth doing on a board with an irreplaceable salvaged CPU, but it should not be presented at the same weight as the measured findings, and 0.5 confidence is if anything generous.

findings.title: 33.3 mm of the clock run sits 0.25 mm from /CPU/TP9 on B.Cu — checked, and it is benign because TP9 is AC-grounded by C64
findings.current_part: Measured from the ECO board file: sampling CXC_CLK at 0.1 mm intervals and taking the edge-to-edge gap to the nearest same-layer track of each other net, 33.3 mm of the 73.5 mm run has a /CPU/TP9 track within 0.5 mm, with a minimum gap of 0.250 mm. GND is the only other net within 0.5 mm and only for 2.7 mm. This is an artefact of the ECO's own maze router, which routed CXC_CLK and the three button nets together through the same B.Cu corridor in the cartridge keepout. TP9's own network on this board is R44 15 Ω in series from SW2, C64 0.01 µF directly from /CPU/TP9 to GND, plus U15 pin 6 (SN74LVC1G332 input) and the CPU.
findings.proposal: No change required, but when the 169 maze-router segments are redrawn by hand (which ECO-6 §6.3 already flags as a cosmetic to-do), pull the clock away from TP9 to ≥0.5 mm at no routing cost. Do not spend a re-route on this alone.
findings.benefit: The numbers say leave it. For two 0.25 mm coplanar tracks 0.25 mm apart over a plane only 0.1 mm below, the plane takes almost all the field: mutual capacitance is on the order of 1–3 % of the line's self-capacitance, so Cm ≈ 0.02 × 0.148 pF/mm × 33.3 mm ≈ 0.1 pF (an estimate from the geometry, not a datasheet figure). At an assumed 1.65 V/ns edge that injects Cm·dV/dt ≈ 0.17 mA into TP9. C64's 0.01 µF presents 1/(2π × 7.34 MHz × 10 nF) = 2.2 Ω at the fundamental and far less at the edge's spectral content, so the disturbance at the CPU end is well under a millivolt; even at the module end, where the node looks like the 42 Ω trace, it is ~7 mV. Against a logic threshold of order 1.5 V that is 200x of margin. Coupling in the reverse direction is a non-issue: TP9 is a DC button line that only changes when a finger moves.
findings.risk: None from leaving it. The estimate of Cm is a geometric approximation rather than a field solve, so it could be out by 2–3x and the conclusion would not change. The one thing this does *not* cover is coupling to nets on other layers directly above or below the run, which is the return-path finding, not this one.
findings.verify_reason: I re-ran the proximity measurement independently: sampling CXC_CLK at 0.1 mm and taking edge-to-edge gaps to same-layer tracks of other nets, 31.99 mm of the run has a /CPU/TP9 track within 0.5 mm, with a minimum gap of 0.250 mm; GND accounts for 2.68 mm at 0.249 mm. The finding says 33.3 mm and 2.7 mm - about 4% high on the TP9 figure, direction and magnitude right. TP9's network is as described: R44 15 ohm in series from SW2, C64 0.01 uF from /CPU/TP9 to GND, U15 (SN74LVC1G332) pin 6, and the CPU - all confirmed from the netlist and BOM. The coupling estimate is declared as a geometric approximation rather than a datasheet number, which is the honest call: Cm ~0.1 pF over 33 mm with the plane only 0.1 mm below is the right order, 0.1 pF x 1.65 V/ns = 0.165 mA, and 0.165 mA x 42 ohm = 6.9 mV at the module end. Conclusion (benign, do not spend a re-route on it, pull it clear when the maze-router segments are redrawn by hand) is correct. Two nits: 'GND is the only other net within 0.5 mm' is not quite true - 0.48 mm of /~{VCNT5} sits at a 0.488 mm gap; and 'C64 presents 2.2 ohm at the fundamental and far less at the edge's spectral content' is wrong in the second half, since above a 10 nF 0603's self-resonance the impedance rises back toward ~1 ohm rather than falling. Neither changes the answer: the disturbance stays sub-millivolt at the CPU against a ~1.5 V threshold.

findings.title: No decoupling capacitor at the module's V+/V− pads — and TP84/TP85 happen to sit 1.55 mm apart, which is an 0603 land
findings.current_part: From ECO-6 §6.5, TP84 (V+, net VDD3) is at (99.450, −37.950) and TP85 (V−, GND) at (101.000, −37.950), ø1.2 mm pads. There is no capacitor between them and none anywhere near the module: the nearest VDD3 bypass caps (C5, C34, C39, C43, C49, C50, C69) are all in the CPU corner. VDD3 reaches TP84 through 7.0 mm of track and 2 vias from P1 pad S1, then 5.9 mm of user-supplied wire to the module. TPS22917 Rds(on) is 90 mΩ typ / 110 mΩ max at VIN = 3.6 V, 200 mA, 25 °C (TI SLVSDS4).
findings.proposal: Add an 0603 capacitor footprint bridging TP84 and TP85. The KiCad C_0603_1608Metric land has its pads 1.575 mm centre-to-centre; TP84 and TP85 are 1.550 mm apart, so the geometry already almost is one — a 0.1 µF X7R (and, if there is room, a 1 µF alongside) drops straight in, and on the board as it stands today a capacitor can be tack-soldered across the two existing pads by hand without any board change at all. Do this at the same time as any other edit; it does not justify a spin on its own.
findings.benefit: Transient, not average. The module's driver has to charge the board's clock capacitance every edge: 73.5 mm of run at 0.148 pF/mm = 10.9 pF, plus the existing CK1 copper 22.9 mm = 3.4 pF, plus the 3.8 mm wire ≈ 0.4 pF, plus an assumed 5 pF of CPU input ≈ 20 pF total. At an assumed 2 ns edge that is 20 pF × 1.65 V/ns = 33 mA of peak supply current at every transition, 14.7 million times a second at 1.75x. The feed inductance is roughly 5.9 nH (wire, ~1 nH/mm) + 1.8 nH (7.0 mm of 42 Ω track, L = Z0·√εeff/c = 0.261 nH/mm) + ~2.4 nH (two full-stack vias) ≈ 10 nH, so L·di/dt = 10 nH × 33 mA/2 ns = 165 mV of droop on the module's own V+ at each edge, which is jitter on the clock it is generating. A 0.1 µF within 2 mm of the module's pads removes essentially all of it. Average power is unaffected — this buys clock quality, not milliwatts.
findings.risk: Honestly: the field-proven stock install is *worse* than this and works. It uses 40–60 mm of flying wire, i.e. roughly 50 nH, which by the same arithmetic would be ~800 mV — so either the module already carries substantial local decoupling or its edges are much slower than 2 ns. Either explanation means this is a nice-to-have. What tilts it is that the board route triples the capacitive load on the driver compared with the flying-wire install (20 pF vs ~8 pF), so the peak current this board asks for is genuinely larger than the one insideGadgets validated. Both the 2 ns edge and the 5 pF CPU input are unverified assumptions.
findings.verify_reason: The geometry is right - better than claimed, in fact - but the benefit is overstated because the cap cannot reach the inductance that dominates. Verified from the board file: TP84 at (99.450, -37.950) on VDD3 and TP85 at (101.000, -37.950) on GND, both o1.2 mm SMD pads, 1.550 mm apart; no capacitor anywhere near them. TPS22917 numbers verified from TI SLVSDS4: RON at VIN = 3.6 V, IOUT = 200 mA, 25 C is 90 mOhm typ / 110 mOhm max (and 140 mOhm at 85 C, which is the number that matters in a sealed shell). The capacitance build-up reproduces: 73.46 mm x 0.1479 = 10.87 pF, plus 22.91 mm of CK1 = 3.39 pF, plus ~0.4 pF of wire, plus an assumed 5 pF of CPU input = 19.7 pF; 19.7 pF x 1.65 V/ns = 32.5 mA; the track inductance 0.261 nH/mm x 7.0 mm = 1.83 nH is right (L = Z0 x sqrt(eps_eff)/c).
findings.correction: Two fixes, one in the finding's favour and one against. (1) In its favour: this board's own 0603 cap land (Bucketmouse:C_0603_1608Metric_Boxed_2) has pads at +/-0.775 mm, i.e. 1.550 mm centre-to-centre - an EXACT match to the TP84/TP85 spacing, not 'the KiCad 1.575 mm land, so almost'. A 0603 drops straight on, and on the existing board it can be hand-tacked with no board change at all. (2) Against it: a cap at TP84/TP85 is still 5.9 mm of V+ wire and 4.7 mm of GND-return wire away from the module - roughly 10.6 nH of the loop that the capacitor cannot short. It removes only the ~4.2 nH of on-board track plus vias, so it cuts the droop by about a third, not 'essentially all of it'. The finding's own 10 nH figure is also low because it omits the GND-return wire; counted properly the baseline is ~15 nH and ~250 mV, falling to ~175 mV with the cap fitted. Genuinely fixing the module's local supply requires the capacitor on the module, not on the board - and the insideGadgets product photo shows the module already carries chip passives beside its controller, which is consistent with the finding's own observation that the field-proven flying-wire install works with far more feed inductance. Keep the footprint (it is free), drop the claim that it removes the problem, and keep the 0 mW power claim - that part is correctly stated.

findings.title: VDD3 is the correct rail for the module — U18's pass element costs 13 µW at 12 mA, and every alternative is worse
findings.current_part: U18 = TPS22917DBV load switch, SOT-23-6, VOUT3 → VDD3, enabled by /PG_2V5. Verified from TI SLVSDS4: input operating range 1 V to 5.5 V, maximum continuous current 2 A, ON-resistance 90 mΩ typ / 110 mΩ max at VIN = 3.6 V and IOUT = 200 mA and 25 °C (80/100 mΩ at 5 V, 120/150 mΩ at 1.8 V), quiescent current 0.5 µA typ enabled, shutdown 10 nA, θJA 183 °C/W in DBV. The module's V+ lands on P1 pad S1, which the netlist puts on VDD3 on AGBM-01, -02 and -11 alike.
findings.proposal: No change. Keep V+ on VDD3 via P1 pad S1 / TP84, exactly as insideGadgets specify and as ECO-6 has drawn it. The alternatives, checked: VOUT3 directly (bypassing U18) saves the switch's loss but gives up the property that the module powers down with the console — and the loss it saves is 13 µW. VDD5 (5.014 V) would make the module dissipate 51 % more for the same load current if it regulates internally, and there is no evidence it needs more than 3.3 V on a GBA. VBATT is upstream of SW1, so tapping it would give the module a permanent standby drain on the pack and would present it with 1.8–3.2 V, below any plausible minimum. There is no pre-boost rail that survives the power switch, so there is no way to avoid paying boost efficiency on the module's current.
findings.benefit: Quantified so the reviewer can stop wondering about it. Through U18 at 12 mA: V drop = 12 mA × 0.090 Ω = 1.08 mV (1.32 mV at the 110 mΩ max), so VDD3 = 3.3349 V, and the dissipation is I²R = 0.012² × 0.090 = 13 µW — five thousand times smaller than the module's own consumption and utterly invisible against a 170 mW idle board. The chain cost that actually matters is the boost: 12 mA × 3.335 V = 40.0 mW at the rail, /0.88 = 45.5 mW at the battery = 19.0 mA at 2.4 V. That is the irreducible price of fitting the module, and no rail choice available on this board changes it by more than a few tens of microwatts. One consequence worth noting: at 43 mA of idle VOUT3 current the LTC3527's converter 2 is already well past its Burst-Mode threshold (datasheet Figure G14 puts it around 15–18 mA for VOUT = 3.3 V at VIN 2.4 V), so adding the module does not change the converter's operating mode and there is no mode-related saving to chase.
findings.risk: One genuine unknown: the module's supply range and whether it has an internal regulator are not published. The only evidence is circumstantial and comes from the install instructions themselves — GBA V+ goes to S1 (3.3 V), while the GBC instruction is 'Device V+ to VCC pad' and the DMG instruction is 'Device V+ to Capacitor +', both 5 V domains. A part specified across 3.3 V and 5 V hosts must either be a wide-Vdd design or carry its own regulator. Since 3.3 V is the vendor's own GBA answer, this is not a risk to act on, but it is unverified.
findings.verify_reason: Every TPS22917 number checks out against TI SLVSDS4, which I read directly: input operating range 1 V to 5.5 V; maximum continuous current 2 A; RON 90 mOhm typ / 110 mOhm max at VIN = 3.6 V, IOUT = 200 mA, 25 C (80/100 at 5 V, 120/150 at 1.8 V, 170/220 at 1.2 V, 220/300 at 1 V); IQ 0.5 uA typ / 1.0 uA max enabled; shutdown 10 nA; junction-to-ambient thermal resistance 183 C/W. The arithmetic reproduces exactly: 12 mA x 0.090 = 1.08 mV drop (1.32 mV at max), I^2R = 13.0 uW; 12 mA x 3.335 V = 40.0 mW at the rail, /0.88 = 45.5 mW at the battery = 19.0 mA at 2.4 V. The rail attribution is verified on the board (P1 pad S1 -> VDD3; U18 VIN = VOUT3, VOUT/QOD = VDD3, ON = /PG_2V5). The alternatives analysis holds: VOUT5 = 1.20 V x (1 + 1.78/0.56) = 5.014 V computed from the LTC3527's verified 1.20 V FB and R21/R22, so a 51% higher dissipation for the same current is right; SW1 is upstream of PTC1/VCC so VBATT really is pre-switch; and there is no pre-boost rail that survives the power switch. Figure G14 exists ('Burst Mode Threshold Current vs VIN for VOUT1 = VOUT2 = 3.3 V', y-axis 0-25 mA over VIN 1.2-3.0 V), and the conclusion is robust to any plausible reading of it - 43 mA of idle VOUT3 current is far past a 15-25 mA threshold either way. The GBC and DMG install quotes are verbatim correct; I fetched the page. Two nits: at an 85 C in-shell junction RON is 140 mOhm, so the loss is 20 uW rather than 13 uW - still five thousand times smaller than the module's own draw, so the conclusion is untouched; and the module's supply range genuinely is unpublished, exactly as the risk section says.

findings.title: U2 (CY62157EV30LL-45) is comfortable at 1.75x: 2.3x timing margin, valid at 2.5 V, and only +0.7 to +2.4 mA of extra VDD2 current
findings.current_part: U2 on the ECO-5 fork is a CY62157EV30LL-45ZXI, 8 Mbit (512K × 16) async SRAM. Verified from Infineon 38-05445 rev *S: 'Wide voltage range: 2.20 V to 3.60 V'; Operating Range table gives Industrial/Automotive-A as −40 to +85 °C at 2.2 V to 3.6 V; Product Portfolio lists VCC min 2.2 / typ 3.0 / max 3.6 with 45 ns speed; ICC at f = 1 MHz is 6 mA typ / 7 mA max, and at f = fmax = 1/tRC is 18 mA typ / 25 mA max; ISB2 standby 2 µA typ / 8 µA max. Critically, the Switching Characteristics table is headed 'Over the Operating Range', so the 45 ns access time is guaranteed at 2.5 V, not only at the 3.0 V typical. On this board its VCC pins (12, 16, 37) are on VDD2 = 2.500 V.
findings.proposal: No change. This is one place where the ECO-5 de-salvage is a straight win over a salvaged original AGB WRAM, and the ClockxControl makes it more of one.
findings.benefit: Timing: the GBA service manual confirms the CPU multiplies the crystal by 4 in GBA mode, so 7.34 MHz in gives a 29.36 MHz core. A 3-cycle 16-bit EWRAM access is therefore 102 ns against the part's 45 ns rating — 2.3x margin, versus 4.0x at stock 16.78 MHz. Current: ICC is essentially linear in address-toggle rate between the two datasheet points, ICC ≈ 6 + 0.566·(f − 1) mA (typ) or 7 + 0.849·(f − 1) mA (max), for f in MHz. Bounding the access rate: 100 % EWRAM utilisation at stock is 16.78/3 = 5.59 M accesses/s → ICC 8.6 mA typ; at 1.75x it is 9.79 M/s → 11.0 mA typ (14.5 mA max-spec). So the absolute worst case the overclock adds on the SRAM's account is +2.4 mA on VDD2, and at a realistic ~30 % EWRAM duty it is +0.7 mA. Either way it is a small fraction of the ~22 mA that the CPU core adds, and it does not move the LDO analysis. Referred to the battery, the SRAM's worst-case increment is 2.4 mA × 3.336 V / 0.88 = 9.1 mW.
findings.risk: None from leaving it. Two caveats on the numbers: the linear ICC-vs-frequency interpolation between 1 MHz and fmax is my construction, not a datasheet curve (the datasheet gives only the two endpoints); and the EWRAM access model assumes the GBA's default 2-wait-state 16-bit external bus, which games can and do change. Neither changes the conclusion, because even the datasheet's own fmax figure of 25 mA max is small against the VDD2 budget.
findings.verify_reason: Every datasheet number checks out against Infineon 38-05445 for the CY62157EV30LL, which I read directly: 'Wide voltage range: 2.20 V to 3.60 V'; the Operating Range table gives Industrial/Automotive-A as -40 C to +85 C at 2.2 V to 3.6 V; ICC at f = fmax = 1/tRC is 18 mA typ / 25 mA max and at f = 1 MHz is 6 mA typ / 7 mA max; ISB2 is 2 uA typ / 8 uA max; the speed grade is 45 ns; and critically both the Electrical Characteristics and the Switching Characteristics tables are headed 'Over the Operating Range', so the 45 ns access time really is guaranteed at 2.5 V. ECO-5 confirms U2 is CY62157EV30LL-45ZXI(T), and the netlist confirms its VCC pins 12/16/37 land on VDD2 = 2.500 V, comfortably above the 2.2 V minimum. I also verified the clock-multiplier claim at source rather than taking it on trust: the Nintendo AGB service manual PDF at the cited iFixit URL, section 2.4 System Timer, says 'The CPU multiplies this signal by 4 to operate on the GBA mode (16,776MHz), or multiplies by 2 for GB' - so 7.34 MHz in gives 29.36 MHz. All the arithmetic reproduces: 3 cycles at 29.36 MHz = 102.2 ns against 45 ns = 2.27x (vs 178.8 ns = 3.97x at stock); the linear ICC fit slopes are 12/21.2 = 0.566 mA/MHz typ and 18/21.2 = 0.849 max with fmax = 1/45 ns = 22.2 MHz; 16.78/3 = 5.59 and 29.36/3 = 9.79 M accesses/s giving 8.60 and 10.97 mA typ, i.e. +2.4 mA worst case; and 2.4 mA x 3.336 V / 0.88 = 9.1 mW at the battery (correct, because the LDO passes VDD2 current 1:1 to VOUT3). The two caveats the finding declares - that the linear ICC interpolation is its own construction and that the EWRAM access model assumes the default wait states - are real and correctly flagged, and neither moves the conclusion since even the datasheet's own 25 mA max at fmax is small against the VDD2 budget.

findings.title: JP3 is the right call, but the stub it isolates is ~11 pF and ~58 ppm, not the ~5 pF and ~40 ppm ECO-6 states
findings.current_part: ECO-6 §6.5 justifies JP3 by saying an ungated CK1 run would be 'roughly 5 pF of added load (about 40 ppm of frequency error) plus a 73 mm antenna'. Computing it from the board's actual stackup instead: a 0.25 mm track 0.1 mm over a plane has εeff = 3.477 and Z0 = 42.0 Ω, giving C = √εeff/(c·Z0) = 0.148 pF/mm. The 73.5 mm run is therefore 10.9 pF, about twice the ECO's estimate. With JP3 open, only the 5.0 mm from CK1 to JP3 pad 1 remains, i.e. 0.74 pF.
findings.proposal: No design change — JP3 stays exactly as drawn, default-open. Correct the number in the ECO text, because it is the number the design decision rests on and it is understated by 2x in the conservative direction.
findings.benefit: Pull calculation, for a 4.194304 MHz crystal with the board's C3 = 27 p / C4 = 33 p load network and assumed C0 = 3 pF, C1 = 15 fF (typical for a fundamental-mode 4 MHz crystal; the AGB part has no published datasheet, so this is an assumption). Nominal CL = (27 × 33)/(27 + 33) = 14.85 pF. Ungated, +10.9 pF on the XIN side takes CL to 17.64 pF, ΔCL = 2.79 pF, and Δf/f = −C1·ΔCL/(2(C0+CL)²) ≈ −58 ppm. Gated, the 0.74 pF residual gives ΔCL = 0.22 pF and Δf/f ≈ −5 ppm. So JP3 turns a 58 ppm pull into a 5 ppm one, and a 73 mm antenna on the oscillator's high-impedance node into a 5 mm stub. The ECO's conclusion is right and now has the right magnitude behind it. Zero power implication either way — this is about not breaking crystal builds.
findings.risk: None. The crystal constants C0 and C1 are assumed, so the ppm figures could be off by a factor of two in either direction; the capacitance figure is computed from the board file and the stackup and is solid. The practical instruction is unchanged: leave JP3 open unless the module is fitted.
findings.verify_reason: The ECO text being corrected is verbatim what the finding quotes - ECO-6_clockxcontrol_footprint.md lines 213-214: 'roughly 5 pF of added load (about 40 ppm of frequency error) plus a 73 mm antenna into the one node that must not be disturbed.' The corrected capacitance is computed from the board's own stackup and I reproduced it exactly: epsilon_eff = 3.4766, Z0 = 42.05 ohm, C = sqrt(eps_eff)/(c x Z0) = 0.1479 pF/mm, so the 73.46 mm run is 10.87 pF - about twice the ECO's estimate, in the direction the finding says. I also confirmed the JP3-open residual by measuring /CPU/CK1 copper on both boards: 17.89 mm on the pre-ECO fork and 22.91 mm on the CXC board, i.e. exactly the 5.0 mm the ECO's routing table claims, = 0.74 pF. JP3 is at (45.000, -64.200) with 1.05 mm pads, as stated, and its two pads sit on CXC_CLK and /CPU/CK1. The pull arithmetic reproduces with the standard formula: CL(nom) = 27x33/60 = 14.85 pF; ungated CL = 37.9x33/70.9 = 17.64 pF; delta_f/f = (C1/2)(1/(C0+CL1) - 1/(C0+CL2)) = 0.0075 x (1/17.85 - 1/20.64) = 56.8 ppm, and 5.1 ppm gated - matching the quoted 58 and 5. C0 = 3 pF and C1 = 15 fF are assumptions with no public AGB crystal datasheet, correctly declared, and the ppm figures scale linearly with C1 so they could be out by 2x either way; the capacitance figure itself is solid. Design conclusion unchanged: JP3 stays default-open, and the ECO text should carry the corrected number since it is the number the design decision rests on.

findings.title: What the overclock asks of VDD2 decoupling: the bulk is fine, the requirement moves from 16.8 to 29.4 MHz, and the burden is entirely on the ceramics' ESL
findings.current_part: VDD2 carries C60 10 µF 0603, C45–C48 4 × 1 µF 0603, and C8/C15/C16/C52/C53 5 × 0.1 µF 0603 — 14.5 µF nominal across 10 parts, plus the LDO. The NCV8164 datasheet states the part is 'stable with standard ceramics capacitors with values of 1 µF or greater' and does not impose a maximum or a minimum ESR, so the count is not a stability problem for U8.
findings.proposal: No change requested from this domain — this is the requirement statement the passives reviewer should size against, so the two audits do not contradict each other. (1) Bulk: unchanged and comfortable. (2) High frequency: the CPU's core-current spectrum moves from a 16.78 MHz fundamental to 29.36 MHz, and the current amplitude rises 1.75x, so the useful decoupling is whatever is still capacitive at ~30 MHz and above. Every 0603 on this rail is above its self-resonance well before 30 MHz, so above SRF the network's impedance is set purely by mounted inductance and the number of parts in parallel, not by capacitance. The right lever is therefore more, shorter-loop parts (and 0402 rather than 0603 where a footprint can be changed), not more microfarads. (3) The 10 µF 0603 (C60) should be checked for DC bias derating at 2.5 V — that is a passives-audit item but it is the one part carrying the bulk transient budget.
findings.benefit: Sizing arithmetic. Charge drawn per clock cycle at 1.75x with I_VDD2 = 82 mA: Q = I/f = 82 mA / 29.36 MHz = 2.8 nC. Against even a heavily derated 5 µF of effective bulk that is ΔV = Q/C = 0.56 mV, so the low-frequency side is a non-issue — the rail cannot droop meaningfully between clock edges. The LDO contributes nothing at these frequencies: its PSRR is specified at 61 dB at 100 kHz and falling, and its loop bandwidth is orders of magnitude below 30 MHz, so 100 % of the cycle-by-cycle charge comes from the ceramics. Setting a target: to hold the rail within 25 mV (1 % of 2.5 V) against a 1.75x-scaled transient of, say, 50 mA of AC content, the network needs ≤0.5 Ω at 30 MHz, which ten parallel 0603s clear with a large margin even taken as pure inductors. So the existing array is adequate; the point of the finding is that the *reason* it is adequate changes at 1.75x, from capacitance to parallelism.
findings.risk: I have deliberately not quoted a self-resonant frequency or an ESL for any specific 0603, because I could not verify one from a manufacturer datasheet and the whole review depends on not inventing datasheet numbers. That means my '≤0.5 Ω at 30 MHz' claim is a target rather than a verified achievement — the passives reviewer should confirm it against the actual MPNs with a manufacturer impedance curve. The transient AC amplitude (50 mA) is an assumption; nothing in the measured board power constrains it.
findings.verify_reason: As a requirement statement rather than a change, this survives. The VDD2 inventory is verified from the netlist - C60 10 uF, C45-C48 4 x 1 uF, C8/C15/C16/C52/C53 5 x 0.1 uF, all 0603, 14.5 uF over ten parts - and the stability claim is verified verbatim in onsemi NCV8164/D Rev. 5: 'The NCV8164 does not require a minimum Equivalent Series Resistance (ESR) for the output capacitor. The device is designed to be stable with standard ceramics capacitors with values of 1 uF or greater', with no upper bound stated, so ten parallel ceramics is not a stability problem for U8. The sizing arithmetic reproduces: Q = 0.082/29.36e6 = 2.79 nC, and 2.79 nC across even a heavily derated 5 uF is 0.56 mV, so the bulk side is genuinely a non-issue and the requirement really does move to parallelism above self-resonance. The frequency claim is right by inspection: a 0.1 uF 0603 with ~1 nH of mounted inductance self-resonates near 16 MHz and a 1 uF near 5 MHz, so every part on the rail is inductive by 30 MHz, and ten of them in parallel taken as pure inductors give ~0.02-0.04 ohm at 30 MHz - the 0.5 ohm target is cleared by more than an order of magnitude. The finding's decision not to quote an ESL or SRF it could not verify from a manufacturer curve is the right call under the rules, and it says so. One correction to the reasoning, not the conclusion: PSRR is input-to-output rejection, not a measure of loop bandwidth, so citing 61 dB at 100 kHz (which is in any case specified for the 3.3 V variant at IOUT = 10 mA) does not establish that the LDO contributes nothing at 30 MHz - the correct argument is simply that the control loop's bandwidth is orders of magnitude below 30 MHz, which the finding also states and which is true. The 50 mA AC transient amplitude is an assumption and is flagged as one.

findings.title: VDD35 has no driver anywhere in the netlist, so the cartridge's supply path — and therefore where the overclock's cart current is billed — cannot be traced from the design files
findings.current_part: Every pad on VDD35 is a load, a bypass or a connector: C6/C7/C17 (0.1 µF), C51 (1 µF), EM3 pad 1 (MH1608-601Y ferrite, whose other side goes to the link port's VDD via P4 pin 1), P1 pin 1 and pad C1 (cartridge VDD), R2 10 k to /CPU/RES, R35 100 k, and U1 pin 38. The CPU symbol declares pin 38 as 'VDD35', pin type power_in. There is no regulator, load switch, ferrite-from-another-rail or zero-ohm link feeding this net on AGBM-01, and grepping the schematics finds VDD35 only as power symbols inside the CPU sheet. The board is field-proven, so it evidently works — which means either the AGB CPU sources the cartridge rail internally out of pin 38 (in which case the symbol's power_in type is wrong and KiCad ERC should be reporting a power net with no driver), or the rail is fed from somewhere I have not found.
findings.proposal: No change to the copper. Two things to do: (a) run ERC on the schematic and see whether it flags VDD35, and if the CPU really does source it, change pin 38's type to power_out or add a PWR_FLAG so the check is meaningful; (b) resolve where the cartridge current is actually billed before anyone relies on the VOUT3 budget above.
findings.benefit: This is not a saving, it is the largest single source of uncertainty in my VOUT3 headroom finding. If VDD35 is generated inside the CPU from VDD3, then every milliamp a cartridge draws lands on VDD3 → U18 → VOUT3 → converter 2, and the cart is one of the three big consumers competing for the ~220 mA that channel can guarantee at 2.4 V. If it comes from somewhere else, the VOUT3 budget improves by however much the cart draws — plausibly 30–60 mA for an Everdrive, which is 15–27 % of converter 2's guaranteed capability and is the difference between the worst case being comfortable and being over budget. Since a 1.75x build is precisely the configuration that pushes converter 2, this needs to be settled with a meter on TP16 rather than reasoned about.
findings.risk: There is a real chance this is simply a symbol-typing artefact of MouseBiteLabs' AGB-CPU library part rather than a design issue — the board demonstrably works and stock GBAs have always fed the cartridge through the CPU. Reporting it because the instruction is to flag things that look wrong even when they are not upgrades, and because in this case the ambiguity propagates into a real margin calculation. No action beyond a meter and an ERC run is warranted.
findings.verify_reason: The netlist observation is exactly right and worth flagging; the consequence drawn from it is not. I dumped the net myself: VDD35 has ten pads and every one is a load, a bypass or a connector - C6/C7/C17 0.1 uF, C51 1 uF, EM3 pad 1 (MH1608-601Y, other side to P4 pin 1 via Net-(P4-VDD35)), P1 pin 1 and pad C1, R2 10 k to /CPU/RES, R35 100 k, and U1 pin 38 declared VDD35. There is no regulator, load switch, ferrite-from-another-rail or zero-ohm link feeding it, and grep confirms VDD35 appears only in CPU.kicad_sch. So the ERC/pin-type flag is legitimate and the recommendation to run ERC and either retype pin 38 or add a PWR_FLAG is fair.
findings.correction: The claim that this is 'the largest single source of uncertainty in my VOUT3 headroom finding' does not survive, and neither does the 30-60 mA swing it implies. I dumped all 128 pads of U1: its only supply pins are VDD2 (44, 65, 115, 117), VDD3 (1, 103, 124) and VDD35 (38), plus GND. Since the netlist is exhaustive and there is literally no other net on VDD35, every path into VDD35 - and therefore every milliamp the cartridge draws - must come through U1's VDD3 and VDD2 pins, both of which are fed from VOUT3. So the cartridge current is billed to converter 2 regardless of how VDD35 is generated internally; the 'if it comes from somewhere else, the VOUT3 budget improves' branch is not a live possibility. The genuine uncertainty is the MAGNITUDE of the cart current (an Everdrive could plausibly be 30 or 80 mA), not which rail it lands on, and that is settled with a meter on TP16, not with an ERC run. Downgrade this to what it is: a symbol-typing defect worth fixing for hygiene, with no bearing on the power budget.

findings.title: ECO-5 fork: RAM VCC (U2 pin 37) sits on an isolated VDD2 island - the RAM has no supply
findings.current_part: AGB-SRAM / CY62157EV30LL on the ECO-5 extended U2 footprint, F.Cu. Pin 37 (VCC) has three pads at (95.10,-58.05), (98.97,-58.05) and (100.31,-58.05), joined by an F.Cu track (98.9575,-58.05)->(95.10,-58.05). They land on an isolated F.Cu VDD2 zone island of 6.89 mm2, bbox x[99.0,101.8] y[-58.9,-54.7]. Verified from AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus.kicad_pcb and from AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb: there is no VDD2 via anywhere with x > 93 in either file, and no VDD2 track leaves that island. The stock AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_pcb has VDD2 vias at (100.8,-56.6) and (100.8,-55.2) which tie that island to the In2 VDD2 plane; the fork deleted both (via-set diff stock vs fork: removed (100.3,-53.3) GND, (101.0,-61.25) GND, (100.8,-62.15) Net-(Q5B-G), (100.8,-56.6) VDD2, (100.8,-55.2) VDD2; nothing added). Separately, C8 (0.1u, the pin-37 decoupler) was relocated to (103.0,-64.9); its VDD2 pad at (102.22,-64.90) sits over the F.Cu GND pour with no VDD2 copper touching it, and the three stock F.Cu tracks that fed it were deleted.
findings.proposal: No part change. Restore two 0.3 mm vias in the F.Cu VDD2 island at approximately (100.8,-56.6) and (100.8,-55.2) - the exact stock coordinates - to reconnect it to the In2 VDD2 plane (which extends to x=101.8 at that y, verified by plane profiling), and route C8's VDD2 pad back to that island. Then re-pour In2. The fork's own README lists this as deliberately left for the interactive router; that is accurate but it means the board as committed will not boot.
findings.benefit: Not an energy finding. Without it the RAM's VCC pin 37 is open: I_VDD2 through that pin is 0 mA and the chip is powered only through pins 12/16 (which ARE connected - the F.Cu VDD2 zone x[74.3,86.0] reaches them and vias at (83.227,-56.074) and (83.4,-45.9) tie it to the In2 plane, verified). On the original GBA SRAM pins 12/16/37 are all VCC, so the part may partially work and behave erratically; on the CY62157 the pin-37 open removes one of the two VCC pins.
findings.risk: Zero risk to fix. Not fixing it: the board is unbuildable or intermittently unstable, and the failure mode (a floating supply pin on a salvaged/expensive RAM) is exactly the kind that looks like a bad solder joint. Note also the F.Cu VDD2 island only extends to x=101.8 while the In2 VDD2 plane ends at x=101.8 too - the vias must land inside both, which (100.8,-55.2)/(100.8,-56.6) do.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced every geometric claim independently from the .kicad_pcb files. Via-set diff stock vs fork is exactly the five stated vias removed, nothing added: (100.3,-53.3) GND, (101.0,-61.25) GND, (100.8,-62.15) Net-(Q5B-G), (100.8,-56.6) VDD2, (100.8,-55.2) VDD2. VDD2 via inventory: stock 16, fork 14, CXC 12 — and NO VDD2 via with x>93 in fork or CXC. U2 pad 37 exists three times at (95.100,-58.050), (98.968,-58.050), (100.310,-58.050); the F.Cu VDD2 island is 6.888 mm2, bbox x[98.968,101.800] y[-58.925,-54.700]; shapely confirms both proposed via sites (100.8,-56.6) and (100.8,-55.2) lie inside BOTH that island and the In2 VDD2 plane (468.04 mm2), so the proposal is geometrically valid. The stock F.Cu tracks feeding C8's old pad — (100.081,-58.525)->(100.081,-56.900), (100.349,-58.525)->(100.800,-58.525), (100.800,-58.525)->(100.081,-58.525) — are present in stock and absent in fork/CXC. C8 old pad1 (100.800,-58.525) vs new pad1 (102.225,-64.900), which sits over the F.Cu GND pour with no VDD2 copper touching it. Pins 12/16 ARE fed: tracks reach (81.302,-58.050) and (81.310,-56.050) from the x[74.34,86.00] F.Cu zone via (83.2273,-56.074), which is inside both that zone and the In2 plane. TWO CORRECTIONS, both making it WORSE than stated. (1) The severity claim 'the pin-37 open removes one of the two VCC pins' and 'the chip is powered only through pins 12/16' is wrong. On the 48-pin TSOP-I CY62157EV30 the pinout is pin 12 = CE2, pin 16 = A18, pin 37 = Vcc — pin 37 is the ONLY Vcc pin, so the part has no supply at all and the board is dead, not 'erratic'. MouseBiteLabs' own footprint agrees: the pinfunction strings on U2 are 12='CE2', 16='NC/VCC', 37='VCC'. (2) The zone fills are byte-identical across stock/fork/CXC, i.e. nobody re-poured after the edit — the orphan island is stale fill, and a re-pour with island removal enabled would delete it, leaving pad 37 on bare laminate. Verdict stands; the fix (restore the two vias at the exact stock coordinates, re-route C8, re-pour In2) is correct as written.

findings.title: ECO-5 fork: a signal via removal has open-circuited Net-(Q5B-G) - the battery-low LED control
findings.current_part: Net-(Q5B-G) connects U17 (TPS3840DL20 supervisor) pad 1 /RESET at (103.04,-54.25) to Q5 (NDC7002N) pad 3 at (102.36,-62.15) and R66 (100k pull-up to VOUT5) pad 2 at (99.42,-62.10). The route is: B.Cu from U17 to (104.3819,-53.3), via at (104.38,-53.30), then 10.56 mm of trace ON THE In1.Cu GROUND PLANE LAYER from (104.3819,-53.3) to (100.8,-62.15), then a via at (100.8,-62.15) back to B.Cu for Q5 and R66. The fork deleted the via at (100.8,-62.15) (confirmed by via-set diff against agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_pcb; both files still contain the In1.Cu segments and the (104.38,-53.30) via).
findings.proposal: Restore the 0.7/0.3 mm via at (100.8,-62.15) on net Net-(Q5B-G). While there, consider re-routing this net off In1.Cu entirely - it is one of 314.1 mm of signal routing that the design puts on the In1 ground plane, each mm of which is a slot in the return path.
findings.benefit: Not an energy finding. As drawn, U17's /RESET output cannot pull Q5B's gate down; R66 holds the gate at VOUT5 so Q5B is permanently on and the low-battery (red) LED indication is broken. This is not mentioned in the fork's README, which lists only five GND stitching vias.
findings.risk: Zero risk to fix. The wider point is that this net is routed inside the GND plane, so any future edit near U2 can silently break it again - moving it to B.Cu removes that trap.
findings.verify_reason: Verified directly. Net-(Q5B-G) segment set is byte-for-byte identical in stock and fork (B.Cu U17->(104.382,-53.300); In1.Cu (104.382,-53.300)->(104.400,-53.318)->(104.400,-58.917)->(101.167,-62.150)->(100.800,-62.150), total 10.57 mm on the GROUND PLANE layer; B.Cu (100.800,-62.150)->(102.362,-62.150) to Q5 pad 3 and ->(99.475,-62.150)->(99.425,-62.100) to R66 pad 2). The via at (100.800,-62.150) is present in stock and absent in BOTH fork and CXC. Pad coordinates confirmed exactly: U17 pad 1 (~RESET) at (103.038,-54.250), Q5 pad 3 at (102.362,-62.150), R66 pad 2 at (99.425,-62.100). Functional consequence independently confirmed: TI's TPS3840 datasheet states TPS3840DL = 'open-drain, active-low (RESET), requires pull-up resistor', VIT- = 2.0 V for the -20 suffix — so R66 (100k to VOUT5) is that pull-up and U17 can only ever pull the node DOWN. With the via gone the pull-down is orphaned, Q5B's gate is held at VOUT5, Q5B is permanently on, and Net-(Q5B-D) is clamped low. Net-(Q5B-D) is U14 pin 3, and U14 is a Microchip MIC1551/53 IttyBitty RC 555-type timer whose pin 3 is the active-low chip-select/reset (pinout T/T, GND, CS, VS, OUT matches). So the blinking low-battery oscillator is permanently held in reset and the schematic's 'Low battery detect circuit' / 'Blinking low power LED circuit' never fires. Divider R58 5.1k / R63 100k means the trip point is ~2.10 V at the pack. Zero-risk fix, correctly specified.

findings.title: PTC1 is at its derated hold current before the overclock and over it after - swap 0805L075 for 0805L110 (drop-in)
findings.current_part: PTC1 = Littelfuse 0805L075SLYR (schematic value), footprint Fuse_0805_2012Metric, in series VBATT -> VCC, i.e. carrying the entire battery current (note SW1 does NOT carry load current - it only gates /EN; VCC is permanently fed through PTC1, verified from the pad-level net map: VCC = {C37.1, L1.1, L2.1, PTC1.2, TP32, U5 VIN1/VIN2/VIN}). Littelfuse 0805L datasheet (rev GD 06/20/24): Ihold 0.75 A, Itrip 1.50 A, Vmax 6 Vdc, Rmin 0.090 Ohm, R1max 0.350 Ohm (max resistance measured one hour after trip or 260 °C reflow). Hold-current temperature rerating table, same datasheet: 0.75 A at 20 °C, 0.63 A at 40 °C, 0.57 A at 50 °C, 0.53 A at 60 °C.
findings.proposal: Littelfuse 0805L110 (part number 0805L110WR), same 0805 land, same Vmax 6 Vdc: Ihold 1.10 A, Itrip 2.00 A, Imax 100 A, Rmin 0.050 Ohm, R1max 0.160 Ohm; rerated hold current 0.92 A at 40 °C, 0.84 A at 50 °C, 0.75 A at 60 °C. All values from the same Littelfuse 0805L datasheet table. Intermediate option if the protection level matters more: 0805L100 (Ihold 1.00 A, Rmin 0.060, R1max 0.210 Ohm, 0.82 A at 40 °C).
findings.benefit: TRIP MARGIN (the real reason to do it). Worst-case battery current: 1175 mW at a 1.9 V end-of-life pack = 618 mA; the ClockxControl's own 12 mA at VDD3 costs 12 mA x 3.336 V / (0.88 x 0.95) = 48 mW = 25 mA at 1.9 V; insideGadgets' +40-60 mA when overclocked. Total ~700 mA. The 0805L075's hold current at a 40 °C internal shell temperature is 0.63 A, so 700 mA is 11% ABOVE hold and it will self-heat into trip; at 50 °C (0.57 A) it is 23% above. Even without the overclock, 618 mA vs 0.63 A is already on the line. The 0805L110 at 40 °C holds 0.92 A - 700 mA is 76% of that, a normal design margin. ENERGY, secondary: at the typical in-use point (800 mW at 2.4 V = 333 mA), I^2 x Rmin = 0.333^2 x 0.090 = 10.0 mW and I^2 x R1max = 0.333^2 x 0.350 = 38.8 mW. With the 0805L110: 0.333^2 x 0.050 = 5.5 mW to 0.333^2 x 0.160 = 17.7 mW. Saving = 4.5 mW (both parts at their minimum resistance) to 21.1 mW (both at their post-reflow maximum). I quote the midpoint ~10 mW and stress that the datasheet gives no typical, only Rmin and R1max, so the true value is anywhere in that band. Overclocked at 2.4 V the current is ~333 + 50 = 383 mA: saving 5.9 mW to 27.9 mW, midpoint ~13 mW. Sanity check against the envelope: 10 mW on an 800 mW system is 1.3% - plausible.
findings.risk: Protection is weakened: Itrip rises from 1.50 A to 2.00 A, so a downstream short is held off longer. F1 (a 2 A fast-acting fuse per the schematic) still backstops it, but see the F1/PTC1 BOM finding - the PCB value contradicts the schematic for both parts, and that must be settled first or the coordination is unknown. The 0805L110 also has a higher Imax (100 A vs 40 A) so it is no worse on fault handling. Same 0805 land, same 6 V rating, same Littelfuse series and price band - genuinely drop-in.
findings.verify_reason: WRONG DATASHEET. PTC1's schematic value is 0805L075SLYR — the 'SL' suffix is Littelfuse's Lo Rho series, not the standard 0805L. DigiKey's page for the exact part gives Resistance-Initial (Ri) 40 mOhm min, Resistance Post Trip (R1) 160 mOhm max, max fault current 50 A, series 'POLY-FUSE LoRho', status Active. The Littelfuse Lo Rho datasheet (rendered from the PDF, p.9) gives 0805L075SLYR: Ihold 0.75 A, Itrip 1.50 A, Vmax 6, Imax 50 A, Rmin 0.040, R1max 0.160. The finding's 0.090/0.350 and Imax 40 A are the STANDARD 0805L (…WR) numbers, and the URL it cites is the 0603L datasheet — a third, different series. Consequences: (a) the proposed 0805L110WR has Rmin 0.050 / R1max 0.160, i.e. HIGHER minimum resistance than the part already fitted, so the swap as specified LOSES about 1 mW rather than saving 10 (0.333^2 x 0.050 = 5.5 mW vs 0.333^2 x 0.040 = 4.4 mW). (b) The rerating table is also from the wrong series: Lo Rho 0805L075SLYR holds 0.75 A at 20 C, 0.62 A at 40 C, 0.47 A at 60 C (there is no 50 C column); the quoted 0.63/0.57/0.53 are the standard-series numbers. (c) The correct like-for-like upgrade is 0805L110SLYR (Lo Rho): Ihold 1.10 A, Itrip 1.80 A (not 2.00), Rmin 0.030, R1max 0.130, rerated 0.83 A at 40 C and 0.55 A at 60 C (not 0.92/0.75). WHAT SURVIVES: the trip-margin argument, and it is if anything worse. At 40 C the fitted part holds 0.62 A, so the ~700 mA worst case is 13% over hold; at 60 C it holds 0.47 A, 49% over. Even the 1.10 A Lo Rho part holds only 0.55 A at 60 C, i.e. still under 700 mA — so the upgrade buys margin at 40 C (84% of hold) but not at 60 C. The current-path verification is correct and I reproduced it: VCC = {C37.1, L1.1, L2.1, PTC1.2, TP32, U5 VIN1/VIN2/VIN} — SW1 gates only the SW node (R11/R12/R58/R3/Q3), so PTC1 does carry the whole load. Battery-current arithmetic checks (1.175/1.9 = 618 mA; 0.012 x 3.336 / 0.836 / 1.9 = 25 mA), but the finding does not flag, as the brief required, that insideGadgets' +40-60 mA is a system-level figure being added directly to battery current.
findings.correction: PTC1 fitted = 0805L075SLYR (Lo Rho): Rmin 0.040 Ohm, R1max 0.160 Ohm, Imax 50 A, Ihold 0.62 A @40 C / 0.47 A @60 C. Do NOT fit 0805L110WR (Rmin 0.050) — it is worse. Fit 0805L110SLYR: Rmin 0.030, R1max 0.130, Itrip 1.80 A, Ihold 0.83 A @40 C / 0.55 A @60 C. Saving at 333 mA = 0.333^2 x (0.040-0.030) = 1.1 mW at Rmin to 0.333^2 x (0.160-0.130) = 3.3 mW at R1max, midpoint ~2 mW. Overclocked at 383 mA: 1.5 to 4.4 mW, midpoint ~3 mW. Still a drop-in 0805, same 6 V rating.

findings.title: F1 and PTC1 both carry PCB value "0467001.NR" while the schematic says two different parts - two 1 A fuses in the battery path
findings.current_part: Verified directly: agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch gives F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR and PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR. All three board files (agbm01, the ECO-5 fork, the ECO-6 CXC file) give BOTH F1 and PTC1 the Value "0467001.NR". 0467001.NR is a Littelfuse 467-series 0603 very-fast-acting thin-film chip fuse, 1 A, 32 V AC/DC, 50 A breaking capacity, body 1.60 x 0.81 x 0.31 mm. F0805B2R00FSTR is MCF0805B2R00FSTR, a Multicomp 0805 fast-acting SMD thin-film fuse: the "2R00" is the CURRENT rating (2.00 A), not a resistance - resistance max 0.08 Ohm at 10% of rated current, max voltage drop 220 mV at 1 x rated (2 A), fusing current within 5 s = 4 A, rated 63 V.
findings.proposal: Fix the PCB values to match the schematic (F1 = MCF0805B2R00FSTR, PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR or the 0805L110 above). Whichever way it is resolved, state it once and keep it consistent - this is a two-part series element in the only path the whole console draws through.
findings.benefit: Not an energy finding directly, but it makes every other number in the battery path unknowable. Series resistance is F1 (<=0.080 Ohm) + PTC1 (0.090-0.350 Ohm) = 0.17-0.43 Ohm, which at the typical 333 mA is 57-143 mV of drop and 19-48 mW, and at the worst-case 700 mA is 119-301 mV and 83-211 mW. If someone instead builds to the PCB values they fit two 1 A 0603 very-fast-acting fuses in series: at 700 mA that is 70% of a 1 A very-fast-acting rating with no continuous-duty derating applied, and the resettable protection is replaced by a one-shot part - a single overload permanently bricks the board.
findings.risk: Reporting only. The one thing that would be wrong is to assume F1 is a 2 Ohm resistor from its "2R00" marking - it is not; 2 Ohm in this path would drop 0.67 V at 333 mA and burn 222 mW, which is flatly incompatible with the measured 800 mW system total, and that inconsistency is how I caught it.
findings.verify_reason: Verified end to end. agbm01/AGBM-01_AA_1-2.kicad_sch gives F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR and PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR; all three board files (stock, ECO-5 fork, ECO-6 CXC) give BOTH footprints Value '0467001.NR'. The string '0467001' occurs 2x in the .kicad_pcb and 0x in the .kicad_sch, and F1/PTC1 are the only two footprints in the board whose Value is not a schematic value. Useful corroboration the finding missed: AGBM-02's board file carries the CORRECT values (F1 = F0805B2R00FSTR, PTC1 = 0805L075SLYR) and AGBM-11 uses '2A'/'750mA' — so AGBM-01 rev 1.2 is the outlier and MouseBiteLabs fixed it in the next revision. Part identifications verified: 0467001.NR = Littelfuse 1 A, 32 V AC/DC, 0603, very-fast-acting, 50 A breaking capacity (Newark). F0805B2R00FSTR = KYOCERA AVX Accu-Guard II 0805 thin-film fuse, 2.00 A, 63 V; the Multicomp/Farnell datasheet for the equivalent MCF0805B2R00FSTR gives current rating 2 A, resistance max 0.08 Ohm at 10% x Irated, voltage drop max 220 mV at 1 x Irated, rated voltage 63 V — so the finding is right that '2R00' is a 2.00 A rating, not 2 Ohm, and its reasoning for catching it is sound. ONE CORRECTION: the series-resistance range is quoted using the wrong PTC datasheet (see ptc1-trip-margin-at-175x). With the real Lo Rho numbers the pair is F1 <=0.080 + PTC1 0.040-0.160 = 0.12-0.24 Ohm, giving 40-80 mV and 13-27 mW at 333 mA and 84-168 mV and 59-118 mW at 700 mA — not 0.17-0.43 Ohm / 19-48 mW / 83-211 mW. Also worth adding: 0467001.NR is a 0603 body being placed on a Fuse_0805_2012Metric land, so building to the PCB value is a footprint mismatch as well as a protection-scheme change.
findings.correction: Series resistance F1+PTC1 = 0.12-0.24 Ohm (not 0.17-0.43): 13-27 mW at 333 mA, 59-118 mW at 700 mA.

findings.title: ECO-6: X1, C3 and C4 are not marked DNP, so the crystal and its load caps ship as fitted - C3 loads the ClockxControl output
findings.current_part: In AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb the ClockxControl install requires X1 removed and CK1 driven externally, but the footprint attribute audit shows 49 DNP-marked footprints and X1 (4.194304MHz, at 41.694,-56.785), C3 (27p, GND to /CPU/CK1, at 45.9,-60.5) and C4 (33p, at 45.9,-51.2) are NOT among them. Net map confirms C3 pad 2 is on /CPU/CK1 (5 pads: C3.2, R1.1, TP80, U1.113 CLK1, X1.1) and the C4/R41 network hangs on /CPU/CK2 (U1.114 CLK2, R1.2, R41.1, TP81).
findings.proposal: Mark X1, C3, C4 (and, if the CXC is a permanent fit, R41) as DNP in the ECO-6 board and schematic. R1 (1.5M) can stay - at 3.34 V it passes 2.2 uA. No copper change; this is a build/BOM option.
findings.benefit: With C3 fitted, the ClockxControl's clock output drives 27 pF of load cap on top of the ~10.9 pF of trace capacitance. Dynamic power P = C x V^2 x f: at 1.75x (7.34 MHz) and VDD3 = 3.336 V, C3 alone is 27e-12 x 3.336^2 x 7.34e6 = 2.21 mW at VDD3, which referred to the battery through the boost (eta 0.88) and the series path (0.95) is 2.64 mW. On the CK2 side the CPU's now-unused oscillator inverter still drives C4 (33 pF) through R41 (2.2k): the RC time constant is 2.2k x 33p = 72.6 ns against a 68 ns half-period at 7.34 MHz, so the node only partly slews and dissipation is bounded by C x V^2 x f = 2.70 mW, realistically 1.5-2.0 mW at VDD3 = 1.8-2.4 mW at the battery. Total ~4.5-5.0 mW at 1.75x, ~2.5-3.0 mW at 1x (4.194 MHz). Small, but it is free and the parts are supposed to be off the board anyway.
findings.risk: None if the ClockxControl is fitted. If someone populates X1 instead, C3/C4 are mandatory - hence build-option rather than a deletion. Do NOT remove R1: it biases the CPU's oscillator inverter and removing it is untested.
findings.verify_reason: The defect was real in the file the engineer reviewed, and is already fixed in the current head. I audited (attr …) on every footprint: prev/agbm-01-clockxcontrol/AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb (05:56) has 252 footprints, 49 DNP, and X1/C3/C4 are NOT among them — exactly as the finding states. The current scratchpad/AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb (19:19) has 52 DNP and X1, C3, C4 ARE marked '(attr smd dnp)'. So the finding was correct when written; anyone reading it against the head file will find it stale. Net topology confirmed: C3 pad 2 on /CPU/CK1 alongside R1.1, TP80, U1.113 (CLK1), X1.1 (plus JP3.1 in the CXC file, which the finding's 5-pad list omits); C4 pad 1 on Net-(C4-Pad1) with X1.2 and R41.2, R41.1 on /CPU/CK2 with U1.114 and TP81. insideGadgets' own install instructions confirm the premise: 'Installation requires a hot air gun to remove the existing crystal'. ENERGY NUMBERS ARE ~20-25% HIGH. C3 is right: 27e-12 x 3.336^2 x 7.34e6 = 2.21 mW at VDD3, /0.836 = 2.64 mW at the battery (and VOUT3 = 1.20 V x (1+1.78/1.00) = 3.336 V is confirmed from the LTC3527's 1.20 V feedback reference). C4/R41 is not '1.5-2.0 mW'. Solving the RC properly: x = exp(-68.1/72.6) = 0.391, so the swing on C4 is 2a = V(1-x)/(1+x) = 0.437 x 3.336 = 1.46 Vpp; charge per half cycle 33p x 1.46 = 48.2 pC; energy from supply per cycle 48.2p x 3.336 = 161 pJ; P = 161p x 7.34e6 = 1.18 mW at VDD3, and less once the CPU inverter's output impedance is included. Total 3.39 mW at VDD3 = 4.06 mW at the battery at 1.75x, and 2.32 mW at 1x — not 4.5-5.0 and 2.5-3.0. R1's 2.2 uA / 7.4 uW is right and the advice to leave it fitted is right.
findings.correction: Corrected saving: ~2.3 mW at 1x, ~4.1 mW at 1.75x (C3 2.21 mW + C4/R41 1.18 mW at VDD3, referred to battery by /0.836). Also note X1/C3/C4 are ALREADY marked DNP in the current head CXC file (19:19); the finding describes the 05:56 version.

findings.title: The 73.5 mm ClockxControl clock run is GND-referenced for only 5.9 mm and changes reference-plane net 15 times
findings.current_part: Measured directly from AGBM-01_AA_1-2_GBE-plus-CXC.kicad_pcb by walking the CXC_CLK polyline and sampling the plane net under each sub-segment: total routed length 73.46 mm (67.46 mm on B.Cu, 6.00 mm on F.Cu, 0.25 mm wide throughout), endpoints (97.90,-37.95) at the module's CLK wire pad and (45.65,-64.20) at JP3. Reference net under the trace, by length: VDD5 35.60 mm, VDD3 13.99 mm, VDD2 7.33 mm, VDD35 4.74 mm, GND 5.91 mm total (4.30 on F.Cu over In1, 1.61 on B.Cu over In2), no plane at all 5.89 mm. The reference net changes 15 times along the run. The trace additionally crosses 5 slots cut in the In2 plane by signal traces routed on that layer (/CPU/TP1, TP2, TP3, TP8, /~VCNT5). Microstrip parameters I derived from the stackup (0.25 mm trace, 0.1 mm prepreg, er 4.5, 35 um Cu): er_eff 3.48, Z0 ~42 Ohm, 0.148 pF/mm, propagation 161 mm/ns so Tpd = 0.457 ns one way. Total trace capacitance to reference ~10.9 pF.
findings.proposal: Three changes, in order of value. (1) Route CXC_CLK on F.Cu instead of B.Cu: F.Cu sits 0.1 mm above the In1 GND plane, which is a single continuous 4023 mm2 island, and the reference-plane audit shows 1614.7 of 1977.5 mm (82%) of existing F.Cu signal routing is already GND-referenced, versus 492.4 of 1522.3 mm (32%) on B.Cu. (2) Flank whatever route is kept with GND stitching vias every ~10 mm so the return current has somewhere to go at each plane change. (3) Fit a 33-47 Ohm series resistor at the SOURCE end (in the module's CLK wire, at TP83) to roughly match the 42 Ohm line and cut the harmonic content; JP3's two 1.05 mm pads on 1.30 mm centres will accept a hand-soldered 0603, but a resistor there is at the far end and only forms an RC with the CPU's XIN pin capacitance (33 Ohm x ~8 pF = 0.26 ns, which does almost nothing) - the source end is where it belongs.
findings.benefit: This is an EMC and margin finding, not an energy one; I am not going to pretend otherwise. The energy number is small and I will state it honestly: charging 10.9 pF at 3.336 V and 7.34 MHz costs C x V^2 x f = 0.89 mW at VDD3 = 1.07 mW at the battery, and shortening the run to ~25 mm would recover about 0.6 mW.
