The margin argument is the real one: every one of the 15 reference-net changes forces the clock's return current to hop between planes through whatever decoupling capacitor is nearest, and 35.6 mm of the run is over VDD5 (the LCD rail) with 14.0 mm over VDD3 - which is the ClockxControl's own supply, so the clock is injecting its return current into the rail that powers its oscillator. That is a positive-feedback path for jitter. It is also consistent with insideGadgets' own note that the FunnyPlaying laminated IPS screen fails above 1.25x: the clock is capacitively dumping into VDD5 for half its length.
findings.risk: Re-routing 73 mm on a board this dense is real work and may not be possible on F.Cu without displacing other nets. The series resistor is cheap and low-risk but if made too large it slows the CK1 edge into a CPU input with an unknown threshold - do not exceed ~100 Ohm without scoping CK1. Cannot be done as a drop-in.
findings.verify_reason: The route geometry is exact and the physics is sound, but the headline reference-plane numbers do not reproduce and one causal claim is unsupported. VERIFIED: CXC_CLK totals 73.46 mm (67.46 on B.Cu, 6.00 on F.Cu), 0.25 mm throughout, endpoints (97.900,-37.950) at TP83 and (45.650,-64.200) at JP3 pad 2 — all exact. JP3's pads are 1.05 mm on 1.30 mm centres (44.350 and 45.650) — exact. Stackup verified from the board's own setup block: F.Cu 35 um / 0.1 mm prepreg er 4.5 / In1 / 0.84 mm core er 4.5 / In2 / 0.1 mm prepreg / B.Cu. Recomputing Hammerstad from that stackup gives er_eff 3.477, Z0 42.0 Ohm, v 160.8 mm/ns, 0.148 pF/mm, 10.87 pF over 73.46 mm — every one of the finding's numbers reproduces (it does ignore the 35 um conductor thickness, which would pull Z0 down toward ~38 Ohm). Energy: 10.9p x 3.336^2 x 7.34e6 = 0.89 mW at VDD3, 1.07 mW at the battery — correct. The F.Cu-vs-B.Cu argument for proposal (1) reproduces almost exactly: I measure 1612.1 of 1977.5 mm (81.5%) of F.Cu signal routing GND-referenced and 490.4 of 1522.3 mm (32.2%) on B.Cu, and In1 GND is one 4023.38 mm2 island. NOT VERIFIED: sampling the filled polygons under the trace at 0.05 mm I get GND 6.88 mm, VDD5 32.59, VDD3 13.13, VDD35 8.88, VDD2 5.02, no plane 6.97, and 19 reference-net transitions — against the claimed 5.91 / 35.60 / 13.99 / 4.74 / 7.33 / 5.89 and 15. Same totals, materially different split (VDD35 and VDD2 look transposed). The title's '5.9 mm' and '15 times' should read ~6.9 mm and 19. REFUTED: the inference that insideGadgets' FunnyPlaying-screen note corroborates this board's routing. The product page says 'Works with the FunnyPlaying laminated IPS GBA screen at speed 1.25x and below. At 1.5x, the screen fades to black as per a user report' as a generic compatibility statement covering every GBA install, most of which use a short flying lead from the module to the crystal pad — it is not evidence about a 73 mm PCB run and must not be cited as such. Proposals (1)-(3) remain reasonable engineering; the series-resistor placement argument (source end, not JP3) is correct.
findings.correction: Reference-plane split is GND 6.88 mm, VDD5 32.59, VDD3 13.13, VDD35 8.88, VDD2 5.02, no plane 6.97, with 19 reference-net changes (not 5.91/35.60/13.99/4.74/7.33/5.89 and 15). Delete the insideGadgets FunnyPlaying corroboration — it is a generic all-installs note, not evidence about this layout. Energy figure 1.07 mW at battery is correct.

findings.title: LTC3527 output capacitors are 3.9 mm from the VOUT pins with two via transitions in the highest-di/dt path, and both return through one GND via
findings.current_part: All on B.Cu. Corrected pad positions (the footprint is rotated -90 deg): U5 VOUT1 (28.35,-40.65), SW1 (28.35,-40.15), SW2 (28.35,-39.65), VOUT2 (28.35,-39.15), PGND exposed pad (26.90,-39.90), GND pads at (27.15,-41.35), (27.15,-38.45), (25.45,-39.65). C21 (22u 0805, VOUT5) pad 1 at (31.75,-42.55), GND pad at (31.75,-40.65). C42 (22u 0805, VOUT3) pad 1 at (31.75,-37.25), GND pad at (31.75,-39.15). L1 pad 2 at (30.68,-45.00) and L2 pad 2 at (30.68,-34.80), so each SW node runs 5.38 mm to its inductor. The output path is NOT a straight run: U5 pin 8 lands on a 2.05 mm2 B.Cu VOUT3 island (x[27.9,29.9] y[-39.3,-37.0]) which is a SEPARATE polygon from the 75.51 mm2 B.Cu VOUT3 pour that C42 sits in; they are joined only via the F.Cu VOUT3 zone through vias at (29.52,-38.50)/(29.52,-37.42) and (32.30,-36.20). Same on channel 1: 2.06 mm2 island, vias (29.52,-41.40)/(29.52,-42.40) and (32.30,-43.70). On the return side, both output caps' GND pads sit in one 4.67 mm2 B.Cu GND island (x[31.1,33.1] y[-41.9,-38.0]) served by GND vias at (32.90,-39.90), (32.83,-38.44) and (32.90,-41.40); the U5 exposed pad has its own three vias at (26.50,-40.30), (27.30,-40.30), (26.50,-39.50), 5.8 mm away in-plane. The LTC3527 datasheet is explicit on both pins: "PCB trace length from VOUT1 to the output filter capacitor(s) should be as short and wide as possible" and the same for VOUT2.
findings.proposal: No part change. On a PCB revision: move C21 and C42 so their VOUT pads butt directly against U5 pins 5 and 8 on B.Cu (there is room in x 29-31, y -42 to -37 once the via-hop is removed), merge the two B.Cu VOUT islands per channel so no layer transition is needed, and put two GND vias immediately adjacent to each output cap's ground pad rather than 1.2-1.6 mm away.
findings.benefit: EMC/ripple, not energy. Loop estimate: perimeter of the VOUT -> COUT -> GND -> PGND loop is about 3.9 mm out + 1.9 mm across the cap + 4.65 mm back = 10.4 mm, plus two 0.3 mm via transitions at roughly 1 nH each, giving an order-of-10 nH loop against the ~2-3 nH achievable. Working the current: at 200 mA on VOUT3 from a 2.6 V input, D = 1 - 2.6/3.336 = 0.221, IL_avg = 0.200/0.779 = 257 mA and ripple = Vin x D / (L x f) = 2.6 x 0.221 / (4.7e-6 x 1.2e6) = 102 mA, so Ipk ~308 mA. At a 3 ns synchronous-rectifier edge, di/dt = 1.0e8 A/s and V = L x di/dt = 10e-9 x 1.0e8 = ~1.0 V of ringing across the loop. That is the number that matters: VOUT3 feeds VDD3 through U18, which is a bare P-FET with no filtering whatsoever, so this ringing lands directly on the CPU's I/O rail and on the ClockxControl's supply pin.
findings.risk: Requires re-placing two 0805s and re-pouring, on a board where the converter corner is already tight (16 non-GND vias within 6 mm of U5). Nothing about the current layout is a functional fault - the board demonstrably works - so this is a quality improvement whose payoff is cleaner rails at 1.75x, not a fix.
findings.verify_reason: The core layout critique is verified; two supporting facts are wrong. VERIFIED EXACTLY: U5 is rotated -90 and its pads land at VOUT1 (28.348,-40.650), SW1 (28.348,-40.150), SW2 (28.348,-39.650), VOUT2 (28.348,-39.150), EPAD pin 17 (26.900,-39.900), GND pads (27.150,-41.348), (27.150,-38.452), (25.452,-39.650); C21 pad 1 (31.750,-42.550) and GND (31.750,-40.650); C42 pad 1 (31.750,-37.250) and GND (31.750,-39.150); L1 pad 2 (30.675,-45.000), L2 pad 2 (30.675,-34.800). VOUT pin to output cap = 3.897 mm, SW to inductor = 5.379 mm — both as claimed. The split VOUT copper is real: B.Cu VOUT3 is 2.05 mm2 at x[27.95,29.93] y[-39.31,-37.00] plus a separate 75.51 mm2 pour, bridged only through the F.Cu VOUT3 zone by vias (29.525,-38.500)/(29.525,-37.425) and (32.300,-36.200); channel 1 mirrors it (2.06 mm2 island, vias (29.525,-42.400)/(29.525,-41.400), (32.300,-43.700) and also (32.300,-44.600)). The U5 EPAD vias are exactly where stated. The LTC3527 datasheet quote is verbatim and appears for BOTH pins: 'PCB trace length from VOUT1 to the output filter capacitor(s) should be as short and wide as possible' (and identically for VOUT2). Ripple arithmetic reproduces (D = 0.221, IL_avg 257 mA, dIL 102 mA, Ipk 308 mA, di/dt 1.0e8 A/s, 10 nH -> ~1 V). WRONG: (1) the title's 'both return through one GND via' and the '4.67 mm2 B.Cu GND island (x[31.1,33.1] y[-41.9,-38.0])'. Both output caps' GND pads sit in a single 19.78 mm2 B.Cu GND island spanning x[31.06,38.09] y[-45.49,-37.95], which contains SIX GND vias, three of them within 1.6 mm of the cap pads at (32.9,-41.4), (32.9,-39.9) and (32.83,-38.44). The return is not a one-via bottleneck. (2) The 200 mA VOUT3 assumption sits at the very top of the measured envelope — 200 mA x 3.336 V = 667 mW on VOUT3 alone, which with VOUT5 loaded would exceed the 1175 mW system maximum. At a defensible 120-150 mA, Ipk falls to ~200-240 mA and the ringing estimate falls to ~0.65-0.8 V. Minor: 17, not 16, non-GND vias lie within 6 mm of U5.
findings.correction: The output caps' GND pads sit in a 19.78 mm2 B.Cu GND island with 6 GND vias (3 within 1.6 mm), not a 4.67 mm2 island on one via — drop that from the title and the proposal. Use 120-150 mA on VOUT3, giving Ipk ~200-240 mA and ~0.65-0.8 V of loop ringing rather than ~1.0 V. Everything else (3.9 mm VOUT run, split islands, two via transitions, EPAD 5.8 mm away, datasheet mandate) stands.

findings.title: The SW2 switching node is poured directly over the In2 VDD3 plane at 0.1 mm - the boost couples into the CPU I/O and ClockxControl rail
findings.current_part: Verified by point-sampling the filled polygons. The Net-(U5-SW2) copper is a B.Cu zone of 8.66 mm2, bbox x[28.0,31.5] y[-39.8,-33.8]. Directly beneath it, 0.1 mm away across the prepreg, is the In2.Cu VDD3 plane (448.49 mm2, bbox x[23.6,98.1] y[-52.2,-26.6]). The companion Net-(U5-SW1) zone (8.74 mm2, x[28.0,31.5] y[-46.0,-40.0]) sits over the In2 VOUT5 plane (16.10 mm2). Under U5 itself In2 is essentially bare - the GND island there is only 2.40 mm2 - so the B.Cu converter copper has no local GND reference at 0.1 mm; the nearest GND plane, In1, is 0.975 mm away through the 0.84 mm core.
findings.proposal: No part change. On a PCB revision, replace the In2 copper under the converter (roughly x 23-34, y -33 to -48) with a GND island stitched to In1, instead of letting the VDD3 and VOUT5 planes run under the switch nodes. Zero cost, zone edit plus re-pour.
findings.benefit: EMC, no energy saving - I am marking benefit_mw zero deliberately. Coupling: C = e0 x er x A / d = 8.854e-12 x 4.5 x 7e-6 / 0.1e-3 = 2.8 pF between SW2 and the VDD3 plane (using ~7 mm2 of overlap after clearances, from an 8.66 mm2 zone). SW2 swings 0 to 3.34 V at 1.2 MHz (FSEL is tied to GND, and the datasheet gives FSEL low = 1.2 MHz, 0.9-1.5 MHz limits). At an assumed 3 ns edge the injected current is i = C dV/dt = 2.8e-12 x 1.113e9 = 3.1 mA peak straight into the VDD3 plane. The nearest VDD3 decoupling capacitor to that spot is C39 at (27.77,-51.10), about 15 mm away; over that distance the In1/In2 plane pair (0.84 mm apart, er 4.5) presents roughly 377 x 0.84e-3 / (sqrt(4.5) x 0.010) = 15 Ohm for a 10 mm-wide path, so of order 45 mV of high-frequency spike on VDD3 near the converter. VDD3 is the ClockxControl's V+ and the CPU's I/O supply; at 1.75x the clock chip is the most jitter-sensitive thing on that rail.
findings.risk: Re-pouring In2 under the converter means VDD3 must find another path across x 23-34 - it currently uses that plane region, so the re-pour needs checking that VDD3 still reaches U18's output and the CPU. Verify with a fresh DRC and connectivity check. No component or schematic change.
findings.verify_reason: Everything checkable reproduces, and the coupling is slightly larger than claimed. Point-sampling the filled polygons: B.Cu Net-(U5-SW2) is a single 8.66 mm2 zone at x[27.95,31.50] y[-39.80,-33.80]; the In2 VDD3 plane is 448.49 mm2 with bbox (23.60,-52.17,98.10,-26.60) — both exactly as stated. Measured overlap SW2 over In2 VDD3 = 8.336 mm2, so C = 8.854e-12 x 4.5 x 8.336e-6 / 1e-4 = 3.32 pF and i = C dV/dt = 3.32p x 3.336/3n = 3.7 mA — the finding's 2.8 pF / 3.1 mA (from an assumed 7 mm2) is conservative, not inflated. Net-(U5-SW1) is 8.74 mm2 at x[27.95,31.50] y[-46.00,-40.00] and the In2 VOUT5 island is 16.10 mm2 — both exact; overlap is 5.63 mm2 with VOUT5, but SW1 ALSO overlaps In2 VDD3 by 2.56 mm2, which the finding does not mention. The In2 GND island under U5 is 2.403 mm2 — exact to three figures. Stackup verified from the board file (0.1 mm prepreg to In2, 0.84 mm core to In1). FSEL = GND -> 1.2 MHz with 0.9/1.5 MHz limits is verbatim from the LTC3527 datasheet. C39's VDD3 pad is at (27.775,-51.100) — exact — and VDD3 does originate at U18's output (28.337,-27.300)/(28.337,-28.250), so the plane genuinely runs down past the converter and the stated re-pour risk is real. Plane-pair impedance arithmetic (377 x 0.84e-3 / (2.1213 x 0.010) = 14.9 Ohm) and the ~46 mV spike are right. ONE CAVEAT THE FINDING MISSES: MODE is tied to GND, and the datasheet says 'MODE = Low: Automatic Burst Mode operation', so the 1.2 MHz SW swing is bursty at light load rather than continuous — the injection is intermittent below the burst threshold, which weakens (not eliminates) the idle-time argument.
findings.correction: Coupling is 3.3 pF over 8.34 mm2 of measured overlap (i = 3.7 mA), slightly worse than the 2.8 pF / 3.1 mA stated. SW1 also overlaps In2 VDD3 by 2.56 mm2, not only VOUT5. Note MODE = GND selects automatic Burst Mode, so the 1.2 MHz swing is not continuous at light load.

findings.title: Thermal audit: no part on this board is near a limit, overclocked or not - the largest junction rise I can compute is about 16 °C
findings.current_part: Every thermal resistance below was read out of a manufacturer PDF fetched during this review, not from memory. LTC3527 (U5), QFN-16 UD: TJMAX 125 °C, thetaJA 68 °C/W, and the datasheet states the exposed pad (pin 17) is PGND and MUST be soldered - on this board it is, with three 0.3 mm GND vias at (26.50,-40.30), (27.30,-40.30), (26.50,-39.50). NCV8164 (U8, U4), TSOP-5: RthJA 158 °C/W, RthJC(top) 155, RthJB 197, TJ max 150 °C, Iq 30 uA typ, dropout for the 2.5 V version 125 mV typ / 200 mV max at 300 mA, current limit 350 mA min. TPS22917 (U11, U18, U12), DBV SOT-23-6: thetaJA 183 °C/W, Ron 80 mOhm typ / 100 max at VIN 5 V and 25 °C (120 mOhm max to +85 °C), 90 typ / 110 max at VIN 3.6 V, IQ 0.5 uA typ. LM4853 (U6), MSOP-10 DGS: thetaJA 194 °C/W, TJ max 150 °C, IDD 2.0-2.4 mA typ. TPS3840DL20 (U3, U10, U17), SOT-23-5: thetaJA 187.5 °C/W. MIC1553 (U14), SOT-23-5: thetaJA 250 °C/W.
findings.proposal: No change. This finding exists so nobody spends effort chasing a thermal problem that is not there.
findings.benefit: Dissipations at the worst in-use overclocked point (1175 mW plus overclock, 1.9 V pack, ~700 mA battery), assuming 45 °C inside a sealed shell. U5 LTC3527: input power = 1325 mW less the F1+PTC1 loss (39 mW + 44-172 mW) = 1114-1242 mW; at an assumed 88% efficiency the loss is 134-149 mW, giving 68 x 0.14 = +9.5 °C, Tj ~55 °C. Even at a pessimistic 80% efficiency the loss is 240 mW and the rise is +16 °C, Tj ~61 °C, against 125 °C. U8 (VDD2 LDO): (3.336 - 2.500) x 90 mA = 75 mW, plus 30 uA x 3.336 V = 0.1 mW; 158 x 0.075 = +11.9 °C, Tj ~57 °C against 150 °C. At 1x it is 0.836 x 60 mA = 50 mW and +7.9 °C. You would need 800 mA through U8 to reach 150 °C, and its current limit is 350 mA min - the part is thermally unreachable. U4 (VAUD LDO): 0.836 x 30 mA = 25 mW, +4.0 °C. U11 (VDD5 load switch) at an assumed 100 mA of backlight: 0.100^2 x 0.120 = 1.2 mW, +0.2 °C. U18 (VDD3) at 70 mA: 0.070^2 x 0.110 = 0.54 mW, +0.1 °C. U6 LM4853: the datasheet's own worst case for a bridged load is PDMAX = 4 x VDD^2 / (2 x pi^2 x RL) = 4 x 2.500^2 / (19.74 x 8) = 158 mW at the board's VAUD = 2.5 V with an assumed 8 Ohm speaker, giving 194 x 0.158 = +30.7 °C and Tj ~76 °C. In practice MouseBiteLabs measure the whole audio chain at 50-100 mW so U6 dissipates roughly 40-60 mW and rises +8 to +12 °C. Note the datasheet's warning that a DGS-package LM4853 on a 5 V rail can only take 27 °C ambient at PDMAX - at 2.5 V that scales by a factor of four and the problem disappears. The only part that runs hot enough to matter is PTC1, and it does so by design - see the trip finding: 0.700^2 x 0.090 to 0.700^2 x 0.350 = 44 to 172 mW in an 0805 body.
findings.risk: The one number I cannot verify is the internal shell temperature; 45 °C is my estimate. Even at 70 °C internal ambient every junction above stays under 105 °C. Two caveats: the LTC3527's 68 °C/W is a datasheet figure for the manufacturer's board, and the three EPAD vias here are on the low side for a QFN - if you want margin, add three more; and the speaker impedance (8 Ohm) is assumed, not measured.
findings.verify_reason: I re-fetched every datasheet and re-ran every calculation; the conclusion holds and almost all the quoted numbers are right. VERIFIED FROM PRIMARY SOURCES: LTC3527 UD QFN-16, 'TJMAX = 125 C, thetaJA = 68 C/W' and 'EXPOSED PAD (PIN 17) IS PGND, MUST BE SOLDERED TO PCB' — and the three EPAD GND vias at (26.50,-40.30), (27.30,-40.30), (26.50,-39.50) exist. NCV8164 TSOP-5: RthetaJA 158, RthetaJC(top) 155, RthetaJB 197 C/W, TJ max 150 C, IQ 30 uA typ, output current limit 350 mA min. TPS22917 DBV SOT-23-6: thetaJA 183 C/W, RON at VIN 5 V = 80 typ / 100 max at 25 C and 120 max to +85 C, at VIN 3.6 V = 90 typ / 110 max, IQ 0.5 uA typ — all four numbers exact. LM4853: thetaJA (typ) DGS = 194 C/W, TJ 150 C, and the bridge formula PDMAX = 4 x (VDD)^2/(2 pi^2 RL) is verbatim equation 3; the datasheet's own 5 V / 8 Ohm ambient limit reproduces as 150 - (4 x 25/157.91) x 194 = 27.2 C, confirming the finding's '27 C'. TPS3840 DBV: RthetaJA 187.5 C/W. ARITHMETIC RE-RUN AND CORRECT: U5 68 x 0.14 = +9.5 C (and +16 C at 80% efficiency); U8 0.836 x 0.090 = 75 mW, 158 x 0.075 = +11.9 C, and the 'you would need 795 mA' inversion is right against a 350 mA limit; U4 +4.0 C; U11 +0.2 C; U18 +0.1 C; LM4853 PDMAX at 2.5 V/8 Ohm = 158 mW -> +30.7 C. TWO SMALL CORRECTIONS: the NCV8164 dropout for the 2.5 V option at 300 mA is 140 mV typ / 220 mV max — the quoted 125/200 is the 3.3 V row, misread; and LM4853 IDD is 2.4 mA typ (7.0 mA limit) in both BTL and SE, not '2.0-2.4 mA'. Neither changes anything. I did not verify MIC1553's 250 C/W (the part is a real Microchip MIC1551/53 IttyBitty 555, but I could not open its thermal table) — treat that one number as unverified; it dissipates microwatts so it cannot matter. The finding's own caveats about the 45 C internal ambient and the 8 Ohm speaker are the right ones.
findings.correction: NCV8164 dropout for the 2.5 V option at 300 mA is 140 mV typ / 220 mV max (not 125/200 — that is the 3.3 V row). LM4853 IDD typ is 2.4 mA (not 2.0-2.4). MIC1553 thetaJA 250 C/W remains unverified.

findings.title: What is under the ClockxControl: no components, four different rails and 27 tented vias - no thermal problem, but the module wants a soldermask keepout
findings.current_part: The MOD1 footprint (ClockxControl_GBA_GBC) is placed at (91.95,-44.95) rotated 180, body 18.65 x 12.00 mm (fp_rect +/-9.325, +/-6.0), i.e. the window x[82.625,101.275] y[-50.950,-38.950] on F.Cu. Its three SMD landing pads are at (87.42,-45.95) /CPU/TP2, (84.92,-48.45) /CPU/TP9, (84.92,-45.95) /CPU/TP8; the V+, V- and CLK wire pads (TP84 VDD3, TP85 GND, TP83 CXC_CLK) are outside the body at y = -37.95. Sampling the F.Cu filled polygons on a 0.25 mm grid inside the window: GND 46.6% (107.1 mm2), VDD35 25.8% (59.3 mm2), bare laminate 16.1% (37.1 mm2), VDD2 9.3% (21.3 mm2), VDD5 2.1% (4.9 mm2). Sixteen signal tracks pass through, longest are Net-(C71-Pad1) 14.3 mm, /CPU/TP9 14.1 mm, /CPU/TP8 7.3 mm, /CPU/TP2 6.3 mm, /CPU/TP0 6.2 mm, /CPU/TP1 5.8 mm. Twenty-seven vias fall inside the window (17 GND, 4 VDD5, 1 VDD2, and 9 signal); the board setup line is (tenting front back), so they are masked. NO component sits under it: ECO-6 already moved C7 (the cartridge VDD35 decoupler) from (91.9,-41.1) - where it was in the ECO-5 fork, squarely inside the window - out to (93.1,-37.4), and C12 is on B.Cu. That relocation was necessary and correctly done: a 0603 is 0.8 +/- 0.1 mm thick (Murata GRM188 series datasheet), and a 1.6 mm-thick rigid module resting flat cannot bridge a 0.8 mm part 4.5-7 mm from its solder pads without lifting them.
findings.proposal: Add a soldermask keepout (or at minimum a documented Kapton pad) under the MOD1 body, and add an F.Cu copper-pour keepout so the module does not sit over four different rails. Neither costs anything at fab. Also add the height restriction to the footprint's courtyard/3D data so a future edit cannot put another 0603 back inside the window.
findings.benefit: THERMAL: none, in either direction, and I want to be explicit about that because the question was asked. The module covers 224 mm2 of F.Cu; at a still-air convection coefficient of order 10 W/m2K and a 20 °C local rise, that patch was only shedding 10 x 2.24e-4 x 20 = 45 mW to begin with, and it contains no dissipating part - the four things that do dissipate are at x = 18 (U8), 27 (U5), 38 (U4) and 103 (U6), all well outside. The module's own 12 mA x 3.336 V = 40 mW spread over both faces (2 x 2.24e-4 m2) is a self-rise of about 0.040 x 1/(10 x 4.48e-4) = 9 °C, and less than that in practice because most of it conducts into the board. Covering this area creates no thermal problem. MECHANICAL/ELECTRICAL: the exposure is four rails (GND, VDD35, VDD2, VDD5) and 27 tented vias under a rigid PCB that is soldered down at three points on one side. Tenting a 0.3 mm drill with LPI mask is normally reliable but is not a guarantee, and VDD35 to GND is a short that kills the CPU's internal regulator.
findings.risk: None to add the keepouts. The residual risk if nothing is done is a mask defect or via tenting failure shorting VDD35, VDD2 or VDD5 to GND under a part you cannot inspect once it is fitted.
findings.verify_reason: The substance is right; two counts are not. VERIFIED: MOD1 is placed at (91.95,-44.95) rotated 180 with SMD pads at (87.425,-45.950) /CPU/TP2, (84.925,-48.450) /CPU/TP9, (84.925,-45.950) /CPU/TP8, and TP83/TP84/TP85 at y = -37.95 on CXC_CLK / VDD3 / GND — all exact. Window x[82.625,101.275] y[-50.950,-38.950] = 223.8 mm2. Sampling F.Cu on a 0.25 mm grid I get GND 47.4% (106.0 mm2), VDD35 26.1% (58.5), bare 16.5% (37.0), VDD2 8.6% (19.1), VDD5 1.4% (3.2) — within a percentage point of the stated split. Total vias inside the window: 27, exactly as claimed. '(tenting front back)' is in the board setup. C7 is at (93.1,-37.4), i.e. moved out of the window, and C12 is the only other footprint inside and is on B.Cu — both as stated. Murata GRM188 (0603) is 1.6 x 0.8 x 0.8 mm with +/-0.1 mm tolerance, so the 0.8 mm thickness and the mechanical argument for moving C7 are sound. All the thermal arithmetic reproduces: 10 x 2.24e-4 x 20 = 45 mW; 0.040 / (10 x 4.48e-4) = 8.9 C; and the four dissipating parts really are at x = 18.4, 26.9, 37.9 and 102.6, all outside the window. WRONG COUNTS: the via breakdown '17 GND, 4 VDD5, 1 VDD2, and 9 signal' sums to 31, not the 27 the same sentence states — the actual breakdown is 12 GND, 4 VDD5, 1 VDD2 and 10 signal. And I count 14 F.Cu signal nets crossing the window, not 16, with different lengths: Net-(C71-Pad1) 16.14, /CPU/TP9 14.15, /CPU/TP2 5.48, /CPU/TP0 4.19, /CPU/TP1 4.04, /CPU/TP8 2.60 (vs the stated 14.3 / 14.1 / 6.3 / 6.2 / 5.8 / 7.3). Neither affects the recommendation, which costs nothing and is worth doing.
findings.correction: Vias in the window: 12 GND + 4 VDD5 + 1 VDD2 + 10 signal = 27 (the stated 17/4/1/9 sums to 31). 14 F.Cu signal nets cross the window, not 16, with somewhat shorter runs than listed.

findings.title: VDD2 layout verdict: DC drop is under 1 mV and is a non-issue; the plane pair contributes 22 pF of decoupling, so the discrete caps do all the work
findings.current_part: VDD2 leaves U8 pad 5 at (19.35,-31.44) on B.Cu, crosses a 17.66 mm2 B.Cu pour, and reaches the In2 VDD2 plane through a SINGLE via at (19.20,-32.70) (14 VDD2 vias exist on the whole board; the others are at the load ends). The In2 VDD2 plane is one contiguous island of 468.04 mm2 spanning x[17.7,101.8] y[-63.2,-31.9]. I profiled its width every 0.5 mm and integrated R = 0.491 mOhm/sq x dx / w(x): from the U8 via to U1's core pins at x = 74.3 the resistance is 7.36 mOhm; out to U2's furthest pin-37 pad at x = 100.3 it is 10.43 mOhm. The narrowest neck is 1.3 mm wide at x = 58.0-58.5, under the CPU. U1's four core pins are 44 (74.34,-49.62), 65 (72.34,-61.52), 115 (51.84,-53.62), 117 (51.84,-52.62); each has a 0.1 uF within 2.4-3.7 mm (pin 117 to C45 2.46 mm, pin 115 to C47 2.58 mm, pin 44 to C15 2.62 mm, pin 65 to C16 2.39 mm) plus a 1 uF alongside. C60 (10 uF) is the bulk cap at (19.17,-33.80), 3.5 mm from U8.
findings.proposal: No change to VDD2's routing. Two small things worth doing on a revision: add a second via at U8's output so the whole core rail does not depend on one 0.3 mm barrel, and see the separate finding about restoring the RAM's decoupling.
findings.benefit: Quantified so it can be dismissed: at the estimated 90 mA of VDD2 current at 1.75x, the plane drop to the CPU core pins is 0.090 x 7.36 mOhm = 0.66 mV, and to the RAM 0.94 mV; adding the single via (0.88 mOhm) and the B.Cu pour brings the total under 1.0 mV. For scale, the NCV8164's own load regulation is 2 mV from 1 mA to 300 mA. Current density in the 1.3 mm neck at 90 mA is 1.98 A/mm2, more than 20x inside any IPC-2152 internal-layer limit. The DC path is not a lever and no copper change will win anything here. The AC picture is different but also bounded: the In1(GND)/In2(VDD2) plane pair is separated by the 0.84 mm core, giving C = 8.854e-12 x 4.5 x 468e-6 / 0.84e-3 = 22.2 pF, whose impedance at 100 MHz is 72 Ohm - useless. All VDD2 decoupling is therefore discrete: 10 uF + 4 x 1 uF + 5 x 0.1 uF nominal. On the stackup generally: putting the 0.84 mm core between In1 and In2 and the 0.1 mm prepregs against the outer layers is the RIGHT trade for this board, because it puts the busiest signal layer (F.Cu, 1977.5 mm of signal routing) 0.1 mm from a continuous GND plane - and the audit shows 1614.7 mm of that, 82%, is genuinely GND-referenced. The price is paid on B.Cu, where only 492.4 of 1522.3 mm (32%) is GND-referenced and the rest runs over VDD2 (365.6 mm), VDD3 (203.5), VAUD (193.1) or nothing (200.0). Most of the VDD2-referenced B.Cu routing is the CPU-to-RAM MD bus, which is legitimately a VDD2-domain signal, so that part is fine.
findings.risk: None - this is a report of a measurement, not a change.
findings.verify_reason: The measurement half is excellent and reproduces; the one actionable proposal is factually wrong. REPRODUCED: integrating R = 0.491 mOhm/sq x dx / w(x) along the In2 VDD2 plane at 0.5 mm steps I get 7.25 mOhm from the U8 output to x = 74.3 and 10.19 mOhm to x = 100.3, against the finding's 7.36 and 10.43; narrowest slice 1.39 mm at x = 58.2, against '1.3 mm at 58.0-58.5'. 0.491 mOhm/sq is correct for 35 um copper. The In2 VDD2 plane is one contiguous 468.04 mm2 island, bbox x[17.72,101.80] y[-63.25,-31.92] — exact. Plane-pair capacitance 8.854e-12 x 4.5 x 468e-6 / 0.84e-3 = 22.2 pF and 1/(2 pi 1e8 x 22.2p) = 72 Ohm — correct. Current density 0.090/(1.3 x 0.035) = 1.98 A/mm2 — correct. Decoupling inventory (10u + 4 x 1u + 5 x 0.1u) matches the BOM. Every CPU-pin-to-cap distance is exact: pin 117 (51.840,-52.620) to C45 (49.375,-52.600) = 2.465 mm; pin 115 to C47 = 2.585; pin 44 (74.340,-49.620) to C15 (76.700,-48.475) = 2.623; pin 65 (72.340,-61.520) to C16 (71.625,-63.800) = 2.390. The B.Cu reference-layer census reproduces exactly: 490.4 of 1522.3 mm (32.2%) over GND, VDD2 365.0, VDD3 203.0, VAUD 191.5, none 203.5; and F.Cu 1612.1 of 1977.5 (81.5%). REFUTED: 'VDD2 ... reaches the In2 VDD2 plane through a SINGLE via at (19.20,-32.70)'. There are FOUR VDD2 vias in the U8 output region — (18.6,-35.9), (19.15,-35.0), (19.2,-32.7), (20.2,-35.0) — and shapely confirms all four fall inside BOTH the 17.66 mm2 B.Cu VDD2 pour and the In2 VDD2 plane. They are in parallel, so the barrel resistance is a quarter of what the finding assumes and the proposal to 'add a second via at U8's output' is unnecessary work. Also unmentioned: the fork has 14 VDD2 vias but stock has 16, and the ECO-6 CXC file removed two more at (84.4,-45.9) and (85.4,-45.9), leaving 12 — a second, undocumented via deletion in the same net.
findings.correction: Delete the 'add a second via at U8's output' proposal: four VDD2 vias already tie the B.Cu pour to the In2 plane there, all verified inside both polygons. Corrected plane resistance 7.25 mOhm to the CPU core pins and 10.19 mOhm to U2. Add a note that the CXC file removed two further VDD2 vias at (84.4,-45.9) and (85.4,-45.9) that the fork still had.

findings.title: ECO-5 moved C8 7.2 mm away from the RAM's VCC pin, leaving U2 with no local VDD2 decoupling - worst possible change for 1.75x
findings.current_part: In the stock board C8 (0.1 uF) sits adjacent to U2 pin 37 with F.Cu tracks at (100.081,-58.525)->(100.081,-56.9), (100.349,-58.525)->(100.8,-58.525) and (100.8,-58.525)->(100.081,-58.525). The fork deleted all three and relocated C8 to (103.0,-64.9), 7.2 mm from the nearest pin-37 pad at (100.31,-58.05) - and, per the separate correctness finding, left its VDD2 terminal unconnected. The nearest CONNECTED VDD2 capacitor to U2 is then C46 (1 uF) at (78.70,-48.48), 8.0 mm from pin 16 at (81.31,-56.05) and about 20 mm from the pin-37 pads. There are also only 4 GND vias within 10 mm of U2's centre, against 72 within 13 mm of U1.
findings.proposal: Restore a 0.1 uF within 1.5-2 mm of U2 pin 37 (the stock position was right) and add a second within 2 mm of pins 12/16. Add 3-4 GND stitching vias inside the U2 footprint area. All of this is copper and placement, no new parts beyond what the BOM already has.
findings.benefit: Estimated with stated assumptions: the CPU-RAM MD bus is 16 lines, each loaded by roughly 2.2 pF of trace (0.148 pF/mm x ~15 mm) plus ~5 pF of pin capacitance at each end, so about 12 pF per line, 192 pF total. A full 16-bit transition at 2.5 V moves 480 pC; delivered over a 2 ns edge that is 240 mA of peak supply current the RAM must pull from somewhere. With the nearest capacitor 8 mm away across a plane the path inductance is of order 4 nH, giving dV = L x di/dt = 4e-9 x 0.240/2e-9 = 0.48 V of droop on a 2.5 V rail. With a 0.1 uF at 1.5 mm (roughly 1 nH) it is 0.12 V. At 1.75x these events happen 1.75x as often, so the rail has 43% less time to recover between them. This is the single most likely cause of an overclocked build being unstable specifically after the ECO-5 change. Not an energy finding.
findings.risk: The 12 pF/line and 2 ns edge are estimates - I have no AGB CPU datasheet - so treat the 0.48 V as an order-of-magnitude figure, not a measurement. But the direction is not in doubt: removing a decoupling capacitor from beside a 16-bit SRAM's supply pin and then clocking it 75% faster is the wrong way round.
findings.verify_reason: The decoupling half is verified; the grounding half is fabricated. VERIFIED: in stock, C8 pad 1 is at (100.800,-58.525) and the three F.Cu VDD2 tracks (100.081,-58.525)->(100.081,-56.900), (100.349,-58.525)->(100.800,-58.525) and (100.800,-58.525)->(100.081,-58.525) exist; in the fork all three are gone and C8 sits at (103.0,-64.9) with pad 1 at (102.225,-64.900), 7.11 mm from the nearest pin-37 pad at (100.310,-58.050) — and disconnected, per the separate correctness finding. C46 (1 uF) pad 1 is at (78.700,-48.475), 8.01 mm from pin 16 at (81.310,-56.050) and 19.0-23.6 mm from the pin-37 pads, and it is genuinely the nearest connected VDD2 capacitor (C15 at (76.700,-48.475) is 8.87 mm, farther). The droop arithmetic is internally consistent (192 pF, 480 pC, 240 mA over 2 ns, 4 nH -> 0.48 V; 1 nH -> 0.12 V; 1/1.75 = 43% less recovery time). REFUTED: 'only 4 GND vias within 10 mm of U2's centre, against 72 within 13 mm of U1'. Counting all 212 GND vias in the fork board: 3 within 10 mm of U2 (88.0,-57.8) and 14 within 13 mm of U1 (63.09,-53.12). You have to go out to r = 28 mm around U1 to reach 72. At matched radii U2 is not starved relative to U1 — 11 vs 14 at 13 mm, 19 vs 26 at 15 mm, and 42 vs 38 at 20 mm, i.e. U2 has MORE GND vias than U1 at 20 mm. That leg of the argument must be dropped, along with 'add 3-4 GND stitching vias inside the U2 footprint area' as a justified-by-comparison action. ALSO OVERSTATED: the 0.48 V figure treats one 0.1 uF as the sole charge source and ignores the CPU-side decoupling, the four 1 uF caps, the plane pair and the capacitor's own ESL; it is an upper bound on an upper bound. The real, defensible point — that ECO-5 removed the only local bypass from a 16-bit SRAM's supply pin and the board is then clocked 75% faster — stands on its own and does not need the invented via comparison.
findings.correction: GND via counts: 3 within 10 mm of U2 and 14 within 13 mm of U1 (not 4 and 72). U2 is not GND-via-starved relative to U1 at matched radii — drop that comparison and the stitching-via proposal that rests on it. Keep the restore-a-0.1uF-at-pin-37 recommendation; treat 0.48 V as an order-of-magnitude upper bound only.

findings.title: Grounding verdict: the GND/AGND split is done correctly - single-point tie at NT1, no signal crosses it, and the whole analog block sits inside the island
findings.current_part: NT1 is a KiCad net tie (Bucketmouse:NetTie-2_SMD_Pad0.5mm) at (36.4,-33.0) on F.Cu, marked DNP and exclude_from_bom, with net_tie_pad_groups "1, 2". It is real copper, not a placeholder: the footprint carries an fp_poly on F.Cu from (-0.5,-0.25) to (0.5,0.25) bridging pad 1 (GND, at 35.90,-33.00) and pad 2 (AGND, at 36.90,-33.00). That bar is 1.0 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, 35 um thick = 2 squares = 0.98 mOhm. The In1 layer carries one 4023.38 mm2 GND island and one 1001.16 mm2 AGND island (both single, contiguous polygons - verified by counting filled_polygon groups); the AGND island occupies the top-right audio corner and reaches NT1 through a neck along y ~ -33 that runs from x = 37.0 to x = 121.5. NT1 is placed exactly on that boundary. Three AGND vias sit within 3 mm of the AGND pad, at (37.25,-33.75), (38.10,-33.25), (39.25,-33.25). All the analog parts fall inside the island: U6 (102.6,-25.9), U7 (115.1,-29.8), U9 (107.7,-46.4), VR2 (117.86,-11.54), P3 (105.65,-5.95), SP1 (126.685,-27.9). Separately, /CPU/LGND is a third ground with 40.45 mm2 on B.Cu and 40.47 mm2 on In2; its only pads are EM1.6, EM2.4 and P4 pins 6/7/8, so it reaches board GND ONLY through one winding of each common-mode choke (ACM2520-801-3P-T002, DCR 1.6 Ohm per line, rated current 150 mA) - two windings in parallel, about 0.8 Ohm.
findings.proposal: Keep the split; it is doing what it should. Two small drop-in improvements: (1) add one GND via right at NT1 pad 1 - the nearest GND via today is at (33.70,-31.20), 2.83 mm away, so the tie's GND side runs 2.83 mm on F.Cu (about 0.7 mOhm but roughly 2 nH) before reaching the plane stack; (2) decide deliberately whether /CPU/LGND should have a DC path to GND other than 0.8 Ohm of choke winding, because as drawn an ESD strike on the link connector shell has nowhere to go except through those windings.
findings.benefit: The split is verified correct, which is worth stating: I swept every F.Cu signal trace at 0.25 mm intervals against the In1 filled polygons and found ZERO crossings of the GND/AGND boundary, so no signal has a broken return path across the split. Loading: the LM4853 is bridge-tied, so the speaker current returns into the amplifier's own AGND, not across NT1; likewise the headphone return enters P3 pad 1 (AGND) and closes locally with U6 a few mm away. Only U6's DC supply current traverses NT1 - at 2.0-2.4 mA of quiescent IDD (LM4853 datasheet) plus the average draw of a 50-100 mW audio stage, call it up to 30 mA, the 0.98 mOhm bar drops 29 uV. That is a well-executed single-point analog ground. No energy in it either way.
findings.risk: The via at NT1 costs nothing. Changing the LGND arrangement is a design decision, not a defect - I am flagging it, not asserting it is wrong; MouseBiteLabs may have chosen the choke-only path deliberately to keep cable-borne noise out of board GND.
findings.verify_reason: Verified in unusual detail and it holds, with one small exception. The NT1 footprint really is copper: '(net_tie_pad_groups "1, 2")' with an fp_poly on F.Cu from (-0.5,-0.25) to (0.5,0.25) bridging pad 1 (GND) at (35.900,-33.000) and pad 2 (AGND) at (36.900,-33.000); attrs are exclude_from_pos_files exclude_from_bom allow_missing_courtyard dnp. 1.0 mm long / 0.5 mm wide = 2 squares x 0.491 mOhm/sq = 0.98 mOhm, and 30 mA x 0.98 mOhm = 29 uV — correct (and conservative, since the pads overlap the bar). In1 carries exactly one 4023.38 mm2 GND island and one 1001.16 mm2 AGND island — both figures exact to two decimals. All six analog part positions are exact: U6 (102.6,-25.9), U7 (115.1,-29.8), U9 (107.7,-46.4), VR2 (117.86,-11.54), P3 (105.65,-5.95), SP1 (126.685,-27.9). The three AGND vias are at (37.25,-33.75), (38.10,-33.25), (39.25,-33.25) and the nearest GND via is at (33.70,-31.20), 2.843 mm away — exact. /CPU/LGND is 40.44 mm2 on B.Cu (two islands) plus 40.47 mm2 on In2, its only pads are EM1.6, EM2.4 and P4 pins 6/7/8, and the choke pairing (EM1 pads 1<->6 GND<->LGND, EM2 pads 3<->4 GND<->LGND) means two windings in parallel; DigiKey confirms ACM2520-801-3P-T002 at 800 Ohm/100 MHz, 150 mA, DCR 1.6 Ohm per line max, 3 lines — so ~0.8 Ohm is right. ONE EXCEPTION: 'ZERO crossings of the GND/AGND boundary' is not quite true. Sweeping every F.Cu signal segment against the In1 filled polygons, one segment crosses: Net-(C71-Pad1) from (97.818,-34.596) to (97.818,-33.245), with 0.19 mm over In1 GND and 0.96 mm over In1 AGND. C71 and R71 are both DNP, so it is a depopulated touch-sensor net and the verdict survives — but the claim should say 'one crossing, on a DNP net' rather than zero. Minor: P3 is 20 mm from U6, not 'a few mm', though both sit inside the AGND island so the return still never traverses NT1.
findings.correction: One F.Cu signal segment does cross the In1 GND/AGND boundary — Net-(C71-Pad1), (97.818,-34.596)->(97.818,-33.245) — but C71/R71 are DNP, so the conclusion is unchanged. P3 is 20 mm from U6, not a few mm.

findings.title: Explicitly checked: neither ferrite bead forms the bead-plus-ceramic resonance, and the link-port chokes are damped by their series resistors
findings.current_part: EM3 and EM7 are Bourns MH1608-601Y, 0603 ferrite beads: 600 Ohm +/- 25% at 100 MHz, 1 A rated, 0.2 Ohm max DCR. EM3 is in series between the VDD35 rail and the link connector's VDD pin - net map confirms Net-(P4-VDD35) has exactly two pads, EM3 pad 2 and P4 pin 1, with NO capacitor. EM7 is in series between /~RESET and Net-(U1H-~RESET), which again has exactly two pads, EM7 pad 2 and U1 pin 125, with no capacitor. EM1/EM2 are TDK ACM2520-801-3P-T002 3-line common-mode chokes: 800 Ohm at 100 MHz, 150 mA rated, 1.6 Ohm DCR per line. On the board side of the chokes each link line passes through RA1 (4 x 330 Ohm array); three of the four have a 100 pF shunt (C18 on Net-(RA1C-R3.2), C19 on Net-(RA1D-R4.2), C20 on Net-(RA1B-R2.2)).
findings.proposal: No change on the resonance question. See the separate finding about the missing fourth 100 pF.
findings.benefit: The classic mistake asked about is NOT present, and here is the arithmetic rather than an assertion. For a resonance you need the bead's inductance working against a capacitor on its far side; both beads have an open-ended far side. Even taking the crudest inductance estimate from the impedance spec, L ~ Z/(2 pi f) = 600/(2 pi x 1e8) = 0.95 uH, and pairing it with the CPU pin's own ~5 pF, f = 1/(2 pi sqrt(0.95e-6 x 5e-12)) = 73 MHz - at which frequency the bead is almost entirely resistive (that is what a 600 Ohm at 100 MHz part is), so Q is far below 1 and there is nothing to peak. On the link chokes, the differential leakage inductance is typically a few percent of the common-mode 1.27 uH (= 800/(2 pi x 1e8)), so take 50 nH against the 100 pF shunt: f = 1/(2 pi sqrt(50e-9 x 100e-12)) = 2.25 MHz, characteristic impedance sqrt(L/C) = 22.4 Ohm, and with RA1's 330 Ohm in series Q = 22.4/330 = 0.068 - heavily overdamped. No peaking anywhere. Also worth stating: VDD35 is not fed by any regulator on this board - the pad-level net map shows its ten pads are C6, C7, C17, C51, EM3.1, P1 pin 1, P1 pad C1, R2.1, R35.2 and U1 pin 38, with no source - so it is generated inside the salvaged AGB CPU and feeds the cartridge. At 1.75x the cartridge bus toggles 75% faster and draws that much more from a regulator whose limit is undocumented; the only board-side lever is bulk capacitance, and VDD35 currently has 3 x 0.1 uF + 1 x 1 uF = 1.3 uF nominal, with C17 stranded at (85.22,-67.00), far from both U1 pin 38 (72.34,-45.22) and the cart pins.
findings.risk: None. If anyone wants to act on the VDD35 observation, adding bulk there is a PCB revision and is speculative until someone actually scopes VDD35 at 1.75x with a cartridge inserted - I would not change it on the strength of this analysis alone.
findings.verify_reason: The load-bearing facts are net-map facts and they are all exact. Net-(P4-VDD35) has exactly two pads, EM3.2 and P4.1 (VDD35) — no capacitor. Net-(U1H-~RESET) has exactly two pads, EM7.2 and U1.125 (~RESET) — no capacitor. So neither bead has a capacitor on its far side and the bead/ceramic resonance genuinely cannot form; that conclusion does not depend on any estimate. VDD35 has exactly the ten pads listed (C6, C7, C17, C51, EM3.1, P1 pin 1, P1 pad C1, R2.1, R35.2, U1 pin 38) with no regulator, confirming it is generated inside the CPU; its bulk is 3 x 0.1u + 1 x 1u = 1.3 uF; and C17's VDD35 pad really is stranded at (85.225,-67.000) while U1 pin 38 is at (72.340,-45.220). RA1's 330 Ohm array feeds three shunted lines. Component specs verified independently: Bourns MH1608-601Y is 600 Ohm +/-25% at 100 MHz, 1 A, DCR 0.2 Ohm max, 0603; TDK ACM2520-801-3P-T002 is 800 Ohm at 100 MHz, 150 mA, 1.6 Ohm DCR per line. The Q arithmetic reproduces (0.95 uH from Z/2pi f, 73 MHz against 5 pF; 1.27 uH common mode, 50 nH leakage against 100 pF -> 2.25 MHz, sqrt(L/C) = 22.4 Ohm, Q = 22.4/330 = 0.068). CAVEAT, which the finding itself flags: L = Z/(2 pi f) is a crude proxy for a lossy bead, and the 5 pF pin capacitance and the 'few percent' leakage inductance are assumptions rather than datasheet values. Because the conclusion rests on the absence of a capacitor rather than on those estimates, it survives. The VDD35 observation is correctly labelled speculative and correctly not acted on.

findings.title: Only three of the four link-port lines get the 100 pF shunt - SCK is unfiltered and unbalances the common-mode choke
findings.current_part: Each of the four link lines passes through RA1 (330 Ohm array) then a common-mode choke winding. Net map: Net-(RA1B-R2.2) has C20 (100p) and EM2 pad 1; Net-(RA1C-R3.2) has C18 (100p) and EM1 pad 2; Net-(RA1D-R4.2) has C19 (100p) and EM1 pad 3. But Net-(RA1A-R1.2) - which goes to EM2 pad 2 and out to P4 pin 5 (SCK) - has NO shunt capacitor; it carries RA1 pad 8 and TP25 (the "SCK" test point) instead. There is no footprint for a fourth capacitor.
findings.proposal: On a PCB revision, add a fourth 100 pF (0603) from Net-(RA1A-R1.2) to GND alongside C18/C19/C20, giving all four lines the same 330 Ohm / 100 pF network (corner frequency 1/(2 pi x 330 x 100e-12) = 4.82 MHz, comfortably above the GBA link's fastest 2 Mbit/s mode). Keep TP25.
findings.benefit: EMC only, and modest. A common-mode choke rejects common-mode current in proportion to how well matched the two lines through it are. On EM2, one line (SD) sees 330 Ohm into 100 pF and the other (SCK) sees 330 Ohm into an open, so the two windings terminate into different impedances and the choke converts common-mode to differential and back. The unfiltered line is also the clock, which is the line with the most harmonic energy and the one that runs to an external cable acting as an antenna. I am not going to put a dB number on it without a chamber measurement.
findings.risk: Low, but it may be deliberate: SCK is the one line where a 4.8 MHz corner could matter if anyone ever pushes the link port hard, and it is the line with the test point. If the intent was to preserve SCK edges, leave it and note the reason in the schematic. Needs a PCB revision either way - there is no spare pad.
findings.verify_reason: The net map is exactly as described. Net-(RA1A-R1.2) carries three pads — EM2.2, RA1.8 and TP25 ('SCK' test point) — and no capacitor; Net-(RA1B-R2.2) has C20 (100p) + EM2.1 + RA1.7; Net-(RA1C-R3.2) has C18 + EM1.2 + RA1.6; Net-(RA1D-R4.2) has C19 + EM1.3 + RA1.5. So three of four lines get a 100 pF shunt and SCK does not, and there is no spare footprint for a fourth. Corner frequency 1/(2 pi x 330 x 100e-12) = 4.82 MHz — correct, and comfortably above the GBA link's 2 Mbit/s maximum. The mode-conversion argument is textbook-correct in direction: EM2's two windings do terminate into different impedances. HOWEVER the finding earns its own low confidence and I would not raise it: it puts no dB number on the effect and explicitly declines to, it concedes the asymmetry may be deliberate (SCK is the one line with a test point), and it needs a PCB revision for an unquantified EMC benefit on a hobbyist board with no emissions requirement. Verified as fact; treat as the lowest-priority item on the list.

findings.title: 314 mm of signal routing is cut through the In1 GND plane and 408 mm through In2 - the buses happen to miss it, but the ClockxControl clock does not
findings.current_part: Routing census over all three board files (identical on the plane layers): In1.Cu carries 314.1 mm of signal trace and 36.8 mm of power trace; In2.Cu carries 408.4 mm of signal and 79.0 mm of power. The biggest offenders are the button lines - /CPU/TP8 124.51 mm on In2, /CPU/TP2 81.53 mm on In2 and 38.66 mm on In1, /CPU/TP3 49.35 mm on In2, /CPU/TP5 37.97 mm on In1, /CPU/TP7 34.92 mm on In1, /CPU/VSHD 30.95 mm on In1 - plus Net-(Q5B-G) 10.56 mm on In1 (see the open-circuit finding). At 0.25 mm trace plus 0.2 mm clearance each side, that is roughly 0.65 mm x 314 mm = 204 mm2 of slot cut into a 5024 mm2 In1 pour, about 4%.
findings.proposal: On any respin, pull signal routing off In1 entirely and off In2 wherever it crosses a fast net's return path. Where that is not possible, at least keep the slots away from the clock and bus regions.
findings.benefit: I tested the actual consequence rather than assuming it, and the result is mixed. GOOD: I checked every F.Cu CPU-to-RAM and CPU-to-cart bus segment (MD, MA, PHI, ~RD, ~WE_RAM, ~OE_RAM) against every In1 signal slot and found ZERO crossings - the buses never have to detour around a slot in their reference plane, which is why the board works well at stock speed. BAD: in the ECO-6 file the CXC_CLK trace on B.Cu crosses 5 slots cut into In2 by /CPU/TP1, TP2, TP3, TP8 and /~VCNT5. That is on top of the 15 reference-net changes already counted in the clock-routing finding, so the 7.34 MHz clock is the one net on the board whose return path is comprehensively broken.
findings.risk: Re-routing plane-layer traces on a board this dense is a substantial respin, and the button lines that are on the planes are DC-slow so there is no urgency for their own sake - the case is entirely about the slots they leave behind. Fixing just the 5 slots the clock crosses is far cheaper than a general cleanup, and is subsumed by moving CXC_CLK to F.Cu.
findings.verify_reason: This is the most precisely reproducible finding in the set — every number matches my independent extraction. Summing segment lengths by layer and classifying power vs signal nets: In1.Cu 314.1 mm signal and 36.8 mm power; In2.Cu 408.4 mm signal and 79.0 mm power — identical across the stock board, the ECO-5 fork and the ECO-6 CXC file, exactly as claimed. Per-net: /CPU/TP8 124.51 mm on In2, /CPU/TP2 81.53 on In2 and 38.66 on In1, /CPU/TP3 49.35 on In2, /CPU/TP5 37.97 on In1, /CPU/TP7 34.92 on In1, /CPU/VSHD 30.95 on In1 — all exact — and Net-(Q5B-G) 10.57 mm on In1 (finding says 10.56). Slot arithmetic 0.65 x 314 = 204 mm2 is right; the 5024 mm2 denominator is the In1 pour taken before subtraction (the GND island alone measures 4023.38 mm2 and AGND 1001.16, summing to 5024.5) — internally consistent, though the resulting '4%' is the fraction of both In1 planes, not of the GND plane alone. The clock-crossing claim is verified and UNDERSTATED: buffering each CXC_CLK segment and testing against every non-power In2 trace, the B.Cu run does cross slots cut by /CPU/TP1, /CPU/TP2, /CPU/TP3, /CPU/TP8 and /~{VCNT5} — the exact five named — and the F.Cu portions additionally cross In1 slots cut by /CPU/Display/VCOM and /CPU/VSHD, which the finding does not mention. The 'buses never cross an In1 slot' claim is consistent with what I see (the MD/MA bus routing on F.Cu sits well away from the In1 signal runs). The recommendation to fix only the five slots the clock crosses, rather than a general cleanup, is the right economic call.

domainSummaries:
[converter] The 29 mW AGBM-01/AGBM-02 idle gap is NOT the "VIN approaches VOUT" hypothesis — with 2xAA (3.2 V fresh alkaline, ~2.5 V eneloop) VIN never reaches VOUT3 = 3.336 V, so the LTC3527 always boosts. The gap is structural: the LTC3527 makes ONE Burst Mode decision for BOTH channels ("both VOUT1 and VOUT2 must be under a light load current condition"), so the ~0.7 mA 5 V rail is forced into fixed-frequency 1.2 MHz PWM whenever the ~37 mA 3.3 V rail is loaded — worth ~6 mW off the datasheet's own burst-vs-fixed curves — plus ~2.3 mW of extra conduction loss and ~2.7 mW of active Iq (500 uA from VOUT vs 2x11 uA for the TPS63802); the residual ~18 mW is 1.2 MHz switching/core loss I cannot separate from published data. The two biggest actionable levers are outside the IC: PTC1 (0805L075SLYR, R up to 160 mOhm post-reflow) carries the entire ~480 mA in-use input current and its 0.47 A hold current at 60 C is already BELOW the peak in-use draw — the same-family 0805L150SLYR is a drop-in that saves ~12 mW in use (~17 mW overclocked) and removes a real nuisance-trip risk; and VOUT3 is wired to the LTC3527's WEAK channel 2 (0.50/0.60 Ohm switches, 400 mA limit) while the light 5 V rail sits on the strong channel 1 (0.30/0.40 Ohm, 800 mA) — swapping them is a zero-BOM-cost schematic/PCB change worth 6-16 mW and it removes a brownout that the ClockxControl otherwise causes at low battery.
  anchors: RAIL VOLTAGES (computed, not assumed): LTC3527 V_FB = 1.20 V typ (1.176-1.224 V), from the datasheet Electrical Characteristics. VOUT5 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78M/560k) = 5.014 V. VOUT3 = 1.20 x (1 + 1.78M/1.00M) = 3.336 V. AGBM-02 for comparison: TPS63802 V_FB = 500 mV, VOUT5 = 0.5 x (1+820k/91k) = 5.006 V, VOUT3 = 0.5 x (1+510k/91k) = 3.302 V. FSEL = GND -> f_sw = 1.2 MHz (0.9/1.2/1.5 MHz min/typ/max).

BATTERY: MouseBiteLabs' Required-Parts wiki states all AGBM-0X testing was done with eneloop pro NiMH, so the measured 170/141 mW are at a NiMH pack voltage, not 3.2 V alkaline. I use V_pack = 2.50 V at idle and 2.45 V at heavy load (2 x 1.25/1.22 V per cell). ESTIMATE; the design envelope is 1.8-3.2 V. Everything below scales as 1/V_pack.

INPUT CURRENT (derived): idle 170 mW / 2.50 V = 68 mA. In use 410 mW / 2.55 V = 161 mA (FP ITA, min brightness) up to 1175 mW / 2.45 V = 480 mA (Hispeedido IPS, max brightness + Everdrive + max volume). All of this flows through F1 and PTC1 (netlist: BT1+ -> F1 -> VBATT -> PTC1 -> VCC -> L1/L2 + U5 VIN/VIN1/VIN2; SW1 is NOT in the power path, it only gates /EN).

VOUT5 LOAD: at idle the only DC load is DL1 (green power LED) through R25 = 3.3 k, plus IC quiescent -> ~0.7 mA, P5 ~3.5 mW. ESTIMATE (LED Vf not verified). In use, the max-vs-min-brightness delta of 1175-568 = 607 mW at the battery is essentially all backlight -> ~88 mA on VOUT5 at max brightness, ~10 mA at min.

VOUT3 LOAD: back-solved from AGBM-02. 141 mW in, minus ~4.4 mW for its 5 V converter, = 136.6 mW into the 3.3 V TPS63802; at 90% (Fig 10-5, VI=2.5 V, VO=3.3 V) that is 123 mW out = 37 mA at 3.336 V. ESTIMATE. In use: 135 mA (min brightness) to ~180 mA (max brightness with audio). I use 150 mA as the typical in-use anchor.

CLOCKxCONTROL: +12 mA on VDD3 (module V+ lands on P1 pad S1 = VDD3, fed from VOUT3 through U18 TPS22917, 1:1 current) and +40-60 mA of extra core current. The AGB core and SRAM are on VDD2 = 2.5 V from U8 NCV8164, an LDO whose input is VOUT3, so an LDO passes that current 1:1 back to VOUT3. Central case +50 mA -> VOUT3 goes 150 -> 212 mA in use, 37 -> 49 mA at idle. FLAG: insideGadgets publish 40-60 mA as a console-level figure, not a per-rail one; if part of it is actually on VDD3 or VDD35 the split changes but the VOUT3 total does not, because every one of those rails is fed from VOUT3.

CONDUCTION-LOSS MODEL (CCM boost, VIN 2.45 V, VOUT3 3.336 V, L 4.7 uH, f 1.2 MHz): D = 1 - 2.45/3.336 = 0.2656. dI_pp = VIN*D/(L*f) = 0.6507/5.64 = 0.1154 A. I_L,avg = Iout/(1-D). I_rms^2 = I_avg^2 + dI^2/12. Effective switch resistance ch2 = 0.2656 x 0.50 + 0.7344 x 0.60 = 0.5734 Ohm; ch1 = 0.2656 x 0.30 + 0.7344 x 0.40 = 0.3734 Ohm; inductor DCR 0.120 Ohm. CCM is valid for the 3.3 V channel at >= ~42 mA out; the 5 V channel at light backlight is in DCM and I do not quote CCM numbers there.

[linear-rails] VOUT3 computes to exactly 3.336 V from the LTC3527's 1.20 V feedback reference and the R23/R55 = 1.78 M/1.00 M divider, which makes both LDOs 74.87% efficient (2.5/3.336 x 30/30.03) — an arithmetic match to MouseBiteLabs' own "roughly 75% efficient" statement about the audio supply, which confirms the whole model. U8 therefore throws away 25.1% of every milliwatt the CPU core draws: 25.2 mW at 1x (27.4 mW referred to the battery, 16% of the 170 mW idle figure) rising to ~40 mW at 1.75x (43.7 mW at the battery), of which ~15 mW is new heat created by the overclock. The real lever is replacing U8 with a switcher: a buck from VOUT3 (TPS62840, D = 0.75, comfortably viable, ~93% from Fig 18) wins 21 mW at 1x / 34 mW at 1.75x, and a buck-boost straight off VCC (TPS63900/TPS63802, skipping the boost entirely) wins 25 mW / 39 mW — but both are blocked by a detail nobody counts: U8's PGOOD output is the enable for U4 and U18 and none of the candidate switchers has one, so this is a schematic change, not a part swap. The cheap partial win — lowering VOUT3 by one resistor — is real but small at 4-10 mW, and there is no drop-in LDO worth anything at all (0.1 mW).
  anchors: RAIL VOLTAGES (computed, not assumed). LTC3527 datasheet EC table: "Feedback Voltage FB1, FB2 | 1.176 | 1.20 | 1.224 V" and pin description "The output voltage can be adjusted from 1.6V to 5.25V by VOUT1 = 1.2[1 + R1/R2]". With R23 = 1.78 M / R55 = 1.00 M: VOUT3 = 1.20 x 2.78 = 3.336 V. Cross-check on the other channel, R21 = 1.78 M / R22 = 560 k: VOUT5 = 1.20 x 4.17857 = 5.014 V — a sane 5 V rail, which confirms the 1.20 V reference reading. Worst case with the +/-2% FB spec and +/-1% resistors, VOUT3 spans 3.228-3.447 V. VDD2 = VAUD = 2.500 V from the NCV8164 ordering table: "NCV8164ASN250T1G | 2.5 V | MP | With Active Output Discharge | TSOP-5 (Pb-Free)".

CURRENTS. There is no published per-rail measurement of the AGB CPU's 2.5 V core current. I looked: the Zekfoo/AGZ circuit-level GBA redesign publishes switching frequencies but no rail currents, and the GBAtemp current-draw threads are system-level only. The only anchor is MouseBiteLabs' own annotation on the AGBM-01 root schematic, placed directly above U8 at (111.76, 90.42) under the heading "2.5V Supply": "2.5V @ ~30mA", part of a block headed "Rough estimates (rounded up)". The same block gives "3.3V@~10mA (no cart)", "3.3V@~20mA", "3.3V@~50mA (Everdrive)", "5.0V @ ~130mA", and next to U4 at (241.3, 138.68): "~100mW" — which matches MBL's public statement that audio is "something like 50 to 100 mW at max volume". So I take I_VDD2(1x) = 30 mA and I_VAUD(max) = 40 mA (100 mW / 2.5 V); I_VAUD(idle) I estimate at ~5 mA, which is my own number chosen to close the idle budget below, not a measured or published one.

BOOST EFFICIENCY (used to refer rail savings back to the battery). MODE = GND and FSEL = GND on this board; the LTC3527 datasheet says "MODE = Low: Automatic Burst Mode operation" and "sets the switching frequency to 1.2MHz if the FSEL pin is below 0.35V". The applicable curve is therefore G05, "Efficiency vs Load Current and VIN for VOUT2 = 3.3V at 1.2MHz", BURST traces: at VIN = 2.4 V and 10-100 mA these sit at 92-94%. I use eta_boost = 0.92.

IDLE RECONCILIATION (this is what validates the 30 mA). VOUT3 draw at idle = U8 input 3.336 x 30.03 mA = 100.2 mW, plus VDD3 at 10 mA (no cart) x 3.336 = 33.4 mW through U18 (TPS22917 Ron ~100 mOhm at 3.3 V, so 6 mV drop at 60 mA — VDD3 = VOUT3 for all practical purposes), plus U4 input at ~5 mA = 16.7 mW, plus the R23+R55 = 2.78 M divider at 1.2 uA = 4 uW. Total 150.3 mW at VOUT3. Divided by 0.92 = 163 mW at the battery. Measured AGBM-01 idle is 170 mW, leaving 7 mW for the LTC3527's own quiescent (12 uA Burst measured on VOUT), three TPS3840 supervisors, the VOUT5 standby loop and the pull-up network. That closes to within 4%, so MBL's ~30 mA is credible.

OVERCLOCK MODEL (this one is modelled, not measured — treat with the confidence I assign it). CPU dynamic power scales with clock; the core and the SRAM are both on VDD2, and SRAM active current also scales with access rate. Model I_VDD2(f) = I_static + 1.75 x I_dyn with I_static + I_dyn = 30 mA at 1x: 100% dynamic gives 52.5 mA (delta 22.5), 80% gives 48.0 mA (delta 18.0), 60% gives 43.5 mA (delta 13.5). I use 48 mA / delta 18 mA as the central case, range 44-53 mA. Cross-check against insideGadgets, verbatim from the product page: "Consumes about 12mA of additional current and when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more." Both of those are stated as additional current the *console* draws, i.e. at the battery, for GBA/GBC/DMG generically — NOT per-rail, and I am not silently treating them as such. At a 2xAA pack around 2.9 V, 40-60 mA is 116-174 mW extra at the battery = ~107-160 mW extra at the rails. My VDD2 delta accounts for 18 mA x 3.336 = 60 mW of that; the balance has to be CPU I/O switching on VDD3 (address/data bus, LCD, cart) plus the cart itself, which is where you would expect it. Consistent, but not independently confirmed. Note where the module's own 12 mA lands: its V+ is on P1 pad S1 = VDD3, so it costs 12 mA x 3.336 = 40.0 mW at VOUT3 (43.5 mW at the battery) and passes through the TPS22917 load switch — it never touches U8.

ENVELOPE CHECK. All savings I quote below are 4-40 mW against a 170 mW idle and a 410-1175 mW in-use envelope. The biggest single number in this domain (39 mW for a buck-boost off VCC at 1.75x) is 23% of idle and 3.3% of the 1175 mW peak. Nothing here is a factor-of-two change.

[battery-path] The whole series path from the pack to the boost is two 0805 parts — F1 (2 A fuse, 0.080 Ω max) and PTC1 (0.75 A LoRho PPTC, 0.040 Ω min / 0.160 Ω max) — for 0.120–0.240 Ω total; board copper adds only ~6 mΩ and SW1 carries no load current at all (verified from the netlist: VBATT→PTC1→VCC goes straight to U5, the switch only drives an enable network drawing ~170 µA). That series R costs 10–20 mW at a typical 700 mW in-use draw and 68–135 mW at the overclocked low-battery peak; a one-part drop-in swap of PTC1 to 0805L150SLYR recovers 2–8 mW typical / 14–53 mW at peak, and a lower-R fuse or a 0 Ω build option in F1 adds another 3–17 mW. The bigger finding is not efficiency but stability: PTC1's hold current derates to 0.62 A at 40 °C and 0.47 A at 60 °C (Littelfuse table), while the ClockxControl pushes peak input current to roughly 0.70–0.78 A at a partly discharged pack — the fitted PPTC sits inside its own indeterminate hold/trip band and will heat, add resistance, and can latch off. Two correctness problems: both PCB footprints carry a stale Value "0467001.NR" which is a 0603 1 A fuse (wrong size, wrong function, no resettable protection), and D1 sits on the wrong side of F1 so its reverse-battery fault current never passes through the fuse.
  anchors: Pack voltage: 2 x AA, 3.2 V fresh to ~1.8 V at end of life. Energizer E91 datasheet gives nominal internal resistance 150-300 mohm per cell fresh (https://data.energizer.com/pdfs/e91.pdf), so pack ESR 0.30-0.60 ohm — 2 to 5x the entire board-side series resistance, which bounds how much of the total loss I can address.

[passives] The passive selection on this board is much better than the "no dielectric in the schematic" worry suggests: the schematic Source fields resolve to real MPNs, and they are conservative parts — 25 V X5R for the 22 uF/10 uF bulk, 16 V and 50 V X7R for the 1 uF/0.1 uF decoupling, C0G for the 15 pF feed-forward, and case-B tantalum (not MLCC) for the 100 uF audio caps. I fetched and digitised the manufacturers' own DC-bias curves: the only significant deration is C21 (22 uF 25 V X5R 0805 -> 10.7 uF at 5.014 V, 49 % of nominal) and the 10 uF 0603s (-26 % at 2.5 V, -39 % at 3.34 V); the 1 uF X7R loses 3 % at 2.5 V and the 0.1 uF loses nothing. None of that breaks a datasheet requirement, so the derating story is a "check and move on", not a lever. The real findings are elsewhere: three assembly/correctness defects (polarized tantalums on a symmetric MLCC land with no polarity silk; CP1 used as a bidirectional AC coupler with 0 V DC bias; the SRAM and the ClockxControl's VDD3 tap both have no local bypass at all), and one honest efficiency lever worth 3-11 mW (L1/L2 DCR) that needs a PCB revision to collect. Total realistic energy recoverable in this domain is roughly 4-12 mW against a 792-1420 mW overclocked in-use budget, i.e. under 1 %. The EM chokes and beads carry no current and are worth exactly 0 mW.

[audio] The audio chain is a 1-bit PWM reconstruction path, not an analogue one: the AGB CPU's SO1/SO2 PWM outputs are re-buffered by U9 onto the 2.5 V VAUD rail (so VAUD is the DAC's full-scale reference, which is why it gets its own low-noise LDO), filtered by a textbook 4th-order Butterworth Sallen-Key at 15.84 kHz built from U7's four sections, attenuated by VR2, and amplified by U6 at a gain of only 0.2. The single biggest thing in this domain is a correctness bug that is also the biggest efficiency lever: U7 is a TLV9364QPWRQ1, whose datasheet minimum supply is 4.5 V and whose input common-mode ceiling is (V+)-2 V — it is being run at 2.5 V with its inputs at 1.25 V, and its rated 2.6 mA/amplifier quiescent is ~10.4 mA, roughly 80% of the whole audio chain's ~12.75 mA standing current. Swapping it for the pin-identical TLV9064IPWR (1.8-5.5 V, RRIO, 538 µA/amp) is a drop-in that both fixes the violation and wins back ~31 mW at the battery — about 18% of AGBM-01's 170 mW idle, and roughly 12-16% of what the ClockxControl costs. Everything else in the domain is either quality-only (worth ~0 mW) or large-but-invasive (a class-D speaker amp is worth ~48 mW at MouseBiteLabs' own max-volume operating point but needs a schematic and PCB redesign and puts a 250 kHz switcher 1.3 mm from the ClockxControl window).

RECONCILIATION AGAINST MOUSEBITELABS' "50 to 100 mW at max volume". The 47.3 mW quiescent floor computed above IS essentially their 50 mW lower bound. Taking their 100 mW upper bound: 100 mW x 0.90 / 3.34 V = 26.9 mA total; minus the 12.75 mA quiescent leaves 14.2 mA of class-AB output-stage current. For a BTL class-AB stage the supply current equals the rectified load current, I_avg = (2/pi)(Vp/RL), so Vp = 14.2 mA x (pi/2) x 8 Ohm = 0.178 V peak differential, i.e. Pout = 0.178^2/(2 x 8) = 2.0 mW into the 8 Ohm speaker. That is a completely realistic max-volume PROGRAM AVERAGE (game audio has 10-15 dB crest factor), so the model closes against their measurement. All output-stage arithmetic below uses this 14.2 mA / 2.0 mW operating point as the "max volume" anchor.

GAIN STRUCTURE / MAX CAPABILITY (from the schematic + LM4853 datasheet). PWM full scale = VAUD = 2.5 Vpp, so a full-scale recovered sine is 1.25 Vpk = 0.884 Vrms at the filter output. LM4853 is inverting with Ri = R30/R31 = 100 k and Rf = R56/R57 = 20 k, so SE gain = 0.2 per channel and BTL AVD = 2 x Rf/Ri = 0.4 per input (L and R are summed internally in BTL mode, so a correlated mono signal sees 0.8). Max speaker output = 0.8 x 0.884 = 0.707 Vrms differential = 62 mW into 8 Ohm (I_avg would be 79.6 mA, 199 mW at VAUD — far above MBL's figure, confirming their number is program-average not sine). Max headphone output = 0.2 x 0.884 = 0.177 Vrms into 32 Ohm = 0.98 mW/channel, which is only ~4% of the LM4853's 25 mW/32 Ohm capability at 2.7 V — a deliberate and good choice for THD and noise.

[clockxcontrol] The single most important answer is negative in a good way: the VDD2 LDO is not the bottleneck. U8 (NCV8164ASN250T1G, TSOP-5) is rated 300 mA with a 350 mA minimum current limit and 158 °C/W θJA; my worst-case VDD2 draw at 1.75x is ~82 mA, giving 68.6 mW of dissipation and an 11 °C junction rise — roughly 3.5x current margin and 4x thermal margin. The real constrained node is one level up: VOUT3 is fed by LTC3527 **converter 2**, the 400 mA-switch channel, and it carries VDD2, VAUD and VDD3 (all logic, all cart, all audio), while the 800 mA channel drives only the screen rail. Converter 2's guaranteed capability at 3.336 V is ~220 mA at VIN 2.4 V and ~178 mA at the 2.0 V supervisor cutoff; my worst-case 1.75x estimate is 150–207 mA, so the overclock consumes most of the remaining margin on nearly-flat cells. The biggest efficiency lever the overclock creates is U8 itself: it burns exactly (3.336−2.500) = 0.836 V × I_VDD2, which is 25.1 mW at 1x idle and 43.9–68.6 mW at 1.75x — replacing it with a ~89 %-efficient buck wins back 21 mW typical and 49 mW at 1.75x in a game, about a third of the whole overclock cost. Everything else in my domain is small: the depopulation of C3 and C4 is worth ~4.9 mW at the battery at 1.75x (and ECO-6's stated reason for removing C4 is wrong — C4 is still tied to CK2 through R41), and the 73.5 mm CLK run is electrically fine for timing but is referenced to a patchwork of five different In2.Cu power islands, which is worth fixing while the ECO is still on paper.

### 2. The same accounting with the ClockxControl fitted

#### 2a. Where the module's current actually lands — and the flag

From the netlist, unambiguously: the module's V+ is on P1 pad **S1 = VDD3**, fed from VOUT3 through U18 (TPS22917, ~90 mΩ, 1 mV of drop — irrelevant). The overclock's extra CPU current is on **VDD2**, which is U8's output; an LDO passes its load current 1:1, so that current appears on **VOUT3** too. CPU I/O switching is on **VDD3**. The cart reaches VDD35, which has **no source anywhere on the board** (verified — all ten pads are loads or connectors), so it is generated inside the salvaged CPU from its VDD3/VDD2 pins and bills to VOUT3 as well.

**Every part of the ClockxControl's cost — module supply, core dynamic power, I/O switching, cart — lands on LTC3527 converter 2, the 400 mA channel.**

**FLAG, as the brief requires.** insideGadgets publish exactly one sentence: *"Consumes about 12mA of additional current and when the GBA/GBC/DMG is overclocked, it too will use 40-60mA more."* Grammatically "it" is the console. There is no measurement point, no speed, no cartridge or screen condition, and the identical 40–60 mA is quoted for the DMG (3x), the GBC (2x) and the GBA (1.75x) — three different CPUs on three different rails. **It is a system-level, battery-side figure and must not be silently treated as a VOUT3 current.** Doing so inflates the overclock's cost by about 60 %: 50 mA read as battery current is 120 mW at the battery; read as a VOUT3 current it becomes 50 × 3.336 / 0.92 ≈ 181 mW plus series, ~190 mW. Several of the domain reviews took the second reading.

#### 2b. My own model, and the cross-check that settles it

CMOS dynamic power scales with clock; leakage does not. Taking VDD2 as 75 % dynamic and VDD3 I/O as 60 % dynamic **[E, stated basis, no public AGB CPU datasheet exists]**:

The overclock also consumes converter 2's margin. ### 4. The honest headline

**No. The energy the ClockxControl costs cannot be won back. At the maximum effort anyone in this review proposed you recover about 43 % of it, and the change class required to get past 20 % is a schematic change plus a PCB revision on the core rail of a board built around irreplaceable salvaged silicon.**

At the 792 mW representative operating point, with a 6.26 Wh pack:

| Configuration | Power | Runtime | vs stock |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stock, 1x, no module | 792 mW | 7 h 54 m | — |
| **ClockxControl fitted, 1.75x, no fixes** | **951 mW** | **6 h 35 m** | **−1 h 19 m** |
| + all Tier 1 drop-in fixes (32 mW) | 919 mW | 6 h 49 m | −1 h 05 m |
| + Tier 3 core-rail redesign (66 mW total) | 885 mW | 7 h 04 m | −50 m |
| + Tier 4 converter transplant (~69 mW total) | 882 mW | 7 h 06 m | −48 m |

Stated as recovery of the 159 mW the module and overclock cost:

- **Drop-in parts only — 32 mW, 20 %.** Six part swaps and two resistor values, all on existing land patterns, applicable to a board already in a shell. This recovers 14 minutes of the 79 minutes of runtime the overclock takes.
- **One PCB revision of the core rail — 66 mW, 41 %.** Recovers 29 of the 79 minutes.
- **Everything, including a full front-end respin — ~69 mW, 43 %.** Recovers 31 of the 79 minutes. The last 3 mW costs an entire converter redesign.

Three things a builder should take from that:

1. **The single most efficient change on the board is not a power part at all.** U7 is a 4.5 V-minimum op-amp being run on 2.5 V with its inputs 0.75 V above the common-mode ceiling. Replacing it with the pin-identical TLV9064IPWR is a correctness fix that also happens to be the largest drop-in saving here — **12 mW, 37 % of everything Tier 1 recovers**, from a part that is cheaper than the one fitted. Do it whether or not you care about runtime.
2. **21.6 % of the overclock's cost is loss, and 9.4 percentage points of that is one LDO.** U8 burns 15 mW of new heat purely because the CPU core rail is made linearly from a boosted rail. That is the only loss the overclock *creates*, and it is the whole case for Tier 3.
3. **The fixed cost of the module is worse than the marginal cost of the overclock, proportionally.** 12 mA on VDD3 is 44–45 mW at the battery whether you overclock or not — 26 % of the board's entire idle figure, for a part that is doing nothing at 1x. There is no lever anywhere in this review that touches it: it is 12 mA into a 3.336 V rail through a 90 mΩ switch, and the only inefficiency in that path is the boost itself.

And the caveat that bounds all of it: **~13 % of the idle budget (22 mW) is unaccounted**, and in use I can bound the model error to about ±5 % but cannot attribute it to a line. The 22 mW is almost certainly LTC3527 light-load overhead — it is the same energy as the measured AGBM-01/AGBM-02 gap — but the published curves say the converter should be doing better than the measurement shows, and I cannot reconcile that from datasheets alone. **Two five-minute measurements would close it: a current probe on TP16 (VOUT3) and TP13 (VOUT5), at idle and with a game running, at 1x and 1.75x.** Every estimated line in this section collapses to a measured one if someone takes them.
